metrics, macro incantations and other font support
font available in Adobe Type 1 format
font providing LaTeX T1 encoding support

caption: BibTeX style for Frontiers in Bioscience

descriptions.text:
A BibTeX style file made with custom-bib to fit Frontiers in Bioscience requirements:

  • all authors, no et al, full author names, initials abbreviated;
  • only abbreviated journal name italicised, no abbreviation dots;
  • only year, no month, at end of reference; and
  • DOI excluded, ISSN excluded.

name: fbs

caption: Computer Science thesis class for University of Dortmund

descriptions.text: At the department of computer science at the University of Dortmund there are cardboard cover pages for research or internal reports like master/phd-theses. The main function of this LaTeX2e document-class is a replacement for the \maketitle command to typeset a title page that is adjusted to these cover pages.

name: fbithesis

caption: Extended \fbox macro from standard LaTeX

descriptions.text:
This package redefines \fbox to allow an optional argument for different frames. It can be any combination of l)eft, r)ight, t)op, and b)ottom, for example: \fbox[lt]{foo}.

Using uppercase letters or a combination of lowercase and uppercase is also possible.

name: fbox

caption: Create an arithmetic flash card

descriptions.text:
The package is used to create an arithmetic flash card. Addition, subtraction, multiplication and division problems are randomly generated.

The flash cards may be customised. Design and build your own flash card using a dvips/Acrobat Distiller work flow, or a pdfTeX work flow.

name: fc-arith

topics.details: typesetting ‘flash’ cards for teaching and learning
create pdf form fields, use form fields as an integral part of the package
convert PostScript to PDF using Adobe Distiller

caption: A thesis class for the FCAV/UNESP (Brazil)

descriptions.text: This package provides a class and a bibliography style for the FCAV-UNESP (Faculdade de Ciências Agrárias e Veterinárias de Jaboticabal UNESP) brazilian university, written based on the institution rules for thesis publications.

name: fcavtex

caption: Fonts for African languages

descriptions.text: The fonts are provided as Metafont source, in the familiar arrangement of lots of (autogenerated) preamble files and a modest set of glyph specifications. (A similar arrangement appears in the ec and lh font bundles.)

name: fc

topics.details: support for more than one (natural) language

caption: Flow diagrams in LaTeX 2.09

descriptions.text: This is not a package, rather a set of macros to be read using \input, offering a means of drawing structures without the use of the picture environment.

name: fchart

topics.details: graphics produced by one of the *TeX engines

caption: Macros for use in the author's documentation

descriptions.text: The package is not advertised for public use, but is necessary for the support of others of the author’s packages (which are compiled under the ltxdoc class).

name: fcltxdoc

topics.details: macros and tools for preparing documentation

caption: Typesetting financial tables

descriptions.text: In financial reports, text and currency amounts are regularly put in one table, e.g., a year balance or a profit-and-loss overview. This package provides the settings for automatically typesetting such columns, including the sum line (preceded by a rule of the correct width) using the specifier “f”.

name: fcolumn

caption: MetaPost macros for 3D

descriptions.text: These macros allow the production of three-dimensional schemes containing: angles, circles, cylinders, cones and spheres, among other things.

name: featpost

caption: A maths symbol font

descriptions.text: FdSymbol is a maths symbol font, designed as a companion to the Fedra family by Typotheque, but it might also fit other contemporary typefaces.

name: fdsymbol

topics.details: fonts that provide collections of symbols
font available in Adobe Type 1 format

caption: LaTeX thesis template for Fudan University

descriptions.text: This package is a LaTeX thesis template package for Fudan University. It can make it easy to write theses both in Chinese and English.

name: fduthesis

topics.details: work done for the project to upgrade LaTeX

caption: Class for academic works at FEI University Center — Brazil

descriptions.text:
fei is a class created by graduate students and LaTeX enthusiasts that allows students from FEI University Center to create their academic works, be it a monograph, masters dissertation or phd thesis, under the typographic rules of the institution.

The class makes it possible to create a full academic work, supporting functionalities such as cover, title page, catalog entry, dedication, summary, lists of figures, tables, algorithms, acronyms and symbols, multiple authors, index, references, appendices and attachments.

fei is loosely based in the Brazilian National Standards Organization (Associação Brasileira de Normas Técnicas, ABNT) standards for the creation of academic works, such as ABNT NBR 10520:2002 (Citations) and ABNT NBR 6023:2002 (Bibliographic References).

name: fei

caption: Commands for CAS-like windows (Xcas or Geogebra) in TikZ

descriptions.text:
This package provides some commands (in French) to display, with TikZ, windows like Xcas or Geogebra :

  • \begin{CalculFormelGeogebra} and \LigneCalculsGeogebra ;
  • \begin{CalculFormelXcas} and \LigneCalculsXcas.

name: FenetreCas

caption: One-shot changes to token registers such as \everypar

descriptions.text:
The bundle provides two packages, fenxitok and fenixpar.

The fenixtok package provides user macros to add material to a token register; the material will be (automatically) removed from the token register when the register is executed. Material may be added either to the left or to the right, and care is taken not to override any redefinition that may be included in the token register itself.

The fenixpar package uses the macros of fenixtok to provide a user interface to manipulation of the \everypar token register.

The packages require the e-TeX extensions; with them, they work either with Plain TeX or with LaTeX.

name: fenixpar

caption: French version of "graphics in LaTeX"

descriptions.text: This is the French translation of epslatex, and describes how to use imported graphics in LaTeX(2e) documents.

name: fepslatex

topics.details: translation of material from the archive, to another language

caption: Extended version of Knuth’s logo typeface

descriptions.text: The fetamont typeface was designed in Metafont and extends the Logo fonts to complete the T1 encoding. The designs of the glyphs A, E, F, M, N, O, P, S and T are based on the Metafont constructions by D. E. Knuth. The glyphs Y and 1 imitate the shapes of the corresponding glyphs in the METATYPE1 logo.

name: fetamont

topics.details: font available in Adobe Type 1 format

caption: Creates a DB of Bible verses from e-Sword, then fetches them on command

descriptions.text:
This bundle provides two packages, bibpes and fetchbibpes. This pair of packages was motivated by a friend, who was preparing Bible studies lessons using a combination of the application e-Sword and LaTeX. He wanted a ‘database’ of Bible packages from which he could simply ‘fetch’ passages into the LaTeX source file.

Package bibpes is used to develop a database of verses, and package fetchbibpes is used to fetch the verses.

name: fetchbibpes

topics.details: typeset devotional texts and other material of interest to theologians

caption: Fetch the current class name

descriptions.text:
With standard LaTeX you are able to check for the class in use invoking the kernel command \@ifclassloaded. However, doing so you cannot get the explicit class name, unless you want to loop over every possible class name until \@ifclassloaded returns true — don't do that!

With the help of the present package you can obtain the name of the current class with significantly less effort. Just load the package as usual: \usepackage{fetchcls}; then, the control sequence \classname will hold the name you were looking for.

name: fetchcls

caption: Typeset Engineering PhD theses at the University of Porto

descriptions.text: A complete template for thesis/works of Faculdade de Engenharia da Universidade do Porto (FEUP) Faculty of Engineering University of Porto.

name: feupphdteses

caption: Reduce the number of unnecessary float pages

descriptions.text: This package implements a float algorithm extension for handling float pages. It attempts to reduce the number of unnecessary (fairly empty) float pages while making sure that floats nevertheless stay close to their call-outs. Several aspects of the algorithm behavior are adjustable.

name: fewerfloatpages

caption: A font for in-text Feynman diagrams

descriptions.text:
Feyn may be used to produce relatively simple Feynman diagrams within equations in a LaTeX document. While the feynmf package is good at drawing large diagrams for figures, the present package and its fonts allow diagrams within equations or text, at a matching size.

The fonts are distributed as Metafont source, and macros for their use are also provided.

name: feyn

caption: Macros and fonts for creating Feynman (and other) diagrams

descriptions.text:
The feynmf package provides an interface to Metafont (inspired by the facilities of mfpic) to use simple structure specifications to produce relatively complex diagrams. (The feynmp package, also part of this bundle, uses MetaPost in the same way.)

While the package was designed for Feynman diagrams, it could in principle be used for diagrams in graph and similar theories, where the structure is semi-algorithmically determined.

name: feynmf

topics.details: use, and support for use, of Metapost

caption: Feynman diagrams in LaTeX 2.09

descriptions.text:
The feynman package uses LaTeX picture mode commands and various sorts of symbols to construct a Feynman diagram as part of the text of a document.

Note that the package was designed for use with LaTeX 2.09, and more modern and flexible packages are available, notably the feyn/feynmf combination; such packages should be used in new work.

name: feynman

caption: Automatic processing of feynmp graphics

descriptions.text:
The package takes care of running Metapost on the output files produced by the feynmp package, so that the compiled pictures will be available in the next run of LaTeX.

The package honours options that apply to feynmp.

name: feynmp-auto

caption: Freeform slides based on the article class

descriptions.text:
The ffslides ("freeform slides") class is intended to make it easier to place various types of content freely on the page, and therefore easier to design documents with a strong visual component: presentations, posters, research or lecture notes, and so on.

The goal of the class is to be less rigid and less complex than some of the popular presentation-making options. It is essentially a small set of macros added to the article class. A well-organized template file is included, and the documentation is itself an extensive example of the class's capabilities.

name: ffslides

caption: Fixed-font code blocks formatted nicely

descriptions.text: This LaTeX package helps you write source code in your academic papers and make it looks neat. It uses minted and tcolorbox, configuring them the right way, to ensure that code fragments and code blocks look nicer.

name: ffcode

caption: A font for Frege's Grundgesetze der Arithmetik

descriptions.text: The fonts are provided as Metafont source and Adobe Type 1 (pfb) files. A small LaTeX package (fge) is included.

name: fge

topics.details: font available in Adobe Type 1 format

caption: Draw rulers on the foreground or in the text

descriptions.text:
This package draws horizontal and vertical rulers on the foreground of every (or the current) page at absolute positions. In this way, you can check the page layout dimensions. You can also draw various rulers in the text.

The fgruler package requires the services of the following packages: kvoptions, etoolbox, xcolor, graphicx, eso-pic.

name: fgruler

caption: Tools for installing Type 1 fonts in MiKTeX

descriptions.text: Preparing Type1 fonts for MiKTeX is a tedious work. This package contains a small guideline for the font installation and a binary (and its BASIC source) that performs the necessary .pfb conversions. The tool requires the fontinst package. It is specific to MiKTeX 2.3.

name: fi2t1

topics.details: process fonts for use with TeX (includes installation)

caption: Beamer theme for thesis defense presentations at Masaryk University (Brno, Czech Republic)

descriptions.text: A beamer theme for the typesetting of thesis defense presentations at the Masaryk University (Brno, Czech Republic). The theme has been designed for easy extensibility by color themes of other academic institutions.

name: fibeamer

caption: Generate Fibonacci numbers

descriptions.text:
The package provides an expandable command to provide the Fibonacci number for a given index. The command is only limited by the ability of a TeX integer to represent the resulting number,

The package is distributed as part of the oberdiek distribution.

name: fibnum

caption: Filtering files using TeX

descriptions.text:
The package parses plain text or TeX files, using TeX; it generalises the philosophy behind docstrip, based on TeX macro argument processing. The results are not then processed, but written to another file (possibly for later processing by TeX).

The package finds practical application in the author's makedoc package.

The package is part of the author’s nicetext bundle.

name: fifinddo

topics.details: macros and tools for preparing documentation

caption: German HTML beamer presentation on nicetext and morehype

descriptions.text:
The bundle:

  • exhibits the process of making an “HTML beamer presentation” with the blogdot package from the morehype bundle, and
  • HTML generation based on the fifinddo package.

name: fifinddo-info

caption: FIFO and stack implementation for package writers

descriptions.text:
A LaTeX implementation of a combined FIFO Stack modified from the existing stack package by Benjamin Bayart.

The package renames the original’s \Push and \Pop commands \FSPush and \FSPop, and which work on the top/end of the FIFO/Stack), and adds the ability to \FSUnshift and \FSShift from the bottom (front) of the FIFO/Stack.

name: fifo-stack

caption: Convert fig files to English

descriptions.text: This is a program for converting Fig 2.1 graphics language files into understandable English.

name: fig2eng

caption: Convert .fig files to vector graphics

descriptions.text:
The fig2lat program converts Fig drawings created in XFig, jFig or WinFIG to vector graphics formats used in LaTeX/pdfLaTeX environments.

Note that earlier versions of the program were called fig2vect.

The program is part of the dktools bundle, which is no longer hosted on CTAN.

name: fig2lat

caption: Convert fig output to Metafont

descriptions.text: The generated Metafont code uses the mfpic macros.

license.name: Do Not Sell Except by Arrangement

name: fig2mf

topics.details: convert a foreign graphics format for use with TeX

caption: Convert fig output to mfpic

descriptions.text: This package is based on fig2mf, and is firmly targeted at mfpic.

name: fig2mfpic

topics.details: convert a foreign graphics format for use with TeX

caption: Use fig as layout designer for LaTeX

descriptions.text: Fig2sty allows you to generate fancy layouts with LaTeX. The basic idea is to draw layout definitions interactively with XFig and transform this definition to a LaTeX style file. You can then use LaTeX to typeset your text into arbitrarily shaped polygons (frames) within the layout; the setup can also include background figures derived from your fig.

name: fig2sty

topics.details: layout of objects on the page

caption: Yet another Fig to vector converter

descriptions.text:
This package is now distributed as part of the dktools bundle, under a new name: fig2lat.

(Note: dktools is no longer hosted on CTAN.)

name: fig2vect

topics.details: convert a foreign graphics format for use with TeX

caption: Management of figures for large LaTeX documents

descriptions.text:
Fig4LaTeX simplifies management of the figures in a large LaTeX document. Fig4LaTeX is appropriate for projects that include figures with graphics created by XFig — in particular, graphics which use the combined PS/LaTeX (or PDF/LaTeX) export method.

An example document (with its output) is provided.

name: fig4latex

caption: Mini-fonts for figured-bass notation in music

descriptions.text: This package consists of three mini-fonts (and associated metrics) of conventional ligatures for the figured-bass notations 2+, 4+, 5+, 6+ and 9+ in music manuscripts. The fonts are usable with Computer Modern Roman and Sans, and Palatino/Palladio, respectively.

name: figbas

caption: Collect figure captions for later printing

descriptions.text:
This package allows the figure captions to be collected throughout the paper and printed on a separate page at the end. The figures themselves will not appear in the text. This is for purposes of a manuscript for submission. Similarly, tables are not printed in the text, but are outputted at the end, after the figure captions. This package may optionally be used with the longtable environment defined in the package of the same name.

The package is part of the preprint bundle.

name: figcaps

caption: Organize figure databases with BibTeX

descriptions.text:
FigBib lets you organize your figures in BibTeX databases. Some FigBib features are:

  • Store and manage figures in a BibTeX database;
  • Include figures in your LaTeX document with one short command;
  • Generate a List of Figures containing more/other information than the figure captions;
  • Control with one switch where to output the figures, either as usual float objects or in a separate part at the end of your document.

name: FigBib

caption: Pictures for creating children’s activities

descriptions.text: This package was created with the aim of facilitating the work of Elementary School teachers who need to create colorful and attractive activities for their students. It is a product of the Computational Mathematics discipline offered at the Federal University of Viçosa — Campus UFV — Florestal by professor Fernando de Souza Bastos. It makes use of the TikZ and xcolor packages.

name: figchild

topics.details: support for teachers and teaching administrators
jokes, distractions, tongue-in-cheek packages, and other entertainment material

caption: Flow text around a figure

descriptions.text:
Provides a Plain TeX macro \figflow that allows one to insert a figure into an area inset into a paragraph. Command arguments are width and height of the figure, and the figure (and its caption) itself. Usage details are to be found in the TeX file itself.

The package does not work with LaTeX; packages such as wrapfig, floatflt and picins support the needs of LaTeX users in this area.

name: figflow

topics.details: flow text round an insertion in the paragraph

caption: Convert xfig figures with embedded LaTeX commands to EPS

descriptions.text: Figfrag generates EPS from xfig figures replacing all text with its LaTeX equivalent. Consequently, the EPS may be converted to PDF for use with pdfLaTeX. Figfrag includes support for colour and font style.

name: figfrag

caption: Floating figures in Plain TeX

descriptions.text: The macros implement a single stack of floats, and insert a maximum of two per page; the output routine used is an extension of the Plain version.

name: figplace

topics.details: extensions to Plain TeX for higher-level constructs

caption: Create interactive figures in LaTeX

descriptions.text: FigPut allows figures to be specified using JavaScript. The resulting document can be viewed as a static PDF, as usual, or the document can be viewed in a web-browser, in which case the figures are interactive. A variety of interactive widgets are included.

name: figput

topics.details: support for LaTeX(-alike) on the web, or feeding into other applications
call external code and process the result

caption: A tutorial on figures in LaTeX 2.09

descriptions.text: A brief (and not entirely comprehensive) tutorial on the state of graphics in LaTeX 2.09 at the end of the time that version was current.

name: figsinltx

caption: Auto-size graphics

descriptions.text: The FigSize package enables automatic sizing of graphics, especially when including graphics with the graphicx package. The user only has to specify the number of graphics that should fit to a page or fraction there of and the package will dynamically calculate the correct graphics sizes relative to the page size. Thus, graphics can be auto-sized to fill a whole page or fraction and manual changes of graphic sizes are never needed when changing document layouts. Finally, the package's dynamic lengths can be used to allow other document element sizes to be dynamic.

name: FigSize

caption: Hyphenation patterns for Finnish language

descriptions.text:
Two sets of hyphenation patterns are provided; fihyph.tex, and fi8hyph.tex (which is modified from fihyph.tex to make the Finnish accented letters to work with LaTeX2e, adding some \catcode, \uccode, and \lccode commands after the model used in the hyphenation files for the other European languages).

The package is superseded by the Finnish patterns available in the hyph-utf8 bundle.

name: fihyph

caption: Create an external file from within a LaTeX document

descriptions.text:
LaTeX2e’s filecontents and filecontents* environments enable a LaTeX source file to generate external files as it runs through LaTeX. However, there are two limitations of these environments: they refuse to overwrite existing files, and they can only be used in the preamble of a document. The filecontents package removes these limitations, letting you overwrite existing files and letting you use filecontents/filecontents* anywhere.

As of September 2019 the author tells us: “This package is no longer necessary due to its functionality having moved into recent LaTeX kernels. It’s probably better not to move the package to obsolete because users may need it to rebuild old documents. Version 1.5 provides full functionality when run with an older kernel but issues a warning message and disables itself when run with a newer kernel.”

Supply the overwrite option to LaTeX’s built-in filecontents environment to mimic this package’s behavior:

\begin{filecontents}[overwrite]{my-file}...\end{filecontents}

name: filecontents

caption: filecontents + macro + verbatim

descriptions.text:
The package provides two environments called filecontentsdef and filecontentshere. They are derived from the LaTeX filecontents environment as provided by Scott Pakin's filecontents package. In addition to the file creation they either store the (verbatim) contents in a macro (filecontentsdef) or typeset them (verbatim) on the spot (filecontentshere).

The author developed the package to display TeX code verbatim in documentation and the same time produce the corresponding files during the LaTeX run in order to embed them in the PDF as file attachment annotations (by using Scott Pakin's package attachfile).

name: filecontentsdef

caption: Access and compare info and modification dates

descriptions.text: The package provides basic access to the date of a LaTeX source file according to its \Provides... entry (the “info date”) as well as to its modification date according to \pdffilemoddate if the latter is available.

name: filedate

caption: LaTeX’s mechanisms for dealing with file errors

descriptions.text:
Provides files to be used in subverting the response to TeX’s ‘file not found’ errors, when running LaTeX.

This package is part of the latex-tools bundle in the LaTeX required distribution.

name: fileerr

caption: Self-descriptions in file headers

descriptions.text: Functions for GNU Emacs Lisp to add “standard” file headers to a file. These headers contain everything you might want to about a package (and a lot you probably wouldn’t), except that they don't hold any information about distribution or licensing.

name: filehdr

topics.details: plug-ins for editors, for better (La)TeX and Meta* support

caption: Hooks for input files

descriptions.text: The package provides several file hooks (AtBegin, AtEnd, …) for files read by \input, \include and \InputIfFileExists. General hooks for all such files (e.g. all \included ones) and file specific hooks only used for named files are provided; two hooks are provided for the end of \included files — one before, and one after the final \clearpage.

name: filehook

caption: Enhanced display of LaTeX File Information

descriptions.text: The bundle provides two packages, readprov and myfilist. The readprov package provides a means of reading file information without loading the body of the file. The myfilist package uses readprov and controls what \listfiles will report.

name: fileinfo

topics.details: support for keeping track of document development

caption: Provide file modification times, and compare them

descriptions.text: The package provides macros to read and compare the modification dates of files. The files may be .tex files, images or other files (as long as they can be found by LaTeX). It uses the \pdffilemoddate primitive of pdfLaTeX to find the file modification date as PDF date string, parses the string and returns the value to the user. The package will also work for DVI output with recent versions of the LaTeX compiler which uses pdfLaTeX in DVI mode. The functionality is provided by purely expandable macros or by faster but non-expandable ones.

name: filemod

caption: Typeset answers to overprint on printed forms

descriptions.text: The package places picture environments according to a proforma file, and typesets the associated text in the environments. The resulting file is designed to be printed on a single-sheet feed printer, on top of the form itself.

license.name: Do Not Sell Except by Arrangement

name: fillform

caption: Find bibliographic details from SPIRES

descriptions.text:
Findbib is a shell script that enables the user to avoid writing BibTeX database entries for papers that appear on SPIRES: if the citation key is in SPIRES standard form, or is an arXiv preprint number, the bibliographic details are retrieved on-line.

A companion script, addbib, adds the information to an existing BibTeX database.

name: findbib

topics.details: derive BibTeX data from resources other than BibTeX libraries

caption: Find hyphenated words in a document

descriptions.text: Findhyph is a Perl script that will analyse the log file from running your document with \tracingparagraphs=1 set. The output contains enough context to enable you to find the hyphenated word that’s being referenced.

name: findhyph

topics.details: support for generating or improving hyphenation tables

caption: Comfortably draw and typeset finite state machines

descriptions.text: Finomaton is a TCL program that allows users to comfortably draw and typeset finite state machines (automata). The resulting graphs can be exported to plain MetaPost and subsequently be included in TeX and LaTeX documents for excellent typesetting quality. In contrast to many other packages, the mouse can be used to interactively move objects around. States are magnetic to facilitate connection, and any TeX command can be embedded in the labels of states and lines.

name: Finomaton

topics.details: finite-state machines, automata, labelled graphs, etc.

caption: The LaTeX2e File Name Keeper

descriptions.text:
This package “looks over your shoulder” and keeps track of files \input’ed (the LaTeX way) or \include’ed in your document. You then have permanent access to the name of the file currently being processed through the macro \finkfile. FiNK also comes with support for AUC-TeX.

As of version 2.2.1, FiNK has been deprecated and is not maintained anymore. People interested in FiNK's functionality are invited to use a package named currfile instead.

name: FiNK

caption: A Finnish version of plain.bst
name: finplain

caption: Adjust behaviour of the ends of footnotes

descriptions.text: The LaTeX internal command \@finalstrut is used automatically used at the end of footnote texts to insert a strut to avoid mis-spacing of multiple footnotes. Unfortunately the command can cause a blank line at the end of a footnote. The package provides a solution to this problem.

name: finstrut

caption: Fira fonts with LaTeX support

descriptions.text: This package provides LaTeX, pdfLaTeX, XeLaTeX and LuaLaTeX support for the Fira Sans and Fira Mono families of fonts designed by Erik Spiekermann and Ralph du Carrois of Carrois Type Design. Fira Sans is available in eleven weights with corresponding italics: light, regular, medium, bold, …

name: fira

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other font support
font available in Adobe Type 1 format
font designed for use as body font for Latin-based script documents
font providing LaTeX T1 encoding support

caption: Fira sans serif font with Unicode math support

descriptions.text: Fira Math is a sans-serif font with Unicode math support. The design of this font is based on Fira Sans and FiraGO. Fira Math is distributed in OpenType format and can be used with the unicode-math package under XeLaTeX or LuaLaTeX. More support is offered by the firamath-otf package.

name: firamath

caption: Firefox search proformas for CTAN

descriptions.text: Two Firefox plugins for searching CTAN.

name: firefox-ctan-plugins

topics.details: support for work with the CTAN archive

caption: Use OpenType math font Fira Math

descriptions.text: The package offers XeTeX/LuaTeX support for the Sans Serif OpenType Fira Math Font.

name: firamath-otf

caption: A document for absolute LaTeX beginners

descriptions.text:
The document leads a reader, who knows nothing about LaTeX, through the production of a two page document.

The user who has completed that first document, and wants to carry on, will find recommendations for tutorials.

name: first-latex-doc

caption: A short list of go-to LaTeX packages, aimed at a beginner

descriptions.text:
A list of suggested packages for most of what beginners want to do. The goal is to cite one package in each area that is capable and reliable, and that is in MacTeX, MiKTeX, and TeX Live.

This package has become part of latex-doc-ptr as of January 2021.

name: first-packages

caption: Print the first line of a paragraph in a different font

descriptions.text:
This sample file defines a command \firstline. Place the command \firstline at the start of a paragraph, and it will set the first line subject to the font command \Firstlinefont.

The file is part of the Plain TeX samples collection.

name: firstline

topics.details: layout of objects on the page

caption: Examples from “First steps in LaTeX”

descriptions.text: These are the examples that appear in the author’s book, which was published by Birkhäuser, 1999, ISBN 0-8176-4132-7. Among the examples are a number of templates for LaTeX documents.

name: firststeps-xampl

topics.details: copies of examples from a published book

caption: Access to 150 paragraphs of Lorem Fistrum very dummy text

descriptions.text:
Fistrum is a LaTeX package forked from lipsum that produces dummy text for use in documents and examples. The paragraphs were taken with permission from https://www.chiquitoipsum.com/.

Fistrum es un paquete de LaTeX derivado de lipsum que produce texto de ejemplo para usarlo en documentos y ejemplos. Los párrafos se han tomado con permiso de https://www.chiquitoipsum.com/.

name: fistrum

topics.details: dummy text generator for tests and examples

caption: Fit graphics on a page

descriptions.text: The package allows a box (usually an \includegraphics box) to fit on the page. It scales the box to the maximal allowed size within the user-set limits. If there is not enough space on the page, the box is moved to the next one.

name: fitbox

caption: LaTeX macros for Fitch-style natural deduction

descriptions.text: The package provides macros for typesetting natural deduction proofs in Fitch style, with subproofs indented and offset by scope lines.

name: fitch

caption: Thesis class and template for Masaryk University (Brno, Czech Republic)

copyright.owner: Daniel Marek, Jan Pavlovič, Vít Novotný, Tereza Vrabcová, and Petr Sojka

descriptions.text: A document class for the typesetting of theses at the Masaryk University (Brno, Czech Republic). The class has been designed for easy extensibility by style and locale files of other academic institutions.

name: fithesis

caption: Set a rectangular destination and jump to it

descriptions.text:
The package is an implementation of the FitR view-type destination as described in the PDF Reference; it defines one new command \jdRect. The command (optionally) sets a jump to and/or sets a destination of a FitR (Rectangle). (Can you see where \jdRect comes from?).

The package requires eforms (part of the AeB) and collectbox (by Martin Scharrer). Drivers supported are dvips and dvipsone (using Adobe Distiller as the PDF creator); pdfTeX (including LuaTeX); and dvipdfm, dvipdfmx, and XeTeX.

The package was developed in response to a user of the AeB Bundle who was interested in developing documents for students with low vision; the idea is to magnify regions of the document so the student can read more comfortably. Optional special effects are included (JavaScript functions) to help focus one the rectangle as it is magnified, and as the previous view is restored.

name: FitR

topics.details: support for typesetting with low-vision readers in mind
create pdf form fields, use form fields as an integral part of the package
convert PostScript to PDF using Adobe Distiller

caption: Patch bibliographies inappropriately broken by BibTeX

descriptions.text: This Python script deals with the well-known BibTeX bug(feature) whereby BibTeX inserts a "%" in a url to cause the bibliography line to fit into its minuscule vision of what is an acceptable input line for TeX.

name: fixbbl

caption: Permit Computer Modern fonts at arbitrary sizes

descriptions.text:
Overrides the (original) LaTeX restrictions on the sizes at which CM and EC fonts may be used.

This package is part of the LaTeX distribution.

name: fix-cm

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other font support

caption: Fix miscellaneous two column mode features

descriptions.text:
OBSOLETE: do not use in new documents.

This package will do nothing in LaTeX formats after 2015/01/01 as the fixes that it implements were incorporated into the fixltx2e package, which is itself obsolete as since the 2015/01/01 release these fixes are in the LaTeX format itself.

Fix mark handling so that \firstmark is taken from the first column if that column has any marks at all; keep two column floats like figure* in sequence with single column floats like figure.

name: fix2col

topics.details: support for variations of typographic style

caption: Fully scalable version of Computer Modern Math Extension font

descriptions.text:
This package provides a fully scalable version of the Computer Modern Math Extension font for curing sizing problems mainly with lmodern.

It can be used when the main font of the document is Computer Modern (or European Modern, if T1 encoding is selected), or Latin Modern. It redefines the math extension font so that it becomes arbitrarily scalable, using the optical size fonts provided by the AMS together with the original cmex10 font.

name: fixcmex

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other support for maths fonts

caption: Macros for typesetting differential operators

descriptions.text:
This package redefines the \d command in LaTeX and provides an interface to define new commands for differential operators.

It is compatible with pdfTeX, XeTeX and LuaTeX, and can also be used with the unicode-math package.

name: fixdif

caption: Multiple use of the same footnote text

descriptions.text: Provides a \DeclareFixedFootnote command to provide a single command for a frequently-used footnote. The package ensures that only one instance of the footnote text appears on each page (LaTeX needs to be run several times to achieve this).

name: fixfoot

caption: Patches for LaTeX

descriptions.text:
This package does nothing other than issue a warning in current LaTeX Releases.

In earlier releases it was used to distribute bug fixes and improvements to the LaTeX kernel.

See the latexrelease package for further details of the new bug fix policy.

name: fixltx2e

topics.details: support for variations of typographic style

caption: Fix JFM (for *pTeX)

descriptions.text: This package fixes several bugs in the JFM format. Both LaTeX and plain TeX are supported.

name: fixjfm

caption: Improve Latvian language support in XeLaTeX

descriptions.text: The package offers improvement of the Latvian language support in polyglossia, in particular in the area of the standard classes.

name: fixlatvian

topics.details: extra language ‘drivers’ for existing multilingual packages

caption: Allow hyphenation of partially-emphasised substrings

descriptions.text:
The package fixes the problem of TeX failing to hyphenate letter strings that seem (to TeX) to be words, but which are followed by an apostrophe and then an emphasis command. The cause of the problem is not the apostrophe, but the font change in the middle of the string.

The problem arises in Catalan, French, Italian and Romansh.

name: fixltxhyph

topics.details: documentation in and support for typesetting Catalan

caption: Make maths comply with ISO 31-0:1992 to ISO 31-13:1992

descriptions.text:
LaTeX’s default style of typesetting mathematics does not comply with the International Standards ISO 31-0:1992 to ISO 31-13:1992 which require that uppercase Greek letters always be typset upright, as opposed to italic (even though they usually represent variables) and allow for typsetting of variables in a boldface italic style (even though the required fonts are available). This package ensures that uppercase Greek be typeset in italic style, that upright $\Delta$ and $\Omega$ symbols are available through the commands \upDelta and \upOmega; and provides a new math alphabet \mathbold for boldface italic letters, including Greek.

This package used to be part of the was bundle, but has now become a package in its own right.

name: fixmath

caption: Collaborative annotation tool for LaTeX

descriptions.text:
FiXme is a collaborative annotation tool for LaTeX documents. Annotating a document here refers to inserting meta-notes, that is, notes that do not belong to the document itself, but rather to its development or reviewing process. Such notes may involve things of different importance levels, ranging from simple “fix the spelling” flags to critical “this paragraph is a lie” mentions. Annotations like this should be visible during the development or reviewing phase, but should normally disappear in the final version of the document.

FiXme is designed to ease and automate the process of managing collaborative annotations, by offering a set of predefined note levels and layouts, the possibility to register multiple authors, to reference annotations by listing and indexing etc. FiXme is extensible, giving you the possibility to create new layouts or even complete “themes“, and also comes with support for AUCTeX.

name: FiXme

topics.details: general notes (not including endnotes or footnotes)

caption: Add support for dvips+ps2pdf, XeLaTeX, dvipdfmx to the ocgx package

descriptions.text:
This package extends the usability of the ocgx package by Paul Gaborit for creating PDF Layers to all known engines including:

  • LaTeX -> dvips -> ps2pdf/Distiller
  • (Xe)LaTeX(x) -> dvipdfmx

(pdfLaTeX and LuaLaTeX are already supported by ocgx.)

It also ensures compatibility with the media9 and animate packages.

Note that the author now considers the package obsolete; users of the package are advised to switch to using ocgx2.

name: fixocgx

topics.details: convert PostScript to PDF using Adobe Distiller

caption: Fix magnification in pdfTeX

descriptions.text: A recent change to pdfTeX has caused magnification to apply to page dimensions. This small package changes the values set in the page dimension variables from pt to truept, thus evading the effects of \mag.

name: fixpdfmag

caption: Add notes on document development

descriptions.text:
The package provides tools to highlight FIXME and TODO annotations.

The command \listofnotes prints a list of outstanding notes, with links to the pages on which they appear.

name: fixmetodonotes

topics.details: general notes (not including endnotes or footnotes)

caption: A MetaPost library for physics textbook illustrations

descriptions.text: This MetaPost library was initially written to automate some elements of black and white illustrations for a physics textbook. It provides functions to draw things like lines of variable width, shaded spheres, and tubes of different kinds, which can be used to produce images of a variety of objects. The library also contains functions to draw some objects constructed from these primitives.

license.name: GNU General Public License, version 3 or newer

name: fiziko

caption: A selection of layout styles

descriptions.text: The package provides several page layouts, selectable by package options.

name: fjodor

caption: Labels for files and folders

descriptions.text: Macros for typesetting pretty labels (optionally colored) for the back of files or binders (currently only the special A4 “Leitz-Ordner” ring binder is supported).

name: flabels

topics.details: typeset sets of labels (for cutting out, etc.)

caption: Flag style derivation package

descriptions.text: The flagderiv package is used to create mathematical derivations using the flag/flagpole notation. The package features an intuitive command syntax, opening and closing multiple flagpoles, different comment styles, customizable symbols and label namespaces.

name: flagderiv

caption: Typeset flash cards

descriptions.text: Flash cards are often used for revision; they are cards with a question on one side and the answer on the other (though the mechansim could be adapted for other purposes).

name: flashcard

topics.details: typesetting ‘flash’ cards for teaching and learning

caption: Generate flashcards for printing

descriptions.text: The flacards class provides an easy interface to produce flashcards. It will print several cards per page, on both sides of the paper.

name: flacards

topics.details: typesetting ‘flash’ cards for teaching and learning

caption: Setting and clearing of flags in bit fields

descriptions.text:
This package allows the setting and clearing of flags in bit fields and converts the bit field into a decimal number. Currently the bit field is limited to 31 bits.

It is now deprecated because of new more powerful package bitset.

The package is part of the oberdiek bundle.

name: flags

caption: A class for typesetting flashcards

descriptions.text: The FlashCards class provides for the typesetting of flash cards. By flash card, we mean a two sided card which has a prompt or a question on one side and the response or the answer on the flip (back) side. Flash cards come in many sizes depending on the nature of the information they contain.

license.name: GNU General Public License, version 2 or newer

name: flashcards

topics.details: typesetting ‘flash’ cards for teaching and learning

caption: Directly embed flash movies into PDF files

descriptions.text:
The package allows direct embedding of flash movies into PDF files. It is designed for use with pdfLaTeX.

The package takes advantage of the embedded Adobe Flash player in Adobe Reader 9; the reader is invoked with the ‘rich media annotation’ feature, described in “Adobe Supplement to the ISO 32000 BaseVersion: 1.7 ExtensionLevel: 3”.

This method of embedding movies is attractive since it removes all platform dependencies; however, the user is required to use Acrobat 9.

name: flashmovie

caption: Flatten \input, etc., in a LaTeX file

descriptions.text: A C program to flatten a LaTeX file into a single file, by explicitly including the files inclued by \include and \input commands. Also, if BibTeX is being used, then includes the bbl file into the resulting file. The result is therefore a stand-alone LaTeX file that can be emailed to a collaborator.

name: flatex

caption: Flatten \input, etc., in a LaTeX file

descriptions.text: A program to flatten a LaTeX root file by copying \input and \includeed files into the root file.

name: flatten

caption: Flexible page geometry with marginalia

descriptions.text: This package allows easy page layout if marginalia is required. Mid document changes are possible such as: new marginal width, full width text, and landscape text without marginal. Partners well with the package sidenotesplus. The package also aids the layout for book printing, allowing for binding corrections and adding page bleed, if required.

name: flexipage

caption: Create a Flash slide show of digital photos

descriptions.text:
The package uses the rmannot package (thus requiring an Adobe Distiller workflow) to create what the author calls “an AcroTeX Flash Digital Gallery”; that is, a Flash slide show that displays a series of digital images (PNG, JPG or GIF formats). The document author describes the digital images (path and caption) from the LaTeX source; on compilation, fldigigal writes an XML file, which Distiller embeds in the PDF. The digital images may be embedded in the PDF, or be accessed remotely (reducing filesize). Three layouts are offered: vertical thumbnails, horizontal thumbnails, or no thumbnails.

This package has become obsolete after December 2020. Since December 2020, Adobe no longer supports Flash player (SWF, FLV). This package uses a custom SWF file (fdg_ht1.swf, eg); as a result this package will no longer function in Adobe Acrobat Reader DC. The package will continue to produce PDFs as designed, but only if built using Acrobat XI (or a version Acrobat prior to 2021) and viewed in Adobe Acrobat Reader XI (or a version of Reader prior 2021).

name: fldigigal

topics.details: create pdf form fields, use form fields as an integral part of the package
convert PostScript to PDF using Adobe Distiller

caption: Symbol manipulation for breqn

descriptions.text:
Flexisym converts mathematical symbol definitions to the form they need for breqn to work.

The package offers support for breqn and is part of the bundle of the same name.

name: flexisym

topics.details: construction or application of mathematical symbols

caption: Typeset flipbook animations, in the corners of documents

descriptions.text:
The package provides techniques for adding flip book animations in the corner of your LaTeX documents (using images or ASCII art).

Animations are defined as a set of numbered files (e.g., "im1.pdf", "im2.pdf", "im3.pdf", …). The package relies on fancyhdr to control the corners.

name: flipbook

caption: Horizontal flipping of pages with pdfLaTeX

descriptions.text:
The package allows the production of a document with pages “mirrored”. This is sometimes required by publishers who want camera-ready documents to be printed on transparent film (to be viewed from the “wrong” side).

The package only works with pdfLaTeX or LuaLaTeX in PDF output mode. Package everypage is required on LaTeX releases before Fall 2020.

name: flippdf

caption: An enhancement to package float using package tocbasic

descriptions.text: This package adds usage of package tocbasic to package float. This not only improves compatibility with KOMA-Script but also adds several new features to float like optional automatic entries to the table of contents for the lists of new floats, optional numbering of the lists of new floats etc.

name: floatbytocbasic

caption: Improved interface for floating objects

descriptions.text:
Improves the interface for defining floating objects such as figures and tables. Introduces the boxed float, the ruled float and the plaintop float. You can define your own floats and improve the behaviour of the old ones.

The package also provides the H float modifier option of the obsolete here package. You can select this as automatic default with \floatplacement{figure}{H}.

name: float

caption: Deprecated: Allows text to be wrapped around figures

descriptions.text:
The package floatfig was a style option for LaTeX 2.09. It has been extended somewhat for LaTeX2e and renamed floatflt. Floatfig does not itself work under current LaTeX.

The package is retained only as a ZIP archive.

license.name: Do Not Sell Except by Arrangement

name: floatfig

topics.details: package only known to work with LaTeX 2.09
flow text round an insertion in the paragraph

caption: Wrap text around floats

descriptions.text: The package can float text around figures and tables which do not span the full width of a page; it improves upon floatfig, and allows tables/figures to be set left/right or alternating on even/odd pages.

name: floatflt

topics.details: flow text round an insertion in the paragraph

caption: Suppress page headings on float-only pages

descriptions.text: The package suppresses page headers on float-only pages. Although the package was written for LaTeX 2.09, the technique will work with LaTeX 2e, though the effect is better achieved using \iffloatpage command in the fancyhdr package.

name: floatnohead

caption: Different pagestyles on float pages

descriptions.text:
The package provides commands to specify the pagestyle to be used on ‘ordinary’ float pages and rotated float pages (from the rotating package), as well as a command \thisfloatpagestyle to apply just to the float in which it was issued.

The package is part of the sttools bundle.

name: floatpag

caption: An enhancement to package floatrow using package tocbasic

descriptions.text: This package adds usage of package tocbasic to package floatrow. This not only improves compatibility with KOMA-Script but also adds several new features to floatrow like optional automatic entries to the table of contents for the lists of new floats, optional numbering of the lists of new floats etc.

name: floatrowbytocbasic

caption: Draw flow diagrams in picture mode

descriptions.text: Flow is a small program that parses a flowchart description and produces LaTeX picture environment code.

name: flow

caption: Modifying the layout of floats

descriptions.text: The floatrow package provides many ways to customize layouts of floating environments and has code to cooperate with the caption 3.x package. The package offers mechanisms to put floats side by side, and to put the caption beside its float. The floatrow settings could be expanded to the floats created by packages rotating, wrapfig, subfig (in the case of rows of subfloats), and longtable.

name: floatrow

caption: Shapes for drawing flowcharts, using TikZ

descriptions.text:
The package provides a set of ‘traditional’ flowchart element shapes; the documentation shows how to build a flowchart from these elements, using pgf/TikZ.

The package also requires the makeshape package.

name: flowchart

caption: Create text frames for posters, brochures or magazines

descriptions.text: The flowfram package enables you to create frames in a document such that the contents of the document environment flow from one frame to the next in the order in which they were defined. This is useful for creating posters or magazines, indeed any form of document that does not conform to the standard one or two column layout.

name: flowfram

topics.details: layout of objects on the page
magazines, newspapers and other ephemeral pubications

caption: Vector graphics application with support for flowfram.sty

descriptions.text:
FlowframTk is a graphics application written in Java designed for use with flowfram and pgf, but can also be used to create standalone image files.

You can use FlowframTk to:

  • Construct frames for use with the flowfram package.
  • Construct shapes using lines, moves and cubic Bezier segments.
  • Edit shapes by changing the defining control points.
  • Add symmetry to shapes.
  • Convert shapes into patterns (rotational, scaled, spiral).
  • Incorporate text and bitmap images (for annotation and background effects).
  • Display text along a shape.
  • Extract the parameters for TeX’s \parshape command and for \shapepar (defined in the shapepar package).

Pictures can be saved in FlowframTk’s native binary format (JDR) or native ascii format (AJR) or can be exported as:

  • a pgfpicture environment for use in LaTeX documents with the pgf package;
  • a LaTeX class or package that loads the flowfram package;
  • a PostScript file;
  • a PDF file;
  • a PNG image file; or
  • an SVG image file.

Alternative text can be specified to use when exporting to a LaTeX file (e.g. if the text contains symbols or if it should be set in maths mode).

Mappings can be used to specify what LaTeX font declarations should be used when exporting to a LaTeX file.

To install, download and run the installer application flowframtk- version -installer.jar (where version is the version number).

This application replaces the now obsolete JpgfDraw.

name: FlowframTk

caption: Place caption on an adjacent page

descriptions.text: Defines environments FPfigure and FPtable, analogous to figure and table. In twoside mode, the caption for one of the ‘new’ environments, will be set on the opposite page of a figure/table which needs a whole page. In oneside mode the caption will be set on the preceding or following page.

name: fltpage

caption: Simple floating point arithmetic

descriptions.text: The package provides simple floating point operations (addition, subtraction, multiplication, division and rounding). Used, for example, by rccol.

name: fltpoint

topics.details: macros that are independent of the (TeX) format in use

caption: Balancing columns at last page

descriptions.text:
LaTeX’s built-in two-column code finishes off a document exactly where the text stops; this will typically leave an isolated left-hand column, or a right-hand column shorter than the left-hand one. This package modifies the LaTeX output routine to make the two columns as nearly of the same length as possible.

The package is part of the sttools bundle.

name: flushend

topics.details: more than one column on the page

caption: Include Functional MetaPost in LaTeX
name: fmp

caption: Display the value of a LaTeX counter in a variety of formats

descriptions.text:
The package provides commands that display the value of a LaTeX counter in a variety of formats (ordinal, text, hexadecimal, decimal, octal, binary etc). The package offers some multilingual support; configurations for use in English (both British and American usage), French (including Belgian and Swiss variants), German, Italian, Portuguese and Spanish documents are provided.

This package was originally provided as part of the author’s datetime package, but is now distributed separately.

name: fmtcount

caption: Warn for split footnotes

descriptions.text: This package detects footnotes that are split over several pages, and writes a warning to the log file.

name: fnbreak

caption: Convert footnotes to endnotes

descriptions.text: Defines macros \makeendnotes, which converts \footnote to produce endnotes; and \theendnotes which prints them out.

name: fn2end

caption: Seven predefined chapter heading styles

descriptions.text: Each style can be modified using a set of simple commands. Optionally one can modify the formatting routines in order to create additional chapter headings. This package was previously known as FancyChapter.

name: fncychap

caption: Alter the format of \label references

descriptions.text:
LaTeX provides a mechanism for altering the appearance of references to labels, but it’s somewhat flawed, and requires that the user manipulate internal commands. The package solves the problem, by providing a \labelformat command for changing the format of references to labels.

The package also provides a \Ref command to make reference to such redefined labels at the start of a sentence.

name: fncylab

caption: Number the lines of footnotes

descriptions.text:
The package extends the lineno package so that even lines within a \footnote are numbered and may be referred to using \linelabel, \ref, etc.

The package is delivered as part of the ‘lineno bundle’

name: fnlineno

caption: Auto-numbered footnotes in Plain TeX
name: fnote

caption: Footnotes in paragraphs

copyright.owner: Chris Rowley, Dominik Wujastyk and Bradley A. Smith

descriptions.text: Typeset footnotes in run-on paragraphs, instead of one above another; this is a re-seating, for the LaTeX environment, of an example in the TeXbook. The same basic code, improved for use in e-TeX-based LaTeX, appears in the comprehensive footnote package footmisc, and superior versions are also available in the manyfoot and bigfoot packages.

name: fnpara

caption: Footnotes in paragraphs

descriptions.text: Typeset footnotes in run-on paragraphs, instead of one above another, as in the ‘Dirty Tricks’ on pp 398–400 of the TeXbook. This code formed the basis of a LaTeX fnpara package, and has been further adapted and made more robust for use in e-TeX, appears in the comprehensive footnote package footmisc.

name: fnpara-pln

caption: Manage footnote marks’ interaction with punctuation

descriptions.text:
The package moves footnote marks after following punctuation (comma or full stop), and adjusts kerning as appropriate.

As a side effect, a change to the handling of multiple footnotes is provided.

name: fnpct

caption: Control the position of footnotes on the page

descriptions.text:
The fnpos package controls the positions of footnotes, in circumstances where the footnote would ordinarily attach itself to the bottom of the text (rather than the bottom of the page) as in the “bottom” option of the footmisc package.

The package has a clear advantage over footmisc in its commands to control the position of footnotes relative to floats on the page.

The package is part of the yafoot bundle of footnote facilities.

name: fnpos

caption: Macros for supporting mainly students of FNSPE CTU in Prague

descriptions.text:
This package is primary intended for students of FNSPE CTU in Prague but many other students or scientists can found this package as useful.

This package implements different standards of tensor notation, interval notation and complex notation. Further many macros and shortcuts are added, e.q. for spaces, operators, physics unit, etc.

name: fnspe

caption: Docmentation of LaTeX font commands

descriptions.text:
Documentation of commands for selecting fonts, as well as those for defining the data-structures used by the selection commands.

For further guidance, two papers may be helpful — “Essential NFSS” by Sebastian Rahtz, written shortly after the appearance of LaTeX2e, and “Font selection in LaTeX” by Walter Schmidt.

Fntguide is part of a set of documentation that also covers new LaTeX 2e commands, class and package writing, typesetting Cyrillic, LaTeX font encodings, configuration options and modification of latex.

name: fntguide

caption: A programmable font test pattern generator

descriptions.text: The package implements all the font testing commands of Knuth’s testfont.tex, but arranges that information necessary for each command is supplied as arguments to that command, rather than prompted for. This makes it possible to type all the tests in one command line, and easy to input the package in a file and to use the commands there. A few additional commands supporting this last purpose are also made available.

name: fntproof

topics.details: support for font development, testing and characterisation

caption: Print a number in ‘appropriate’ format

descriptions.text:
The package defines two macros which decide to typeset a number either as an Arabic number or as a word (or words) for the number. If the number is between zero and twelve (including zero and twelve) then words will be used; if the number is outside that range, it will be typeset using the package numprint

Words for English representation of numbers are generated within the package, while those for German are generated using the package zahl2string.

name: fnumprint

caption: The title font of the Mads Føk magazine

descriptions.text:
The bundle provides an Adobe Type 1 font, and LaTeX support for its use.

The magazine web site shows the font in use in a few places.

name: foekfont

topics.details: font available in Adobe Type 1 format
fonts designed more for fun than for actual use

caption: Interface between foiltex and LaTeX2HTML

descriptions.text: Provides integration between FoilTeX and LaTeX2HTML, adding sectioning commands and elements of logical formatting to FoilTeX and providing support for FoilTeX commands in LaTeX2HTML.

name: foilhtml

caption: A LaTeX2e class for overhead transparencies

descriptions.text:
This is a venerable package, which used to have many admirers. It has not, however, been adopted by any of those developing screen-projector packages (as for example seminar was adopted by the developers of prosper).

The class may be used with fancybox to place a variety of borders around the slides.

license.name: Do Not Sell Except by Arrangement

name: foiltex

caption: Use folio numbers to replace page numbers

descriptions.text:
This package adds functionality to create several styles of folio numbers. Folio numbering preceded the modern page numbering convention and was in common use until the 18th century. In folio numbering the numbers are placed only on odd (right-side) pages and the numbers typically comprise of two parts: quire and folio numbers.

The intended use for this package is to help creating old-style books.

name: foliono

topics.details: control sequence and typesettting of page numbers

caption: Support for the Danish "Dania" phonetic system

descriptions.text:
Fonetika Dania is a font bundle with a serif font and a sans serif font for the danish phonetic system Dania. Both fonts exist in regular and bold weights. LaTeX support is provided.

The fonts are based on URW Palladio and Iwona Condensed, and were created using FontForge.

name: fonetika

topics.details: fonts with specific small application areas

caption: Macros to change text and mathematics fonts in plain TeX

descriptions.text:
Macros to Change Text and Mathematics fonts in TeX: 45 Beautiful Variants

The macros are written for plain TeX and may be used with other packages like AmSTeX, eplain, etc. They also work with XeTeX.

The macros allow users to change the fonts (for both text and mathematics) in their TeX document with only one statement. The fonts may be used readily at various predefined sizes.

All the fonts called by these macro files are free and are included in current MiKTeX and TeX Live distributions.

name: font-change

topics.details: extensions to Plain TeX for higher-level constructs
metrics, macro incantations and other font support

caption: Macros to change text and mathematics fonts in plain XeTeX

descriptions.text:
This package consists of macros that can be used to typeset “plain” XeTeX documents using any OpenType or TrueType font installed on the computer system.

The macros allow the user to change the text mode fonts and some math mode fonts. For any declared font family, various font style, weight, and size variants like bold, italics, small caps, etc., are available through standard and custom TeX control statements. Using the optional argument of the macros, the available XeTeX font features and OpenType tags can be accessed.

Other features of the package include activating and deactivating hanging punctuation, and support for special Unicode characters.

name: font-change-xetex

topics.details: XeTeX, material supporting it, and packages requiring it
metrics, macro incantations and other font support
extensions to Plain TeX for higher-level constructs

caption: Font containing web-related icons

descriptions.text:
The package offers access to the large number of web-related icons provided by the included font.

The package requires the package, fontspec, if run with XeTeX or LuaTeX.

name: fontawesome

topics.details: font available in Adobe Type 1 format
metrics, macro incantations and other support for symbol fonts
fonts that provide collections of symbols

caption: Font selection for plain TeX

descriptions.text: Font selection for plain TeX, featuring: 21 sizes in the range 7 to 154 points; 16 typefaces, including Italic Bold, Calligraphic Bold, Sans Serif, Sans Serif Italic, and Sans Serif Bold; Boldmath, inclusive of subscripts, superscripts, and symbols; and a few other useful macros.

name: font_selection

topics.details: extensions to Plain TeX for higher-level constructs

caption: Font Awesome 5 with LaTeX support

descriptions.text: This package provides LaTeX support for the included “Font Awesome 5 Free” icon set. These icons were designed by Fort Awesome and released under the SIL OFL 1.1 license. The commercial “Pro” version is also supported, if it is installed and XeLaTeX or LuaLaTeX is used.

name: fontawesome5

topics.details: fonts that provide collections of symbols
font available in Adobe Type 1 format
metrics, macro incantations and other support for symbol fonts

caption: Additional font axes for LaTeX

descriptions.text: The package adds several new font axes on top of LaTeX’s New Font Selection Scheme. In particular, it splits the shape axis into a primary and a secondary shape axis, and it adds three new axes to deal with the different figure versions offered by many professional fonts.

name: fontaxes

caption: A font sampler

descriptions.text: An interactive program, that asks for font name and magnification, and then sets a table, a lower- and an upper-case alphabet listing, and a short text sample. This sample reflects a combination of the options available in testfont (in the Plain TeX distribution).

name: fontbl

topics.details: support for font development, testing and characterisation

caption: Generate a font book

descriptions.text: The package provides a means of producing a ‘book’ of font samples (for evaluation, etc.).

name: fontbook

topics.details: support for font development, testing and characterisation

caption: A font sampler

descriptions.text: Produces a font sample that is in some ways simpler than that produced by testfont (in the Plain TeX distribution), but which shows strikingly large glyph images, and avoids some difficulties with boundary characters, such as are often used in Greek fonts (and fonts for similar writing systems).

name: fontchart

topics.details: support for font development, testing and characterisation

caption: Changing fonts, sizes and encodings in Plain TeX

descriptions.text:
The fontch macros allow the user to change font size and family anywhere in a plain TeX document. Sizes of 8, 10, 12, 14, 20 and 24 points are available. A sans serif family (\sf) is defined in addition to the families already defined in plain TeX. Optional support for Latin Modern T1 and TS1 fonts is given. There are macros for non-latin1 letters and for most TS1 symbols. Math mode always uses CM fonts.

A command for producing doubled-spaced documents is also provided.

The present version of the package is designed to deal with the latest release of the Latin Modern fonts version 1.106. Unfortunately, it can no longer support earlier versions of the fonts, so an obsolete version of the package is retained for users who don't yet have access to the latest version of the fonts.

name: fontch

topics.details: extensions to Plain TeX for higher-level constructs

caption: An introduction to font usage in LaTeX (German)

descriptions.text: A German translation of a guide by Javier Bezos on how to use fonts in LaTeX.

name: fonteinf

caption: Standard package for selecting font encodings

descriptions.text:
The package allows the user to select font encodings, and for each encoding provides an interface to ‘font-encoding-specific’ commands for each font. Its most powerful effect is to enable hyphenation to operate on texts containing any character in the font.

The package supersedes t1enc; it is distributed as part of the latex distribution.

name: fontenc

caption: Help with installing fonts for TeX and LaTeX

descriptions.text:
TeX macros for converting Adobe Font Metric files to TeX metric and virtual font format. Fontinst helps mainly with the number crunching and shovelling parts of font installation. This means in practice that it creates a number of files which give the TeX metrics (and related information) for a font family that (La)TeX needs to do any typesetting in these fonts. Fontinst furthermore makes it easy to create fonts containing glyphs from more than one base font, taking advantage of (e.g.) “expert” font sets.

Fontinst cannot examine files to see if they contain any useful information, nor automatically search for files or work with binary file formats; those tasks must normally be done manually or with the help of some other tool, such as the pltotf and vptovf programs.

name: fontinst

topics.details: convert a font to a form usable with TeX

caption: Font installation guide

descriptions.text: This guide discusses the most common scenarios you are likely to encounter when installing Type 1 PostScript fonts. While the individual tools employed in the installation process are documented well, the actual difficulty most users are facing when trying to install new fonts is understanding how to put all the pieces together. This is what this guide is about.

name: fontinstallationguide

topics.details: documentation about choosing installing and using fonts

caption: A partial font downloading utility

descriptions.text:
The tool scans a PostScript file, and replaces the embedded Adobe Type 1 fonts with appropriately subsetted versions. The process of scanning the file is done using a PostScript program executing in ghostscript.

The need for the tool has largely disappeared, for (La)TeX users, following the introduction of the partial-downloading capabilities of current versions of dvips.

descriptions.text:
This package provides tools to simplify using OpenType fonts with LaTeX.

By far the most important program in this bundle is autoinst:

  • autoinst – a wrapper script around Eddie Kohler’s LCDF TypeTools. Autoinst aims to automate the installation of OpenType fonts in LaTeX by calling the LCDF TypeTools (with the correct options) for all fonts you wish to install, and generating the necessary .fd and .sty files.

In addition, this bundle contains a few other, less important utilities:

  • afm2afm – re-encode .afm files,

  • splitttc – split an OpenType Collection file (ttc or otc) into individual fonts.

Fontspec is a package for XeLaTeX and LuaLaTeX. It provides an automatic and unified interface to feature-rich AAT and OpenType fonts through the NFSS in LaTeX running on XeTeX or LuaTeX engines.

The package requires the l3kernel and xparse bundles from the LaTeX3 development team.

caption: Print a sample of a font

descriptions.text:
Provides a package which defines a command \fontsample (which will print a sample of the current font), and a document which prompts for a font family name (such as “cmr”) and prints a sampler of the whole family.

This package is part of the latex-tools bundle in the LaTeX required distribution.

name: fontsmpl

caption: Print font tables from a LaTeX document

descriptions.text:
This is a package version of nfssfont.tex (part of the LaTeX distribution); it enables you to print a table of the characters of a font and/or some text (for demonstration or testing purposes), from within a document. (Packages such as testfont and nfssfont.tex provide these facilities, but they run as interactive programs: the user is expected to type details of what is needed.)

Note that the package mftinc also has a \fonttable function; the documentation explains how avoid a clash with that package.

name: fonttable

caption: Bind fonts to specific unicode blocks

descriptions.text:
The package (which runs under XeLaTeX) lets you bind fonts to specific unicode blocks, for automatic font tagging of multilingual text.

The package uses Perl (via perltex) to construct its tables.
