descriptions.text: A script that enables Vim (a popular text editor) to convert a bibliographic database from ISI (Institute of Scientific Information, Web of Science) export format to BibTeX format.

name: isi2bib-vim

topics.details: derive BibTeX data from resources other than BibTeX libraries

caption: Hyphenation patterns for Icelandic

descriptions.text: These patterns are supposedly based on the encoding of the ‘Icelandic Roman’ fonts, so are probably of little use nowadays without some translation process; the icehyph is probably a better bet, nowadays.

name: ishyph

topics.details: support for typesetting the Icelandic language

caption: Display (La)TeX accented letters in GNU Emacs

descriptions.text:
GNU Emacs modes to display letters with standard TeX accents as the character they are supposed to represent (for example "\'e" would display as "é". This provides an alternative approach to that provided by inputenc, in which the user types the desired character and (La)TeX transparently executes the commands needed to produce the character in the typeset output.

The package is said to be capable of working with GNU Emacs version 19 or later.

name: ISO-TeX

topics.details: plug-ins for editors, for better (La)TeX and Meta* support

caption: Generic ISO standards typesetting macros

descriptions.text:
Generic class and package files for typesetting ISO International Standard documents. Several standard documents have been printed by ISO from camera-ready copy prepared using LaTeX and these files.

The class makes use of the isorot package, rather than use other mechanisms directly.

name: iso

topics.details: typeset documents about standards, or the standards themselves

caption: Converter for ISI to  BibTeX
name: isi2bibtex

topics.details: derive BibTeX data from resources other than BibTeX libraries

caption: Typesetting the STEP standards

descriptions.text: Class and package files building on iso for typesetting the ISO 10303 (STEP) standards. Standard documents prepared using these packages have been published by ISO.

name: iso10303

topics.details: typeset documents about standards, or the standards themselves

caption: A document style for ISO standards

descriptions.text: An early predecessor of Wilson’s iso.

name: iso209

topics.details: typeset documents about standards, or the standards themselves
package only known to work with LaTeX 2.09

caption: Tune the output format of dates according to language

descriptions.text:
This package provides ten output formats of the commands \today, \printdate, \printdateTeX, and \daterange (partly language dependent).

Formats available are: ISO (yyyy-mm-dd), numeric (e.g. dd.\,mm.~yyyy), short (e.g. dd.\,mm.\,yy), TeX (yyyy/mm/dd), original (e.g. dd. mmm yyyy), short original (e.g. dd. mmm yy), as well as numerical formats with Roman numerals for the month.

The commands \printdate and \printdateTeX print any date. The command \daterange prints a date range and leaves out unnecessary year or month entries.

This package supports German (old and new rules), Austrian, US English, British English, French, Danish, Swedish, and Norwegian.

name: isodate

caption: Mathematics style for science and technology

descriptions.text: The package provides tools for a mathematical style that conforms to the International Standard ISO 80000-2 and is common in science and technology. It changes the default shape of capital Greek letters to italic, sets up bold italic and sans-serif bold italic math alphabets with Latin and Greek characters, and defines macros for markup of vector, matrix and tensor symbols.

name: isomath

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other support for maths fonts

caption: A LaTeX class for typesetting letters and invoices

descriptions.text:
The isodoc class can be used for the preparation of letters and invoices (and, in the future, similar documents). Documents are set up with options, thus making the class easily adaptable to user’s wishes and extensible for other document types.

The class is based on the NTG brief class by Victor Eijkhout, which implements the NEN1026 standard.

name: isodoc

caption: An obsolete means to use ISO 8859-1 with TeX

descriptions.text:
The package represents an outdated mechanism for reading ISO Latin-1 (ISO/IEC 8859-1) by means of setting the printing glyphs in the upper half of the character set to category code “active”, and defining them all.

While this mechanism is broadly that employed by the standard LaTeX inputenc package, the standard package has several advantages, including a more satisfactory approach to undefined character codes, better integration with other input encodings and generally improved robustness.

name: isolatin1

topics.details: package only known to work with LaTeX 2.09
input encoding support for TeX engines

caption: Display numbers in maths mode according to ISO 31-0

descriptions.text: The package makes a quick hack to ziffer to display numbers in maths mode according to ISO 31-0, regardless of input format (European $1.235,7$ or Anglo-American $1,235.7$). The options [euro, anglo] control the global input format. Default input format is anglo. Documentation is included as comments to the text source.

name: isonums

caption: Writing a TeX length with a space between number and unit

descriptions.text: Writing a TeX length with \the writes the value and the unit without a space. Package isopt provides a macro \ISO which inserts a user defined space between number and unit.

name: isopt

caption: Rotation of document elements

descriptions.text: The package is for rotation of document elements. It is a combination of the lscape package and an extension of the rotating package. The package is designed for use with the iso class but may be used with any normal class.

name: isorot

topics.details: rotate typeset objects on their page

caption: Provides ISO signs and colors according to the standards 7010 and 3864

descriptions.text: The package provides safety colors (ISO 3864) and safety signs (ISO 7010) from the ISO. It can be useful when creating instructions for chemical or physical experiments.

name: isosafety

topics.details: typeset documents about standards, or the standards themselves

caption: A package for typesetting isotopes

descriptions.text: The package provides a command \isotope for setting the atomic weight and atomic number indications of isotopes. (The naive way of doing the job with (La)TeX mathematics commands produces an unsatisfactory result.)

name: isotope

topics.details: position sub- and superscripts (left and right sides)

caption: Multi-platform spell checker

descriptions.text:
Ispell is a fast screen-oriented spelling checker that shows you your errors in the context of the original file, and suggests possible corrections when it can figure them out. Compared to UNIX spell, it is faster and much easier to use. Ispell can also handle languages other than English.

Ispell is now largely superseded by aspell, a package that seasoned ispell users will find a comfortable home.

name: ispell

caption: Simple way to write nice formulas

descriptions.text: This package provides an easy way to write mathematical and physical formulas and arguments in scientific notation in an elegant way.

name: isphysicalmath

caption: Produce external links instead of internal ones

descriptions.text:
The PDF visualizer http://issuu.com/ISSUU is a popular service which shows PDF documents “a page a time”. Due to the way it is implemented, internal links in these documents are not allowed. Instead, they must be converted to external ones in the form http://issuu.com/action/page?page=PAGENUMBER.

The package patches hyperref to produce external links in the required form instead of internal links created by \ref, \cite and other commands.

Since the package redefines the internals of hyperref, it must be loaded it AFTER hyperref.

name: issuulinks

caption: Title page for the old BSI IST/21 committee

descriptions.text: A variant of the standard LaTeX 2.09 titlepage package, designed for the working papers, etc., of the committee. (The committee covered, at various times, standardisation of OSI architecture, OSI upper layers, distributed processing, databases and graphics.)

name: ist21

topics.details: typeset badges, covers or labels for things (or people)

caption: Draw Game Trees with TikZ

descriptions.text:
This LaTeX package provides macros based on TikZ to draw a game tree. The main idea underlying its core macros is the completion of a whole tree by using a sequence of simple ‘parent-child’ tree structures, with no longer nested relations involved (like the use of ‘grandchildren’ or ‘great-grandchildren’).

Using this package you can draw a game tree as easily as drawing a game tree with pen and paper.

This package depends on expl3, TikZ, and xparse.

The ‘ist’ prefix stands for “it’s a simple tree” or “In-Sung’s simple tree.”

name: istgame

topics.details: process game diagrams, gamebooks, and other amusements

caption: Automatic italic correction for italic and slanted text

descriptions.text: The package defines commands \ital and \slant, somewhat simpler than those in ital, which package has wider coverage.

name: italic

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other font support

caption: Automatic italic correction

descriptions.text:
The package defines commands \ital and \slant that provide the requisite italic correction at the end of their argument, and the command \upright that provides italic correction in front of its argument as necessary. A command \emph is also provided, choosing between \ital and \upright according to the state of the surrounding text.

These facilities are (of course) provided in LaTeX 2e, with different names as part of the distribution.

name: ital

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other font support

caption: Interactive TeX editor

descriptions.text: iTe is an easy to use, interactive authoring tool for LaTeX and TeX documents. With iTe running inside emacs, it is possible to select arbitrary display fragments such as figures, equations, labels, captions, etc. These fragments can then be freely moved, rotated and scaled.

name: iTe

topics.details: plug-ins for editors, for better (La)TeX and Meta* support

caption: Hyphenation patterns for the Italian language

descriptions.text: These hyphenation patterns for the Italian language are supposed to comply with the Recommendation UNI 6461 on hyphenation issued by the Italian Standards Institution (Ente Nazionale di Unificazione UNI).

name: ithyph

caption: Spell numbers in words (Italian)

descriptions.text:
Sometimes we need to say “Capitolo primo” or “Capitolo uno” instead of “Capitolo 1”, that is, spelling the number in words instead of the usual digit form.

This package provides support for spelling out numbers in Italian words, both in cardinal and in ordinal form.

name: itnumpar

caption: Transliteration of Indian Languages

descriptions.text:
Itrans is a pre-processor: it converts English-encoded text into various Indian Language scripts for printing or for display.

The input text to itrans is in a transliterated form: each letter in an Indian Script is assigned an English equivalent, and the English letters are used to represent what will eventually print out in the Indian Language Script.

name: itrans-processor

topics.details: support for languages of the Indian subcontinent

caption: Convert IVD-DVI files to DVI

descriptions.text: The TeX extension TeX-XeT (single hyphen: not to be confused with TeX--XeT) produces ‘IVD-DVI’ files which extend DVI files with ‘reflection’ commands for horizontal reversal of text. In general, IVD-DVI files cannot be processed by an ordinary DVI processor; ivd2dvi will convert such a file to DVI so that it can be processed by a normal DVI driver.

name: ivd2dvi

caption: Halle Institute for Economic Research (IWH) Discussion Papers

descriptions.text:
The document class is for creating Discussion Papers of the Halle Institute for Economic Research (IWH) in Halle, Germany.

The class offers options for both English and German texts.

name: iwhdp

caption: A two-element sans-serif font

descriptions.text:
Iwona is a two-element sans-serif typeface. It was created as an alternative version of the Kurier typeface, which was designed in 1975 for a diploma in typeface design at the Warsaw Academy of Fine Arts under the supervision of Roman Tomaszewski.

This distribution contains a significantly extended set of characters covering the following modern alphabets: latin (including Vietnamese), Cyrillic and Greek as well as a number of additional symbols (including mathematical symbols). The fonts are prepared in Type 1 and OpenType formats. For use with TeX the following encoding files have been prepared: T1 (ec), T2 (abc), and OT2—Cyrillic, T5 (Vietnamese), OT4, QX, texansi and nonstandard (IL2 for the Czech fonts), as well as supporting macros and files defining fonts for LaTeX.

name: iwona

topics.details: font available in Adobe Type 1 format

caption: LaTeX support for scaled Iwona math fonts

descriptions.text:
This package provides an interface to the Iwona math fonts by Janusz Marian Nowacki. It allows to use Iwona as math complement for sans serif fonts without native math.

The package allows font scaling, the choice of light and condensed versions, and the creation of multiple math versions.

name: iwonamath

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other support for maths fonts

caption: Support for the old Russian font "Izhitsa"

descriptions.text: Includes Metafont code and LaTeX style file.

name: izhitsa

topics.details: fonts for a script or language now obsolete
fonts for Cyrillic and related scripts

caption: Metafont version of tiles in the style of Slavik Jablan

descriptions.text: This is a small Metafont font to implement the modular tiles described by Slavik Jablan. For an outline of the theoretical structure of the tiles, see (for example) Jablan’s JMM 2006 Exhibit.

name: jablantile

topics.details: fonts designed more for fun than for actual use

caption: Graphical frontend to manage BibTeX databases

descriptions.text:
JabRef is a graphical frontend to manage BibTeX (and BibLaTeX) databases having BibTeX as internal format. It offers quality checks for entries; fetching complete bibliographic information based on ISBN, DOI, PubMed-ID and arXiv-ID; searching across many online scientific catalogues such as CiteSeer, CrossRef, Google Scholar, IEEEXplore, INSPIRE-HEP, Medline PubMed, MathSciNet, Springer, arXiv, and zbMATH.

It allows for grouping entries (and storing the group information in the .bib file itself), advancing searching and filtering, finding duplicate entries, attaching and renaming PDFs (e.g., according to the BibTeX key), and generating BibTeX keys.

Since JabRef fully relies on BibTeX, additional information such as ranking, priority, printed-flag, and quality-assured-flag are stored in the BibTeX entry in the .bib file itself.

name: jabref

caption: A class for submissions to the proceedings of conferences on JACoW.org

descriptions.text: The jacow class is used for submissions to the proceedings of conferences on Joint Accelerator Conferences Website (JACoW), an international collaboration that publishes the proceedings of accelerator conferences held around the world.

name: jacow

caption: Macros supporting Jade DSSSL output

descriptions.text: Macro package on top of LaTeX to typeset TeX output of the Jade DSSSL implementation.

name: jadetex

topics.details: import files in a non-TeX (or different TeX) format

caption: Expanded Times Roman fonts

descriptions.text:
The package offers LaTeX support for the expanded Times Roman font, which has been used for many years in the Journal d'Analyse Mathématique.

Mathematics support is based on the Belleek fonts.

name: jamtimes

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other font support

caption: Compiling basic math formulas in Japanese using LuaLaTeX

descriptions.text:
This is a style file for compiling basic maths formulas in Japanese using LuaLaTeX.

\NewDocumentCommand allows you to specify whether the formula should be used within a sentence or on a new line.

The main packages used in japanese-mathformulas.sty are amsmath, amssymb, siunitx, ifthen, xparse, TikZ, mathtools, and graphics.

name: japanese-mathformulas

topics.details: LuaTeX and packages that require it

caption: Advanced font selection for platex and its friends

descriptions.text: The package contains pLaTeX support files and virtual fonts for supporting a wide variety of fonts in LaTeX using the pTeX engine.

name: japanese-otf

topics.details: fonts for far eastern languages (Chinese, Japanese and Korean)

caption: Support for Japanese OTF files in upLaTeX

descriptions.text: This bundle has been merged into japanese-otf.

name: japanese-otf-uptex

topics.details: fonts for far eastern languages (Chinese, Japanese and Korean)

caption: BibTeX style for American Meteorological Society (AMS)

descriptions.text:
This style is based on an earlier style jas99; the package acquired a new name since the original authors (of jac99.bst) aren't contactable.

Modifications are simply for better conformance to the AMS' requirements for journals Journal of Atmospheric Science, Journal of Applied Meteorology and Monthly Weather Review..

name: jas99_m

caption: BibTeX style for American Meteorological Society (AMS)

descriptions.text: This style is a development of newapa.bst, and is in its turn superseded by jas99_m.bst.

name: jas99

caption: A 'standard' thesis class

descriptions.text: A class that produces theses in the format required by the University of Bristol (UK). This is close to the requirements of the standard BS 4821:1990.

name: jasthesis

caption: A BibTeX file manager written in Java

descriptions.text: JavaBib reads the whole BibTeX file into memory and presents an index to the file and editing and management facilities.

name: JavaBib

caption: Documenting source code

descriptions.text:
The package processes source code in a manner based on the javadoc system for documenting Java (and other language) source; its output is LaTeX, via a ‘doclet’.

A package for processing this output is provided.

name: javadoc

caption: DVI viewer and printer coded in Java

descriptions.text: javaDVI is a DVI viewer and printer coded in Java, and running under the Java RTE 1.3 using the BaKoMa True Type fonts. The fonts are included as a .zip file, a format suitable for use with javaDVI.

name: javaDVI

topics.details: convert DVI files for (direct) printing, etc.

caption: Add buttons to a PDF to easily get and post web content

descriptions.text: This small package adds commands for LaTeX to create buttons with which to fetch content from the internet. The content can optionally be transformed with Javascript and displayed in textfields. For these interactive elements to work, a PDF using the commands provided by this package must be opened in Acrobat Pro.

name: JavascriptHTTP

topics.details: relies on availability of Adobe Acrobat, etc.

caption: Small MikTeX-editor for Win32 Intel platform

descriptions.text:
A small editor for MikTeX as an HTML application (~20kb). Works on MS-Windows with Internet Explorer 5.0 and later. You can run it as JS-TeX.hta from command line or start JS-TeX.hta filename.tex

If you have help for LaTeX in HTML you can use it by filling the HELP field in Options.

name: javascript_TeXed

topics.details: editor designed (or adapted) for use with (La)TeX

caption: A Java implementation of TeX

descriptions.text:
At root, this is a ‘small’ TeX (memmax=64K), but a larger version may be built.

The implementation was in essence an experiment, and performance proved so poor that the author considers it unusable in practice.

name: javatex

caption: BibTeX style for biology journals

descriptions.text:
The style is a development of apalike.bst in the BibTeX bundle.

The style serves two journals — if the user executes “\nocite{TitlesOn}”, the style serves for the Journal of Theoretical Biology; otherwise it serves for the Journal of Molecular Biology.

name: jbact

caption: Managing citations in BibTeX format

descriptions.text: JBibtexManager is a front-end to BibTeX database. You can add, edit, sort and search. Furthermore, you can find and delete duplicate entries. You can customize BibTeX templates, fonts, colors and more. JBibtexManager is a java GUI for managing citations in BibTeX format. The citations are presented in a spreadsheet format and allows sorting based on year, journal, and key. Furthermore, it allows searching for text in the author and title fields, and allows printing in the spreadsheet format. Requires java 1.4 and should work on all platforms.

name: JBibtexManager

caption: Build a jeopardy game in LaTeX

descriptions.text:
The jeopardy package allows to build a jeopardy game with pdfLaTeX. It is based on the jj_game class and exerquiz package, written by D. P. Story. The author of the game can use multichoice questions or fill-in questions. The answer for fill-in questions is either a mathematical formula or text string (see the documentation of exerquiz and \RespBoxMath and \RespBoxTxt commands to learn more about the capabilities). JavaScripts are written to record the score. If the score is greater than a given value, a hidden string is shown. The user should use the style with some screen presentation package, such as web.

The package is distributed with some example games, including both 1- and 2-player games.

name: jeopardy

topics.details: process game diagrams, gamebooks, and other amusements

caption: Modified LaTeX2.09 article and report styles

descriptions.text: A personal adaptation of LaTeX standard code, with adjustment of the default page size, code to allow the user to customise section headers, an early version of fancy headers, compact lists and table of contents.

name: jeep

caption: BibTeX style file for J. Comp. Chem

descriptions.text:
jcc.bst is a BibTeX style for J. Comp. Chem. originally dating from 2000.

It is now modified to make it really compliant with the journal’s present style requirements, as: author’s initials after the name, authors’ names separated by “;”, no brackets around the year…

name: jcc

caption: Macros to insert playing cards

descriptions.text: This package provides macros to insert playing cards, single, or hand, or random-hand, Poker or French Tarot or Uno, from png files.

name: JeuxCartes

topics.details: process game diagrams, gamebooks, and other amusements

caption: Convert JFlap file into a LaTeX file depicting the automaton using TikZ

descriptions.text: JFlap is an excellent piece of software for experimenting with finite state machines, Turing machines and for exploring many aspects of the theory of computation. JFLAP2TikZ is a script that converts a JFlap ‘jff’ file representing a finite automaton, push down automaton, or Turing machine to LaTeX file depicting the automaton graphically using TikZ.

name: jflap2tikz

caption: Utility to process pTeX-extended TFM and VF

descriptions.text:
This program provides functionality to process data files (JFM and VF) that form logical fonts used in (u)pTeX. The functions currently available include:

  • The mutual conversion between Japanese virtual fonts (pairs of VF and JFM) and files in the “ZVP format”, which is an original text format representing data in virtual fonts. This function can be seen as a counterpart to the vftovp/vptovf programs.
  • The mutual conversion between VF files alone and files in the “ZVP0 format”, which is a subset of the ZVP format.

name: jfmutil

topics.details: process fonts for use with TeX (includes installation)

caption: Font maps and configuration tools for Japanese fonts

descriptions.text:
The package offers font maps, and supporting material, that make various Japanese fonts available to users of (u)ptex and related programs or formats.

The package does not ship any of the fonts mentioned in the documentation, but only map files for use with dvipdfmx; the user must obtain the other fonts separately. The first exception is that ipa and ipaex the respective fonts are shipped as part of the TeX Live distribution and are available for free. The other exception is that the Yu Mincho/Gothic fonts are available to Windows and MacOSX users, as part of their operating system distribution.

This package has now been superseeded by ptex-fontmaps.

name: jfontmaps

caption: Class for JHEP

descriptions.text: A LaTeX class used to typeset manuscripts in JHEP style.

name: jhep

caption: UnofficiaL BibTeX style for citing Japanese articles in IEEE format

descriptions.text: This package provides an unofficial BibTeX style for authors trying to cite Japanese articles in the Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE) format.

name: jIEEEtran

caption: Draw jigsaw pieces with TikZ

descriptions.text: This is a small LaTeX package to draw jigsaw pieces with TikZ. It is possible to draw individual pieces and adjust their shape, create tile patterns or automatically generate complete jigsaws.

name: jigsaw

caption: A LaTeX class to construct Jeopardy-like games

descriptions.text:
The class defines a Jeopardy-like game; question answers may be multiple choice, or text or mathematics ‘fill-ins’.

The basic game can be constructed using dvipsone, dvips, pdftex or dvipdfm. The ‘pro’ option of the game works with dvipsone or dvips only, and requires Adobe Acrobat Pro 7.0 (or later), with its distiller.

The game requires the AcroTeX education bundle, and (for the pro option) AeB pro.

Also, the eforms package dated 2016-08-29 or later is required.

Samples of sources for games are provided.

name: jj-game

topics.details: process game diagrams, gamebooks, and other amusements
convert PostScript to PDF using Adobe Distiller
create pdf form fields, use form fields as an integral part of the package

caption: Macros for mathematics that make the code more readable

descriptions.text: Inspired by the physicspackage on CTAN, the package defines some simple macros for mathematical notation which make the code more readable and/or allow flexibility in typesetting material.

name: jkmath

caption: Miscellaneous packages by Joerg Knappen

descriptions.text:
Miscellaneous macros by Jörg Knappen, including:

  • represent counters in greek;
  • Maxwell's non-commutative division;
  • latin1jk, latin2jk and latin3jk, which are their inputenc definition files that allow verbatim input in the respective ISO Latin codes;
  • blackboard bold fonts in maths;
  • use of RSFS fonts in maths;
  • extra alignments for \parboxes;
  • swap Roman and Sans fonts;
  • transliterate semitic languages;
  • patches to make (La)TeX formulae embeddable in SGML;
  • use maths “minus” in text as appropriate;
  • simple Young tableaux.

name: jknappen

caption: Document class for formatting a thesis

descriptions.text: For use for dissertations in the Heinrich-Heine-Universität Düsseldorf.

name: jkthesis

caption: Make letter-sized pages of labels

descriptions.text: The package provides controls for the numbers of rows and columns.

name: jlabels

topics.details: typeset sets of labels (for cutting out, etc.)

caption: Jörg's LaTeX Mode - an advanced LaTeX mode for Jed

descriptions.text:
JLM is an advanced LaTeX mode for the Jed editor. Its aim is to help the user by taking over annoying and stupid things that need to be done, like adding \usepackage when you add a command or environment from this package, or placing dollar signs around mathematical commands and move the cursor to an appropriate point.

JLM does not think for you. If you want a tabular but insert an itemize, JLM doesn't prevent this. So, you should be familiar with LaTeX and know what environments and commands are, and where to place them in a document; JLM is there to help writing them.

name: jlm

topics.details: plug-ins for editors, for better (La)TeX and Meta* support

caption: Japanese document class based on requirements for Japanese text layout

descriptions.text:
This package provides a Japanese document class based on requirements for Japanese text layout.

The class file and the JFM (Japanese font metric) files for LuaTeX-ja / pLaTeX / upLaTeX are provided.

name: jlreq

topics.details: fonts for far eastern languages (Chinese, Japanese and Korean)

caption: Multi-weight Japanese font support for the jlreq class

descriptions.text: This package provides multi-weight Japanese font support for the jlreq class.

name: jlreq-deluxe

topics.details: fonts for far eastern languages (Chinese, Japanese and Korean)

caption: A Java interface to Ghostscript to convert PDF to PDF/X

descriptions.text: The package provides Java GUI application that uses Ghostscript to convert PDF files to PDF/X. There is a choice of CMYK or greyscale profile. This uses Ghostscript’s /prepress setting, which is analogous to Acrobat Distiller's “Prepress Optimized” setting.

name: jmakepdfx

caption: Class files for the Journal of Machine Learning Research

descriptions.text:
The jmlr bundle provides a class for authors (jmlr) and a class for production editors (jmlrbook).

The jmlrbook class can be used to combine articles written using the jmlr class into a book. The class uses the combine class and the hyperref package to produce either a colour hyperlinked book for on-line viewing or a greyscale nonhyperlinked book for printing.

Production editors can use makejmlrbookgui to help build the proceedings from the articles.

name: jmlr

caption: BibTeX style for the Journal of Theoretical Biology

descriptions.text:
This BibTeX bibliography style is for the Journal of Molecular Biology and Journal of Theoretical Biology; the accompanying LaTeX (2.09) package is a close relative of apalike.sty in the BibTeX distribution; it features author-date references.

The bibliography style has control over whether to print reference titles; if your database contains an article with the cite key "TitlesOn", and you invoke it by \nocite{TitlesOn}, titles will be printed; otherwise titles will not be printed.

name: jmb

caption: A package for compositional delimiter sizing

descriptions.text:
Correctly sizing delimiters is very difficult, particularly in well-architected documents: a correctly engineered mathematical document will include macros for all operations, and these macros necessarily will include delimiters (such as parentheses). However, the correct size for the delimiter cannot be chosen ahead of time, because it will depend on the arguments; two options are available:

  1. Provide optional arguments to each notation macro for choosing delimiter sizes. This is nearly intractable to do in practice.
  2. Ignore delimiter sizes.

With jmsdelim we offer an alternative: the correct delimiter sizes can be set at the leaf nodes of a mathematical expression, and magically bubble upward through the delimiters.

name: jmsdelim

caption: Exam class for Jinan University

descriptions.text: The package provides an exam class for Jinan University (China).

name: jnuexam

caption: BibTeX style for the Journal of Neuroscience

descriptions.text:
This is a slightly modified version of the namedplus style, which fully conforms with the Journal of Neuroscience citation style.

It should be characterised as an author-date citation style; a BibTeX style and a LaTeX package are provided.

name: jneurosci

caption: Compile differently based on the filename

descriptions.text: This package allows to compile a document differently depending on the portion of the document’s file name (internally, the \jobname) that comes after the first “-” character. This allows one to have one source file and multiple links to this source file that each compile differently.

name: jobname-suffix

caption: Join boxes vertically or horizontally

descriptions.text: This package can join boxes vertically or horizontally. When using vertical joining, all boxes to be joined will keep same width, while when using horizontal joined, all boxes to be joined keep same height.

name: joinbox

caption: Josefin fonts with LaTeX support

descriptions.text: This package provides LaTeX, pdfLaTeX, XeLaTeX and LuaLaTeX support for the Josefin Sans family of fonts, designed by Santiago Orozco of the Typemade foundry in Monterey, Mexico. Josefin Sans is available in seven weights, with corresponding italics.

name: josefin

topics.details: font providing LaTeX T1 encoding support
font available in Adobe Type 1 format
font designed for use as body font for Latin-based script documents
metrics, macro incantations and other font support

caption: Cover letter for journal submissions

descriptions.text:
Paper submissions to journals are usually accompanied by a cover letter. This package provides a LaTeX class and a template for such a cover letter with the following main features:

  • Minimalistic design.
  • Custom image.
  • Pre-defined commands for journal name, author, date, etc.
  • Many macros contained in this package speed up the process of preparing the necessary ingredients for the cover letter.
  • Macros for recommending up to three reviewers and/or editors.
  • ORCID logo and link to the submitting author’s ORCID page.
  • Controls for adding a “Conflict of interest” statement and declaration.
  • Custom greeting (e.g., “Dear Editor” for a regular submission, “Dear Editor-in-Chief” for a submission to a journal’s special issue, etc.)
  • Predefined valedictions for different types of submissions (e.g., Yours sincerely, Yours faithfully, Best regards, etc.)

name: jourcl

caption: A LaTeX template for journal rebuttal letters

descriptions.text:
This package provides an elegant LaTeX template designed for crafting professional rebuttal letters in response to editors or reviewers.

It consists of a LaTeX class and a template, fine-tuned to support your publishing journey with several pre-defined commands that drastically speed up the process of preparing letters during the revision process.

The repository hosts a template for writing responses to editors/reviewers comments for journal submissions written in LaTeX that is minimalistic in one way while pre-defined with several commands that drastically speed up the process of preparing letters during the revision process.

Main Features of this template:

  • With front page included
  • Response ticks to mark as completed
  • Custom response color
  • Minimalistic design
  • Everything is customizable
  • Predefined commands for a journal name, submission ID, author, editor, associate editor, date, etc.
  • Many macros included
  • Predefined different valedictions for different types of submissions (e.g., Yours sincerely, Yours faithfully, Best regards, etc.)
  • Custom greeting (e.g., “Dear Editor” or bDear Editor-in-Chief” for regular submission, etc.)
  • (Optional) Table of contents, jump to the reply you wish to address
  • Option to add custom Signature (i.e. an image of your hand-written signature)

name: jourrr

caption: User documentation for the AMS-TeX macro collection

descriptions.text:
This distribution makes the full text of the most recent reprint of the second edition of “The Joy of TeX” by Michael Spivak available for the first time, as a pdf file: joyt2.pdf. “Joy” is the user documentation for AMS-TeX. (Please note that AMS-TeX is no longer supported by the AMS, nor is it used by the AMS publishing program.)

joyt2.pdf — The Joy of TeX, second edition: A Gourmet guide to typesetting with the AMS-TeX macro package, by M. D. Spivak. This is the final edition, printed with corrections by the American Mathematical Society in 2004.

Any material in this guide may be reproduced or duplicated for personal or educational use.

name: joy-of-tex

caption: JPEG to PostScript converter for OS/2

descriptions.text: OS/2 port of jpeg2ps.

name: jpeg2ps-os2

descriptions.text: The BibTeX style comes with a supporting LaTeX package.

name: jphysiol

caption: A graphical editor generating LaTeX commands

descriptions.text: JPicEdt is a graphical editor, written in Java (so portable to most machines), that can read (and generates output in) LaTeX picture mode, optionally including eepic commands. JPicEdt can also generate output as PSTricks macros.

name: JPicEdt

caption: Enumerative expressions in Japanese education

descriptions.text: Mathematical equation representation in Japanese education differs somewhat from the standard LaTeX writing style. This package introduces enumerative expressions in Japanese education.

name: jpneduenumerate

caption: Mathematical equation representation in Japanese education

descriptions.text: Mathematical equation representation in Japanese education differs somewhat from the standard LaTeX writing style. This package introduces mathematical equation representation in Japanese education.

descriptions.text: This is a derivative work of Oren Patashnik's apalike BibTeX style. It is a BibTeX file for the Journal of Quality Technology that can be used with natbib. It puts semicolons between authors, quotes around titles, and 'pp.' before page numbers.

name: jqt1999

caption: Miscellaneous macros from Joachim Schrod

descriptions.text:
A bunch of packages, including:

  • idverb.tex, for ‘short verbatim’;
  • xfig.tex, for including xfig/transfig output in a TeX document; and
  • cassette.tex for setting cassette labels.

name: js-misc

caption: Classes tailored for use with Japanese

descriptions.text:
Classes jsarticle and jsbook are provided, together with packages okumacro and okuverb.

These classes are designed to work under ASCII Corporation’s Japanese TeX system ptex.

name: jsclasses

caption: Creation and management of university course material

descriptions.text:
The jslectureplanner package facilitates the generation and management of university course material. It provides an interface to set up and access centralized course data that can be reused in all course documents. Furthermore, the package is able to calculate the session dates of a whole semester and generate course programs, if the course is held weekly and the date of the first lecture is specified. Moreover, the package can be used to generate a sectioned course bibliography via BibLaTeX.

The bundle also includes a package jsmembertable.sty that helps in generating course member and presence lists.

name: jslectureplanner

topics.details: support for teachers and teaching administrators

caption: An ASCII file spelling checker

descriptions.text: A spelling checker for use under MS-DOS.

name: jspell

caption: BibTeX style for Journal of Theoretical Biology

descriptions.text: This style is a derivative of humanbio.bst, which is in turn derived from astron.bst.

name: jtb

caption: BibTeX style for Journal of Theoretical Biology

descriptions.text: Developed using makebst; apparently intended to supersede jtb.bst.

name: jtbnew

caption: Articles with teasers and continuation later on

descriptions.text:
Jumplines is a package for typesetting (newspaper) articles that show a teaser (some few lines of text/content) and are continued at a later place, with optional hyperlinking and a list of articles.

It requires lualatex for colour support in split boxes.

name: jumplines

topics.details: LuaTeX and packages that require it

caption: A TrueType font for mediaevalists

descriptions.text: Junicode is a TrueType font with many OpenType features for antiquarians (especially medievalists) based on typefaces used by the Oxford Press in the late 17th and early 18th centuries. It works well with Xe(La)TeX.

name: junicode

topics.details: fonts for a script or language now obsolete

caption: Include whole or partial Jupyter notebooks in LaTeX documents

descriptions.text:
This package provides a python3 script and a LaTeX .sty file which can be used together to include Jupyter Notebooks (all of them, or some specific cells) as part of a LaTeX document.

It will convert the Jupyter Notebook format to proper LaTeX so it gets included seamlessly, supporting text, LaTeX, images, etc.

name: jupynotex

topics.details: run an external program from within a document
import files in a non-TeX (or different TeX) format

caption: A document class for German legal texts

descriptions.text: Implements the standard layout for German term papers in law (one-and-half linespacing, 7 cm margins, etc.). Includes alphanum that permits alphanumeric section numbering (e.g., A. Introduction; III. International Law).

name: jura

topics.details: typesetting legal documents or study material

caption: Abbreviations for typesetting (German) juridical documents

descriptions.text: This package should be helpful for people working on (German) law. It helps you to handle abbreviations and creates a list of those (pre-defined) abbreviations that have actually been used in the document

name: juraabbrev

topics.details: typesetting legal documents or study material

caption: Extended BibTeX citation support for the humanities and legal texts

descriptions.text: This package enables automated citation with BibTeX for legal studies and the humanities. In addition, the package provides commands for specifying editors in a commentary in a convenient way. Simplified formatting of the citation as well as the bibliography entry is also provided. It is possible to display the (short) title of a work only if an authors is cited with multiple works. Giving a full citation in the text, conforming to the bibliography entry, is supported. Several options are provided which might be of special interest for those outside legal studies—for instance, displaying multiple full citations. In addition, the format of last names and first names of authors may be changed easily. Cross references to other footnotes are possible. Language dependent handling of bibliography entries is possible by the special language field.

name: jurabib

caption: Citations of judgements and official documents in (German) juridical documents

descriptions.text: This package should be helpful for people working on (German) law. It (ab)uses BibTeX for citations of judgements and official documents. For this purpose, a special BibTeX-style is provided.

name: jurarsp

topics.details: typesetting legal documents or study material

caption: Typesetting German juridical documents

descriptions.text: A collection of classes for typesetting court sentences, legal opinions, books and dissertations for German lawyers. A jurabook class is also provided, which may not yet be complete.

name: juramisc

topics.details: typesetting legal documents or study material

caption: JustFontIt TeX Edition

descriptions.text:
JustFontIt TeX Edition for Win32 is a tool for TeX users. It helps installing fonts in Type1 Binary (PFB), Type1 ASCII (PFA), TrueType and OpenType/CFF to use with TeX.

The major features of JustFontIt TeX Edition are:

  • Functionality of the pltotf, tftopl, vftovp, vptovf tools, all developed by Prof. D. E. Knuth;
  • Direct production of TFM and PL TeX metric files from various sources (PFA, PFB, TTF, OTF, AFM, PFM), including reencoding;
  • Support for response files and recursive directory search;
  • Clear command-line interface; and
  • High performance.

license.name: Do Not Sell Except by Arrangement

name: JustFontItTE

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other font support

caption: A personal class for writing journals

descriptions.text: This LaTeX document class enables the user to turn simple pure text entries into a colorful and nicely formatted journal.

name: jwjournal

topics.details: LaTeX article classes and their developments
support for more than one (natural) language

caption: A replacement for LaTeX's verbatim package

descriptions.text:
This package provides a LaTeX environment listing, an alternative to the built-in verbatim environment. The listing environment is tailored for including listings of computer program source code into documents.

The main advantages over the original verbatim environment are:

  • environments automatically fixes leading whitespace so that the environment and program listing can be indented with the rest of the document source, and;
  • listing environments may easily be customised and extended.

name: jvlisting

caption: Print dates according to the classical Latin calendar

descriptions.text: kalendarium is a LaTeX3 package that provides several macros with which to print dates in classical Latin given days on the Julian or Gregorian calendars, using the same syntax used by ancient Roman authors. The format of these dates may be customised either in the package options or on a per-command basis; these options also allow for the generation of date strings according to different eras of the Classical period.

name: kalendarium

topics.details: work done for the project to upgrade LaTeX
typeset calendars, diaries, planning charts, etc.

caption: Produce page-per-day calendars

descriptions.text:
Prints a calendar/timetable from a given date for a given number of days. The parameters are read interactively; prompts (and output) are in German.

The code is written for LaTeX 2.09, but it works with no problems under LaTeX 2e.

name: kalender-209

topics.details: typeset calendars, diaries, planning charts, etc.
package only known to work with LaTeX 2.09

caption: Create a calendar, in German

descriptions.text:
The package defines a macro \Kalender, which takes one argument, and generates a calendar for the year the argument specifies. The calendar provides a table of conversion of days to day of week, for the whole year plus December of the previous year and January of the following year.

The macros use packages calc and ifthen.

name: kalender

topics.details: typeset calendars, diaries, planning charts, etc.

caption: Kana parser for LuaTeX

descriptions.text:
The package provides a kana parser for LuaTeX. It is a set of 4 macros that handle transliteration of text:

  1. from hiragana and katakana to Latin
  2. from Latin and katakana to hiragana
  3. from Latin and hiragana to katakana

It can be used to write kana directly using only the ASCII character set or for education purposes. The package has support for obsolete and rarely used syllables, some only accessible via the provided toggle macro.

name: kanaparser

topics.details: LuaTeX and packages that require it

caption: Typeset kanbun-kundoku with support for kanbun annotation

descriptions.text:
This package allows users to manually input macros for elements in a kanbun-kundoku (漢文訓読) paragraph.

More importantly, it accepts plain text input in the “kanbun annotation” form when used with LuaLaTeX, which allows typesetting kanbun-kundoku paragraphs efficiently.

name: kanbun

topics.details: package will use LuaTeX facilities if available

caption: Generate sentences in Kant's style

descriptions.text:
The package spits out sentences in Kantian style; the text is provided by the Kant generator for Python by Mark Pilgrim, described in the book “Dive into Python”.

The package is modelled on lipsum, and may be used for similar purposes.

name: kantlipsum

topics.details: dummy text generator for tests and examples

caption: Typeset Karnaugh-Veitch-maps

descriptions.text: The package provides macros for typesetting Karnaugh-Maps and Veitch-Charts in a simple and user-friendly way. Karnaugh-Maps and Veitch-Charts are used to display and simplify logic functions “manually”. These macros can typeset Karnaugh-Maps and Veitch-Charts with up to ten variables (=1024 entries).

name: karnaugh

topics.details: typesetting associated with engineering of whatever sort

caption: LaTeX package for drawing karnaugh maps with up to 6 variables

descriptions.text:
This package draws karnaugh maps with 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6 variables. It also contains commands for filling the karnaugh map with terms semi-automatically or manually. Last but not least it contains commands for drawing implicants on top of the map.

This package depends on the keyval, kvoptions, TikZ, xparse, and xstring packages.

name: karnaugh-map

topics.details: typesetting associated with engineering of whatever sort

caption: Typeset Karnaugh maps

descriptions.text:
This package provides an easy to use interface to typeset Karnaugh maps using TikZ.

Though similar to the karnaugh macros, it provides a key-value system to customize karnaughmaps and a proper LaTeX package.

name: karnaughmap

topics.details: typesetting associated with engineering of whatever sort

caption: Cartographic signs

descriptions.text:
Metafont description of a font karta15. The Metafont as written is somewhat unsatisfactory: a tidied version, the font nkarta (which also has the glyphs as MetaPost figures) is to be preferred.

A PostScript Type 1 copy of karta15 is available from the niceframe fonts bundle.

name: karta

topics.details: fonts that provide collections of symbols

caption: Practical manual for LaTeX (Finnish)

descriptions.text: “Käytännöllistä Latexia” is a practical manual for LaTeX written in the Finnish language. The manual covers most of the topics that a typical document author needs. So it can be a useful guide for beginners as well as a reference manual for advanced users.

name: kaytannollista-latexia

caption: Easily typeset Control Block Diagrams and Signal Flow Graphs

descriptions.text: Kblocks defines a number of commands to make drawing control block diagrams using TikZ/PGF more structured and easier. It reduces the learning curve forTikZ/PGF and serves as a frontend, by focusing on the block resp. flow diagrams only.

name: kblocks

caption: LaTeX version of \bordermatrix

descriptions.text: The package defines \kbordermatrix along the lines of Plain TeX's \bordermatrix.

name: kbordermatrix

caption: Document classes for Karel de Grote University College

descriptions.text:
The bundle provides two classes for usage by KdG professors and master students:

  • kdgcoursetext: for writing course texts, and
  • kdgmasterthesis: for writing master's theses.

The bundle replaces the original kdgcoursetext package (now removed from the archive).

name: kdgdocs

caption: Covers for books published by Kindle Direct Publishing

descriptions.text: The problem this class solves is the necessity to change the size of the cover PDF according to the number of pages in the book — the bigger the book, the larger the spine of the book must be. The provided class makes the necessary calculations on-the-fly, using the qpdf tool. Obviously, you need to have it installed. Also, you must run pdflatex with the --shell-escape option, in order to allow LaTeX to run qpdf.

name: kdpcover

topics.details: typeset badges, covers or labels for things (or people)

caption: Simple fonts for Greek

descriptions.text:
Brian Hamilton Kelly developed these fonts for personal use, taking the Greek mathematical symbols from the Computer Modern fonts as a starting point. The fonts are available in several styles, as Metafont source; the transliteration used is described in a paper accompanying the distribution.

Macro support is available, for use with LaTeX 2.09 (only).

name: kelly-greek-font

caption: Kerkis (Greek) font family

copyright.owner: Department of Mathematics, University of the Aegean

descriptions.text:
Sans-serif Greek fonts to match the URW Bookman set (which are distributed with Kerkis). The Kerkis font set has some support for mathematics as well as other glyphs missing from the base URW Bookman fonts. Macros are provided to use the fonts in OT1, T1 (only NG/ng glyphs missing) and LGR encodings, as well as in mathematics; small caps and old-style number glyphs are also available.

The philosophy, and the design process, of the Kerkis fonts is discussed in a paper in TUGboat 23(3/4), 2002.

name: kerkis

topics.details: font available in Adobe Type 1 format
font providing LaTeX T1 encoding support
metrics, macro incantations and other font support
font for Greek (archaic, classical and modern)

caption: Greek fonts and macros

descriptions.text:
The fonts are distributed as Metafont source; the design derives from Silvio Levy’s fonts, but has also been influenced by Yannis Haralambous’ work. They are 8-bit fonts which, the author believes, leads to more robust macro programming. Both ancient and modern Greek are supported.

Macros to work with Plain TeX (‘greektex’) and with LaTeX 2.09 (‘grlatex’) are provided.

name: kdgreek

caption: Print tables and generate control files to adjust kernings

descriptions.text:
This class makes it easy to generate tables that show many different kerning pairs of an arbitrary font, usable by LaTeX. It shows the kerning values that are used in the font by default.

In addition, this class enables the user to alter the kernings and to observe the results. Kerning pairs can be defined for groups of similar glyphs at the same time. An mtx file is generated automatically. The mtx file may then be loaded by fontinst to introduce the user-made kernings into the virtual font for later use in LaTeX.

name: kerntest

topics.details: support for font development, testing and characterisation

caption: Creating graphics for TeX using Cinderella

descriptions.text:
KeTCindy combines a plugin to Cinderella with free mathematical software (R, Maxima, …) to produce high-quality LaTeX graphics.

Using Cinderella to generate graphics in an interactive environment, the generated image can be fine-tuned using KeTCindy commands embedded into CindyScript, the scripting language of Cinderella.

KeTCindy can be regarded as a prominent scheme to establish an effective linkage between visualization tools and editing tools. Moreover, KeTCindy enables the importation of data calculated or simulated using other mathematical software such as Maxima, Fricas, Risa/Asir and R, and to combine them with the graphical data, so that an extremely wide range of mathematical objects can be presented.

license.name: GNU General Public License, version 3 or newer

name: ketcindy

caption: Simple creation of commands with key-value arguments

descriptions.text:
The package (which requires e-TeX) provides a natural way to define commands with optional keys.

The package provides \newkeycommand, \renewkeycommand, \providekeycommand, \newkeyenvironment and \renewkeyenvironment, together with \keycmd for a more advanced interface.

The package is based on kvsetkeys by Heiko Oberdiek.

name: keycommand

caption: A robust interface to xkeyval

descriptions.text:
The package provides a robust interface to controlling keys in xkeyval, removing some of that package’s restrictions.

The package also addresses some of the issues now covered by the author’s ltxkeys package, which was assumed to be a replacement for keyreader. Since keyreader has remained a favourite with users, it has been reinstated.

name: keyreader

caption: Key based parser

descriptions.text: This LaTeX package provides an interface to define and evaluate key-based replacement rules. It can be used to parse the argument specification of a document command.

name: keyparse

caption: Provides a key/value interface for generating floats

descriptions.text:
The keyfloat package provides a key/value user interface for quickly creating figures with a single image each, figures with arbitrary contents, tables, subfloats, rows of floats, floats located [H]ere, floats in the [M]argin, and floats with text [W]rapped around them.

Key/value combinations may specify a caption and label, a width proportional to \linewidth, a fixed width and/or height, rotation, scaling, a tight or loose frame, an \arraystretch, a continued float, additional supplemental text, and an artist/author's name with automatic index entry. When used with the tocdata package, the name also appears in the List of Figures.

Floats may be placed into a row environment, and are typeset to fit within the given number of columns, continuing to the next row if necessary. Nested sub-rows may be used to generate layouts such as two small figures placed vertically next to one larger figure.

Subfloats are supported by two environments.

name: keyfloat

caption: Index entries by key lookup

descriptions.text: The package provides functionality for producing an index without directly entering index entries into the text using the \index command, but instead by looking up short keys and printing a predefined string in the main text and adding a corresponding index entry. The standard use case is the production of an index of names.

name: keyindex

caption: Graphical representation of keys on keyboard

descriptions.text: A LaTeX package which provides macros for the graphical representation of the keys on a computer keyboard.

name: keystroke

topics.details: macros and tools for preparing documentation

caption: Re-usable table layouts separating content and presentation

descriptions.text:
The main goal of this package is to offer means for typesetting tables easily and yet still looking rather nicely in a way that separates content from presentation and with re-usable layout for tables of the same type.

For this purpose, the package provides the environment KeyValTable, which allows one to typeset tables that have a previously defined column layout and whose rows can be produced in a key-value fashion.

name: keyvaltable

caption: Process 'key=value' schemes

descriptions.text:
The package offered the first key-value decoder for LaTeX 2e; its original user was the graphicx package, but it is widely used elsewhere in common LaTeX packages.

The package is part of the latex-graphics bundle, which is one of the collections in the LaTeX ‘required’ set of packages.

name: keyval

caption: A lightweight and robust key-value parser

descriptions.text: The package provides lightweight and robust facilities for creating and managing keys. Its machinery isn’t as extensive as that of, e.g., the ltxkeys package, but it is equally robust; ease of use and speed of processing are the design aims of the package.

name: keyval2e

caption: A LaTeX document style to produce homework, quiz and exam papers

descriptions.text: The package provides commands and environments that simplify and streamline the process of preparing homework, quiz and exam papers according to apreffered style. The default style is based on the guidelines set by the department of mathematics at King Fahd University of Petroleum and Minerals (KFUPM). It can be easily customized to fit any style for any institution.

name: kfupm-math-exam

caption: Arabic font for university articles

descriptions.text:
This font family is a modification of “cm-unicode” fonts, with Arabic support.

It was originally made for a group of undergraduate students at Misr University For Science And Technology (Egypt) many years ago. After a few semesters, it had become the main font for their articles and assignments. Now, it is on CTAN for easier access.

khatalmaqala = khat (font) + maqala (article) = font for article

name: khatalmaqala

topics.details: font designed for use as body font for Latin-based script documents

caption: A user friendly TeX/LaTeX editor for KDE

descriptions.text: The Kile project is developing a user friendly TeX/LaTeX editor. It will run on systems with the KDE desktop environment. (KDE is available for many architectures with Linux installed.)

name: kile

caption: Design kinematic chains and mechanisms

descriptions.text: This package provides functionalities to draw kinematic diagrams for mechanisms using dedicate symbols (some from the ISO standard and others). The intention is not to represent CAD mechanical drawings of mechanisms and robots, but only to represent 2D and 3D kinematic chains. The package provides links, joints and other symbols, mostly in the form of TikZ pic objects. These pics can be placed in the canvas either by a central point for joints, and start and end points for some links.

name: kinematikz

caption: Typeset KIX codes

descriptions.text: Implements KIX codes as used by the Dutch PTT for bulk mail addressing. (Royal Mail 4 State Code.) KIX is a registered trade mark of PTT Post Holdings B. V.

name: kix

caption: A font for KIX codes

descriptions.text:
The KIX code is a barcode-like format used by the Dutch PTT to encode country codes, zip codes and street numbers in a machine-readable format. If printed below the address line on bulk mailings, a discount can be obtained.

The font is distributed in Metafont format, and covers the numbers and upper-case letters.

name: KIXfont

topics.details: fonts with specific small application areas

caption: A Klingon font

descriptions.text: Offers a full set of upper case and small caps letters, together with numbers and some punctuation. The font is distributed in Metafont format.

name: klinz

topics.details: font for an ‘invented’ language or script

caption: Hyphenation patterns for Kurmanji, T1 encoded

descriptions.text:
These are patterns for the Kurmanji language (Northern Kurdish, as spoken in Turkey and by the Kurdish diaspora in Europe).

The patterns are generated from a word list of approximately 2500 hyphenated words, and are presented in T1 encoding.

name: kmrhyph

caption: Tangle and weave with multiple change files

descriptions.text: Knit and twist are represented as change files from tangle and weave (respectively). In each case, they act in the same way as the parent program, but can process more than one change file at the same time.

name: knit

caption: Create knitting patterns

descriptions.text: The class provides a simple, effective method for knitters to produce high-quality, attractive patterns using LaTeX. It does this by providing commands to handle as much of the layout of the document as possible, leaving the author free to concentrate on the pattern.

name: knittingpattern

caption: A Celtic knotwork font

descriptions.text:
The package provides a set of (basically similar) fonts. The glyphs of each font may be assembled into a knotwork pattern.

The fonts are distributed as Metafont source; a TeX document to test the fonts is supplied.

name: knot

caption: Displaying, hyperlinking, and indexing notions in a document

descriptions.text: The package offers a systematic way to handle notions/concepts/terms throughout a document. It helps building an index. In combination with hyperref it makes it easy to have every reference of a concept linked to its introduction. It also offers simple notations.

name: knowledge

caption: Multiple-guess tests

descriptions.text: A package supporting the generation and correction of multiple option tests as appears in TUGBoat Volume 17, Number 3: “Fast and secure multiple option tests”.

name: knst

topics.details: extensions to Plain TeX for higher-level constructs

caption: Produce knitting charts, in Plain TeX or LaTeX

descriptions.text: The package provides symbol fonts and commands to write charted instructions for cable and lace knitting patterns, using either plain TeX or LaTeX. The fonts are available both as Metafont source and in Adobe Type 1 format.

name: knitting

topics.details: fonts that provide collections of symbols
font available in Adobe Type 1 format

caption: The current state of Knuth's contributions

descriptions.text:
This directory tree holds copies of material on Knuth’s mirror site. The material is divided into two main parts:
– the distribution, and
– Knuth’s local information.

name: knuth-base

caption: The current state of Knuth's contributions

descriptions.text:
This directory tree represents a snapshot of Knuth's own sources (including those of TeX and Metafont) and documentation (including The TeXbook and The METAFONTbook).

The tree may be browsed from this directory, but all significant items on the tree have their own catalogue entries.

name: knuth-dist

caption: Knuth’s published errata

descriptions.text: These files record details of problems reported in Knuth's ‘Computers and Typesetting’ series of books, for the Computer Modern fonts, and for TeX, Metafont and related programs.

name: knuth-errata

topics.details: lists of errata in published books

caption: HINT collection of typeset C/WEB sources in TeX Live

descriptions.text:
The knuth-hint package contains the large collection of HINT documents for many of the CWEB amd WEB sources of programs in the TeX Live distribution (and, for technical reasons, a PDF document for XeTeX). Each program is presented in its original form as written by the respective authors, and in the “changed” form as used in TeX Live. Care has been taken to keep the section numbering intact, so that you can study the codes and the changes in parallel. Also included are the “errata” for Donald Knuth’s “Computers & Typesetting”.

HINT is the dynamic document format created by Martin Ruckert’s HiTeX engine that was added to TeX Live 2022. The HINT files can be viewed on Linux, Windows, and Android with the hintview application. The knuth-hint package is a showcase of HiTeX’s capabilities.

name: knuth-hint

caption: Knuth’s example letter macros

descriptions.text: These are Knuth’s own letter macros. Documentation is entirely missing from the archive, but the macros are discussed in some detail in the TeXbook (which says it is describing letterformat.tex).

name: knuth-letter

topics.details: extensions to Plain TeX for higher-level constructs

caption: Knuth’s local information

descriptions.text: A collection of experimental programs and developments based on, or complementary to, the matter in his distribution directories.

name: knuth-local

caption: PDF collection of typeset C/WEB sources in TeX Live

descriptions.text:
Here you find a large collection of PDF documents for many C/WEB programs in TeX Live, both in their original form as written by their respective authors, and in the changed form as they are actually used in the TeX Live system. Care has been taken to keep the section numbering intact, so that you can study the sources and their changes in parallel. Also included is the collection of “errata” for Donald Knuth’s “Computers & Typesetting series”.

Although not all the texts here are written or maintained by Donald Knuth, it is more convenient for everything to be collected in one place for reading and searching. They all stem from the system that Knuth created. The central entry point is the “index” file, with links to the individual documents, either in HTML or in PDF format.

name: knuth-pdf

caption:
Makes the style and command of moderncv (style classic) available
       for koma-classes and thus compatible with BibLaTeX

descriptions.text: This package provides an imitation of the moderncv class with the classic style (by Xavier Danaux), to be used in conjunction with the koma-classes. Thus it is possible to configure pagelayout, headings etc. the way it is done in koma-classes. Moreover, it is possible to use BibLaTeX, while the original moderncv-class is incompatible with BibLaTeX.

name: koma-moderncvclassic

caption: Core TeX and Metafont sources from Knuth

descriptions.text: A collection of core TeX and Metafont macro files from DEK, apart from the plain format and base. Includes the MF logo font(s), webmac.tex, etc.

name: knuth-lib

caption: A bundle of versatile classes and packages

descriptions.text:
The KOMA-Script bundle provides replacements for the article, report, and book classes with emphasis on typography and versatility. There is also a letter class.

The bundle also offers:

  • a package for calculating type areas in the way laid down by the typographer Jan Tschichold,
  • packages for easily changing and defining page styles,
  • a package scrdate for getting not only the current date but also the name of the day, and
  • a package scrtime for getting the current time.

All these packages may be used not only with KOMA-Script classes but also with the standard classes.

Since every package has its own version number, the version number quoted only refers to the version of scrbook, scrreprt, scrartcl, scrlttr2 and typearea (which are the main parts of the bundle).

name: koma-script

topics.details: typesetting legal documents or study material
deal with Tables of Contents, and of other such things
support for managing packages within documents
lists of addresses, for a personal directory (or the like)
general notes (not including endnotes or footnotes)

caption: Examples from the KOMA-Script book

descriptions.text:
This package contains some examples from the 6th edition of the book »KOMA-Script«, »Eine Sammlung von Klassen und Paketen für LaTeX2e« by Markus Kohm, published by Lehmanns Media.

There are no further descriptions of these examples.

name: koma-script-examples

topics.details: copies of examples from a published book

caption: KOI-8 input support

descriptions.text: A package to perform internal translation from the KOI-8 encoding (de-facto standard of the Russian Unix world) to the “alternative encoding” used by most (pre-UTF-8) Cyrillic packages. You still need one of these packages for the actual Russian typesetting. The style works with all major Cyrillic packages, including cmcyr, cmcyralt, LH.

name: koi8

topics.details: support languages written using Cyrillic alphabets

caption: Examples from the 3rd edition of the KOMA-Script book

descriptions.text:
This package contains some examples from the 3th edition of the book «KOMA-Script—Eine Sammlung von Klassen und Paketen für LaTeX2e» by Markus Kohm and Jens-Uwe Morawski.

There are no further descriptions of these examples.

name: koma-script-examples-3

topics.details: copies of examples from a published book

caption: Examples from the 4th edition of the KOMA-Script book

descriptions.text:
This package contains some examples from the 4th edition of the book «KOMA-Script—Eine Sammlung von Klassen und Paketen für LaTeX2e» by Markus Kohm and Jens-Uwe Morawski.

There are no further descriptions of these examples.

name: koma-script-examples-4

topics.details: copies of examples from a published book

caption: Examples from the 5th edition of the KOMA-Script book

descriptions.text:
This package contains some examples from the 5th edition of the book »KOMA-Script«, »Eine Sammlung von Klassen und Paketen für LaTeX2e« by Markus Kohm, published by Lehmanns Media.

There are no further descriptions of these examples.

name: koma-script-examples-5

topics.details: copies of examples from a published book

caption: Deprecated packages from koma-script

descriptions.text:
The bundle provides copies of old versions of packages in the current koma-script bundle.

Packages in the obsolete ‘distribution’ are scrlettr, scrpage, scrpage2, and tocstyle; they should not be used in new documents, but are preserved for use in existing documents.

name: koma-script-obsolete

caption: Koma-script letter class option for Finnish

descriptions.text: A koma-script parameter set for letters on A4 paper, complying with Finnish standards SFS 2486, 2487 and 2488; suitable for window envelopes with window on the left size in the sizes C5, C65, E5 and E65 (although, because the address window is smaller, for sizes E5 and E65 the address may not fit within the window, but ordinary 3-line address should fit).

name: koma-script-sfs

caption: Typesetting a beautiful CV with various style options

descriptions.text: The class simplifies the creation of beautiful CV. The user may choose between different styles, and may adjust settings to tune the output.

name: komacv

caption: LaTeX packages that aid in creating CVs based on the komacv class and creating related documents

descriptions.text:
The komacv-rg bundle provides packages that aid in creating CVs based on the komacv class and creating related documents, such as cover letters and cover sheets for job applications. Concretely, the bundle consists of three packages: komacv-addons, komacv-lco, and komacv-multilang.

  • komacv-addons is a small collection of add-ons and fixes for the komacv class;
  • komacv-lco enables the use of letter class options from scrlttr2 also in komacv-based and other non-scrlttr2-based documents;
  • komacv-multilang enables the provisioning of CVs in multiple languages and the selection of a language via babel or polyglossia.

name: komacv-rg

caption: A program for automatic numbering of compounds in chemical publications

descriptions.text: Konwerter automatically numbers compounds in chemical publications created by LaTeX. It is written in C++ and works both in Unix and Windows operating systems. It works similar to LaTeX \label and \ref commands. Instead of giving number to every compound you give them labels and then refer to the structure in the text using the same label. The konwerter is able to resolve labels to numbers both in the eps files and in the text.

name: konwerter

caption: A LaTeX document class for typesetting Korean documents

descriptions.text:
The class is based on memoir, and is adapted to typesetting Korean documents.

The bundle (of class and associated packages) belongs to the ko.TeX bundle.

It depends on memoir and kotex-utf to function.

name: kotex-oblivoir

caption: Typeset articles using KorigamiK’s document class

descriptions.text: The KorigamiK class is used for typesetting documents for university or school projects and lab reports. It is based on the article class with modifications to allow for more flexible front-matter among other small changes.

license.name: GNU General Public License, version 3 or newer

name: KorigamiK

topics.details: LaTeX article classes and their developments

caption: Macros for typesetting Korean under Plain TeX

descriptions.text:
The package provides macros for typesetting Hangul, the native alphabet of the Korean language, using plain *TeX. Input Korean text should be encoded in UTF-8.

The package belongs to the ko.TeX bundle.

name: kotex-plain

topics.details: extensions to Plain TeX for higher-level constructs

caption: Typeset Hangul, coded in UTF-8

descriptions.text:
The package typesets Hangul, which is the native alphabet of the Korean language; input Korean text should be encoded in UTF-8.

The bundle (of class and associated packages) belongs to the ko.TeX bundle.

name: kotex-utf

caption: Utility scripts and support files for typesetting Korean

descriptions.text:
The bundle provides scripts and support files for index generation in Korean language typesetting.

The files belong to the ko.TeX bundle.

name: kotex-utils

caption: Path searching library for TeX-related files

descriptions.text: Kpathsea is a library and utility programs which provide path searching facilities for TeX file types, including the self-locating feature required for movable installations, layered on top of a general search mechanism. It is not distributed separately, but rather is released and maintained as part of the TeX Live sources.

name: kpathsea

caption: A complete set of fonts for text and mathematics

descriptions.text:
The family contains text fonts in roman, sans-serif and monospaced shapes, with true small caps and old-style numbers; the package offers full support of the textcomp package. The mathematics fonts include all the AMS fonts, in both normal and bold weights.

Each of the font types is available in two main versions: default and ‘light’. Each version is available in four variants: default; oldstyle numbers; oldstyle numbers with old ligatures such as ct and st, and long-tailed capital Q; and veryoldstyle with long s. Other variants include small caps as default or ‘large small caps’, and for mathematics both upright and slanted shapes for Greek letters, as well as default and narrow versions of multiple integrals.

The fonts were originally derived from URW Palladio (with URW’s agreement) though the fonts are very clearly different in appearance from their parent.

name: kpfonts

topics.details: font available in Adobe Type 1 format

caption: BibTeX style for KSFH Munich

descriptions.text: The package supports bibliographies as standard for KSFH (Katholische Stiftungsfachhochschule) Munich. BibTeX entries in article, book, inbook, incollection and misc formats are supported.

name: ksfh-nat

caption: OTF version of the Kp-fonts

descriptions.text:
This bundle provides OpenType versions of the Type1 Kp-fonts designed by Christophe Caignaert. It is usable with LuaTeX or XeTeX engines only.

It consists of sixteen Text fonts (eight Serif, four Sans-Serif, four Monotype) and six Math fonts.

Serif and Sans-Serif families have small caps available in two sizes (SmallCaps and PetitesCaps), upper and lowercase digits, real superscripts and subscripts; ancient ligatures (ct and st), ancient long-s and a long-tailed capital Q are available via font features.

Math fonts cover all usual symbols including AMS’; a full list of available symbols is provided, see the ‘List of glyphs’.

name: kpfonts-otf

topics.details: font designed for use as body font for Latin-based script documents
metrics, macro incantations and other font support

caption: A LaTeX class for theses published with KIT Scientific Publishing

descriptions.text:
This package provides a LaTeX class intended for authors who want to publish their thesis or other scientific work with KIT Scientific Publishing (KSP).

The class is based on the scrbook class of the KOMA-script bundle in combination with the ClassicThesis and ArsClassica packages. It modifies some of the layout and style definitions of these packages in order to provide a document layout that should be compatible with the requirements by KSP.

name: ksp-thesis

caption: Graphical frontend to TeX

descriptions.text: KTeXShell is a KDE frontend to (La)TeX. The intended audience is the difference between the set of all (explicit and implicit) TeX-users and that of users of tools like LyX or KLyX.

name: KTeXShell

caption: Extract subsets of documents

descriptions.text:
The package defines an exercice environment which numbers every exercise, and a command \get to extract a collection whose argument is a comma-separated set of exercise index numbers.

While the package was designed for teachers constructing tables of exercises, it plainly has more general application.

name: ktv-texdata

topics.details: select data from sets in the TeX file

caption: Copenhagen University or faculty logo for front page

descriptions.text: A comprehensive package for adding University of Copenhagen or faculty logo to your front page. For use by student or staff at University of Copenhagen (Københavns Universitet).

name: ku-template

topics.details: symbols or drawings to specify an object, including icons

caption: A ‘lipsum’ package for the Kurdish language

descriptions.text:
This package provides lipsum-like facilities for the Kurdish language.

The package gives you easy access to the Kurdish poetry and balladry texts of the Diwany Vafaiy, Ahmedy Xani, Naly, Mahwy,....

The package needs to be run under XeLaTeX.

name: kurdishlipsum

topics.details: XeTeX, material supporting it, and packages requiring it
dummy text generator for tests and examples

caption: A two-element sans-serif typeface

descriptions.text:
Kurier is a two-element sans-serif typeface. It was designed for a diploma in typeface design at the Warsaw Academy of Fine Arts under the supervision of Roman Tomaszewski.

This distribution contains a significantly extended set of characters covering the following modern alphabets: latin (including Vietnamese), Cyrillic and Greek as well as a number of additional symbols (including mathematical symbols). The fonts are prepared in Type 1 and OpenType formats.
