For use with TeX the following encoding files have been prepared: T1 (ec), T2 (abc), and OT2—Cyrillic, T5 (Vietnamese), OT4, QX, texansi and—nonstandard (IL2 for the Czech fonts), as well as supporting macros and files defining fonts for LaTeX.

name: kurier

topics.details: font available in Adobe Type 1 format

caption: Drawing macros and fonts for diagrams

descriptions.text: Commutative diagrams using PostScript specials (uses \special definitions for dvips, but the macros are designed for flexibility in this respect).

name: kuvio

caption: Define keys for use in the kvsetkeys package

descriptions.text: The package provides a macro \kv@define@key (analogous to keyval’s \define@key, to define keys for use by kvsetkeys.

name: kvdefinekeys

caption: Key value format for package options

descriptions.text: This package offers support for package authors who want to use options in key-value format for their package options.

name: kvoptions

caption: Key value parser with default handler support

descriptions.text: This package provides \kvsetkeys, a variant of package keyval's \setkeys. It allows the user to specify a handler that deals with unknown options. Active commas and equal signs may be used (e.g. see babel's shorthands) and only one level of curly braces are removed from the values.

name: kvsetkeys

caption: Create Karnaugh maps with LaTeX

descriptions.text: This LaTeX package allows the creation of (even large) Karnaugh maps. It provides a tabular-like input syntax and support for drawing bundles (implicants) around adjacent values. It is based on an answer at StackExchange.

name: kvmap

topics.details: typesetting associated with engineering of whatever sort

caption: LaTeX pictures "how-to" (German)

descriptions.text: The document (in German) is a collection of “how-to” notes about LaTeX and pictures. The aim of the document is to provide a solution, in the form of some sample code, for every problem.

name: l2picfaq

caption: LaTeX to ASCII

descriptions.text: L2a attempts to remove LaTeX markup commands, leaving only the body of text. It is intended to be used when journal editors request plain ASCII text for typesetting, or when you want to post a plain version of a LaTeX document on an electronic conference system.

name: l2a

topics.details: derive plain text from a TeX document

caption: English translation of "Obsolete packages and commands"

descriptions.text: English translation of the l2tabu practical guide to LaTeX2e by Mark Trettin. A list of obsolete packages and commands.

name: l2tabu-english

topics.details: translation of material from the archive, to another language

caption: Obsolete packages and commands

descriptions.text:
The “sins” of LaTeX users, and how to correct them. The document provides a list of obsolete packages and commands.

This original is in German; it has been translated into English, French, Italian, and Spanish.

name: l2tabu

caption: French translation of l2tabu

descriptions.text: French translation of l2tabu.

name: l2tabu-french

caption: Spanish translation of "Obsolete packages and commands"

descriptions.text: A Spanish translation of the l2tabu practical guide to LaTeX2e by Mark Trettin. A list of obsolete packages, commands and usages.

name: l2tabu-spanish

caption: Italian Translation of Obsolete packages and commands

descriptions.text: Italian translation of the l2tabu practical guide to LaTeX2e (a list of obsolete packages and commands).

name: l2tabu-italian

caption: LaTeX to ASCII

descriptions.text: L2x is a general-purpose LaTeX converter. It consists of a parser written in C, which then calls Tcl functions for each LaTeX function. The Tcl functions return the translated value. A number of Tcl functions are provided: for example l2html.tcl (for HTML file output) and ms.tcl (for nroff/troff -ms macros).

name: l2x

topics.details: convert TeX-ish sources to some other markup (than HTML)

caption: LaTeX3 backend drivers

descriptions.text:
This package forms parts of expl3, and contains the code used to interface with backends (drivers) across the expl3 codebase.

The functions here are defined differently depending on the engine in use. As such, these are distributed separately from l3kernel to allow this code to be updated on an independent schedule.

name: l3backend

topics.details: work done for the project to upgrade LaTeX

caption: Strip documentation in LaTeX3 source

descriptions.text:
The package provides, for the LaTeX 3 distribution, the same function as does docstrip for LaTeX 2e code — to remove comments from a source file, to provide a faster-running (and more compact) version of the .dtx source.

The package is distributed as part of the l3kernel bundle.

name: l3docstrip

topics.details: work done for the project to upgrade LaTeX
macros and tools for preparing documentation

caption: A testing and building system for (La)TeX

descriptions.text:
The build system supports testing and building LaTeX3 code, on Linux, Mac OS X and Windows systems. The package offers:

  • A unit testing system for (La)TeX code (whether kernel code or contributed packages);
  • A system for typesetting package documentation; and
  • An automated process for creating CTAN releases.

The package is essentially independent of other material released by the LaTeX3 team, and may be updated on a different schedule.

name: l3build

topics.details: support for work with the CTAN archive

caption: Experimental LaTeX3 concepts

descriptions.text:
The l3experimental packages are a collection of experimental implementations for aspects of the LaTeX3 kernel, dealing with higher-level ideas such as the Designer Interface. Some of them work as stand alone packages, providing new functionality, and can be used on top of LaTeX2e with no changes to the existing kernel.

The present release includes:

  • l3benchmark for measuring the time taken by TeX to run certain code;
  • l3draw, a code-level interface for constructing drawings;
  • l3graphics, an interfaces for the inclusion of graphics files;
  • l3opacity, support for opacity in PDF output;
  • l3str, support for string manipulation;
  • l3sys-shell, which provides abstractions for common shell functions like file deletion and copying;
  • xcoffins, which allows the alignment of boxes using a series of ‘handle’ positions, supplementing the simple TeX reference point;
  • xgalley, which controls boxes receiving text for typesetting.

name: l3experimental

topics.details: layout of objects on the page
work done for the project to upgrade LaTeX

caption: LaTeX3 programming conventions

descriptions.text: The l3kernel bundle provides an implementation of the LaTeX3 programmers’ interface, as a set of packages that run under LaTeX2e. The interface provides the foundation on which the LaTeX3 kernel and other future code are built: it is an API for TeX programmers. The packages are set up so that the LaTeX3 conventions can be used with regular LaTeX2e packages.

name: l3kernel

topics.details: work done for the project to upgrade LaTeX

caption: High-level LaTeX3 concepts

descriptions.text:
This collection contains implementations for aspects of the LaTeX3 kernel, dealing with higher-level ideas such as the Designer Interface. The packages here are considered broadly stable (The LaTeX3 Project does not expect the interfaces to alter radically). These packages are built on LaTeX2e conventions at the interface level, and so may not migrate in the current form to a stand-alone LaTeX3 format.

Packages provided:

  • xparse, which provides a high-level interface for declaring document commands
  • xfp, an expandable IEEE 754 FPU for LaTeX
  • l3keys2e, which makes the facilities of the kernel module l3keys available for use by LaTeX 2e packages
  • xtemplate, which provides a means of defining generic functions using a key-value syntax
  • xfrac, which provides flexible split-level fractions

name: l3packages

topics.details: work done for the project to upgrade LaTeX

caption: Sorting within TeX

descriptions.text: Macros for sorting items within TeX. Two sorting algorithms are provided: heapsort and quicksort.

name: laansort

caption: LaTeX2e option processing using LaTeX3 keys

descriptions.text:
The package provides an interface whereby LaTeX 2e users may use the key-value functions provided in the LaTeX 3 kernel distribution.

The key-value system implemented is more similar to that of pgfkeys than to any other extant package.

The package is part of the l3packages bundle.

name: l3keys2e

topics.details: work done for the project to upgrade LaTeX

caption: School handwriting fonts

descriptions.text:
This package comprises two fonts, la and lla (provided as Metafont source); their glyphs simulate handwriting as taught in (German) primary schools. The fonts come with a brief (LaTeX 2.09) example file.

Macro support under LaTeX 2e is provided by the la package in the fundus bundle, which should be used in preference to the LaTeX 2.09 macros that come with the font.

name: la

caption: Print address labels in three columns

descriptions.text: Input may be a set of labels in-line in a document, or a file of labels.

name: label-pln

topics.details: extensions to Plain TeX for higher-level constructs
typeset sets of labels (for cutting out, etc.)

caption: Regular expression facilities for LaTeX

descriptions.text:
The package provides regular expression testing, extraction of submatches, splitting, and replacement, all acting on token lists. The syntax of regular expressions is mostly a subset of the PCRE syntax (and is very close to Posix), with some additions arising from the fact that TeX manipulates tokens rather than characters.

For performance reasons, only a limited set of features are implemented. Notably, back-references are not supported.

The package is currently distributed as part of the LaTeX3 l3kernel bundle.

name: l3regex

topics.details: work done for the project to upgrade LaTeX

caption: Check the existence of labels, and fork accordingly

descriptions.text:
The package defines two commands:

  • \eachlabelcase, which distinguishes whether a set of labels is defined, and for each label either queues action accordingly, or appends the action to a macro; and
  • \lotlabelcase, which takes a comma-separated list of label names, and distinguishes the resulting action on whether all were defined, whether none were defined, whether not all were defined, or whether the lest is empty (again, the action resulting from \lotlabelcase may be written to a macro).

name: labelcas

caption: Label LaTeX 2.09 figures included in documents

descriptions.text:
The user specifies a table of labels (in a group \SetLabels ... \endSetLabels), and then includes the graphic and places the labels at the same time using the command \AffixLabels.

The package can draw a grid over your figure, to ease estimation of the labels' required location.

name: labelfig

caption: Print Avery 5160 labels for laser printers

descriptions.text: Accepts \address commands, whose arguments are printed 30 to a page, in boxes of dimension 2.625" x 1".

name: labelmac3

topics.details: typeset sets of labels (for cutting out, etc.)

caption: Typeset laboratory journals

descriptions.text: This class is designed to typeset laboratory journals that contain chronologically ordered records about experiments. From the sectioning commands, an experiment index is generated. The class is based on the KOMA-Script class scrbook.cls. There can be several index entries for one experiment.

name: labbook

caption: Manage a collection of labels

descriptions.text: A MS-Win32 program for managing a collection of labels to be typeset by TeX and printed on demand. The collection will be held together within a single file; labels may be kept within categories. As an advanced feature, mailing labels, e.g., may query an ODBC data source.

name: labelmag

topics.details: typeset sets of labels (for cutting out, etc.)

caption: Print sheets of sticky labels

descriptions.text: A LaTeX package to print a regular grid of ragged-right labels on a page, suitable for sheets of labels which can be fed through a printer. Macros are provided to allow easy input of names and addresses in a form free of TeX markup. Equally useful is a feature for making multiple copies of a single label, e.g., return address stickers to go with the labels. Rows, columns, borders can all be specified to match the label sheet being used.

name: labels

topics.details: typeset sets of labels (for cutting out, etc.)

caption: Add reference labels to easylist items

descriptions.text: This package provides the \itemLabel macro for adding configurable reference labels to easylist items.

name: labels4easylist

caption: List names of labels in a document

descriptions.text:
A derivative of the file lablst.tex (in the LaTeX distribution); embeds itself in \end{document} and prints, below the end of the document itself, a list of labels used.

(Such a package today would use \AtEndDocument from LaTeX 2e, but this package hacks itself in without ceremony.)

name: lablst-pkg

topics.details: package only known to work with LaTeX 2.09
support for package or document debugging

caption: Label diagrams produced in Metafont

descriptions.text: Comes with a Metafont support file, which is to be input by the diagram file.

name: labtex

topics.details: graphics produced by one of the *TeX engines

caption: Draw labyrinths and solution paths

descriptions.text: The labyrinth package provides code and an environment for typesetting simple labyrinths with LaTeX, and generating an automatic or manual solution path.

name: labyrinth

topics.details: process game diagrams, gamebooks, and other amusements

caption: Draw simple ladder diagrams using TikZ

descriptions.text:
This package permits the creation of simple ladder diagrams within LaTeX documents.

Required packages are tikz, ifthen, and calc.

name: ladder

caption: LaTeX checker

descriptions.text: Lacheck is a tool for finding common mistakes in LaTeX documents. The distribution includes sources, and executables for OS/2 and Win32 environments.

name: lacheck

caption: Identify labels which cause endless “may have changed” warnings

descriptions.text:
Several conditions can cause LaTeX labels to keep changing, no matter how many times a document is recompiled.

This package helps diagnose the cause of repeated “Label(s) may have changed” warnings. The names and before/after definitions of changing labels are printed at the end of each compile.

Multiply-defined labels are printed as well.

name: labelschanged

caption: Hyphenation patterns for the Latin language

descriptions.text:
These are patterns for the Latin language mainly in modern spelling (u when u is needed and v when v is needed); medieval spelling with the ligatures \ae and \oe and the (uncial) lowercase ‘v’ written as a ‘u’ is also supported; apparently there is no conflict between the patterns of modern Latin and those of medieval Latin.

The patterns support the restricted character set of the OT1-encoding (obviously without the ligature characters), as well as T1-encoded usage.

name: lahyph

topics.details: support for typesetting Latin (ancient, medieval and ‘modern’)

caption: Los Alamos letter style

copyright.owner: The Regents of the University of California

descriptions.text: Format letters for Los Alamos, in accordance with the Laboratory’s “Office Procedures Manual”

name: laletter

topics.details: package only known to work with LaTeX 2.09

caption: Lists in TeX's mouth

descriptions.text: These list-processing macros avoid the reassignments employed in the macros shown in Appendix D of the TeXbook: all the manipulations take place in what Knuth is pleased to call “TeX’s mouth”.

name: lambda-lists

caption: Use Lambda expression within LaTeX

descriptions.text: This package provides Lambda expressions. It is an interface to specify the parameters and replacement code of a document-command, and then to evaluate it with compatible arguments. Optionally, it can be used recursively.

name: lambdax

caption: Memo style as used at Los Alamos

copyright.owner: The Regents of the University of California

descriptions.text: Provides a memo style conforming to the office procedures manual of the Los Alamos National Laboratory.

name: lamemo

topics.details: package only known to work with LaTeX 2.09
typeset memorandum or other short note

caption: A PostScript translator for a subset of LaTeX

descriptions.text:
LameTeX is a direct PostScript generator for a (very limited) subset of LaTeX. One of its original design goals, the inclusion of PostScript commands directly in a LaTeX document, has been superseded by PSTricks. However, one of the side effects of a special-purpose translator for LaTeX is the ability of that translator to produce different kinds of output, including plain ASCII.

The system only understands a subset of LaTeX, and is not set up to use Type 1 fonts; however, it is capable of doing some interesting tricks.

license.name: Do Not Sell Except by Arrangement

name: lametex

caption: A merge of the best in AMS-TeX and LaTeX

descriptions.text:
The package was produced in response to a perceived demand from AMSTeX users for the sorts of facilities that LaTeX provides. (In the event, most such users use AMS-LaTeX, which the AMS develops.)

The distribution comprises TeX source and set of fonts (as Metafont source) that are used in the package's commutative diagram macros.

Furthermore, two applications are associated with LamsTeX, an index-processor that deals with LamsTeX's indexing commands, and dvipaste.

name: LamsTeX

caption: Set up for typesetting in landscape

descriptions.text:
The landscape package is long superseded by the geometry package, which has sophisticated controls on page layout.

If your need is for occasional pages in landscape layout, consider lscape, or rotating for rotated float pages.

name: landscape

topics.details: print landscape orientation, manipulate landscape material
layout of objects on the page

caption: Simple language-dependent settings based on language codes

descriptions.text:
The package provides a command \uselangcode{<code>} to adjust language-dependent settings such as key words, typographical conventions and language codes (ISO 639-1).

The package provides a means of selecting macros according to the specified code, for preparing a document that is to be separately typeset in different laguages.

The package is dependent on the plainpkg package, and is already in use in the morehype and catcodes packages.

name: langcode

topics.details: macros that are independent of the (TeX) format in use
support for more than one (natural) language

caption: Index processor for LamsTeX

descriptions.text: This index processor deals with indexing commands from LamsTeX usage, only. An MS-DOS executable is provided.

name: lamstex-index

caption: Name languages and their genetic affiliations consistently

descriptions.text: This package attempts to make the typing of language names, codes, and families slightly easier by providing macros to access pre-defined language—code—family combinations from two important databases, as well as the possibility to create new combinations. It may be particularly useful for large, collaborative projects as well as typologically minded ones with a variety of language examples.

name: langnames

topics.details: macros for defining abbreviations in documents

caption: Typeset books for publication with Language Science Press

descriptions.text:
This package allows you to typeset monographs and edited volumes for publication with Language Science Press (http://www.langsci-press.org).

It includes all necessary files for title pages, frontmatter, main content, list of references and indexes. Dust jackets for BoD and Createspace (print-on-demand service providers) can also be produced.

name: langsci

caption: PDF drawing directly in TeX documents

descriptions.text:
The package provides the means to use PDF drawing primitives to produce high quality, colored graphics. It

  • uses Bézier curves (integral and rational) from degree one to seven,
  • allows TeX typesetting in the graphic,
  • offers most of the standard math functions,
  • allows plotting normal, parametric and polar functions.

The package has linear, logx, logy, logxy and polar grids with many specs;

  • it can rotate, clip and do many nice things easily
  • it has two looping commands for programming and many instructive example files.

The package requires pdfTeX but otherwise only depends on the calc package.

name: lapdf

topics.details: graphics produced by one of the *TeX engines

caption: Zero-width boxes for annotations, etc

descriptions.text:
Provides macros extends the \llap/\rlap set in Plain TeX:

  • \ulap and /dlap are up and down laps, in the same series as the originals;
  • \xlap and \ylap are laps in the horizontal and vertical directions, respectively, and
  • \zlap provides a box of zero dimensions in both axes, centred on its midpoint.

name: laps

topics.details: extensions to Plain TeX for higher-level constructs

caption: Record the number of citations in a document

descriptions.text: The package records the number of citations in a document, and provides a command (\LastBib) to print the number.

license.name: Do Not Sell Except by Arrangement

name: lastbib

caption: Collect and order authors and affiliations

descriptions.text:
This package provides a command \ResolveAffiliations, which collects author–affiliation pairs and outputs them according to the user configuration. The package uses LaTeX3 data types. It is aimed at class authors, i.e. maintainers of document templates in publishing houses, universities, etc. It is probably not that useful to document authors.

As of March 2021, this package is distributed as part of the langsci bundle.

name: langsci-affiliations

caption: Feature structures and attribute-value matrices (AVM)

descriptions.text:
A package for typesetting feature structures, also known as attribute-value matrices (AVMs), for use in linguistics.

The package provides a minimal and easy to read syntax. It depends only on the array package and can be placed almost everywhere, in particular in footnotes or graphs and tree structures. The package serves the same purpose as, Christopher Manning’s avm package, but shares no code base with that package.

name: langsci-avm

caption: Indicates the last loaded package

descriptions.text:
This package may be used to define the last point where some code shall be executed. Its provides a package name for use in package-placing commands from the author’s templatetools.

Usage examples are provided in the documentation.

name: lastpackage

topics.details: construction of a LaTeX document preamble

caption: Graphical LaTeX picture editor

descriptions.text: A graphical editor for drawings in the LaTeX picture environment. It runs under MS-DOS and MS-Windows. The distribution includes full sources, including LaTeX source for its documentation.

license.name: Do Not Sell Except by Arrangement

name: lated

topics.details: graphics editor whose output is good for TeX

caption: A near-WYSIWYG editor for LaTeX tables

descriptions.text:
A LaTeX table editor for Windows machines with the following features:

  • real-time LaTeX code preview;
  • limited clipboard support for import/export into other spreadsheet and text editors;
  • CSV support;
  • support for ‘tabular’, ‘array’ and custom environments;
  • custom column formats.

license.name: Do Not Sell Except by Arrangement

name: LaTable

topics.details: Read, process and convert CSV data
editor designed (or adapted) for use with (La)TeX

caption: A TeX macro package that defines LaTeX

descriptions.text:
LaTeX is a widely-used macro package for TeX, providing many basic document formating commands extended by a wide range of packages. It is a development of Leslie Lamport’s LaTeX 2.09, and superseded the older system in June 1994. The basic distribution is catalogued separately, at latex-base; apart from a large set of contributed packages and third-party documentation (elsewhere on the archive), the distribution includes:

– a bunch of required packages, which LaTeX authors are “entitled to assume” will be present on any system running LaTeX; and
– a minimal set of documentation detailing differences from the ‘old’ version of LaTeX in the areas of user commands, font selection and control, class and package writing, font encodings, configuration options and modification of LaTeX.

For downloading details, see the linked catalogue entries above.

name: latex

caption: Development pre-release of the LaTeX amsmath bundle

copyright.owner: The LaTeX Project and American Mathematical Society

descriptions.text: This is a pre-release version of the standard LaTeX amsmath bundle. It accompanies the pre-testing kernel code (latex-base-dev), and is intended for testing by knowledgeable users.

name: latex-amsmath-dev

caption: Reference last page for Page N of M type footers

descriptions.text: Reference the number of pages in your LaTeX document through the introduction of a new label which can be referenced like \pageref{LastPage} to give a reference to the last page of a document. It is particularly useful in the page footer that says: Page N of M.

name: lastpage

caption: AMS mathematical facilities for LaTeX

copyright.owner: LaTeX3 Project and American Mathematical Society

descriptions.text:
The package provides the principal packages in the AMS-LaTeX distribution. It adapts for use in LaTeX most of the mathematical features found in AMS-TeX; it is highly recommended as an adjunct to serious mathematical typesetting in LaTeX.

When amsmath is loaded, AMS-LaTeX packages amsbsy (for bold symbols), amsopn (for operator names) and amstext (for text embedded in mathematics) are also loaded.

amsmath is part of the LaTeX required distribution; however, several contributed packages add still further to its appeal; examples are empheq, which provides functions for decorating and highlighting mathematics, and ntheorem, for specifying theorem (and similar) definitions.

name: latex-amsmath

caption: Base sources of LaTeX

descriptions.text: This bundle comprises the source of LaTeX itself, together with several packages which are considered ‘part of the kernel’. This bundle, together with the required packages, constitutes what every LaTeX distribution should contain.

name: latex-base

caption: Examples for the book Bibliografien mit LaTeX

descriptions.text: The bundle provides a collection of files containing every example in the second edition of "Bibliografien mit LaTeX", by the package author.

name: latex-bib2-ex

topics.details: copies of examples from a published book

caption: Development pre-release of the LaTeX kernel

descriptions.text: This package provides a testing release for upcoming LaTeX2e kernel changes. Testing by the LaTeX team itself suggests that the code is stable and usable, but wider use by knowledgeable users is required by adding these changes to the release LaTeX kernel. Typically, the code here will be used by a TeX system to create dedicated formats, for example pdflatex-dev, which can then be used explicitly for testing.

name: latex-base-dev

caption: LaTeX macros for typing BNF specifications

descriptions.text: The package defines an environment grammar. The contents of the environment is a context-free grammar, and the environment will pretty-print it.

name: latex-bnf

caption: Examples for the book Bibliografien mit LaTeX

descriptions.text: The bundle provides a collection of files containing every example in the book “Bibliografien mit LaTeX” (ISBN 978-3865414151), by the package author.

name: latex-bib-ex

topics.details: copies of examples from a published book

caption: A publicity flyer for LaTeX

descriptions.text:
The document is designed as a publicity flyer for LaTeX, but also serves as an interesting showcase of what LaTeX can do.

The flyer is designed for printing, double-sided, on A3 paper, which would then be folded once.

name: LaTeX-brochure

caption: Legacy stub to allow loading pictex as m-pictex

descriptions.text:
m-pictex.sty was a wrapper for a ConTeXt module making picTeX more easily usable in classic TeX with no e-TeX extensions.

m-pictex.sty is here adjusted to be a stub loading pictex.sty. This has not been needed in LaTeX or ConTeXt for decades, but old documents may be using this name.

name: latex-context-ppchtex

topics.details: graphics produced by one of the *TeX engines
support for other packages or for drivers

caption: A LaTeX course as a projected presentation

descriptions.text: A brief Beamer-based slide presentation on LaTeX, based on Rupprecht's LaTeX 2.09 course, which the author has translated to English and taken to LaTeX2e/Beamer. Additional material was taken from the Short Introduction to LaTeX.

name: latex-course

caption: Support for Cyrillic fonts in LaTeX

descriptions.text:
This bundle of macros files provides macro support (including font encoding macros) for the use of Cyrillic characters in fonts encoded under the T2* and X2 encodings. These encodings cover (between them) pretty much every language that is written in a Cyrillic alphabet.

This directory is part of the LaTeX “required” distribution.

name: cyrillic

topics.details: support languages written using Cyrillic alphabets

caption: A direction-finder for LaTeX resources available online

descriptions.text:
A brief set of recommendations for users who need online documentation of LaTeX.

The document supports the need for documentation of LaTeX itself, in distributions. For example, it could be used in the command texdoc latex, in the TeX Live distribution.

name: latex-doc-ptr

caption: Documentation supplied as part of the LaTeX distribution

descriptions.text: A collection of documentation that is provided with LaTeX itself, listed in the latex-base package. Note that (apart from notices of releases) the documentation mostly covers changes and details of adaptations; there are no complete tutorials, such as you might find in the Not so short introduction or the Beginner’s guide.

name: latex-doc

caption: Errata for the LaTeX Manual

descriptions.text: These are all the errors and omissions to the manual, LaTeX: A Document Preparation System, second edition, published by Addison-Wesley, reported as of 18 Jan 2006.

documentation.details: Errata to the Second Edition of the LaTeX Manual

name: latex-errata

topics.details: lists of errata in published books

caption: Essential information for writing LaTeX documents

descriptions.text: A brief introduction to LaTeX2e.

name: latex-essential

caption: First aid for external LaTeX files and packages that need updating

descriptions.text:
This package contains some first aid for LaTeX packages or classes that require updates because of internal changes to the LaTeX kernel that are not yet reflected in the package’s or class’s code.

The file latex2e-first-aid-for-external-files.ltx provided by this package is meant to be loaded during format generation and not by the user.

name: latex-firstaid

topics.details: correct a problem, ahead of the “proper” fix

caption: Development pre-release of the LaTeX firstaid package

descriptions.text: This is a pre-release version of the standard LaTeX firstaid package. It accompanies the pre-testing kernel code (latex-base-dev), and is intended for testing by knowledgeable users.

name: latex-firstaid-dev

topics.details: correct a problem, ahead of the “proper” fix

caption: A tutorial aimed at introducing undergraduate students to LaTeX

descriptions.text: A tutorial aimed at introducing undergraduate students to LaTeX, including an introduction to LaTeX Workshop in Visual Studio Code and an example package of user-defined LaTeX commands.

name: latex-for-undergraduates

caption: Typeset git log information

descriptions.text:
The program is run within a git repository, and outputs the entire version history, as a LaTeX table.

That output will typically be redirected to a file; the author recommends typesetting in landscape orientation.

license.name: GNU General Public License, version 3 or newer

name: latex-git-log

caption: A collection of fonts used in LaTeX distributions

descriptions.text:
This is a collection of fonts for use with standard LaTeX packages and classes. It includes ‘invisible’ fonts (for use with the slides class), line and circle fonts (for use in the picture environment) and ‘LaTeX symbol’ fonts.

For full support of a LaTeX installation, some Computer Modern font variants cmbsy(6-9), cmcsc(8,9), cmex(7-9) and cmmib(5-9) from the amsfonts distribution, are also necessary.

The fonts are available as Metafont source, and metric (tfm) files are also provided. Most of the fonts are also available in Adobe Type 1 format, in the amsfonts distribution.

name: latex-fonts

topics.details: fonts that provide collections of symbols

caption: The LaTeX standard graphics bundle

descriptions.text:
This is a collection of LaTeX packages for:

  • producing colour
  • including graphics (eg PostScript) files
  • rotation and scaling of text

in LaTeX documents.

It comprises the packages color, graphics, graphicx, trig, epsfig, keyval, and lscape.

name: latex-graphics

caption: Development pre-release of the LaTeX graphics bundle

descriptions.text: This is a pre-release version of the standard LaTeX graphics bundle. It accompanies the pre-testing kernel code (latex-base-dev), and is intended for testing by knowledgeable users.

name: latex-graphics-dev

caption: A VMS help file for LaTeX 2.09

descriptions.text:
The file is a replacement for the LaTeX help file in the VMS help library. It derives from the DECUS help file, with the LaTeX command strings copied to a higher level.

The file dates from 1993, so the information is all related to LaTeX 2.09.

name: latex-hlp

caption: LaTeX laboratory

descriptions.text:
This bundle holds optional files that are loaded in certain situations by kernel code (if available). While this code is still in development and the use is experimental, it is stored outside the format so that there can be intermediate releases not affecting the production use of LaTeX.

Once the code is finalized and properly tested it will eventually move to the kernel and the corresponding file in this bundle will vanish.

Note that none of these files are directly user accessible in documents (i.e., they aren’t packages), so the process is transparent to documents already using the new functionality.

name: latex-lab

caption: Unofficial reference manual for LaTeX

descriptions.text:
An unofficial reference manual covering LaTeX 2e.

The Texinfo source was originally derived from the VMS help file in the DECUS TeX distribution of 1990, with many subsequent changes. All the other formats are derived from the Texinfo source, as usual.

This package is now stale. Please refer to latex2e-help-texinfo instead.

name: latex-info

caption: LaTeX laboratory: Development pre-release

descriptions.text: This package provides a testing release for upcoming changes to the latex-lab bundle, which provides a route for additions to the LaTeX kernel to be stablised. It accompanies the pre-testing kernel code (latex-base-dev), and is intended for testing by knowledgeable users.

name: latex-lab-dev

caption: Easy compiling of complex (and simple) LaTeX documents

descriptions.text:
This package provides several tools that aim to simplify the compilation of LaTeX documents:

  • LaTeX.mk: a Makefile snippet to help compiling LaTeX documents in DVI, PDF, PS, … format. Dependencies are automatically tracked: one should be able to compile documents with a one-line Makefile containing 'include LaTeX.mk'. Complex documents (with multiple bibliographies, indexes, glossaries, …) should be correctly managed.
  • figlatex.sty: a LaTeX package to easily insert xfig figures (with \includegraphics{file.fig}). It can interact with LaTeX.mk so that the latter automatically invokes transfig if needed.
  • And various helper tools for LaTeX.mk

This package requires GNUmake (>= 3.81).

name: latex-make

caption: A practical guide to LaTeX and Polyglossia for Marathi and other Indian languages

descriptions.text: The package provides a short guide to LaTeX and specifically to the polyglossia package. This document aims to introduce LaTeX and polyglossia for Indian languages. Though the document often discusses the language Marathi, the discussion applies to other India languages also, with some minute changes which are described in Section 1.2. We assume that the user of this document knows basic (La)TeX or has, at least, tried her hand on it. This document is not very suitable for first time users.

name: latex-mr

topics.details: support for languages of the Indian subcontinent

caption: Calculate LaTeX settings for any font and paper size

descriptions.text:
The package is a Python script, whose typical use is when preparing printed material for users with low vision. The most effective way of doing this is to print on (notional) small paper, and then to magnify the result; the script calculates the settings for various font and paper sizes.

More details are to be read in the script itself.

name: latex-papersize

topics.details: layout of objects on the page

caption: Chinese Introduction to TeX and LaTeX

descriptions.text: The document is an introduction to TeX/LaTeX, in Chinese. It covers basic text typesetting, mathematics, graphics, tables, Chinese language & fonts, and some miscellaneous features (hyperlinks, long documents, bibliographies, indexes and page layout).

name: latex-notes-zh-cn

caption: LaTeX for pragmatists

descriptions.text: Prakticky pojatý úvod do LaTeXu v češtině. Od úplných základů přes pokročilejší konstrukce (tabulky, matematické vzorce) až po vybrané rozšiřující balíčky (sazba do sloupců, barva).

An introduction to LaTeX from the practical point of view. From the bare essentials over more complex constructs (tables, mathematics) up to selected packages (multicolumn typesetting, color).

Written in Czech language.

name: latex-pro-pragmatiky

caption: Examples from the book "LaTeX Referenz"

descriptions.text:
This bundle contains all the examples, as source, eps and pdf, of the author’s book “LaTeX Referenz” (2nd ed.), published by DANTE/Lehmanns.

The examples can be run, using the example class (ttctexa.cls) in the distribution.

name: LaTeX-Referenz

topics.details: copies of examples from a published book

caption: LaTeX Reference Sheet for a thesis with KOMA-Script

descriptions.text: This LaTeX Reference Sheet is for writing a thesis using the KOMA-Script document classes (scrartcl, scrreprt, scrbook) and all the packages needed for a thesis in natural sciences.

name: latex-refsheet

caption: (Xe)LaTeX Appliqué aux sciences humaines

descriptions.text: The package provides a published book (in French); the book is also available on paper.

name: latex-sciences-humaines

topics.details: support for studies in the humanities

caption: LaTeX Tabellen

descriptions.text: The examples from the book «Tabellen mit LaTeX», 2nd ed.

name: latex-tabellen

topics.details: copies of examples from a published book

caption: The LaTeX standard tools bundle

descriptions.text: A collection of (variously) simple tools provided as part of the LaTeX required tools distribution, comprising the packages: afterpage, array, bm, calc, dcolumn, delarray, enumerate, fileerr, fontsmpl, ftnright, hhline, indentfirst, layout, longtable, multicol, rawfonts, shellesc, showkeys, somedefs, tabularx, theorem, trace, varioref, verbatim, xr, and xspace.

name: latex-tools

caption: Development pre-release of the LaTeX tools bundle

descriptions.text: This is a pre-release version of the standard LaTeX tools bundle. It accompanies the pre-testing kernel code (latex-base-dev), and is intended for testing by knowledgeable users.

name: latex-tools-dev

caption: A structured copy of the LaTeX distribution

descriptions.text:
This bundle provides a set of zip file modules containing TDS-compliant trees for items of the LaTeX distribution (both the base system and required packages), together with ‘user-friendly’ documentation (PDF files with navigation support using bookmarks and links).

A further module (knuth) performs the same service for Knuth’s software distribution.

This bundle has been moved to the /obsolete branch of the archive as of April 2020 because the LaTeX files are now very much out of date.

name: LaTeX-tds

caption: Universal inputenc, fontenc, and babel for pdfLaTeX and LuaLaTeX

descriptions.text: This package provides a LaTeX style file which makes it easy to use input encoding (UTF-8 by default, can be changed), fontspec.sty (optional), font encoding (T1 if fontspec.sty is not used), babel (English language by default), hyphenation, underline (with soul.sty), default text and math fonts (Computer Modern or Times), and paper sizes correctly with both pdfLaTeX and LuaLaTeX.

name: latex-uni8

topics.details: input encoding support for TeX engines
Unicode, material supporting it, and packages requiring it

caption: The Very Short Guide to LaTeX

descriptions.text: This is a 4-page reminder of what LaTeX does. It is designed for printing on A4 paper, double-sided, and folding once to A5. Such an ‘imposed’ version of the document is provided in the distribution, as PDF. An analogous version is provided in ‘legal’ format.

documentation.details: The document itself, imposed for 1 sheet of A4 paper

name: LaTeX-veryshortguide

caption: A LaTeX course written in brazilian portuguese language

descriptions.text: This is a LaTeX2e course written in brazilian portuguese language.

license.name: GNU General Public License, version 2 or newer

name: latex-via-exemplos

caption: Old, unsupported, LaTeX

descriptions.text:
The distribution of LaTeX 2.09 was last updated in 1993. A copy is kept for its possible historical interest: it is not recommended for current use—all current distributions provide LaTeX 2e (now known simply as ‘LaTeX’. Bug fixes, when they arise, are applied to current LaTeX, not to LaTeX 2.09.

A large number of packages were contributed for use with LaTeX 2.09, and while many have been discarded or converted for use with current LaTeX, a significant number await classification.

name: latex209

caption: A French translation of “latex2e-help-texinfo”

descriptions.text: This package provides a complete French translation of latex2e-help-texinfo.

name: latex2e-help-texinfo-fr

caption: Unofficial reference manual covering LaTeX2e

descriptions.text:
The manual is provided as Texinfo source (which was originally derived from the VMS help file in the DECUS TeX distribution of 1990, with many subsequent changes). This is a collaborative development, and details of getting involved are to be found on the package home page. A Spanish translation is included here, and a French translation is available as a separate package.

All the other formats in the distribution are derived from the Texinfo source, as usual.

name: latex2e-help-texinfo

caption: A reference for LaTeX in HTML

descriptions.text: The HTML hyper-document provides a thorough (though slightly dated) discussion of LaTeX 2e.

name: latex2e-reference

caption: Translate LaTeX-based manual pages into Unix man format

descriptions.text:
Latex2man is a tool to translate UNIX manual pages written with LaTeX into the troff format understood by the UNIX man(1) command. Alternatively HTML, TexInfo, or LaTeX code can be produced too. Output of parts of the text may be supressed using the conditional text feature (for this, LaTeX generation may be used).

There is a LaTeX package (latex2man.sty) for writing the man page and a Perl script (latex2man) that does the actual translation.

name: latex2man

topics.details: convert TeX-ish sources to some other markup (than HTML)

caption: Write data to file in Python literal format

descriptions.text: This package writes data to file using Python literal syntax. The data may be loaded safely in Python using the ast.literal_eval() function or the latex2pydata Python package. The data can also be hashed within LaTeX (mdfivesum) so that it is possible to check for the existence of external cached content generated with the data.

name: latex2pydata

caption: Convert LaTeX into HTML documents

descriptions.text:
A Perl program that translates LaTeX into HTML (HyperText Markup Language), optionally creating separate HTML files corresponding to each unit (e.g., section) of the document.

LaTeX2HTML proceeds by interpreting LaTeX (to the best of its abilities). It contains definitions from a wide variety of classes and packages, and users may add further definitions by writing Perl scripts that provide information about class/package commands.

name: latex2html

caption: Convert LaTeX source to Braille with math in Nemeth

descriptions.text:
After many failed attempts to transcribe real math notes and books to Braille/Nemeth in order to deal with a real situation (blind student in Math Dept.), we decided to develop a new program that follows a direct, from LaTeX to Braille/Nemeth, approach.

Our main target was the Greek language which is only Braille level 1, but English at level 1 is supported as well. Simple pictures in PSTricks are also supported in order to produce tactile graphics with specialized equipment.

Note that embossing will need LibreOffice and odt2braille as this project does not deal with embossers’ drivers.

What’s new in version 1.1

In this version, the support of the user level commands of the amsmath package was added, as described in its user guide, with the exception of commutative diagrams (amscd package) as well as structures that are irrelevant to visually impared persons.

Also, the Unicode mathematics symbols of the unicode-math package that are represented by the Nemeth code are now supported by latex2nemeth.

We would like to acknowledge support by the TUGfund for this project (TUGfund project 33).

name: Latex2Nemeth

topics.details: convert TeX-ish sources to some other markup (than HTML)

caption: Convert LaTeX into Rich Text Format

descriptions.text: Translates LaTeX text into RTF (Rich Text Format as used by Microsoft Word and the like). Graphics and tables are converted as are cross references and the bibliography; many packages are supported (in whole or as implementation of a subset of their commands) — for example, the whole of natbib is implemented.

name: latex2rtf

topics.details: convert TeX-ish sources to some other markup (than HTML)

caption: A much enhanced LaTeX mode for the Jed editor

descriptions.text: This S-Lang file for the Jed editor provides a much enhanced LaTeX mode in the fashion of AUC TeX: menus, shortcuts, templates, syntax highlighting, document outline, integrated debugging,symbol completion, full integration with external programs, and more. It was designed with both the beginner and the advanced LaTeX user in mind.

name: latex4jed

topics.details: plug-ins for editors, for better (La)TeX and Meta* support

caption: LaTeX guide for word processor users, in Italian

descriptions.text: The package provides a version of the document in Italian

name: latex4wp-it

caption: A guide for combining LaTeX and music

descriptions.text: This guide, “LaTeX for Musicians”, explains how to create LaTeX documents that include several kinds of music elements: music symbols, song lyrics, guitar chords diagrams, lead sheets, music excerpts, guitar tablatures, multi-page scores.

name: LaTeX4Musicians

caption: Embed Mathematica code and plots into LaTeX

descriptions.text:
This LaTeX package allows you to embed and execute your Wolfram Language (Mathematica) source code in a LaTeX document. When the document is compiled, the computation results will be inserted into the compiled file. In addition to general Wolfram Language computations it is also quite easy to generate plots or animations with this package. Moreover, all the embedded code can be executed either locally (via locally installed Mathematica) or on the cloud (via Wolfram Cloud).

The main features of this package are somewhat similar to SageTeX, but here we use Wolfram Language (Mathematica) instead of Sage.

The package is heavily inspired by LaTeX-Alpha, which also explains the name “latexalpha2”. Unfortunately, LaTeX-Alpha has been down for a while. The objective of latexalpha2 is to replace LaTeX-Alpha and at the same time provide various new features.

name: latexalpha2

topics.details: call external code and process the result

caption: A LaTeX guide specifically designed for word processor users

descriptions.text: “LaTeX for Word Processor Users” is a guide that helps converting knowledge and techniques of word processing into the LaTeX typesetting environment. It aims at helping WP users use LaTeX instead.

name: LaTeX4WP

caption: Enhanced LaTeX integration for Bangla

descriptions.text:
This package simplifies the process of writing Bangla in LaTeX and addresses most of the associated typesetting issues.

Notable features:

  • Automated transition from Bangla to English and vice versa.
  • Patch for the unproportionate whitespace issue in popular Bangla fonts.
  • Full support for all the common commands and environments.
  • Bangla numbering for page, section, chapter, footnotes etc. (extending polyglossia's support).
  • New theorem, problems, example, solution and other environments, all of which are in Bangla.

name: latexbangla

topics.details: support for languages of the Indian subcontinent

caption: Bug-classification for LaTeX related bugs

descriptions.text: The package is written in order to help identifying the rightful addressee for a bug report. The LaTeX team asks that it will be loaded in any test file that is intended to be sent to the LaTeX bug database as part of a bug report.

name: latexbug

caption: A LaTeX cheat sheet

descriptions.text: A LaTeX reference sheet for writing scientific papers. Unlike many other such sheets, this sheet does not focus on typesetting mathematics (though it does list some symbols).

name: latexcheat

caption: A CAD drawing package
name: latexcad

topics.details: graphics generator whose output is good for use with TeX

caption: A LaTeX cheat sheet, in Brazilian Portuguese

descriptions.text: This is a translation to Brazilian Portuguese of Winston Chang’s LaTeX cheat sheet

name: latexcheat-ptbr

caption: A LaTeX cheat sheet, in German

descriptions.text:
This is a translation to German of Winston Chang’s LaTeX cheat sheet (a reference sheet for writing scientific papers).

It has been adapted to German standards using the KOMA script document classes.

name: latexcheat-de

caption: A LaTeX cheat sheet, in Spanish

descriptions.text: This is a translation to Spanish (Castellano) of Winston Chang’s LaTeX cheat sheet (a reference sheet for writing scientific papers).

name: latexcheat-esmx

caption: Use color definitions from latexcolor.com

descriptions.text: Built on top of the xcolor package, the latexcolors package defines the set of colors shown on latexcolor.com for use in documents typeset with LaTeX & friends.

name: latexcolors

caption: Perl script to count words of LaTeX documents

descriptions.text: The latexcount script gives a reasonably accurate count of the number of words in the main text of an article, the number of words in footnotes, and the number of words total. The list of tags that don't get counted can be extended as needed.

name: latexcount

caption: Demonstrate LaTeX code with its resulting output

descriptions.text: The package provides configurable tools to print out LaTeX code and the resulting output in the same document. It also supports printing the result inside a conditional sequence; thus one may suppress printing if the code would not compile.

name: latexdemo

topics.details: print (La)TeX code verbatim alongside the rendered result

caption: A LaTeX course book

descriptions.text: The package provides the book and practice files for a LaTeX course that the author has give several times at the Rijksuniversiteit Groningen (Netherlands).

name: latexcourse-rug

caption: CAD oriented drawing program

descriptions.text: An X-Windows based CAD orientated drawing program which generates LaTeX output using latexdraw.sty, based on pstricks. The picture may be generated as complete LaTeX-source or as a picture-environment to be included in other documents. You must translate the dvi-file generated by LaTeX to a PostScript-file using dvips before you can view or print the document.

name: latexdraw

topics.details: package using PStricks for graphical output
graphics produced by one of the *TeX engines

caption: Determine and mark up significant differences between LaTeX files

descriptions.text: Latexdiff is a Perl script for visual mark up and revision of significant differences between two LaTeX files. Various options are available for visual markup using standard LaTeX packages such as color. Changes not directly affecting visible text, for example in formatting commands, are still marked in the LaTeX source. A rudimentary revision facilility is provided by another Perl script, latexrevise, which accepts or rejects all changes. Manual editing of the difference file can be used to override this default behaviour and accept or reject selected changes only.

name: latexdiff

topics.details: support for keeping track of document development

caption: Integrates LaTeX and SQL databases

descriptions.text: LaTeXDB brings together LaTeX and a MySQL database. You can use SQL queries in your LaTeX document and loop over the result sets creating tables, serial letters, and other stuff.

name: LaTeXDB

caption: A comparison of packages showing LaTeX file information

descriptions.text:
The package provides an HTML file that lists and compares CTAN packages that display LaTeX source file information from \ProvidesClass, \ProvidesFile, and \ProvidesPackage commands in the LaTeX file.

Five packages of the author’s, and several other packages are discussed; revision control systems are mentioned briefly.

name: latexfileinfo-pkgs

topics.details: document reviewing subjects relevant for TeX users

caption: Prints the version and date of a LaTeX class or style file

descriptions.text:
This simple shell script prints the version and date of a LaTeX class or style file.

Syntax: latexfileversion <file>

This programme handles style files (extension .sty), class files (extension .cls), and other TeX input files. The file extension must be given.

name: latexfileversion

caption: Texinfo for LaTeX 2.09

descriptions.text:
A LaTeX 2.09 extension of texinfo, together with Emacs 18 elisp support files (“manual generator” commands).

While the package showed some promise, it hasn't been followed up to current LaTeX or current Emacs.

name: latexinfo

topics.details: macros and tools for preparing documentation

caption: LaTeX Makefile

descriptions.text:
This is a generic Makefile for use with make(1), to create output from a LaTeX file. It will run the designated LaTeX FILE through TeX in turn until all cross-references are resolved, building all indices. The directory containing each FILE is searched for included files.

Latexmake can also generate .pdf, .html, .txt or .rtf files.

name: latexmake

caption: Indent a LaTeX document, highlighting the programming structure

descriptions.text:
The Perl script processes a LaTeX file, indenting parts so as to highlight the structure for the reader.

Included are also binary (executable) files for Windows, Ubuntu Linux, and macOS.

name: latexindent

topics.details: improve the appearance of LaTeX code

caption: A LaTeX git wrapper

descriptions.text:
This package provides several macros to fetch git information and typeset it.

The macros defined by LaTeXgit can be helpful to documentation authors and others to whom clear document versioning is important.

name: LaTeXgit

topics.details: support for keeping track of document development

caption: Fully automated LaTeX document generation

descriptions.text:
Latexmk completely automates the process of generating a LaTeX document. Given the source files for a document, latexmk issues the appropriate sequence of commands to generate a .dvi, .ps, .pdf or hardcopy version of the document.

An important feature is the “preview continuous mode”, where the script watches all of the source files (primary file and included TeX and graphics files), and reruns LaTeX, etc., whenever a source file has changed. Thus a previewer can offer a display of the document’s latest state.

name: latexmk

caption: An integrated development environment for Windows

descriptions.text:
LaTexMng is an easy to use integrated development environment for Windows. The application integrates all the tools needed for the creation of LaTeX documents, under Windows 2000, XP or later editions of MS Windows.

LaTexMng is distributed as LaTexMngSetup.exe. Run LaTexMngSetup.exe and simply follow the on-screen instructions to install LaTexMng. A free 30 day trial licence is offered.

name: LaTexMng

caption: Interface for LaTeX-based typesetting in MetaPost

descriptions.text: The MetaPost package latexMP implements a user-friendly interface to access LaTeX-based typesetting capabilities in MetaPost. The text to be typeset is given as string. This allows even dynamic text elements, for example counters, to be used in labels. Compared to other implementations it is much more flexible, since it can be used as direct replacement for btex.etex, and much faster, compared for example to the solution provided by tex.mp.

name: latexMP

caption: Expand \input and \include in a LaTeX document

descriptions.text: Latexpand is a Perl script that simply replaces \input and \include commands with the content of the input or included file. The script does not deal with \includeonly commands.

name: latexpand

caption: LaTeX picture editor for Windows

descriptions.text: LaTeXPiX is a picture editor for LaTeX and works on all Microsoft Windows versions. LaTeXPiX offers advanced picture drawing, editing and generation beyond the scope of most other available editors. Features include: drawing and resizing squares and circles; show the bounding box of inserted images; Polish and Japanese translations.

name: LaTeXPiX

topics.details: graphics editor whose output is good for TeX

caption: Run LaTeX as many times as needed

descriptions.text: A csh script to run LaTeX as many times as needed (and hopefully no more) on a given file to resolve cross references, and to ensure that the table of contents and index (if any) are up-to-date.

name: latexn

caption: LaTeX release emulation

descriptions.text:
This package provides both forward and backward compatibility of the LaTeX kernel, i.e. older kernels can be made to behave like a current one (if you have a current latexrelease but an old format) and a current kernel can be asked to emulate an older kernel version.

The package is part of the LaTeX distribution.

name: latexrelease

caption: Use LaTeX in PHP programs

descriptions.text: LatexRender is a set of scripts that allows one to call LaTeX from PHP programs; in particular, this allows users to enter LaTeX commands in a forum and, on posting, have it replaced by a suitable gif or png. LatexRender requires LaTeX and ImageMagick to be installed. The open source PHP code was originally designed for use with phpBB, but it can be adapted for use with other PHP programs. Details and example installations may be found in the maintainer's home page.

name: LatexRender

topics.details: support for LaTeX(-alike) on the web, or feeding into other applications

caption: Multifunctional editor for LaTeX

descriptions.text: LaTeX WIDE is an editor for use under Windows, which has low impact on the Windows system, yet offers rich functionality for the user; in particular, help is available both in English and in Russian.

name: LaTeX-WIDE

topics.details: editor designed (or adapted) for use with (La)TeX

caption: Latin language definition for Babel

descriptions.text:
This is an interim release of a new version of the Latin language definition for Babel. It can be used to replace the Latin support already present in Babel.

The ecclesiastic package may be used to adjust the packages settings for use with Christian sacred text.

name: latin

topics.details: extra language ‘drivers’ for existing multilingual packages
support for typesetting Latin (ancient, medieval and ‘modern’)

caption: Create the header of a LaTeX document

descriptions.text: A tool to create the header of a LaTeX document. It guides you within a few steps through the more or less important options and packages.

name: latexwizard

topics.details: editor designed (or adapted) for use with (La)TeX

caption: Inputenc encoding for verbatim ISO 8859-1 use

descriptions.text:
A definition file for the inputenc package, in which all characters from ISO/IEC 8859-1 (ISO Latin-1) are loaded as text characters. This allows verbatim setting of Latin-1 encoded files.

The file is part of Jörg Knappen’s collection.

name: latin1jk

topics.details: input encoding support for TeX engines

caption: LaTeX support for documents written in Peano’s Interlingua

descriptions.text:
Latino sine Flexione (or Interlingua) is a language constructed by Giuseppe Peano at the beginning of the last century. This simplified Latin is designed to be an instrument for international cooperation, especially in the academic sphere. (Note that this “Interlingua” is different from the “Interlingua” that was created a few decades after Peano’s work and which is supported by babel-interlingua!)

This package provides the necessary translations to use the language within a LaTeX document. It also imports fontenc in order to be able to use ligatures and quotation marks.

Finally, it offers a text in Interlingua that can be used as a dummy text: Fundamento de intelligentia. This article by H. Bijlsma was first published in Schola et Vita Anno I (1926).

name: latino-sine-flexione

caption: Inputenc encoding for verbatim ISO 8859-3 use

descriptions.text:
A definition file for the inputenc package, in which all characters from ISO/IEC 8859-3 (ISO Latin-3) are loaded as text characters. This allows verbatim setting of Latin-3 encoded files.

The file is part of Jörg Knappen’s collection.

name: latin3jk

topics.details: input encoding support for TeX engines

caption: Inputenc encoding for verbatim ISO 8859-2 use

descriptions.text:
A definition file for the inputenc package, in which all characters from ISO/IEC 8859-2 (ISO Latin-2) are loaded as text characters. This allows verbatim setting of Latin-2 encoded files.

The file is part of Jörg Knappen’s collection.

name: latin2jk

topics.details: input encoding support for TeX engines

caption: Lato font family and LaTeX support

descriptions.text:
Lato is a sanserif typeface family designed in the Summer 2010 by Warsaw-based designer Łukasz Dziedzic for the tyPoland foundry. This font, which includes five weights (hairline, light, regular, bold and black), is available from the Google Font Directory as TrueType files under the Open Font License version 1.1.

The package provides support for this font in LaTeX. It includes the original TrueType fonts, as well as Type 1 versions, converted for this package using FontForge for full support with Dvips.

name: lato

topics.details: font available in Adobe Type 1 format

caption: A package to improve the A4 page layout

descriptions.text: This package produces a wide page layout for documents that use A4 paper size. Moreover, LayAureo provides both a simple hook for leaving an empty space which is required if pages are bundled by a press binding (use option binding=length), and an option called big which it forces typearea to become maximum.

name: Layaureo

topics.details: layout of objects on the page

caption: View the layout of a document

descriptions.text:
The package defines a command \layout, which will show a summary of the layout of the current document.

This package is part of the latex-tools bundle in the LaTeX required distribution.

name: layout

caption: Lowercased (spaced) small capitals

descriptions.text:
This little package serves the purpose of providing a uniform method to use lowercased small capitals and spaced lowercased small capitals.

It relies on the iftex, textcase, and microtype packages and comes with four new user macros: \textlcc, the main feature: lowercased small capitals; \spacedcaps, a prefix to small capitals text commands to slightly increase their spacing; \textslcc and \textssc, which are shortcuts for \spacedcaps\textlcc and \spacedcaps\textsc (accordingly).

name: lccaps

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other font support

caption: Display various elements of a document's layout

descriptions.text: Display information about a document, including: text positioning on a page; disposition of floats; layout of paragraphs, lists, footnotes, table of contents, and sectional headings; font boxes. Facilities are provided for a document designer to experiment with the layout parameters.

name: layouts

caption: Lists in TeX’s “mouth”

descriptions.text:
The package was developed to provide flexible lists, whose ordering can be altered on the fly.

The implementation involves a pile of lambda-calculus and list-handling macros of an incredibly obtuse nature. The TUGboat paper serves as a manual for the macros.

Having said all of which, confidence is enhanced by the knowledge that the TeX code was formally verified.

name: lazylist

caption: Examples from “Der LaTeX Begleiter”

descriptions.text: The source of the examples printed in the book, together with necessary supporting files. The book was published by Addison-Wesley, 2005, ISBN 3-8273-7166-X.

name: lb2-examples

topics.details: copies of examples from a published book

caption: A bundle of outline font manipulation tools

descriptions.text:
This bundle of tools comprises:

  • Cfftot1, which translates a Compact Font Format (CFF) font, or a PostScript-flavored OpenType font, into PostScript Type 1 format. It correctly handles subroutines and hints;
  • Mmafm and mmpfb, which create instances of multiple-master fonts (mmafm and mmpfb were previously distributed in their own package, mminstance);
  • Otfinfo, which reports information about OpenType fonts, such as the features they support and the contents of their ‘size’ optical size features;
  • Otftotfm, which creates TeX font metrics and encodings that correspond to a PostScript-flavored OpenType font. It will interpret glyph positionings, substitutions, and ligatures as far as it is able. You can say which OpenType features should be activated;
  • T1dotlessj, creates a Type 1 font whose only character is a dotless j matching the input font’s design;
  • T1lint, which checks a Type 1 font for correctness;
  • T1reencode, which replaces a font’s internal encoding with one you specify; and
  • T1testpage, which creates a PostScript proof for a Type 1 font. It is preliminary software.

name: LCDF-typetools

topics.details: support for font development, testing and characterisation

caption: Alphanumerical LCD-style displays

descriptions.text: A LaTeX package that will display text as on an (early) LCD display (the output is very visibly pixellated). Assumes 8-bit input in its internal verbatim-style environment.

name: lcd

topics.details: graphics produced by one of the *TeX engines

caption: Define leading with a length

descriptions.text: The package defines a command \leading, whose argument is a <length> that specifies the nominal distance between consecutive baselines of typeset text. The command replaces the rather more difficult LaTeX command \linespread{<ratio>}, where the leading is specified by reference to the font size.

name: leading

topics.details: layout of objects on the page
support for variations of typographic style

caption: Generate random integers

descriptions.text: The lcg package generates random numbers (integers) via a linear congruential generator (Schrage’s method). The random numbers are written to a counter. The keyval package is used for the user to provide values for the range and a seed, and for the name of the counter to be used.

name: lcg

caption: Make Classic Cyrillic CM fonts accessible in LaTeX

descriptions.text: The package makes the classic CM Cyrillic fonts accessible for use with LaTeX.

name: lcyw

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other font support

caption: Typesetting leadsheets and songbooks

descriptions.text: This LaTeX package offers support for typesetting simple leadsheets of songs, i.e. song lyrics and the corresponding chords.

name: leadsheets

topics.details: chord notations, as for song books

caption: Circuit symbols for use in LaTeX picture mode

descriptions.text: The set includes all basic logic gates in four orientations, FETs, power supply pins, transmission gates, capacitors, resistors and wiring T-junctions.

name: lcircuit

topics.details: graphics produced by one of the *TeX engines

caption: A script for marking the differences between two LaTeX files

descriptions.text: The Ldiff (LaTeX diff) script takes two LaTeX (or LyX) files as input and generate a PostScript file that contains the changes between the two files: Text that appears in both files is shown in black, text that appears only in the first file is shown in red and is crossed out, and text that appears only in the second file is shown in blue. Note that in some cases, Ldiff will not give correct results.

name: ldiff

caption: Create small handouts (flyers)

descriptions.text:
A document class to create small hand-outs (flyers) that fit on a single sheet of paper which is then folded twice. Pages are rearranged by LaTeX so that they print correctly on a single sheet — no external script is necessary. (Works with PostScript and PDF.)

This is a complete reimplementation with permission of the original author Jürgen Schlegelmilch.

name: leaflet

topics.details: layout of objects on the page

caption: On-screen presentations for (almost) all formats

descriptions.text:
The package creates slides for on-screen presentations based on PDF features without manipulating TeX’s typesetting process. The presentation flow relies on PDF’s abilities to display content step by step.

Features include:

  • Free positioning of anything anywhere in painted areas on the slide, as well as in the main textblock;
  • Numerous attributes to control the layout and the presentation flow, from TeX's primitive dimensions to the visibility of steps;
  • Feature inheritance from global to local settings, with intermediate types;
  • Basic drawing facilities to produce symbols, e.g., for list items or buttons;
  • Colours, transparency, shades, and pictures;
  • Navigation with links, pop-up menus, and customizable bookmarks;
  • Easy switch between presentation and handout; and
  • PDF transitions.

Besides the traditional documentation, the distribution includes visual documentation and six demo presentations ranging from geometric abstraction to classic style to silly video game.

Lecturer is designed to work with all formats, but presently fails with ConTeXt MkIV (because of clashes in management of PDF objects, probably), works only with pdfTeX and LuaTeX for the time being, and requires texapi and yax, both v.1.02.

name: lecturer

caption: LaTeX support for use of ITC Leawood font family

descriptions.text: The package provides all of the files needed to make the ITC Leawood font available to TeX and LaTeX. Note that the font itself is not freely available; the leawood package assumes you have already purchased ITC Leawood.

name: leawood

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other font support

caption: Write your articles in a colorful way

descriptions.text:
This package provides a LaTeX class for typesetting articles with a colorful design.

Currently, it has native support for Chinese (simplified and traditional), English, French, German, Italian, Japanese, Portuguese (European and Brazilian), Russian and Spanish typesetting. It compiles with either XeLaTeX or LuaLaTeX.

This is part of the colorist class series and depends on colorist.sty from the colorist package.

The package name “lebhart” is taken from the German word “lebhaft” (“vivid”), combined with the first three letters of “Artikel” (“article”).

name: lebhart

topics.details: support for more than one (natural) language
LaTeX article classes and their developments

caption: A document class for quickly drafting nice looking lecture notes

descriptions.text: This LaTeX documentclass provides a number of gimmicks to draft nice looking lecture notes, such as a number of theorem environments, automatic spacing and alignment of figures and much more. More information is available in the package readme.

name: lectures

topics.details: support for teachers and teaching administrators

caption: Combine single PDF files into one file

descriptions.text: This package makes it easy to combine and index individual PDF files into one large PDF file.

name: lectureslides

caption: An environment for LaTeX document development

descriptions.text:
LEd (LaTeX Editor) is a free environment for rapid TeX/LaTeX document processing.

LEd includes a project manager, a powerful editor, an integrated spellchecker and thesaurus, a built-in DVI viewer, descriptive hints for LaTeX commands, a code completion mechanism, a multilingual environment, and more.

name: LEd

topics.details: editor designed (or adapted) for use with (La)TeX

caption: Typeset scholarly editions in arabic

descriptions.text:
Ledarab extends the ledmac package for typesetting texts in the Arabic script, as implemented by ArabTeX.

Ledarab is distributed with ledmac and another related package ledpar.

name: ledarab

caption: Typeset scholarly editions

descriptions.text:
A macro package for typesetting scholarly critical editions. The ledmac package is a LaTeX port of the plain TeX EDMAC macros. It supports indexing by page and line number and simple tabular- and array-style environments.

The package is distributed with the related ledpar and ledarab packages.

The package is now superseded by reledmac.

name: ledmac

caption: Left and right subscripts and superscripts in math mode

descriptions.text: Left and right subscripts and superscripts are automatically raised for better fitting to the symbol they belong to.

name: leftidx

topics.details: position sub- and superscripts (left and right sides)

caption: Typeset scholarly editions in parallel texts

descriptions.text:
Ledpar provides parallel-text typesetting (either in parallel columns, or on opposing pages), for the ledmac package.

Ledpar is distributed with ledmac and with another related package ledarab.

name: ledpar

caption: Left indices with better spacing

descriptions.text: This package provides commands for typesetting left indices. Unlike other similar packages, leftindex also indents the left superscript, providing much better spacing in general.

name: leftindex

topics.details: position sub- and superscripts (left and right sides)

caption: Typeset and index linguistic gloss abbreviations

descriptions.text: The leipzig package provides a set of macros for standard glossing abbreviations, with options to create new ones. They are mnemonic (e.g. \Acc{} for accusative, abbreviated acc). These abbre can be used alone or on top of the glossaries package for easy indexing and glossary printing.

name: leipzig

caption: A letter class for Leiden University

descriptions.text:
This package is a LaTeX implementation of the business letter formatting that is used at Leiden University, using the institute graphic identity as specified on www.leidenuniv.nl.

The LEIletter class is an extension of the standard KOMA-script letter class scrlttr2. It is intended to be used for writing business letters. It is compliant to the house style and allows for using windowed envelopes of the DL format, with right-aligned window.

The class requires and uses the following packages that are part of most modern LaTeX distributions: graphicx, ifthen, array, babel, ragged2e, hyperref, textcase, microtype, scrlayer-scrpage, geometry, setspace, lipsum, and minionpro.

The package relies on the Minion Pro fonts from Adobe, which are commercial but easily available.

name: LEIletter

caption: Express lengths in arbitrary units

descriptions.text:
The package provides a command to convert a length to any of a large selection of units.

The package relies on the LaTeX3 programming environment.

name: lengthconvert

caption: Let assignment for LaTeX macros

descriptions.text: TeX’s \let assignment does not work for LaTeX macros with optional arguments or for macros that are defined as robust macros by \DeclareRobustCommand. This package defines \LetLtxMacro that also takes care of the involved internal macros.

name: letltxmacro

caption: Class for the newsletter “La Lettre GUTenberg” of the French TeX User Group GUTenberg

descriptions.text:
The French TeX User Group GUTenberg has been publishing “The GUTenberg Letter”, its irregular newsletter, since February 1993.

For this purpose, a dedicated, in-house (La)TeX class was gradually created but, depending on new needs and on the people who were publishing the Newsletter, its development was somewhat erratic; in particular, it would not have been possible to publish its code as it was. In addition, its documentation was non-existent.

The Board of Directors of the association, elected in November 2020, wished to provide a better structured, more perennial and documented class, able to be published on the CTAN. This is now done with the present ‘letgut’ class.

# French

L’association GUTenberg publie “La Lettre GUTenberg”, son bulletin irrégulomestriel, depuis février 1993.

Pour ce faire, une classe (La)TeX dédiée, maison, a peu à peu vu le jour mais, au gré des nouveaux besoins et des personnes qui ont assuré la publication de la Lettre, son développement a été quelque peu erratique ; il n’aurait notamment pas été possible de publier son code en l’état. En outre, sa documentation était inexistante.

Le Conseil d’Administration de l’association, élu en novembre 2020, a souhaité fournir une classe mieux structurée, davantage pérenne et documentée, à même d’être publiée sur le CTAN. C’est désormais chose faite avec la présente classe letgut.

name: letgut

topics.details: magazines, newspapers and other ephemeral pubications
LuaTeX and packages that require it

caption: The standard LaTeX2e letter document class

descriptions.text: This is the Standard Letter Document Class for LaTeX version 2e.

name: letter

caption: Letter formatting macros

descriptions.text: A simple set of macros, which acts as a driver file for producing a letter.

name: letter1

topics.details: extensions to Plain TeX for higher-level constructs

caption: The Adobe Type 1 font family Letter GothicType

descriptions.text:
This bundle provides the Adobe Type 1 font family Letter Gothic which URW has made available for free under the Aladdin Free Public License.

The original distribution site of the font files is http://www.artifex.com/downloads/.

The fonts are accompanied by the TeX font metrics, virtual fonts, font definition and font mapping files to use them with LaTeX. The support material is released under the LPPL.

name: lettergothic

topics.details: font available in Adobe Type 1 format

caption: Letter macros for Plain TeX
