descriptions.text: This package provides macros to typeset some general mathematical operators (identity operator, trace, diagonal, rank, ...), a powerful implementation of the bra-ket notation (kets, bras, brakets, matrix elements etc. which can be sized as required), delimited expressions such as averages and norms, and some basic Lie algebra/group names. Macros for entropy measures for quantum information theory (smooth min- and max-entropy, smooth relative entropies, etc.) are also provided.

name: phfqit

caption: Quote verbatim text without white space formatting

descriptions.text: This package provides an environment for displaying block text with special characters, such as verbatim quotes from a referee report which may contain pseudo-(La)TeX code. This behaves like a verbatim environment, except that it displays its content as normal paragraph content, ignoring any white space preformatting.

name: phfquotetext

caption: Watermarks with version control information from SVN

descriptions.text: This package allows you to add version control information as a gray watermark on each page of your document. The SVN info is read from keyword tags such as $Id$, $Date$, and $Author$ via the svn or svn-multi packages.

name: phfsvnwatermark

topics.details: support for keeping track of document development
separate printing, under (or over) the page as a whole

caption: Goodies for theorems and proofs

descriptions.text: This package provides enhanced theorem and proof environments based on the amsthm original versions. It allows for hooks to be placed, adds some default goodies and is highly customizable. In particular, it can connect theorems to proofs, automatically producing text such as “See proof on page XYZ” and “Proof of Theorem 4: ...”.

name: phfthm

caption: Cross references for named and numbered environments

descriptions.text:
Philex provides means for creating and cross-referencing named or numbered environments. Possible uses would be equations, example sentences (as in linguistics or philosophy) or named principles. Cross references may refer either to the number, or to a short name of the target environment, or to the contents of the environment.

Philex builds on the facilities of the linguex package.

name: philex

caption: A font to typeset the Philokalia Books

descriptions.text:
The philokalia package has been designed to ease the use of the Philokalia-Regular OpenType font with XeLaTeX.

The font started as a project to digitize the typeface used to typeset the Philokalia books.

name: philokalia

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other font support
font for Greek (archaic, classical and modern)

caption: Typesetting articles for "Philosophers' Imprint"

descriptions.text:
In its mission statement we read “Philosophers’ Imprint is a refereed series of original papers in philosophy, edited by philosophy faculty at the University of Michigan, with the advice of an international Board of Editors, and published on the World Wide Web by the University of Michigan Digital Library. The mission of the Imprint is to promote a future in which funds currently spent on journal subscriptions are redirected to the dissemination of scholarship for free, via the Internet”.

The class helps authors to typeset their own articles in “Web-ready” format. No assumption is made about the fonts available to the author: the class itself is restricted to freely available and freely distributed fonts, only.

name: philosophersimprint

caption: Format telephone number lists

descriptions.text:
This (Plain TeX) program formats a list of telephone numbers into 9x9 grids on a page. The author uses these lists as wallet-sized directories.

The program is distributed with an example data file.

name: phoncard

caption: Fonts for the Phoenician script in use from about 1600 BC

descriptions.text:
The (Semitic) Phoenician script is in a direct line of ancestry for all the western world's alphabets. The fonts provide Mirrored forms for typesetting either left-to-right or right-to-left (as the Phoenicians did). The fonts are provided in Adobe Type 1 format.

This is one of a series of archaic fonts.

name: phoenician

topics.details: fonts reproducing archaic scripts or inscriptions
font available in Adobe Type 1 format

caption: Typesetting telephone numbers with LaTeX

descriptions.text:
The phonenumbers package makes it possible to typeset telephone numbers according to different national conventions. German, Austrian, French, British and North American phone numbers are supported. Phone numbers from other countries are supported rudimentarily.

The user can select from various formatting options, including the additional output of the country calling code. The package is able to check if a phone number is valid according to the national rules. It also allows to link phone numbers using the hyperref package.

name: phonenumbers

topics.details: lists of addresses, for a personal directory (or the like)

caption: Metafont Phonetic fonts, based on Computer Modern

descriptions.text: The fonts are based on Computer Modern, and specified in Metafont. Macros for the fonts’ use are provided, both for LaTeX 2.09 and for current LaTeX.

name: phonetic

topics.details: fonts with specific small application areas

caption: Typeset linear phonological rules

descriptions.text: The package provides macros for typesetting phonological rules like those in ‘Sound Pattern of English’ (Chomsky and Halle 1968).

name: phonrule

caption: A float environment for photographs

descriptions.text: This package introduces a new float type called photo which works similar to the float types table and figure. Various options exist for placing photos, captions, and a “photographer” line. In twocolumn documents, a possibility exists to generate double-column floats automatically if the photo does not fit into one column. Photos do not have to be placed as floats, they can also be placed as boxes, with captions and photographer line still being available.

name: photo

caption: A document class for typesetting photo books

descriptions.text: The photobook LaTeX document class extends the book class defining a set of parameters, meta-macros, macros and environments with reasonable defaults to help typeset, build and print books mainly based on visual/image content.

name: photobook

caption: A collection of BibTeX styles for physics journals

descriptions.text: Proto BibTeX styles (.btx files) are provided, together with a GNU-emacs lisp program to generate usable .bst files. A set of actual .bst files, together with the required LaTeX packages, is also provided.

name: phy-bstyles

caption: Macros for commonly used physical constants

descriptions.text:
This package consists of several macros that are shorthand for a variety of physical constants, e.g. the speed of light. The package developed out of physics and astronomy classes that the author has taught and wanted to ensure that he had correct values for each constant and did not wish to retype them every time he uses them.

The constants can be used in two forms, the most accurate available values, or versions that are rounded to 3 significant digits for use in typical classroom settings, homework assignments, etc.

Most constants are taken from CODATA 2018, with the exception of the astronomical objects, whose values are taken from International Astronomical Union specified values. Constants that are derived from true constants, e.g. the fine structure constant, have been calculated using the accepted values of the fundamental constants.

name: physconst

caption: Macros supporting the Mathematics of Physics

descriptions.text: The package defines simple and flexible macros for typesetting equations in the languages of vector calculus and linear algebra, using Dirac notation.

name: physics

caption: Macros for typesetting maths faster and more simply

descriptions.text:
The physics2 package defines commands for typesetting maths formulae faster and more simply. physics2 is a modularized package, each module provides its own function. You can load modules separately after loading physics2.

Modules of physics provide the following support:

  • Automatic braces;
  • Dirac bra-ket notation;
  • Easy way to typeset diagonal matrices and matrices with similar entries;
  • Double cross and double dot (binary) operators for tensors.

name: physics2

caption: The PHYSE format

descriptions.text: PHYSE is a format for writing physics papers, based on Knuth's plain.

name: physe

caption: Macros for commonly used physical units

descriptions.text: This package provides a collection of macros to simplify using physical units (e.g. m for meters, J for joules, etc.), especially in math mode. All major SI units are included, as well as some cgs units used in astronomy.

name: physunits

topics.details: support for writers of scientific documents

caption: Assorted macros for Physicists

descriptions.text:
The package contains a large collection of small macros that may be useful to physicists and occasionally some mathematicians. It streamlines writing Dirac notation, derivatives, vector variables, unit vectors, scientific notation, elementary particles, and many other things.

This package has been declared obsolete by its author.

name: physymb

caption: A TeX format for physicists

descriptions.text: The macros were developed at SLAC, and were updated after the transition from TeX 97 to TeX 1.0.

name: phyzzx

caption: Calculate pi

descriptions.text:
Generates pi, using the formula: Pi=16*arctan(1/5)-4*arctan(1/239) and leaves the result in an array \xr, printing what is calculated as it goes along.

The number of digits you can compute depends on your implementation of TeX. The last digit may be wrong, and if it's 0 or 9, the penultimate digit may also be wrong.

name: pi

caption: Typeset a basic 2-octave piano diagram

descriptions.text:
This package adds the \keyboard[1][2]..[7] command to your project. When used, it draws a small 2 octaves piano keyboard on your document, with up to 7 keys highlighted.

Keys go : Co, Cso, Do, Dso, Eo, Fo, Fso, Go, Gso, Ao, Aso, Bo, Ct, Cst, Dt, Dst, Et, Ft, Fst, Gt, Gst, At, Ast and Bt. (A working example is included in the README file.)

name: piano

caption: Insert pictures into paragraphs

descriptions.text:
A legacy package for creating ‘windows’ in paragraphs, for inserting graphics, etc. (including “dropped capitals”).

Users should note that Pieter van Oostrum (in a published review of packages of this sort) does not recommend this package; Picins is recommended instead.

name: picinpar

topics.details: flow text round an insertion in the paragraph

caption: A picture mode in Plain TeX

descriptions.text: The package provides a subset of LaTeX's facilities, but also has quadratic spline macros.

name: picmac

topics.details: graphics produced by one of the *TeX engines

caption: Insert pictures into paragraphs

descriptions.text: Wraps the text of the paragraph around the inserted picture.

name: picins

topics.details: flow text round an insertion in the paragraph

caption: New implementation of picture commands

copyright.owner: Rolf Niepraschk, Hubert Gaesslein, Josef Tkadlec

descriptions.text:
This package was described in the 2nd edition of ‘LaTeX: A Document Preparation System’, but the LaTeX project team declined to produce the package. For a long time, LaTeX included a ‘pict2e package’ that merely produced an apologetic error message.

The new package extends the existing LaTeX picture environment, using the familiar technique (cf. the graphics and color packages) of driver files (at present, drivers for dvips, pdfTeX, LuaTeX, XeTeX, VTeX, dvipdfm, and dvipdfmx are available). The package documentation has a fair number of examples of use, showing where things are improved by comparison with the LaTeX picture environment.

name: pict2e

topics.details: graphics produced by one of the *TeX engines

caption: Picture drawing macros for TeX and LaTeX

descriptions.text: PicTeX is an early and very comprehensive drawing package that mostly draws by placing myriads of small dots to make up pictures. It has a tendency to run out of space; packages m-pictex and pictexwd deal with the problems in different ways.

name: PicTeX

topics.details: graphics produced by one of the *TeX engines

caption: Automatic computation of bounding boxes with PiCTeX

descriptions.text: This package makes PiCTeX recognize lines and arcs in determining the “bounding box” of a picture. (PiCTeX so far accounted for put commands only). The “bounding box” is essential for proper placement of a picture between running text and margins and for keeping the running text away.

name: pictex-autoarea

topics.details: graphics produced by one of the *TeX engines

caption: Adds relative coordinates and improves the \plot command

descriptions.text: Adds two user commands to standard PiCTeX. One command uses relative coordinates, thus eliminating the need to calculate the coordinate of every point manually as in standard PiCTeX. The other command modifies \plot to use a rule instead of dots if the line segment is horizontal or vertical.

name: pictex2

topics.details: graphics produced by one of the *TeX engines

caption: A patched version of PicTeX using fewer registers

descriptions.text:
This is a patched version of PicTeX that overcomes one of the significant problems with PicTeX, viz., the number of dimension registers it uses. It should be loaded in place of PicTeX. (Note that pictexwd.sty is also available, for use when loading the package in LaTeX.)

A similar function (reducing the number of dimension registers needed) is performed by m-pictex.

The files are available as part of the PicTeX distribution.

name: pictexwd

topics.details: graphics produced by one of the *TeX engines

caption: A summary of PicTeX commands

descriptions.text: The document summarises the commands of PicTeX. While it is no substitute for the PicTeX manual itself (available from Personal TeX inc.), the document is a useful aide-memoire for those who have read the manual.

name: PicTeXsum

caption: Dimens for picture macros

descriptions.text: There are macro and environment arguments that expect numbers that will internally be multiplied by \unitlength. This package extends the syntax of these arguments, so that dimensions with calculation support may be used for these arguments.

name: picture

caption: Draw pie-charts using MetaPost

descriptions.text: The piechartmp package is an easy way to draw pie-charts with MetaPost. The package implements an interface that enables users with little MetaPost experience to draw charts. A highlight of the package is the possibility of suppressing some segments of the chart, thus creating the possibility of several charts from the same data.

name: piechartmp

caption: Simple pie-charts with PSTricks

descriptions.text: A pair of shell+AWK scripts that uses small parameter files to generate pie-charts (expressed as (La)TeX code using PSTricks).

name: piechart

topics.details: package using PStricks for graphical output

caption: Macro tools by Mike Piff

descriptions.text:
The set (now) consists of:

  • a small package for dealing with duplicate-numbered output pages;
  • newproof, for defining mathematical proof structures;
  • onepagem for omitting the page number in one-page documents and
  • time, which prints a 12-hour format time.

name: piff

caption: Early macros for using AMS fonts

descriptions.text: This package was created (in its present form) after the advent of LaTeX 2e, but before the corresponding macros from the AMS itself had arrived. Those macros are now part of the standard LaTeX distribution as part of AMS-LaTeX.

name: piff-ams

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other font support

caption: Access to PostScript standard Symbol and Dingbats fonts

descriptions.text:
The package provides commands for Pi fonts (Dingbats, Symbol, etc.); all commands assume you know the character number within the font of the symbol within the font.

The package is distributed as part of the psnfss, which is itself part of the LaTeX ‘required’ set of packages.

name: pifont

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other font support

caption: A font for the pigpen (or masonic) cipher

descriptions.text:
The Pigpen cipher package provides the font and the necessary wrappers (style file, etc.) in order to write Pigpen ciphers, a simple substitution cipher.

The package provides a font (available both as Metafont source, and as an Adobe Type 1 file), and macros for its use.

name: pigpen

topics.details: font available in Adobe Type 1 format

caption: Draw chip pinouts with TikZ

descriptions.text:
The package provides a set of macros for typesetting electronic chip pinouts.

It is designed as a tool that is easy to use, with a lean syntax, native to LaTeX, and directly supporting PDF output format. It has therefore been based on the very impressive TikZ package.

name: pinouTikZ

caption: A TeX labelling package

descriptions.text:
Pinlabel is a labelling package for attaching perfectly formatted TeX labels to figures and diagrams in both eps and pdf formats. It is suitable both for labelling a new diagram and for relabelling an existing diagram.

The package uses coordinates derived from GhostView (or gv) and labels are placed with automatic and consistent spacing relative to the object labelled.

name: pinlabel

caption: Documentation macros

descriptions.text:
The bundle provides macros that the author uses when writing documentation (for example, that of the texapi and yax packages).

The tools could be used by anyone, but there is no documentation, and the macros are subject to change without notice.

name: pitex

topics.details: macros and tools for preparing documentation

caption: Electronic Theses and Dissertations at Pitt

descriptions.text: A document class for theses and dissertations. Provides patch files that enable pittetd to use files prepared for use with the pittdiss or pitthesis classes. The manual provides a detailed guide for users who wish to use the class to prepare their thesis or dissertation.

name: pittetd

caption: Document class for University of Pittsburgh theses

descriptions.text: A class that may be used for the two major styles of thesis at Pittsburgh university, viz., Engineering, and “the rest”.

name: pitthesis

caption: Typeset Python listings with LPEG

descriptions.text:
This package uses the Lua library LPEG to typeset and highlight informatic listings in several languages (Python, OCaml, SQL and C++).

It requires the use of LuaLaTeX. It won’t work with XeLaTeX, nor pdfLaTeX.

name: piton

topics.details: LuaTeX and packages that require it
highlight syntax of computer code, etc.

caption: Draw pixel-art pictures

descriptions.text: A LuaLaTeX package to draw pixel-art pictures using TikZ.

name: pixelart

topics.details: LuaTeX and packages that require it

caption: Work with PixelArts, with TikZ

descriptions.text: The package defines commands and an environment for displaying pixel arts.

name: PixelArtTikz

caption: Derive glyph bounding boxes by building PK file

descriptions.text: The author found that AFM files generated by pfm2afm lacked glyph bounding box information, so that they are not much use for generating TFM files. This package proceeds by generating a PK file from the Type 1 font by use of ps2pk, and then using information from that to generate a more nearly valid AFM file from the original.

name: pkbbox

caption: Replace pk fonts in PostScript with Type 1 fonts

descriptions.text: The perl script pkfix looks for DVIPSBitmapFont comments in PostScript files, generated by ‘not too old’ dvips, and replaces them by type 1 versions of the fonts, if possible.

name: pkfix

caption: A ‘find’ command which understands pk files

descriptions.text: The TDS standard specifies that pk and gf files contain \special strings to identify the contents of the files. Pkfind is a variant of the GNU find utility modified to understand those specials, and to act on them in some cases. For example, it can be used to delete all pk files created by gsftopk from a subdirectory tree.

name: pkfind

caption: Make PostScript files accessible to pkfix

descriptions.text:
Pkfix is a useful utility for replacing resolution-dependent bitmapped fonts in a dvips-produced PostScript file with the corresponding resolution-independent vector fonts. Unfortunately, pkfix needs to parse certain PostScript comments that appear only in files produced by dvips versions later than 5.58 (ca. 1996); it fails to work on PostScript files produced by older versions of dvips.

Pkfix-helper is a program that attempts to insert newer-dvips comments into an older-dvips PostScript file, thereby making the file suitable for processing by pkfix. pkfix-helper can sometimes process documents fully autonomously but does require the user to verify and, if needed, correct its decisions.

documentation.details: Encoding tables and how to use them

name: pkfix-helper

caption: CTAN package checker

descriptions.text:
Packages uploaded to CTAN will be checked by the CTAN team before they get installed.

This package provides the pkgckeck command line utility used by CTAN members for carrying out those checks that can be performed in an automated way.

pkgcheck is a 64-bit static Linux binary, and runs out of the box. The only prerequisites is that pdfinfo is available.

A Windows version is not planned.

name: pkgcheck

topics.details: support for work with the CTAN archive

caption: Manage the options and loading order of other packages

descriptions.text:
The package seeks to address the frustration caused by package conflicts. It is in an early stage of its development, and should probably not be used as a matter of course; however the author welcomes feedback via the home page link given in this catalogue entry.

Nevertheless, the author urges users to try the package and to report issues (or whatever) via the package’s repository.

To use pkgloader you need, apart from packages installed by default, the lt3graph package.

name: pkgloader

topics.details: support for package or document debugging

caption: LaTeX template for dissertations in Peking University

descriptions.text: The package provides a simple, clear and flexible LaTeX template for dissertations in Peking University.

name: pkuthss

caption: Literate Programming for Prolog with LaTeX

descriptions.text: Instead of having to transform the common source into program or documentation, the central idea was to develop a method to have one common source which can be interpreted by a Prolog system as well as by LaTeX, whether that Prolog system be C-Prolog, Quintus-Prolog, or ECLiPSe.

name: pl

caption: Utility programs for use with PK bitmap fonts

descriptions.text:
pktype verifies a PK-format bitmap font. pktogf converts a PK-format bitmap font to GF format.

These programs were originally written by Tomas Rokicki as part of his Stanford Ph.D. work, and have always been distributed alongside the other programs coming from the Stanford TeX project, though they are not maintained by Donald Knuth.

The related program gftopk[.web], however, is maintained by DEK and is part of the "mfware" collection, gftopk is by far the most commonly used of the PK font utilities.

name: pkware

topics.details: convert a font to a form usable with TeX

caption: Polish extension of Computer Modern fonts

descriptions.text: The Polish extension of the Computer Modern fonts (compatible with CM itself) for use with Polish TeX formats. The fonts were originally a part of the MeX distribution (and they are still available that way).

name: pl-mf

caption: Control float placement

descriptions.text: Defines a \FloatBarrier command, beyond which floats may not pass; useful, for example, to ensure all floats for a section appear before the next \section command.

name: placeins

topics.details: layout of objects on the page

caption: Absolute content positioning

descriptions.text: The package provides commands so that the user of LuaLaTeX may position arbitrary content at any position specified by absolute coordinates on the page. The package draws a grid on each page of the document, to aid positioning (the grid may be disabled, for ‘final copy’ using the command \placeatsetup).

name: placeat

topics.details: layout of objects on the page
LuaTeX and packages that require it

caption: Insertions that keep their place

descriptions.text: This TeX file provides various mechanisms (for plain TeX and close relatives) to let insertions (footnotes, topins, pageins, etc.) float within their appropriate section, but to prevent them from intruding into the following section, even when sections do not normally begin a new page. (If your sections normally begin a new page, just use \supereject to flush out insertions.)

name: placeins-plain

topics.details: layout of objects on the page

caption: The Plain TeX format

descriptions.text: Contains files used to build the Plain TeX format, as described in the TeXbook, together with various supporting files (some also discussed in the book).

name: plain

caption: Make plain TeX files LaTeXable

descriptions.text:
The package plain.sty defines a LaTeX environment which can process a document written to use Knuth's basic Plain TeX macros.

Inside the environment, not everything is as Knuth intended (some Plain commands are suppressed, some are faked, and some basic mechanisms—such as font selection and the output routine—remain as in LaTeX). Thus “simple” documents will run, but elaborate macros defined in the document have a chance of failing.

The package is distributed as part of the carlisle bundle.

name: plain-ltx

topics.details: import files in a non-TeX (or different TeX) format

caption: Variable sized fonts in Plain TeX

descriptions.text: A font-selection system for Plain TeX, that allows users to choose sizes other than 10pt as the base size of their document, and to use ‘relative’ sizes like \big, \Big (and so on) as commands taking an argument to be set in a larger-than-base size.

name: plain-cm

caption: A minimal method for making generic packages

descriptions.text: The package provides a minimal method for making generic (i.e., TeX-format-independent) packaged, combining maybeload functionality, fallback definitions for LaTeX \ProvidesPackage and \RequirePackage functionality, and handling of arbitrary (multiple) “private letters” (analagous LaTeX packages’ use of “@”) in nested package files. The documentation contains a central reference for making and using generic packages based on the package.

name: plainpkg

topics.details: macros that are independent of the (TeX) format in use

caption: Miscellaneous contributed macros for plain TeX
name: plainmisc

topics.details: Root directory of a (sub-)tree of the archive

caption: Plain bibliography style, sorted by year first

descriptions.text:
This is a version of the standard plain BibTeX style, modified to sort chronologically (by year) first, then by author, title, etc.

(The style's name isn't what the author submitted: it was renamed for clarity.)

name: plainyr

caption: Write labels for plants

descriptions.text:
The package defines a command \plant, which has three mandatory and seven optional argument.

The package uses the labels

name: plantslabels

topics.details: typeset badges, covers or labels for things (or people)

caption: Support for rendering UML diagrams using PlantUML

descriptions.text:
PlantUML is a program which transforms text into UML diagrams. This LaTeX package allows for embedding PlantUML diagrams using the PlantUML source.

Currently, this project runs with LuaLaTeX only.

name: plantuml

topics.details: support for Universal Modelling Language diagrams
LuaTeX and packages that require it

caption: Typesetting stageplay scripts

descriptions.text: Plari (the name comes from the Finnish usage for the working copy of a play) is a report-alike class, without section headings, and with paragraphs vertically separated rather than indented.

name: plari

caption: pLaTeX2e and miscellaneous macros for pTeX

descriptions.text:
The bundle provides pLaTeX2e and miscellaneous macros for pTeX and e-pTeX.

This is a community edition forked from the original ASCII edition (ptex-texmf-2.5).

name: platex

caption: Arrange for "plates" sections of documents

descriptions.text: The plates package provides a simple facility for inserting colour figures in a document when they should be gathered and printed together as in a book's section of colour plates. The package provides a plate environment that takes the place of the figure environment for such colour images.

name: plates

caption: pLaTeX standard tools bundle

descriptions.text: This bundle is an extended version of the latex-tools bundle developed by the LaTeX team, mainly intended to support pLaTeX2e and upLaTeX2e. Currently patches for the latex-tools bundle and Martin Schröder’s ms bundle are included.

name: platex-tools

caption: A LaTeX cheat sheet, in Japanese

descriptions.text:
This is a translation to Japanese of Winston Chang’s LaTeX cheat sheet (a reference sheet for writing scientific papers).

It has been adapted to Japanese standards using pLaTeX, and also attached additional information of "standard LaTeX" (especially about math-mode).

name: platexcheat

caption: Automated patches for pLaTeX/upLaTeX

descriptions.text:
Japanese pLaTeX/upLaTeX formats and packages often conflict with other LaTeX packages which are unaware of pLaTeX/upLaTeX. In the worst case, such packages throw a fatal error or end up with a wrong output.

The goal of this package is that there should be no need to worry about such incompatibilities, because specific patches are loaded automatically whenever necessary. This helps not only to simplify source files, but also to make the appearance of working pLaTeX/upLaTeX sources similar to those of ordinary LaTeX ones.

name: plautopatch

topics.details: correct a problem, ahead of the “proper” fix
support for package or document debugging

caption: Typeset drama using LaTeX

descriptions.text: A class and style file that supports the typesetting of plays, including options for line numbering.

name: play

caption: The Play font face with support for LaTeX and pdfLaTeX

descriptions.text: This package provides the Play family of fonts designed by FontFuror, with support for LaTeX and pdfLaTeX.

name: play-font

topics.details: font providing LaTeX T1 encoding support
font available in Adobe Type 1 format
font designed for use as body font for Latin-based script documents
metrics, macro incantations and other font support

caption: A simple template for drawing playcards

descriptions.text: This small package provides commands for drawing customized playcards with width 59mm and height 89mm, which are typical card dimensions.

name: playcards

topics.details: process game diagrams, gamebooks, and other amusements

caption: Playfair Display fonts with LaTeX support

descriptions.text:
This package provides the PlayFairDisplay family of fonts, designed by Claus Eggers Sørensen, for use with LaTeX, pdfLaTeX, XeLaTeX and LuaLaTeX.

PlayFairDisplay is well suited for titling and headlines. It has an extra large x-height and short descenders. It can be set with no leading if space is tight, for instance in news headlines, or for stylistic effect in titles. Capitals are extra short, and only very slightly heavier than the lowercase characters. This helps achieve a more even typographical colour when typesetting proper nouns and initialisms.

name: playfair

topics.details: font designed for use as body font for Latin-based script documents
metrics, macro incantations and other font support
font available in Adobe Type 1 format
font providing LaTeX T1 encoding support

caption: Plain macros for making nice calendars
name: plcalendar

topics.details: typeset calendars, diaries, planning charts, etc.

caption: Support for IBM Plex fonts

copyright.owner: IBM Corp. with Reserved Font Name Plex

descriptions.text: The package provides LaTeX, pdfLaTeX, XeLaTeX and LuaLaTeX support for the IBM Plex families of fonts. Serif, Sans and Mono families are available in eight weights: Regular, Light, ExtraLight, Thin, Bold, Text, Medium and SemiBold (with corresponding italics).

name: plex

topics.details: font designed for use as body font for Latin-based script documents
font providing LaTeX T1 encoding support
font available in Adobe Type 1 format

caption: Support for the OpenType font IBM Plex

descriptions.text:
This package supports the free otf fonts from the IBM Plex project which are available from GitHub or already part of your system (Windows/Linux/…).

This package supports only XeLaTeX or LuaLaTeX; for pdfLaTeX use plex-mono.sty, plex-sans.sty, and/or plex-serif.sty from the plex package.

IBM Plex has no math symbols. You will have to use one of the existing math fonts if you need them.

name: plex-otf

topics.details: support is for a font not available on CTAN

caption: Polish extension to Computer Modern fonts

name: plhyph

caption: Fonts with the Plimsoll symbol and LaTeX support

descriptions.text: This package provides access to the Plimsoll symbol for use with LaTeX. The Plimsoll symbol is sometimes used in chemistry for denoting standard states and values. The LaTeX package provides access to this notation as well. The syntax for denoting the standard state is the same as suggested in the Comprehensive LaTeX Symbol List for emulating the Plimsoll mark.

caption: 'Lorem ipsum' for Plain TeX developers

descriptions.text: The package provides a paragraph generator designed for use in Plain TeX documents. The paragraphs generated contain many ‘f-groups’ (ff, fl etc.) so the text can act as a test of the ligatures of the font in use.

name: plipsum

topics.details: dummy text generator for tests and examples

caption: Polish extension of CM fonts in Type 1 format

descriptions.text: This package is the Polish extension of the Computer Modern fonts (known as PL fonts),in Adobe Type 1 (PostScript) format. The fonts use the same .tfm files as for the version generated by Metafont. This release of fonts was adapted to the (mostly guessed) demands of the Windows environment, while keeping the fonts usable with TeX; however, encoding files are now added, as Windows and TeX use different encoding schemes.

name: plpsfont

caption: Font selection for Plain TeX

descriptions.text: Plnfss is a set of macros to provide easy font access (somewhat similar to NFSS but with some limitations) with Plain TeX. Plnfss can automatically make use of PSNFSS fd files, i.e., when an Adobe Type 1 is used the relevant fd file will be loaded automatically. For cmr-like fonts (ec, vnr, csr or plr fonts), a special format called pfd (plain fd) is required and must be loaded manually. See ot1cmr.pfd for further information.

name: plnfss

topics.details: extensions to Plain TeX for higher-level constructs

caption: St. Mary’s Road font support for plain TeX

descriptions.text: The package provides commands to produce all the symbols of the St Mary’s Road fonts, in a Plain TeX environment.

name: plstmary

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other support for symbol fonts

caption: Poor man ISO math for pdfLaTeX users

descriptions.text: This small package realizes a poor man approximation of the ISO regulations for physical sciences and technology. Contrary to other more elegant solutions, it does not load any math alphabet, since pdfLaTeX can use only a maximum of such alphabets. The necessary user macros are defined for typsetting common math symbols that require special ISO treatment.

name: pm-isomath

caption: Typeset partitioned matrices

name: pmat

caption: LaTeX in emTeX IDE/FrontEnd for EPM

descriptions.text: A macro package that implements many (em)TeX related features for the OS/2 EPM editor. A menu item is added to the EPM menu, a new toolbar is provided, and hotkeys for some (La)TeX commands are defined.

name: pmcstex

topics.details: plug-ins for editors, for better (La)TeX and Meta* support

caption: Poor man’s box drawing characters

descriptions.text: This package declares box drawing characters of old code pages, e.g. cp437. It uses rules instead of using a font.

name: pmboxdraw

topics.details: graphics produced by one of the *TeX engines

caption: Create a DB (PDF) document for selecting content for inclusion in another documents

descriptions.text:
The “poor man's database” (pmdb) package promotes a workflow for building exams, homework, and other content. The package supports the creation of a PDF document, which is a database of problems (or content) to be included in a target document.

The package inserts checkboxes into the margins of the DB document. The instructor can select which which of the problems are to be included in the target document by checking one ore more of the checkboxes. By clicking the special \displayChoices control, the selected content is copied into the AR/AA console window in the form of \input statements (\input{prob1.tex}, eg), which is then be copied and pasted into the target document. By pressing Ctrl+Click while hovering over a checkbox, the associated content is loaded into the default application, possibly a LaTeX editor. For the Ctrl+Click feature to work, the file aeb-reader.js needs to be installed. As the filename suggests, this file will work for Adobe Acrobat Reader (DC), as well as for the magnificent Adobe Acrobat itself.

name: pmdb

topics.details: create pdf form fields, use form fields as an integral part of the package

caption: Examples from "Praca magisterska i dyplomowa"

descriptions.text: The package provides machine readable copies of the examples from the book ‘Praca magisterska i dyplomowa z programem LaTeX’ (on writing a thesis with LaTeX, in Polish).

name: pmdpl

topics.details: copies of examples from a published book

caption: Draw elements of partition monoids

descriptions.text: This package allows you to draw elements of Partition Monoids, commonly referred to as diagrams. The package provides a lot of flexibility to draw most diagrams and can be customised as needed.

name: pmdraw

caption: "Poor man's" graphics

descriptions.text: A set of extensions to LaTeX picture environment, including a wider range of vectors, and a lot more box frame styles.

name: pmgraph

caption: Preprocessor for MusicTeX

descriptions.text: PMTeX is the MusicTeX predecessor of pmx (by the same author).

name: pmtex

caption: Preprocessor for MusiXTeX

descriptions.text:
PMX provides a preprocessor for MusiXTeX.

pmxab builds a TeX input file based on a .pmx input file in a much simpler language, making most of the layout decisions by itself. It has most of MusiXTeX's functionality, but it also permits in-line TeX to give access to virtually all of MusiXTeX. For proof-listening, pmxab will make a MIDI file of your score.

scor2prt is an auxiliary program that makes parts from a score.

name: pmx

caption: Poor man’s Hangul Jamo input method

descriptions.text:
This package provides a Hangul transliteration input method that allows to typeset Korean letters (Hangul) using the proper fonts.

The name is derived from “Poor man’s Hangul Jamo Input Method”.

The use of XeLaTeX is recommended. pdfTeX is not supported.

name: pmhanguljamo

topics.details: XeTeX, material supporting it, and packages requiring it

caption: Produce chord information to go with pmx output

descriptions.text:
The bundle supplements pmx, providing the means of typesetting chords above the notes of a score.

The bundle contains:

  • macros for typing the chords;
  • a Lua script to transpose chord macros to the required key signature; and
  • support scripts for common requirements.

name: pmxchords

caption: BibTeX style for PNAS (old version)

descriptions.text:
This style produces bibliographies in the format of “Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, USA”. The style was derived from the standard unsrt.bst.

It is obsolete and replaced by pnas2009.bst.

name: PNAS

caption: BibTeX style for PNAS (newer version)

descriptions.text: This style produces bibliographies in the format of “Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, USA”. The style was derived from the standard unsrt.bst and adapted to the new (2009) formatting rules.

name: PNAS 2009

caption: PNG to PDF converter

descriptions.text:
The png2pdf program converts PNG images to PDF. An alpha channel in the PNG file can be used to mix against a specified background color and/or to create a PDF image mask or PDF alpha channel. The program may be of interest for pdfLaTeX users creating posters, flyers having colored background, etc.

The package’s functionality is now replaced by bmpp, which is part of dktools.

name: png2pdf

caption: Support for Adobe Poetica fonts in  Type 1 format

descriptions.text:
The fonts offer huge numbers of swashed and ligatured versions of glyphs, which are difficult for any software to control in a Type 1 font. This package (with some expenditure of effort in the user) will allow some really remarkable typeset effects.

Note: poetica has been re-released as an OpenType font; the macros of this package would need some work before they would work with this alternate form.

name: poetica

topics.details: support is for a font not available on CTAN
metrics, macro incantations and other font support

caption: Typesetting Critical Editions of Poetry

descriptions.text: The package offers LaTeX macros for typesetting critical editions of poetry. Its features include automatic linenumbering, generation of separate endnotes sections for emendations, textual collations, and explanatory notes, special marking for cases in which page breaks occur during stanza breaks, running headers of the form ‘Notes to pp. xx–yy‘ for the notes sections, index of titles and first lines, and automatic generation of a table of contents.

name: poemscol

caption: Facilities for typesetting poetry and poetical structure

descriptions.text: This package provides some macros and general doodads for typesetting poetry. There is, of course, already the excellent verse package, and the poetrytex package provides some extra functionality on top of it. But poetry provides much of the same functionality in a bit of a different way, and with a few additional abilities, such as facilities for a list of poems, an index of first lines, and some structural commands.

name: poetry

caption: Typeset anthologies of poetry

descriptions.text: The package is designed to aid in the management and formatting of anthologies of poetry and other writings; it does not concern itself with actually typesettinig the verse itself.

name: poetrytex

caption: 12" Ruler containing Points and Inches

descriptions.text: This 12 inch ruler has a points scale (72.27 points/inch) and an inches scale. It's useful for precision measuring of LaTeX documents.

name: pointruler

caption: PoiretOne family of fonts with LaTeX support

descriptions.text: This package provides LaTeX, pdfLaTeX, XeLaTeX and LuaLaTeX support for the PoiretOne family of fonts, designed by Denis Masharov. PoiretOne is a decorative geometric grotesque with a hint of Art Deco and constructivism. There is currently just a regular weight and an artificially emboldened bold.

name: poiretone

caption: A parser for polynomial expressions

descriptions.text:
The package provides a parser \poldef of algebraic polynomial expressions. As it is based on xintexpr, the coefficients are allowed to be arbitrary rational numbers.

Once defined, a polynomial is usable by its name either as a numerical function in \xintexpr/\xinteval, or for additional polynomial definitions, or as argument to the package macros. The localization of real roots to arbitrary precision as well as the determination of all rational roots is implemented via such macros.

Since release 0.8, polexpr extends the xintexpr syntax to recognize polynomials as a new variable type (and not only as functions). Functionality which previously was implemented via macros such as the computation of a greatest common divisor is now available directly in \xintexpr, \xinteval or \poldef via infix or functional syntax.

name: polexpr

topics.details: macros that are independent of the (TeX) format in use

caption: A TeX macro package for prepress

descriptions.text: A set of macros (employing PostScript) supporting professional page preparation for prepress; includes color separation (it needs cmyk-hax package), crop-marks, colour and grey scale bars, etc.

name: poligraf

topics.details: fine-tuning details of output, for printing

caption: Typeset Polish documents with LaTeX and Polish fonts

descriptions.text:
Tools to typeset monolingual Polish documents in LaTeX2ε without babel or polyglossia. The package

  • loads Polish hyphenation patterns,
  • ensures that a font encoding suitable for Polish is used; in particular it enables Polish adaptation of Computer Modern fonts (the so-called PL fonts),
  • provides translations of \today and names like “Bibliography” or “Chapter”,
  • redefines math symbols according to Polish typographical tradition,
  • provides macros for dashes according to Polish orthography,
  • provides a historical input method for “Polish characters”,
  • works with traditional TeX as well as with Unicode aware variants.

(This package was previously known as platex, but has been renamed to resolve a name clash.)

name: polski

caption: Antykwa Półtawskiego Family of Fonts

copyright.owner: Bogusław Jackowski, Janusz M. Nowacki and P. Strzelczyk

descriptions.text:
The package contains the Antykwa Półtawskiego family of fonts in the PostScript Type 1 and OpenType formats. The original font was designed in the twenties of the XX century by the Polish typographer Adam Półtawski(1881-1952).

Following the route set out by the Latin Modern and TeX Gyre projects (https://www.gust.org.pl/projects/e-foundry), the Antykwa Półtawskiego digitisation project aims at providing a rich collection of diacritical characters in the attempt to cover as many Latin-based scripts as possible. To our knowledge, the repertoire of characters covers all European languages as well as some other Latin-based alphabets such as Vietnamese and Navajo; at the request of users, recent extensions (following the enhancement of the Latin Modern collection) provide glyphs sufficient for typesetting of romanized transliterations of Arabic and Sanskrit scripts.

The Antykwa Półtawskiego family consists of 4 weights (light, normal, medium, bold), each having upright and italic forms and one of 5 design sizes: 6, 8, 10, 12 and 17pt. Altogether, the collection comprises 40 font files, containing the same repertoire of 1126 characters.

The preliminary version of Antykwa Półtawskiego (antp package) released in 2000 is rendered obsolete by this package.

name: poltawski

topics.details: font available in Adobe Type 1 format

caption: An alternative to babel for XeLaTeX and LuaLaTeX

descriptions.text: This package provides a complete Babel replacement for users of LuaLaTeX and XeLaTeX; it relies on the fontspec package, version 2.0 at least.

name: polyglossia

support for more than one (natural) language
package will use LuaTeX facilities if available

caption: A TikZ package for drawing polyhedra

descriptions.text: This package provides macros for creating polyhedral objects in 2D and 3D. It requires TikZ and tikz-3dplot. The macros provided can be used for drawing vertices, edges, rays, polygons and cones.

name: polyhedra

caption: Typeset (univariate) polynomials

descriptions.text: The package offers an easy way to write (univariate) polynomials and rational functions. It defines two commands, one for polynomials \polynomial{coeffs} and one for rational functions \polynomialfrac{Numerator}{Denominator}. Both commands take lists of coefficients as arguments, and offer limited optional behaviour.

name: polynomial

caption: Macros for manipulating polynomials

descriptions.text: The polynom package implements macros for manipulating polynomials, for example it can typeset long polynomial divisions. The main test case and application is the polynomial ring in one variable with rational coefficients.

name: polynom

caption: Tabular-like environments with named columns

descriptions.text:
This package implements a variant of tabular-like environments where columns can be given a name and entries can flexibly be placed between arbitrary columns. Complex alignment-based layouts, for example for program code, are possible.

The package depends on lazylist.

name: polytable

caption: Raster Chinese and Japanese fonts

copyright.owner: Humanities and Arts Computing Center, University of Washington

descriptions.text:
The poorman's fonts, pmC and pmJ, are less than ideal implementations of Chinese and Japanese for TeX. They are less than ideal because they use fonts based on 24x24 dot-matrix fonts, and don't do vertical format typesetting and so forth.

The poorman's bundle provides a Metafont code generator, which reads a dot matrix font, and emits code to represent it. Also provided are macros that permit use of the fonts in a TeX document.

name: poorman

topics.details: support for font development, testing and characterisation

caption: Logarithms and powers with (almost) 9 digits

descriptions.text:
This small package (usable with Plain e-TeX, LaTeX, or others) with no dependencies provides two fast expandable macros computing logarithms in base 10 and fractional powers of 10.

They handle arguments of 9 digit tokens which stand for either 1 <= d.dddddddd < 10 (for the log) or 0.xxxxxxxxx (for powers of 10). They achieve a precision of 1ulp for the logarithm and 2ulp for fractional powers of ten.

Extension to other numerical ranges has to be done by user, via own macros or some math engine.

The xintexpr package (at 1.3f) imports the poormanlog macros as core constituents of its log10(), pow10(), log(), exp() and pow() functions.

name: poormanlog

caption: Create popup menus in PDF files

descriptions.text:
The package is used to create a menu structure. This menu structure (an array of menu items) is passed to the Acrobat JavaScript method app.popUpMenuEx() method to create a popup menu. Using the environments defined in the package, and the command \popUpMenu, you can create and display hierarchical menus. The menu items can have JavaScript actions associated with them, they can be marked and disabled.

The package only requires hyperref. Thus, users of pdfTeX, dvipdfm and dvips can use this package. An example is included in the distribution.

name: popupmenu

topics.details: create pdf form fields, use form fields as an integral part of the package

caption: Simple portrait/landscape switching

descriptions.text:
The portland package provides portrait and landscape environments, that set page dimensions but don't provide any hints to output devices. Thus, while you can sometimes read the resulting text in a previewer, special measures have to be taken to print the output.

The potential user will probably be better served by the lscape package (for DVI oriented output) or pdflscape (if using pdfLaTeX).

name: portland

topics.details: layout of objects on the page

caption: Instructions for setting up MikTeX on a portable device

descriptions.text:
The file offers instructions for setting up a portable installation of MikTeX (≥2.5), Ghostscript and GSView on external storage devices such as USB sticks or mapped network drives. The instructions cover systems running Windows 2000, XP and 2003.

The instructions are now obsolete; the user is advised to use MikTeX's own portable distribution.

name: Portable MikTeX

caption: Position things at absolute positions on the page

descriptions.text: Defines a command \at(HPOS,VPOS){TEXT}, which positions TEXT at HPOS from the left edge, VPOS from the top of the current page.

name: pos-at

topics.details: layout of objects on the page

caption: Stamp letters with »Deutsche Post«'s service »Internetmarke«

descriptions.text:
The postage package is used for franking letters with »Deutsche Post«’s online postage service »Internetmarke«.

Note that in order to print valid stamps you must point to a valid PDF of »Deutsche Post«’s »Ausdruck 4-spaltig (DIN A4)«.

name: postage

caption: Scale PostScript images for larger media or tiling

descriptions.text: Enlarge PostScript images and print them on larger media and/or tile them to print on multiple sheets. Supports foreign (non ISO A*) media sizes. An OS/2 port (suitable also for DOS) is available (see the os2 sub-directory).

name: poster

caption: Facilitates mass-mailing of postcards (junkmail)

descriptions.text: A modification of the standard LaTeX letter class which prints multiple, pre-stamped, 5.5" by 3.5" postcards (a US standard size) via the envlab and mailing packages. An address database is employed to address the front side of each postcard and a message is printed on the back side of all. An illustrative example is provided.

name: postcards

caption: A LaTeX package for displaying Post-it notes

descriptions.text:
This package provides some commands and options for creating Post-it-like boxes with tcolorbox:

  • an environment PostIt with customizations;
  • a command \MiniPostIt to display a simple Post-It.

name: postit

topics.details: highlighting typeset material, fancy frames, watermarks, etc.

caption: Make posters and banners with TeX

descriptions.text:
The package offers macros for making posters and banners with TeX. It is compatible with most TeX macro formats, including Plain TeX, LaTeX, AmSTeX, and AmS-LaTeX. The package creates a poster as huge box, which is then distributed over as many printer pages as necessary.

The only special requirement is that your printer not be bothered by text that lies off the page. This is true of most printers, including laser printers and PostScript printers.

name: poster-mac

caption: Endnotes for LaTeX

descriptions.text: This is an endnotes package for LaTeX. Its user interface provides means to print multiple sections of notes along the document, and to subdivide them either automatically — by chapter, by section — or at manually specified places, thus being able to easily handle both numbered and unnumbered headings. The package also provides infrastructure for setting up contextual running headers for printed notes. The default is a simple but useful one, in the form “Notes to pages N-M”, but more elaborate ones can be built. When hyperref is loaded, postnotes provides hyperlinked notes, including back links.

name: postnotes

caption: A presentation class

descriptions.text: Powerdot is a presentation class for LaTeX that allows for the quick and easy development of professional presentations. It comes with many tools that enhance presentations and aid the presenter. Examples are automatic overlays, personal notes and a handout mode. To view a presentation, DVI, PS or PDF output can be used. A powerful template system is available to easily develop new styles. A LyX layout file is provided.

name: powerdot

caption: Powerdot, using the style of FU Berlin

descriptions.text:
The bundle provides a powerdot-derived class and a package for use with powerdot to provide the corporate design of the Free University in Berlin.

Users may use the class itself (FUpowerdot) or use the package in the usual way with \style=BerlinFU as a class option.

Examples of using both the class and the package are provided; the PDF is visually identical, so the catalogue only lists one; the sources of the examples do of course differ.

documentation.details: Example of use of the class

name: powerdot-fuberlin

caption: A style package for Powerdot to provide the design of TULIP Lab

descriptions.text: powerdot-tuliplab is the LaTeX package used in TULIP Lab for presentation drafting. It comes with several sample .tex files so that you can quickly start working with it.

name: powerdot-tuliplab

topics.details: symbols or drawings to specify an object, including icons

caption: Typeset chemical formula diagrams

descriptions.text: ppchTeX is a separate module of the ConTeXt macro package for TeX. It seems to be in its final state (having not changed for more than 10 years).

name: ppchtex

caption: A postprocessor for PDF presentations

descriptions.text:
Ppower4 is post processor for PDF presentations created by pdf(La)TeX. It can be used to prepare presentations which include pages building up step by step when viewed with Acrobat Reader (v4 and later).

The software is written in Java.

name: ppower4

caption: Generate VMS help files from LaTeX 2.09 source

descriptions.text: The package provides a documentstyle, and a processor that converts documents in that style into VMS help format. The processor is written in Pascal (the VAX dialect, by the look of it).

name: pphlp

topics.details: convert TeX-ish sources to some other markup (than HTML)

caption: Prosper preview

descriptions.text: This class is used with LaTeX presentations using the prosper class. ppr-prv stands for ‘Prosper Preview’. The aim of this class is to produce a printable version of the slides written with Prosper, with two slides per page.

name: ppr-prv

caption: Good-looking slide decks à la PowerPoint (PPT)

descriptions.text: This LaTeX package helps you create slide decks as good-looking as with PowerPoint™, but more precise, uniform, and visually strict. Check this series of lectures fully designed with the use of this package.

documentation.details: Package documentation and example of use

name: ppt-slides

caption: Typeset articles for PracTeX

descriptions.text: The pracjourn class is used for typesetting articles in the PracTeX Journal. It is based on the article class with modifications to allow for more flexible front-matter and revision control, among other small changes.

name: pracjourn

caption: Example files for “Practical LaTeX”

descriptions.text: The bundle offers the source of the examples set in the book: “Practical LaTeX, Springer Verlag, New York, 2014.”

name: practical-latex

name: precattl

caption: Some macros for writing practical reports

descriptions.text: This package provides a handful of macros for writing up science practical reports.

name: practicalreports

caption: Mark preliminary copies with a line of information

descriptions.text: A LaTeX 2.09 style option that marks drafts by adding a line stating that it’s a draft to each page. The draftmark gives the status (which is controllable) and the date and time of processing.

name: prelim

caption: Allows the marking of preliminary versions of a document

descriptions.text: Puts text below the normal page content (the default text marks the document as draft and puts a timestamp on it). Can be used together with e.g. the vrsion, rcs and rcsinfo packages. Uses the everyshi package and can use the scrtime package from the koma-script bundle.

name: prelim2e

caption: Preprint macros

descriptions.text: Macros for preparing preprints (not clear whether this is “preprints-in-general”, or for some particular publication).

descriptions.text:
The bundle comprises:

  • authblk, which permits footnote style author/affiliation input in the \author command,
  • balance, to balance the end of \twocolumn pages,
  • figcaps, to send figure captions, etc., to end document,
  • fullpage, to set narrow page margins and set a fixed page style, and
  • sublabel, which permits counters to be subnumbered.

name: preprint

caption: Interactive editor and macro support for prerequisite charts

descriptions.text:
This package consists of prerex.sty, a LaTeX package for producing charts of course nodes linked by arrows representing pre- and co-requisites, and prerex, an interactive program for creating and editing chart descriptions. The implementation of prerex.sty uses PGF, so that it may be used equally happily with LaTeX or pdfLaTeX; prerex itself is written in C.

The package includes source code for a previewer application, a lightweight Qt-4 and poppler-based prerex-enabled PDF viewer.

name: prerex

caption: Examples from the book Presentationen mit LaTeX
