The provided macros have the same names as the original versions but start with an upper-case letter instead. The “long-form” macros, like \Makebox, can also be used as environments, but not the “short-form” macros, like \Mbox. However, normally the long form uses the short form anyway when no optional arguments are used.

name: realboxes

caption: Read, store and recall array-formatted data

descriptions.text:
The package allows the user to input formatted data into elements of a 2-D or 3-D array and to recall that data at will by individual cell number. The data can be but need not be numerical in nature. It can be, for example, formatted text.

While the package can be used for any application where indexed data is called for, the package proves particularly useful when elements of multiple arrays must be recallable and dynamically combined at time of compilation, rather than in advance.

name: readarray

caption: Provides GetFileInfo without the need to load the file

descriptions.text:
The package provides a \GetFileInfo command (as in the LaTeX standard doc package, but without the need to load the doc package). The package also provides new robust (expandable) variants of \GetFileInfo, even without loading the file itself (reading the file is stopped when the requisite information is found). So, for exaple, you can describe packages that are incompatible with each other or with packages that your document uses, or even report about class files (that are plainly not loadable).

Files examined in this way also enter the output of \listfiles.

The package is part of the fileinfo bundle.

name: readprov

topics.details: support for keeping track of document development

caption: Macros for real arithmetic calculations

descriptions.text: There are known problems with this package; an alternative is fp (a LaTeX package, only).

license.name: Do Not Sell Except by Arrangement

name: realcalc

caption: Put real hats on symbols instead of ^

descriptions.text:
This LaTeX package makes \hat put real hats on symbols.

The package depends on amsmath, calc, graphicx, ifthen, lcg, and stackengine.

name: realhats

topics.details: jokes, distractions, tongue-in-cheek packages, and other entertainment material

caption: Access OpenType subscript and superscript glyphs

descriptions.text:
This small package replaces \textsuperscript and \textsubscript commands by equivalent commands that use OpenType font features to access appropriate glyphs if possible.

The package also patches LaTeX’s default footnote command to use this new \textsuperscript for footnote symbols.

The package requires fontspec running on either XeLaTeX or LuaLaTeX.

The package holds functions that were once parts of the xltxtra package, which now loads realscripts by default.

name: realscripts

topics.details: position sub- and superscripts (left and right sides)

caption: Commands to typeset recursion theory papers

descriptions.text: This package is designed to help mathematicians publishing papers in the area of recursion theory (aka Computability Theory) easily use standard notation. This includes easy commands to denote Turing reductions, Turing functionals, c.e. sets, stagewise computations, forcing and syntactic classes.

name: rec-thy

caption: The “real” way to transpose a Matrix

copyright.owner: Lars Quentin, Matthew Scroggs, Adam Townsend

descriptions.text: With realtranspose you can notate the transposition of a matrix by rotating the symbols 90 degrees. This is a hommage to the realhats package.

name: realtranspose

topics.details: jokes, distractions, tongue-in-cheek packages, and other entertainment material

caption: Typeset recipes in note-card-sized boxes

descriptions.text: The recipecard class typesets recipes into note card sized boxes that can then be cut out and pasted on to note cards. The recipe then looks elegant and fits in the box of recipes.

name: recipecard

caption: A LaTeX class to typeset recipes

descriptions.text: The layout design is relatively straightforward (and traditional: see ‘sample output’ under ‘documentation’); the class uses the Bookman and the BrushScript-Italic fonts.

name: recipe

caption: Package to display recorder fingering diagrams

descriptions.text: This package provides support for generating and displaying fingering diagrams for baroque fingering recorders and the tin whistle. Standard fingerings are provided for recorders in both C and F, and the tin whistle in D, along with methods to create and display alternate fingerings for trills, etc.

name: recorder-fingering

caption: Typeset 5.5" x 8" recipes for browsing or printing

descriptions.text:
This is a LaTeX2e class for typesetting recipes. It is designed for typesetting one or two recipes per page, with dimensions of 5.5" x 8.5".

The hyperlinked table of contents (ToC) and page numbers make browsing recipes convenient, and the pages can be joined together or printed two per sheet to normal letterpaper easily.

The size was chosen to work in half-page 3-ring binder cover sheets.

name: recipebook

caption: Recycle top matter

descriptions.text: Saves the arguments of \author and \title for reference (after \maketitle) in a document. (\maketitle simply disposes of the information, in the standard classes and some others.)

name: rectopma

caption: Conditional macro, etc., definitions

descriptions.text: Defines commands ewdef, ewgdef and ewlet that warn the user if a command is redefined using them (if operating under LaTeX, ewcommand is similarly modified). In addition ewif, ewbox, ewcount, ewdimen, ewtoks are modified to detect an error if a conditional or register name is reused.

name: redefine

caption: A Hebrew font

descriptions.text: The font is in Metafont format; a version of it seems to appear in the HebTeX distribution.

name: redis

topics.details: documentation in and support for typesetting Hebrew

caption: A font providing the "recyclable" logo

descriptions.text: This single-character font is provided as Metafont source, and in Adobe Type 1 format. It is accompanied by a trivial LaTeX package to use the logo at various sizes.

name: recycle

topics.details: fonts with specific small application areas
font available in Adobe Type 1 format

caption: Menu-based editor

descriptions.text: REdit (written in Turbo Pascal for DOS) aims to simplify work with LaTeX with menus to insert commands. This should be convenient for beginners, in particular.

name: REdit

topics.details: editor designed (or adapted) for use with (La)TeX

caption: Check references (in figures, table, equations, etc)

descriptions.text: The package checks references in a document, looking for numbered but unlabelled equations, for labels which are not used in the text, for unused bibliography references. It can also display label names in text near corresponding numbers of equations and/or bibliography references.

name: refcheck

topics.details: support for package or document debugging

caption: Counter operations with label references

descriptions.text:
Provides commands \setcounterref and \addtocounterref which use the section (or whatever) number from the reference as the value to put into the counter, as in: 

      ...\label{sec:foo}
      ...
      \setcounterref{foonum}{sec:foo}
Commands \setcounterpageref and \addtocounterpageref do the corresponding thing with the page reference of the label.

No .ins file is distributed; process the .dtx with plain TeX to create one.

name: refcount

caption: Define named items and provide back-references with that name

descriptions.text: The package provides commands to define enumerable items with a number and a long name, which can be referenced later with the name or just the short form. For instance, “Milestone M1: Specification created” can be defined and later on be referenced with ‘M1’ or ‘M1 (“Specification created”)’. The text in the references is derived from the definition and also rendered as hyperlink to the definition.

name: refenums

caption: Convert a BibTeX bibliography to refer format
name: refer

topics.details: convert one format of file to another

caption: Bibliographic software supporting LaTeX/BibTeX

descriptions.text: The package comprises bibliographic software supporting preparation of scientific manuscripts, storage of bibliographic data of articles in periodicals, books and articles in books. The package supports the TeX/LaTeX/BibTeX setup as well as commercial word processors. Bibliographic data in the MEDLINE format may be imported. References may be retrieved by keywords, authors’ or editors’ names, date of publication, strings in the title of an article, in a book title or in journal names. Lists of references may be supplied in a (user-defined) formats.

name: references

topics.details: derive BibTeX data from resources other than BibTeX libraries

caption: Convert between refer format and BibTeX format

descriptions.text:
Various tools, mostly packaged as Unix ‘shar’ archives:

  • ref2bib, an awk script for converting Refer format bibliographies to BibTeX format;
  • refer2bibtex, a Perl script for the same conversion;
  • refer.bst, a tool to convert a BibTeX database to Refer format, using BibTeX itself;
  • tex2refer, an awk-based script for the same conversion;
  • refer-to-bibtex, a GNU-emacs program to convert Refer format bibliographies to BibTeX format;
  • tib-to-bibtex, a C program to convert tib format bibliographies to BibTeX format.

name: refer-tools

caption: Techniques for reflecting graphics

descriptions.text: The package provides a macro for reflecting images, in a number of different ways, in pursuit of “more striking” graphics in a document.

name: reflectgraphics

caption: Format technical reference manuals

descriptions.text: Document classes (report- and article-style) for writing technical reference manuals. It offers a wide left margin for notes to the reader, like some of the manuals distributed by Adobe.

name: refman

caption: Refresh PDF files "remotely"

descriptions.text:
Refreshpdf is an applescript that will ensure the current copy of a PDF file is open in Acrobat reader; this may require that it instructs reader to close and re-open the file.

Users of non-Macintosh X11-based systems may use the commands from the xpdfopen package.

name: refreshpdf

topics.details: view, or control viewing of, PDF

caption: Advanced formatting of cross references

descriptions.text: The package provides a consistent way of producing references throughout a project. Enough flexibility is provided to make local changes to a single reference. The user can configure their own setup. The package offers a direct interface to varioref (for use, for example, in large projects such as a series of books, or a multivolume thesis written as a series of documents), and name references from the nameref package may be incorporated with ease. For large projects such as a series of books or a multi volume thesis, written as freestanding documents, a facility is provided to interface to the xr package for external document references.

name: refstyle

caption: Display the allocation status of the TeX registers

descriptions.text: Adds a macro \rgcounts which displays the allocation status of the TeX registers. The display is written into the .log file as it is a bit verbose. An automatic call to \rgcounts is done at \begin{document} and \end{document}.

name: regcount

topics.details: support for package or document debugging

caption: High level patching of commands

descriptions.text: The package generalises the macro patching commands provided by P. Lehmann’s etoolbox. The difference between this package and its sibling xpatch is that this package sports a very powerful \regexpatchcmd based on the l3regex module of the LaTeX3 experimental packages.

name: regexpatch

caption: Typeset programmable elements in digital hardware (registers)

descriptions.text:
This package is designed for typesetting the programmable elements in digital hardware, i.e., registers. Such registers typically have many fields and can be quite wide; they are thus a challenge to typeset in a consistent manner. Register is similar in some aspects to the bytefield and bitpattern packages. Anyone doing hardware documentation using LaTeX should examine those packages.

Register requires version 2001/07/25 or newer of the float package.

An example Perl module and script are provided, to convert the register specifications into structures suitable for, say, a pre-silicon test environment.

name: register

topics.details: typesetting associated with engineering of whatever sort

caption: Information about register use

descriptions.text: The package will report number of used registers (counter, dimen, skip, muskip, box, token, input, output, math families, languages, insertions), and will compare the number to the maximum available number of such registers.

name: regstats

topics.details: support for package or document debugging

caption: Typeset scholarly editions

descriptions.text:
A package for typesetting scholarly critical editions, replacing the established ledmac and eledmac packages. Ledmac itself was a LaTeX port of the plain TeX EDMAC macros.

The package supports indexing by page and by line numbers, and simple tabular- and array-style environments.

The package is distributed with the related reledpar package.

name: reledmac

caption: Set the font size relative to the current font size

descriptions.text: The basic command of the package is \relsize, whose argument is a number of \magsteps to change size; from this are defined commands \larger, \smaller, \textlarger, etc.

name: relsize

caption: A "relaxed" font encoding

descriptions.text: LaTeX package providing a relaxed font encoding to make available to a font designer more slots for insertion of ligatures and accented characters.

name: relenc

topics.details: support for font development, testing and characterisation

caption: Typeset scholarly editions in parallel texts

descriptions.text:
Reledpar is the replacement for the ledpar and the eledpar packages; it provides parallel-text typesetting (either in parallel columns, or on opposing pages), for the reledmac package.

The package is available as part of the reledmac distribution.

name: reledpar

caption: Remove from counter-reset lists

descriptions.text:
Defines an internal command \@removefromreset, which does the opposite of the (LaTeX internal) \@addtoreset.

The package is one of a collection of fragments designed for use by package writers and others.

name: removefr

caption: Remove counters from reset list

descriptions.text:
\@removefromreset is a companion to the standard \@addtoreset command which allows counters to be removed from the reset list of a controlling counter.

This package is now obsolete as its functionality has been incorporated into the LaTeX format, but it is still distributed as part of the carlisle bundle.

name: remreset

caption: Draw Reo Channels and Circuits

descriptions.text: The package defines macros and other utilities to design Reo Circuits. The package requires PGF/TikZ support.

name: reotex

caption: Multiple versions from the same content

descriptions.text: The package sets up ‘comment’ environments, called renditions; each rendition is thought of as a version of the basic content of the document that includes it.

name: renditions

caption: MetaPost macros for secondary school mathematics teachers

descriptions.text:
This package provides MetaPost macros for drawing secondary school mathematics figures in a coordinate system:

  • axis, grids
  • points, vectors
  • functions (curves, tangents, integrals, sequences)
  • statistic diagrams
  • plane geometry (polygons, circles)
  • arrays and game boards

name: repere

topics.details: support for teachers and teaching administrators

caption: Repeat items in an index after a page or column break

descriptions.text: This Package repeats item of an index if a page or column break occurs within a list of subitems. This helps to find out to which main item a subitem belongs.

name: repeatindex

caption: Repeat execution of macros

descriptions.text:
Repeat is a really general loop macro, which can be nested to arbitrary depth without any grouping or such.

Documentation appears as comments at the start of the package file.

name: repeat

caption: Checksum based rerun checks on auxiliary files

descriptions.text: The package provides additional rerun warnings if some auxiliary files have changed. It is based on MD5 checksum provided by pdfTeX, LuaTeX, XeTeX.

name: rerunfilecheck

caption: A resumé class

descriptions.text: An update, for current LaTeX, of a LaTeX 2.09 document style.

license.name: Do Not Sell Except by Arrangement

name: res

caption: Control how text gets copied from a PDF file

descriptions.text: The repltext package exposes to LaTeX a relatively obscure PDF feature: replacement text. When replacement text is specified for a piece of text, it is the replacement text, not the typeset text that is copied and pasted.

name: repltext

caption: Re-scan tokens with synctex information

descriptions.text: Allow users to execute saved code to typeset text while preserving SyncTeX information.

name: rescansync

caption: Automatically resize overly large equations

descriptions.text:
Equations that are too large are resized to fit the available space. The environment ‘gather’ of package amsmath is supported. Also the environments ‘equation’ and ‘displaymath’ are redefined using ‘gather’ and its starred version.

The package is part of the oberdiek bundle.

name: resizegather

caption: Packages "required" of a LaTeX distribution

descriptions.text:
These are packages that the LaTeX team have declared are ‘required’ of any LaTeX distribution—in the sense that any package writer is entitled to assume the presence of these packages in support of her package.

The set comprises:

  • AmsLaTeX, mathematical support from the AMS;
  • The babel package for multilingual typesetting;
  • Standard LaTeX support for using Cyrillic alphabet fonts;
  • The standard LaTeX graphics and colour packages;
  • Basic support for using common Adobe Type 1 fonts with LaTeX—the “psnfss”; and
  • Basic “LaTeX latex-tools”.

For distribution details, see the individual packages’ catalogue entries.

name: required

topics.details: Root directory of a (sub-)tree of the archive

caption: Typeset a multi-chapter report

descriptions.text: The class provides typesetting rather similar to that of the book class, omitting some features relevant only when professional book-publishing is to be used.

name: report

caption: Measure restriction symbol in LaTeX

descriptions.text: This package provides a simple macro \resmes that prints the measure restriction symbol.

name: resmes

caption: Work on linear systems using xint or pyluatex

descriptions.text:
This package provides some commands (in French) to perform calculations on small (2x2 or 3x3 or 4x4) linear systems, with xint or pyluatex:

  • \DetMatrice or \DetMatricePY to diplay the determinant of a matrix (with formatting options);
  • \MatriceInverse or \MatriceInversePY to display the invers of a matrix (with formatting options) ;
  • \SolutionSysteme or \SolutionSystemePY to display the solution of a linear system (with formatting options);
  • …

name: ResolSysteme

topics.details: package will use LuaTeX facilities if available

caption: Typeset articles for the journal Res Philosophica

descriptions.text:
The bundle provides a class for typesetting articles for the journal Res Philosophica.

This work was commissioned by the Saint Louis University.

name: resphilosophica

caption: Typeset a resume both in English and Chinese

descriptions.text: A LaTeX document class to typeset a resume or CV both in English and Chinese with more ease and flexibility.

name: resumecls

caption: Plain TeX macros for resumés

descriptions.text: A set of macros is provided, together with an file that offers an example of use.

name: resumemac

topics.details: extensions to Plain TeX for higher-level constructs

caption: Describing a rest api

descriptions.text:
This LaTeX package provides macros to describe rest apis for documentation purposes. The endpoints can hold the following information:

  • method
  • description
  • path parameter
  • request body and content type
  • response body, content type and status code

name: rest-api

caption: Semi-automatic grid typesetting

descriptions.text: returntogrid offers a few commands to get something like an simple, semi-automatic grid typesetting. It does more or less what the existing gridset package does. The main differences to gridset are that returntogrid works also with LuaLaTeX and that it has also a command to do some horizontal movements to get to “tab” positions.

name: returntogrid

topics.details: typeset, snapping lines of text to a grid

caption: Playing Reversi in TeX

descriptions.text: Following the lead of xii.tex, this little (938 characters) program that plays Reversi. (The program incorporates some primitive AI.)

name: reverxii

topics.details: TeX code as a source of humour
process game diagrams, gamebooks, and other amusements

caption: Reverse enumerate

descriptions.text: Provides a reverse-enumerate environment (revnumerate) in which items are numbered in reverse order.

name: revnum

caption: Hacks to make writing quantum papers for revtex4-1 less painful

descriptions.text: This package provides a number of useful hacks to solve common annoyances with the revtex4-1 package, and to define notation in common use within quantum information. In doing so, it imports and configures a number of commonly-available and used packages, and where reasonable, provides fallbacks. It also warns when users try to load packages which are known to be incompatible with revtex4-1.

name: revquantum

caption: Styles for various Physics Journals

descriptions.text: Includes styles for American Physical Society, American Institute of Physics, and Optical Society of America. The distribution consists of the RevTeX class itself, and several support packages.

name: revtex

caption: Styles for various Physics Journals (old version)

descriptions.text: This is an old version of revtex, and is kept as a courtesy to users having difficulty with the incompatibility of that latest version.

name: revtex4-0

caption: Generate BibTeX entries for IETF RFCs

descriptions.text:
The script translates an RFC index file from the IETF to a BibTeX file. It is probably GNU gawk-specific.

Please note that this package is now superceded by ietfbibs.

name: rfc2bib

topics.details: derive BibTeX data from resources other than BibTeX libraries

caption: Styles for various Physics Journals

descriptions.text: This is an old version of revtex, and is kept as a courtesy to users having difficulty with the incompatibility of that latest version.

name: revtex4-1

caption: Ruby font installer library

descriptions.text: The Ruby font installer library (RFIL) is another attempt on font installation for TeX fonts. It consists of a set of example programs and several libraries for doing font related tasks, such as read/write tfm, afm, vf and enc files, creating font metrics, doing calculations and the like. The software is all written in Ruby.

name: rfil

topics.details: process fonts for use with TeX (includes installation)

caption: Tables of RGB colour parameters

descriptions.text: The Linux rgb.txt (distributed as part of X11 distributions) is mechanically converted to a LaTeX file, which has been compiled to make the distribution. For details of the procedure, and sources, see the package’s home page.

name: RGB

caption: Common code for documentation of the author’s packages

descriptions.text: This package combines several other packages and defines additional macros and environments for documenting LaTeX code. The package mainly serves the purpose of combining the preferences used in the author’s own package documentations. However, others can use the package as well. Compatibility between versions cannot be guaranteed, however.

name: rgltxdoc

topics.details: macros and tools for preparing documentation

caption: Drawing ribbon proofs

descriptions.text:
The package provides a way to draw “ribbon proofs” in LaTeX.

A ribbon proof is a diagrammatic representation of a mathematical proof that a computer program meets its specification. These diagrams are more human-readable, more scalable, and more easily modified than the corresponding textual proofs.

name: ribbonproofs

caption: Create rich text strings

descriptions.text:
The richtext package is used to create rich text strings that can, in turn,
     be inserted into the RV (and V) keys of text field. 
     Currently, only the eforms package supports the RV key.

name: richtext

topics.details: create pdf form fields, use form fields as an integral part of the package

caption: Malayalam fonts by Rachana Institute of Typography (RIT)

copyright.owner: CV Radhakrishnan and Rachana Institute of Typography

descriptions.text:
The RIT font collection provides versions of ten font families in Malayalam (the language spoken in the southern Indian state of Kerala) script in TrueType and WOFF2 formats. The fonts are:

  • RIT Rachana
  • RIT Panmana
  • RIT MeeraNew
  • RIT TN Joy
  • RIT Karuna
  • RIT Keralayeeam
  • RIT Sundar
  • RIT Uroob
  • RIT Ezhuthu
  • RIT Kutty

A LaTeX package rit-fonts.sty that will help users to make use of these Unicode-compliant fonts in LaTeX documents with XeTeX or LuaTeX is also provided.

name: rit-fonts

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other font support
fonts for languages of the Indian subcontinent

caption: Support for use of \parshape in LaTeX

descriptions.text: The package provides macros and environments that relieve the programmer of some of the difficulties of using \parshape in LaTeX macros. It does not actually calculate shapes in the way that the shapepar package does.

name: rjlparshap

caption: Rewrite labels in EPS graphics

descriptions.text:
A macro package for use with epsf.tex which allows PostScript labels in an Encapsulated PostScript file to be replaced by TeX labels. The package provides commands \relabel (simply replace a PostScript string), \adjustrelabel (replace a PostScript string, with position adjustment), and \extralabel (add a label at given coordinates).

You can, if you so choose, use the facilities of the labelfig package in place of using \extralabel.

name: rlepsf

caption: Create rich media annotations in a PDF file

descriptions.text:
The package is part of the AeB Pro family of packages. It creates rich media annotations, in which MOV, MP4, M4V, 3GP, 3G2, and MP3 files can be played.

Rich media annotation is a feature of Acrobat/Adobe Reader version 9. Acrobat Pro and Distiller version 9.0 or later are required to build a document, and Adobe Reader 9.0 or later is needed to activate the annotation and play the media.

name: rmannot

topics.details: convert PostScript to PDF using Adobe Distiller
create pdf form fields, use form fields as an integral part of the package

caption: Remove incorrect ligatures in German documents

descriptions.text:
Ligatures, which are a pleasing feature of TeX's use of fonts, should not be placed in German words between the word stem and the rest of the word.

The rmligs package is a perl script that takes input in ISO 8859-1 or -15, UTF-8 or LaTeX-style umlaut encodings ("a, "u, etc.), and inserts a break where an inappropriate ligature would appear. So, for example, ‘Auflage’ will be changed to ‘Auf"|lage’, which typesets in a typographically correct fashion.

name: rmligs

topics.details: input encoding support for TeX engines

caption: A package to help change page layout parameters in LaTeX

descriptions.text: The package lets you change page layout parameters in small steps over a range of values using options. It can set \textwidth appropriately for the main fount, and ensure that the text fits inside the printable area of a printer. An rmpage-formatted document can be typeset identically without rmpage after a single cut and paste operation. Local configuration can set defaults: for all documents; and by class, by printer, and by paper size. The geometry package is better if you want to set page layout parameters to particular measurements.

name: rmpage

caption: Repeating of math operator at the broken line and the new line in inline equations

descriptions.text: Repeating of math operators at the broken line and the new line in inline equations is used in Cyrillic mathematical typography (Russian for example), but unfortunately LaTeX does not provide such an option. This package solves the problem by extending ideas described in M. I. Grinchuk “TeX and Russian Traditions of Typesetting”, TUGboat 17(4) (1996) 385 and supports most of LaTeX mathematical packages. See the documentation for details.

name: rmathbr

caption: Use a roman font for theorem statements

descriptions.text:
Modifies the theorem environment of LaTeX 2.09 to cause the statement of a theorem to appear in \rm.

LaTeX 2e users should use a more general package (such as ntheorem) to support this requirement.

name: rmthm

caption: Convert from Runoff to LaTeX

descriptions.text: A (Pascal) program to translate (Digital Standard) Runoff into LaTeX. VAX executables for VMS v6.1 are provided.

name: rnototex

topics.details: import files in a non-TeX (or different TeX) format

caption: A fun demo of AcroTeX eDucation Bundle facilities

descriptions.text: Robot man is distributed as part of the AeB Pro bundle (just for fun); the source is attached to the PDF file.

name: Robot Man

topics.details: process game diagrams, gamebooks, and other amusements

caption: Cache anything (TikZ, python, ...) in a robust, efficient and pure way

descriptions.text:
This package provides a LaTeX library to cache anything (TikZ, python, ...), in a robust, efficient and pure way. We also provide a template system with placeholders to provide configurable templates.

For more information, see the documentation and the github repository.

name: robust-externalize

caption: TikZ powered LaTeX package to draw parameterized 2D robot arms

descriptions.text: This LaTeX package uses TikZ to draw parameterized 2D robot arms, for example to be used in educational material.

name: robotarm

caption: Support for the Roboto family of fonts

descriptions.text: This package provides LaTeX, pdfLaTeX, XeLaTeX and LuaLaTeX support for the Roboto Sans, Roboto Condensed, Roboto Mono, Roboto Slab and Roboto Serif families of fonts, designed by Christian Robertson and Greg Gazdowicz for Google.

name: roboto

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other font support
font designed for use as body font for Latin-based script documents
font providing LaTeX T1 encoding support
font with adaptations to several languages
font available in Adobe Type 1 format
font for Greek (archaic, classical and modern)

caption: Declare robust command, with \newcommand checks

descriptions.text: The package merely provides a variation of \DeclareRobustCommand, which checks for the existence of a command before declaring it robust.

name: robustcommand

caption: Create index with pagerefs

descriptions.text:
Third parties often change the page numbers without rerunning makeindex. One would like to make the page numbers in the index entries more robust.

This bundle provides robustindex.sty and robustglossary.sty, which use the \pageref mechanism to maintain correct page numbers.

name: robustindex

caption: A font with the images of the counties of Romania

descriptions.text:
This package provides a Type 1 font with images of the 42 counties of Romania, constructed using a general method which is described in detail in the documentation.

The package name is an abbreviation of “judeţele României” (= counties of Romania).

name: rojud

topics.details: fonts designed more for fun than for actual use
font available in Adobe Type 1 format

caption: Write roman number with "bars"

descriptions.text:
‘Bars’, in the present context, are lines above and below text that abut with the text. Barred roman numerals are sometimes found in publications.

The package provides a function that prints barred roman numerals (converting arabic numerals if necessary).

The package also provides a predicate \ifnumeric.

name: romanbar

caption: Typesetting roman page numbers

descriptions.text: The package romanbar allows to typeset roman numbers with bars. This package allows you to use those roman numbers as page number.

name: romanbarpagenumber

topics.details: control sequence and typesettting of page numbers

caption: LaTeX support for Romanian

descriptions.text: A LaTeX2e package for typesetting Romanian in a plain TeX environment. For LaTeX use, the package has been superseded by the Romanian option of babel.

name: romaniantex

topics.details: extensions to Plain TeX for higher-level constructs

caption: Romande ADF fonts and LaTeX support

descriptions.text:
Romande ADF is a serif font family with oldstyle figures, designed as a substitute for Times, Tiffany or Caslon. The family currently includes upright, italic and small-caps shapes in each of regular and demi-bold weights and an italic script in regular. The support package renames the fonts according to the Karl Berry fontname scheme and defines four families. Two of these primarily provide access to the “standard” or default characters while the “alternate” families support alternate characters, additional ligatures and the long s. The included package files provide access to these features in LaTeX as explained in the documentation.

The LaTeX support requires the nfssext-cfr and the xkeyval packages.

name: romandeadf

topics.details: font available in Adobe Type 1 format

caption: Roman page numbers negative

descriptions.text: Causes the page numbers in the DVI file (as defined by \count0) to be negative when roman pagenumbering is in effect.

name: romanneg

topics.details: control sequence and typesettting of page numbers

caption: Generate roman numerals instead of arabic digits

descriptions.text: The romannum package changes LaTeX generated numbers to be printed with roman numerals instead of arabic digits. It requires the stdclsdv package. Users of the bookhands fonts may find this package useful.

name: romannum

caption: Rotate TeX boxes

descriptions.text:
Plain TeX macros to rotate boxes, using \special commands appropriate for dvips.

Users should note that the Plain TeX adaptation of the LaTeX graphics package provides this functionality, with more flexibility as to output capabilities.

name: rotate

topics.details: rotate typeset objects on their page

caption: Create ROR symbols which links to the given ROR-IDs

descriptions.text: This package provides an easy to use command. It takes an URL of the Research Organization Registry (ROR) as argument and creates a ROR symbol which links to the given URL — very similar to the orcidlink package from which it is derived. The symbol itself always fits with the choosen font size.

name: rorlink

topics.details: create symbols, rather than select from a font

caption: Using the free Rosario fonts with LaTeX

descriptions.text: The package provides the files required to use the Rosario fonts with LaTeX. Rosario is a set of four fonts provided by Héctor Gatti, Adobe Typekit & Omnibus-Type Team under the Open Font License (OFL), version 1.1. The fonts are copyright (c) 2012-2015, Omnibus-Type.

name: rosario

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other font support
font available in Adobe Type 1 format

caption: Box rotation macros for Textures

descriptions.text:
Provides rotation macros specific to the (commercial) Textures distribution.

Modern users are perhaps better advised to use the (LaTeX) graphics package, or generic relatives, such as its Plain graphics adaptation.

name: rotate-textures

caption: Rotation tools, including rotated full-page floats

descriptions.text:
A package built on the standard LaTeX graphics package to perform all the different sorts of rotation one might like, including complete figures and tables with their captions.

If you want continuous text (i.e., more than one page) set in landscape mode, use the lscape package instead. The rotating packages only deals in rotated boxes (or floats, which are themselves boxes), and boxes always stay on one page.

If you need to use the facilities of the float in the same document, load rotating.sty via rotfloat, which smooths the path between the rotating and float packages.

The package is now part of the latex-graphics bundle, which is one of the collections in the LaTeX ‘required’ set of packages.

name: rotating

topics.details: rotate typeset objects on their page

caption: Perform simple rotation cyphers

descriptions.text:
The package defines a command \EdefRot that defines a macro (whose name is given as an argument) to the rotation of the given string. Available rotations are ROT13 (for letters), ROT5 (for digits), ROT18 (for digits and letters together) and ROT47 (for all ASCII characters).

The package is part of the oberdiek bundle.

name: rotchiffre

caption: Rotate floats

descriptions.text: The float package provides commands to define new floats of various styles (plain, boxed, ruled, and userdefined ones); the rotating package provides new environments (sidewaysfigure and sidewaystable) which are rotated by 90 or 270 degrees. But what about new rotated floats, e.g. a rotated ruled one? This package makes this possible; it builds a bridge between the two packages and extends the commands from the float package to define rotated versions of the new floats, too.

name: rotfloat

caption: Rotunda manuscript book-hand font

descriptions.text:
The rotunda and allrtnd packages provide Metafont fonts based on the Rotunda manuscript book-hand used between the 13th and 15th century AD. The font consists of lower- and uppercase letters, and digits, with some appropriate period punctuation marks. Both normal and bold versions are provided.

This is one of a set of manuscript fonts. Access to the docmfp package is desirable but not essential.

name: rotunda

topics.details: fonts of scripts used for manuscript books
font for gothic or blackletter shapes

caption: Typeset sets of pages upside-down and backwards

descriptions.text: The rotpages package allows you to format documents where small sets of pages are rotated by 180 degrees and rearranged, so that they can be read by turning the printed copy upside-down. It was developed for collecting exercises and solutions: using the package, you can print the exercise text normally and the solutions rotated.

name: rotpages

topics.details: layout of objects on the page

caption: Draw a “question wheel” (roue de questions)

descriptions.text: This package helps to produce a game for students: It is a wheel displaying questions, with hidden answers inside.

name: RoueQuestions

topics.details: process game diagrams, gamebooks, and other amusements

caption: MetaPost macros for highly configurable rounded rectangles (optionally with text)

descriptions.text: The roundrect macros for MetaPost provide ways to produce rounded rectangles, which may or may not contain a title bar or text (the title bar may itself contain text). They are extremely configurable.

name: roundrect

caption: Round boxes in LaTeX

descriptions.text: This package implements a command \roundbox that can be used, in LaTeX, for producing boxes, framed with rounded corners.

name: roundbox

topics.details: highlighting typeset material, fancy frames, watermarks, etc.

caption: Typesetting old-school Dungeons and Dragons modules

descriptions.text:
This package provides a LaTeX class for authors of Role-Playing Game adventure modules for Dungeons and Dragons and similar games. The typesetting is reminiscent of the “old-school” modules published in the early 1980s and attempts to recapture the look and feel of those classic adventures.

The package also includes the Basic Stats style, which contains stat blocks for every monster from the Moldvay/Cook/Marsh Basic/Expert version of the game.

name: rpg-module

topics.details: process game diagrams, gamebooks, and other amusements

caption: Place text over PSTricks objects without obscuring background colors

descriptions.text:
You create a PSTricks figure with regions filled with various colors. You add some lines over the colors. Now you want to add some labels. You’d like these labels to cover the lines but not the background colors. This style provides a way of doing that.

The package is now superseded by package pst-rputover by the same author and Thomas Söll

name: rputover

topics.details: package using PStricks for graphical output

caption: Redefines the plain pagestyle

descriptions.text: The package redefines the LaTeX pagestyle plain so the page numbers appear on the lower corners. The package was superseded by the fancyhdr package and is no longer supported.

name: rplain

caption: Linguistic tree diagrams for Role and Reference Grammar (RRG) with LaTeX

descriptions.text:
A set of LaTeX macros that makes it easy to produce linguistic tree diagrams suitable for Role and Reference Grammar (RRG). This package allows the construction of trees with crossing lines, as is required by this theory for many languages. There is no known limit on number of tree nodes or levels.

Requires the pst-node and pst-tree LaTeX packages.

name: RRGtrees

caption: BibTeX style for use with RSC journals

descriptions.text: The rsc package provides a BibTeX style in accordance with the requirements of the Royal Society of Chemistry. It was originally based on the file pccp.bst, but also implements a number of styles from the achemso package. The package is now a stub for the chemstyle package, which the author developed to unify the writing of articles with a chemistry content.

name: rsc

caption: Drawing rhetorical structure analysis diagrams in LaTeX

descriptions.text:
This package is of interest for people working in linguistics and language technology.

Drawing rhetorical analyses is no fun when you need to change and update diagrams as you refine your work, or, more importantly, if a lot of analyses are to be drawn. Voila, there we go: This package enables us to typeset beautiful diagrams with no hassle. It is oriented towards the style of the diagrams shown in Mann&Thompson's Rhetorical Structure Theory and subsequent works. This package works perfectly with (LaTeX) and pdfLaTeX and does not require any special PostScript capabilities in the output side.

name: RST

caption: Ralph Smith's Formal Script font

descriptions.text:
The fonts provide uppercase ‘formal’ script letters for use as symbols in scientific and mathematical typesetting (in contrast to the informal script fonts such as that used for the ‘calligraphic’ symbols in the TeX maths symbol font). The fonts are provided as Metafont source, and as derived Adobe Type 1 format.

LaTeX support, for using these fonts in mathematics, is available via one of the packages calrsfs and mathrsfs.

name: rsfs

topics.details: font available in Adobe Type 1 format

descriptions.text: The package mediates interaction between LaTeX and R; it allows LaTeX to set R’s parameters, and provides code to read R output.

The output is quite similar to that from the Adobe Mathematical Pi script font.

name: rsfso

metrics, macro incantations and other font support

descriptions.text: The package converts Rich Text Format (RTF) files to LaTeX2e, saving any image files it finds. Visual formatting, such as ruler positions, tabs, paragraph indentations, etc., is ignored. Users should expect the LaTeX output to need some manual editing; the result is not a reproduction of what you see on the WYSIWYG screen.

name: rtf2latex2e

descriptions.text: A translator that uses an existing RTF reader, to produce TeX source (not LaTeX).

name: rtf2tex

topics.details: convert one format of file to another

caption: Draw Real-Time scheduling (GANTT) charts

descriptions.text:
The package offers facilities for drawing GANTT charts (chronograms). Such charts may be used as real-time timing diagrams, often needed for preparing articles, lectures and presentations in Real-Time Scheduling research.

The package relies on packages PSTricks and multido.

name: rtsched

caption: Input encoding with fallback procedures

descriptions.text:
The rtkinenc package is functionally similar to the standard LaTeX package inputenc: both set up active characters so that an input character outside the range of 7-bit visible ASCII is coverted into one or more corresponding LaTeX commands. The main difference lies in that rtkinenc allows the user to specify a fallback procedure to use when the text command corresponding to some input character isn't available.

Names of commands in rtkinenc have been selected so that it can read inputenc encoding definition files, and the aim is that rtkinenc should be backwards compatible with inputenc. rtkinenc is not a new version of inputenc though, nor is it part of standard LaTeX.

For an example of how rtkinenc is used, the user may look at the tclldoc class.

name: rtkinenc

topics.details: input encoding support for TeX engines

caption: Document Rubik cube configurations and rotation sequences

descriptions.text:
The bundle provides four packages:

  • rubikcube provides commands for typesetting Rubik cubes and their transformations,
  • rubiktwocube provides commands for typesetting Rubik twocubes and their transformations,
  • rubikrotation which can process a sequence of Rubik rotation moves, with the help of a Perl package executed via \write18 (shell escape) commands, and
  • rubikpatterns, a collection of well known patterns and their associated rotation sequences.

The package provides LaTeX commands and macros for typesetting Rubik cube (3x3x3) notation, configurations, and rotation sequences, using the TikZ graphic language.

The package serves as part of the rubik bundle.

topics.details: problems and puzzles, and their solutions

name: ruhyphen

caption: Typeset Rubik TwoCubes and move notation

descriptions.text:
The package provides LaTeX commands and macros for typesetting Rubik TwoCube (2x2x2) notation, configurations, and rotation sequences, using the TikZ graphic language.

The package serves as part of the rubik bundle.

name: rubiktwocube

topics.details: problems and puzzles, and their solutions

descriptions.text: These are still further developments of the fabled Plain TeX ‘tables’ macros, but are substantially rewritten from the original.

name: ruled-tables

caption: Provide LaTeX3 commands for typesetting rules

descriptions.text:
The package provides rule commands in a structure appropriate for use in LaTeX3 documents.

The package is distributed as part of the GS1 distribution.

name: rule-d

descriptions.text: The file processes to produce (real) rulers; the author suggests printing them on transparent plastic and trimming for use as a “real” ruler. The rule widths are 0.05mm, which can be challenging for (old) laser printers.

name: ruler

caption: Draw rulers around a box

descriptions.text: This is a LaTeX package for drawing rulers around a box. This might be useful when showing the absolute size of something in electronic documents, or designating the relative scale in printed materials.

name: rulerbox

caption: A TikZ library for straight-edge and compass diagrams

descriptions.text: The package defines some commands and styles to support drawing straight-edge and compass diagrams with TikZ.

name: rulercompass

caption: Execute foreign source code and embed the result in the pdf file

descriptions.text:
This LaTeX package executes programming source codes (including all command line tools) from within LaTeX and embeds the output in the resulting .pdf file. Many programming languages can be easily used and any command-line executable can be invoked when preparing the .pdf file from a .tex file.

It is however recommended to use this package in server-mode together with the Python talk2stat package. Currently, this server-mode supports Julia, MatLab, Python, and R. More languages will be added. For more details and usage examples, refer to the package’s github repository.

name: runcode

topics.details: call external code and process the result

caption: Windows program to run TeX variant and various utils as needed

You can ask it to delete temporary files if nothing went wrong.

name: runtex

caption: Fonts for Anglo-Saxon futharc script

descriptions.text: Fonts and macros for runic writing. The futharks script remained in use in England until just after printing was established. This is one of a series of archaic fonts.

fonts reproducing archaic scripts or inscriptions

caption: LaTeX in Russian, without babel

descriptions.text:
The package aims to facilitate Russian typesetting (based on input using MicroSoft Code Page 1251). Russian hyphenation is selected, and various mathematical commands are set up in Russian style.

Furthermore all Cyrillic letters’ catcodes are set to “letter”, so that commands with Cyrillic letters in their names may be defined.

caption: A Lua script running LaTeX document files with TeX-style shebang

descriptions.text:
In short, a TeX-style shebang (%#!) is a special kind of TeX comment that you include in your TeX/LaTeX document file to tell the operating system’s shell how to run the file for the rest of the file: 

      %#!lualatex foo.tex
      \documentclass{article}
      \begin{document}
        Hello, {\LaTeX} World!

        Happy {\TeX}ing.
      \end{document}

If you are using a TeX-style shebang, it must appear on the line that matched 20 lines or less in your LaTeX document, and it has to start with a TeX comment symbol (%) followed by a hash sign (#) and an exclamation mark (!), colloquially known as the bang, hence the name shebang for TeX/LaTeX.

name: runtexshebang

descriptions.text:
The rustic and allrust packages provide Metafont fonts based on the Rustic manuscript book-hand used between the 1st and 6th century AD. The font consists of majuscules only, with some appropriate period punctuation marks. Both normal and bold versions are provided.

This is one of a set of manuscript fonts. Access to the docmfp package is desirable but not essential.

caption: Relative Viewport for Graphics Inclusion

descriptions.text:
Package graphicx provides a useful keyword viewport which allows to show just a part of an image. However, one needs to put there the actual coordinates of the viewport window. Sometimes it is useful to have relative coordinates as fractions of natural size. For example, one may want to print a large image on a spread, putting a half on a verso page, and another half on the next recto page. For this one would need a viewport occupying exactly one half of the file's bounding box, whatever the actual width of the image may be.

This package adds a new keyword rviewport to the graphicx package specifiying Relative Viewport for graphics inclusion: a window defined by the given fractions of the natural width and height of the image.

name: rviewport

caption: Increase the number of available output streams in LaTeX

descriptions.text:
The package addresses, for LaTeX documents, the severe limitation on the number of output streams that TeX provides.

The package uses a single TeX output stream, and writes “marked-up” output to this stream. The user may then post-process the marked-up output file, using LaTeX, and the document’s output appears as separate files, according to the calls made to the package.

The output to be post-processed uses macros from the widely-available ProTeX package.

name: rvwrite

caption: Convert bitmap formats to compact PS/PDF

descriptions.text:
Sam2p is a UNIX command line utility written in ANSI C++ that converts many raster (bitmap) image formats into Adobe PostScript or PDF files and several other formats. The images are not vectorized. sam2p gives full control to the user to specify standards-compliance, compression, and bit depths. In some cases sam2p can compress an image 100 times smaller than the PostScript output of many other common image converters. Sam2p provides ZIP, RLE and LZW (de)compression filters even on output destined for PostScript Level 1 devices.

The author provides a script bundle, a2ping, that uses sam2p as part of a generic format conversion mechanism.

name: sam2p

caption: Sanskrit hyphenation patterns

These patterns define hyphenation of Unicode input of Sanskrit and Prakrit in Devanagari, Bengali, Kannada, Malayalam and Telugu scripts.

The patterns are structured for use with XeTeX.

caption: Redefine symbols where names conflict

descriptions.text: There are a number of symbols (e.g., \Square) that are defined by several packages. In order to typeset all the variants in a document, we have to give the glyph a unique name. To do that, we define \savesymbol{XXX}, which renames a symbol from \XXX to \origXXX, and \restoresymbols{yyy}{XXX}, which renames \origXXX back to \XXX and defines a new command, \yyyXXX, which corresponds to the most recently loaded version of \XXX.

Also included is the package sbbm, an alternative to access the bbm fonts.

Nevertheless, savetrees is a simple way to save paper when printing draft copies of a document. It can also be useful when trying to meet a tight page-length requirement for a conference or journal submission.

Most of the package options cover specific modifications to typesetting rules, but there are also options subtle, moderate and extreme options for the “broad brush” approach.

name: savetrees

name: sbtex

caption: Title page for the old ISO TC97/SC21 committee

descriptions.text: A variant of the standard LaTeX 2.09 titlepage package, designed for “N-numbered” papers for the committee. (The committee covered, at various times, standardisation of OSI architecture, OSI upper layers, distributed processing, databases and graphics.)

name: sc21

caption: Title page for the old ISO TC97/SC21/WG1 working group

descriptions.text: A variant of the standard LaTeX 2.09 titlepage package, designed for “N-numbered” papers for the group. (The group covered, at various times, standardisation of OSI architecture, developments of the OSI model and distributed processing.)

name: sc21-wg1

caption: Create scalebars for maps, diagrams or photos

descriptions.text: This is a small package to create scalebars for maps, diagrams or photos. It was designed for use with cave maps but can be used for anything from showing a scalebar in kilometres for topographic maps to a scalebar in micrometres for an electron microscope image.

name: scalebar

caption: Scale document by sqrt(2) or magstep(2)

descriptions.text: A package to scale a document by sqrt(2) (or by \magstep{2}). This is useful if you are preparing a document on, for example, A5 paper and want to print on A4 paper to achieve a better resolution.

name: scale

caption: Rescale fonts to arbitrary sizes

descriptions.text:
\scalefont{2} selects the current font in twice the current size. \scalefont{.75} reduces the current font size by three quarters.

Note that the effectiveness of such operations depends on the LaTeX font selection for that font; it will typically work well for ordinary Type 1 fonts, but Metafont fonts are usually set up to work only at a discrete set of sizes.

The package is distributed as part of the carlisle bundle.

name: scalefnt

caption: Constrained scaling and stretching of objects

descriptions.text:
The package provides four commands for vertically scaling and stretching objects. Its primary function is the ability to scale/stretch and shift one object to conform to the size of a specified second object. This feature can be useful in both equations and schematic diagrams.

Additionally, the scaling and stretching commands offer constraints on maximum width and/or minimum aspect ratio, which are often used to preserve legibility or for the sake of general appearance.

name: scalerel

caption: Support importing and embellishing scanned documents

descriptions.text: The bundle provides support for the process of creating documents based on pre-TeX-era material that is available as scanned pages, only.

name: scanpages

caption: Typeset schedules

descriptions.text: The package implements a document style which enables the user to construct diagrams showing the planned progress of projects, etc. This package seems unrelated to the schedule package written for use with LaTeX 2e. The two packages provide very similar facilities, but the present package’s use of PostScript features (for shading schedule entry backgrounds) is entirely ad hoc.

name: schedule209

topics.details: package only known to work with LaTeX 2.09

caption: Weekly schedules

descriptions.text: Automatically format weekly schedules using LaTeX’s picture environment. It requires the packages calc and color. Its main feature is the accuracy with which appointments are represented: boxes drawn to represent a particular appointment are accurate to the minute — i.e., a 31-minute appointment will have a box 1/30th longer than a 30-minute appointment. A number of features are included to allow the user to customize the output.

name: schedule

caption: Draw block diagrams, using TikZ

descriptions.text:
The package provides a set of macros for constructing block diagrams, using TikZ.

(The blox package is an “English translation” of this package.)

name: schemabloc

caption: Print topical diagrams

descriptions.text: The package facilitates the creation of “topical schemata”, i.e. outlines that use braces (or facsimiles thereof) to illustrate the breakdown of concepts and categories in Scholastic thought from late medieval and early modern periods.

name: schemata

topics.details: typeset devotional texts and other material of interest to theologians
macros that are independent of the (TeX) format in use

caption: Typesetting Scheme programs with LaTeX

descriptions.text: A sort of literate programming mechanism for Scheme. Prettily formats documentation and comments, leaving the Scheme code unchanged.

name: schemeTeX

caption: Simple support for literate programming in Lisp

descriptions.text: SchemeWEB is a Unix filter that allows you to generate both Lisp and LaTeX code from one source file. The generated LaTeX code formats Lisp programs in typewriter font obeying the spacing in the source file. Comments may include arbitrary LaTeX commands. SchemeWEB was originally developed for the Scheme dialect of Lisp, but it can easily be used with most other dialects.

name: schemeweb

caption: Using the OpenType fonts TeX Gyre schola

descriptions.text:
This package can only be used with LuaLaTeX or XeLaTeX. It does the font setting for the OpenType font TeX Gyre Schola for text and math.

The missing typefaces like bold math and slanted text are also defined

name: schola-otf

topics.details: XeTeX, material supporting it, and packages requiring it
LuaTeX and packages that require it

caption: Various layout styles for school documents

descriptions.text: The aim of this package is to offer diverse layout styles for school-related documents. It serves well in creating exercise sheets, exams, course materials. The package sets the page geometry (dimensions of text and margins) and the title formatting. Various styles are available defining settings for headers, footers or alternative title formatting, providing many customizable features.

name: schooldocs

topics.details: support for teachers and teaching administrators

caption: Extension of TeXGyreSchola (New Century Schoolbook) with math support

descriptions.text:
This package contains an extension of TeXGyreSchola with extensive superiors, inferior figures, upright punctuation glyphs added to the Italic face for a theorem font, plus slanted and bold slanted faces.

Math support is provided by one of two options to newtxmath, one of which uses an adaptation of the fourier math Greek letters.

name: ScholaX

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other font support
font providing LaTeX T1 encoding support
font available in Adobe Type 1 format
font designed for use as body font for Latin-based script documents

caption: Support for teachers at German schools

copyright.owner: Johannes Pieper, André Hilbig, Johannes Kuhaupt,                     Daniel Spittank, Ludger Humbert, Adrian Salamon

descriptions.text:
The ‘schule’ bundle was built to provide packages and commands that could be useful for documents in German schools. At the moment its main focus lies on documents for informatics as a school subject. An extension for physics is currently in progress. Extensions for other subjects are welcome.
For the time being, the whole package splits up into individual packages for informatics (including syntax diagrams, Nassi–Shneiderman diagrams, sequence diagrams, object diagrams, and class diagrams) as well as classes for written exams (tests, quizzes, teaching observations, information sheets, worksheets, and answer keys).

name: schule

topics.details: support for teachers and teaching administrators

caption: Commands and document classes for German-speaking teachers of mathematics and physics

descriptions.text: The schulmathematik bundle provides two LaTeX packages and six document classes for German-speaking teachers of mathematics and physics.

name: schulmathematik

topics.details: support for teachers and teaching administrators

caption: German “school scripts” from Suetterlin to the present day

descriptions.text: Das Paket enthält im wesentlichen die Metafont-Quellfiles für die folgenden Schulausgangsschriften: Suetterlinschrift, Deutsche Normalschrift, Lateinische Ausgangsschrift, Schulausgangsschrift, Vereinfachte Ausgangsschrift. Damit ist es möglich, beliebige deutsche Texte in diesen Schreibschriften zu schreiben.

name: schulschriften

caption: Typeset the German chess magazine “Die Schwalbe”

descriptions.text: The package is based on chess-problem-diagrams, which in its turn has a dependency on the bartel-chess-fonts.

name: schwalbe-chess

topics.details: process game diagrams, gamebooks, and other amusements

caption: Provides cover page and affirmation at the end of a thesis

descriptions.text: Institutions require a cover page and an affirmation at the end of a thesis. This package provides both.

name: scientific-thesis-cover

topics.details: support for writers of scientific documents

caption: Calligraphic font for typesetting handwriting in Schwell style

descriptions.text: Calligraphic font for typesetting handwriting in a variation of the Sütterlin handwriting, invented by Ludwig Sütterlin, a German teacher and typographer.

name: schwell

caption: Visual LaTeX editor

descriptions.text: Scientific Author is a visual LaTeX editor for mathematicians, scientists and engineers, supporting industry standards like LaTeX 2e. It is a visual document editor, which exports LaTeX for rendering by tools such as MiKTeX. Scientific Author also supports editing of mathematical notation through tool palettes and templates. LaTeX symbols are also supported, including American Mathematical Society symbols. It also enables easy editing of tables, footnotes, and margin notes.

name: scientificauthor

topics.details: editor designed (or adapted) for use with (La)TeX

caption: Format a scientific paper for journal publication
name: scientificpaper

caption: Mark research contributions in scientific documents and embed them in PDF metadata

descriptions.text: Scientific Knowledge Graph TeX (SciKgTeX) is a LuaLaTeX package which makes it possible to annotate specific research contributions in scientific documents. SciKGTeX will enrich the document by adding the marked contributions to PDF metadata in a structured XMP format which can be picked up by search engines and knowledge graphs.

name: SciKGTeX

topics.details: LuaTeX and packages that require it

caption: MacKichan software viewer

descriptions.text:
Scientific Viewer allows the user to read or print docuemnts created with MacKichan Scientific Notebook, Scientific Word or Scientific Workplace; it may also be used to view many ‘native’ LaTeX documents.

The viewer does not enable the user to manipulate the document in any way.

name: scientificviewer

topics.details: application for viewing a typeset document on screen

caption: Use Scientific Word/WorkPlace files with another TeX

descriptions.text: These macros allows you to combine the power of the graphical front-end of Scientific Word/Scientific WorkPlace (SW/SWP) with one's own favourite TeX compiler (for example, MiKTeX). Currently includes support for Russian language; other languages can be handled easily.

name: SciWordConv

topics.details: import files in a non-TeX (or different TeX) format

caption: Make posters of ISO A3 size and larger

descriptions.text:
This collection of files contains LaTeX packages for posters of ISO A3 size and larger (ISO A0 is the default size). American paper sizes and custom paper are supported. In particular, sciposter.cls defines a document class which allows cutting and pasting most of an article to a poster without any editing (save reducing the size) — see the manual.

Sciposter does work for LaTeX, not just pdfLaTeX. However, xdvi produces strange results, though a recent version of dvips does create good ps-files from the dvi files.

Also note that logos must either be put in the current working directory or in the directories of your LaTeX distribution. For some reason graphicspath settings are ignored.

name: sciposter

caption: Typeset scripts with Plain TeX
name: scmac

caption: Prettyprinting SuperCollider source code

descriptions.text: Built on top of the listings package, the package allows effortless prettyprinting of SuperCollider source code in documents typeset with LaTeX & friends.

name: sclang-prettifier

topics.details: highlight syntax of computer code, etc.

caption: Stores LaTeX contents in memory or files

descriptions.text: This package stores valid LaTeX code in memory (sequences) using the l3seq module of expl3. The stored content (including verbatim) can be used as many times as desired in the document, additionally can be written to external files if desired.

name: scontents

caption: Format a Baseball scorecard

descriptions.text: Formats a scorecard with which to score a baseball game, with additional space to record information with which to submit a details to newspapers, league offices, etc. Also provides boxes for other summary statistics.

name: scorecard

topics.details: typeset cards for business, filing, etc.

caption: Provide data from scrlttr2's address files

descriptions.text: The package is a part of the Koma-Script suite. The package uses adr-files to generate circular letters. The package provides commands to read the adr-files and to use the data of the address entries, not only with scrlttr2 class and not only for circular letters.

name: scraddr

topics.details: lists of addresses, for a personal directory (or the like)

caption: Commands for Scrabble boards

descriptions.text:
This package provides some commands (in English and in French) to work with a Scrabble Board :

  • \ScrabbleBoard and \begin{EnvScrabble} and \ScrabblePutWord for the English version,
  • \PlateauScrabble and \begin{EnvScrabble} and \ScrabblePlaceMot for the French version.

name: Scrabble

topics.details: process game diagrams, gamebooks, and other amusements

caption: Create and print scrambled environments

descriptions.text:
This package allows you to create and print scrambled environments for purposes such as randomized hint environments. You can mark a location with a series of hints, and then print the hints at the end in a pseudo-random order.

The general structure follows: there is an outer environment which creates the label, an inner environment that creates the references, and a print command that prints out all of the hints.

This generalizes beyond hints; one can create scrambled solutions as well, etc.

name: scrambledenvs

topics.details: general notes (not including endnotes or footnotes)

caption: Koma-Script ‘article’ class

descriptions.text:
The class provides the “article”-like element of the koma-script collection.

The document layout of the class is less ‘strident’ than that of article, and it offers much more flexibility than article via other elements of the koma-script collection.

name: scrartcl

topics.details: LaTeX article classes and their developments

caption: Draw programs like “scratch”

descriptions.text:
This package is now obsolete. From now on, scratch at scratch.mit.edu is now version3 with a new design. Please, use the “scratch3” package to draw blocks with the new design.

This package permits to draw program charts in the style of the scatch project (scratch.mit.edu).

It depends on the other LaTeX packages TikZ and simplekv.

name: scratch

topics.details: process game diagrams, gamebooks, and other amusements

caption: Include Scratch programs in LaTeX documents

descriptions.text:
This package can be used to include every kind of Scratch program in LaTeX documents. This may be particularly useful for Math Teachers and IT specialists.

The package depends on the following other LaTeX packages: calc, fp, ifsym, multido, tikz, xargs, and xstring.

name: ScratchX

topics.details: process game diagrams, gamebooks, and other amusements

caption: Draw programs like “scratch”

descriptions.text:
This package permits to draw program charts in the style of the scatch project (scratch.mit.edu).

It depends on the other LaTeX packages TikZ and simplekv.

name: scratch3

topics.details: process game diagrams, gamebooks, and other amusements

caption: Provide basic features for KOMA-Script

descriptions.text:
The package is part of the KOMA-Script suite; it provides some basic functions used by KOMA-Script, that may also be useful to authors and users of other classes and packages.

Most notably, the package provides conditionals and an extended “key=value” handling mechanism that may be used for run-time options of classes and packages. Several packages of a family may share options and all the options of one family may be changed with a single command.

name: scrbase

caption: Koma-Script ‘book’ class

descriptions.text:
The class provides the “book”-like element of the koma-script collection.

The document layout of the class is more ‘calm’ than that of book, and it offers much more flexibility than book via other elements of the koma-script collection.

name: scrbook

caption: Calendar date operations

descriptions.text: The package provides several operations with calender dates, such as to show the century or the decade of a year, calculate the day of the week of a given calender date, show the current calender date in ISO form. The package offers support for output in several languages.

name: scrdate

caption: Prepare a document for a simple previewer

descriptions.text: A small package designed to set geometry to prepare a (LaTeX 2.09) document for viewing with something like crudetype.

name: screen

caption: A class file to typeset screenplays

descriptions.text: The class implements the format recommended by the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences.

name: screenplay

caption: Package version of the screenplay document class

descriptions.text:
This package implements the tools of the screenplay document class in the form of a package so that screenplay fragments can be included within another document class.

For full documentation of the available commands, please consult the screenplay class documentation in addition to the included package documentation.

name: screenplay-pkg

caption: Use of components of KOMA-Script by other packages

descriptions.text: The package makes some features of the KOMA-Script classes available for other classes, e.g., for the standard classes.

name: scrextend

topics.details: export features from a class for use elsewhere

caption: Make index package work with Koma-script classes

descriptions.text:
This package redefines environment `theindex' of package `index', if a class from KOMA-Script is loaded. Also option `idxtotoc' is supported. Index preambles can be given either by means of package `index' or via the interface provided by KOMA-Script.

The package is part of the oberdiek bundle.

name: scrindex

caption: Variant report and book styles

descriptions.text: A “jiffy” conversion to LaTeX2e of some old document styles.

name: script

caption: Handwriting font

descriptions.text: A font that “resembles the author’s handwriting”, distributed as Metafont source.

name: script-font

caption: A summary of mathematical script fonts for LaTeX users

descriptions.text:
A development, with examples, of an answer in the UK TeX FAQ, showing the fonts generally available to the user of LaTeX.

The source isn't readily compilable, but contains notes on how it should be compiled.

name: scriptfonts

caption: Macros for scripts and screenplays

descriptions.text: ScriptTeX provides Plain TeX macros to support both Screenplays and Stage Plays.

name: ScriptTeX

caption: A LaTeX style for typesetting Bible quotations

descriptions.text: The scripture package provides a set of macros for typesetting quotations from the Bible. It provides many features commonly seen in Bibles such as dropped text for chapter numbers, superscripts for verse numbers, indented lines for poetry sections, narrow sections and hanging paragraphs. A reference for the quotation can optionally be added.

name: scripture

topics.details: typeset devotional texts and other material of interest to theologians

caption: Manage text ‘layers’ within Koma-Script

descriptions.text: The package is part of the koma-script bundle, and provides control of ‘background’ and ‘foreground’ layers for a page style description.

name: scrlayer

caption: Koma-Script support for lawyers, etc

descriptions.text:
The package is part of the Koma-Script bundle. It provides environments for contracts, laws, acts or other legal puposes. It features support for automatic numbering of paragraphs, and semi-automatic numbering of sentences.

Support is offered for both German and English texts.

name: scrjura

topics.details: typesetting legal documents or study material

caption: Typeset diaries or journals

descriptions.text: A class, based on scrbook, designed for typesetting diaries, journals or devotionals.

name: scrjrnl

caption: Combining package fancyhdr with KOMA-Script’s scrlayer

descriptions.text:
This LaTeX package uses KOMA-Script’s scrlayer to redefine the page styles of package fancyhdr. This allows the combination of features of fancyhdr with features of scrlayer.

Before KOMA-Script v3.33 scrlayer-fancyhdr was part of KOMA-Script itself.

name: scrlayer-fancyhdr

caption: Control note columns parallel to the main text

descriptions.text:
The package provides an end user interface to define and manage note columns, above scrlayer.

The note columns provide similar facilities to those of the LaTeX \marginpar command, extending them to more than a single column. The package provides page breaks inside note columns, and synchronisation netweem the main text and note columns.

name: scrlayer-notecolumn

topics.details: general notes (not including endnotes or footnotes)

caption: Define and manage page styles

descriptions.text: This package is the part of the Koma-Script bundle that provides an end user interface to scrlayer, allowing the user to define and manage page styles by controlling page headers and footers. The end user interface is compatible enough to that of the earlier scrpage2 package, so that users should easily be able to switch from the older package to the newer, more powerful, one.

name: scrlayer-scrpage

caption: Letter extention to KOMA-Script classes

descriptions.text:
Used in conjunction with one of the Koma-Script (scrartcl, scrreprt, scrbook) or standard classes (article, report, book), this package provides the features of the letter class scrlttr2.

The package is part of the Koma-Script bundle.

name: scrletter

caption: Koma-Script ‘letter’ class

descriptions.text:
The class was designed ‘from scratch’ as a replacement for the standard LaTeX letter class.

Its interface is (“basically”) a key-value mechanism, with a wide range of parameters that define the basic layout of the letter.

name: scrlttr2

caption: Installation control for koma-script packages

descriptions.text:
The package provides hooks for the execution of commands before or after loading files, classes or packages. The package can also

  • execute commands after loading files, classes or packages,
  • prevent a package from being loaded, and
  • schedule the execution of commands before or after closing the .aux file at \end{document}

The package is part of the Koma-Script bundle.

name: scrlfile

topics.details: support for managing packages within documents

caption: A letter class option file for the automatic creation of copies

descriptions.text:
The file copy.lco provides the new class option “copy” for the KOMA-Script letter class scrlttr2.

If the option “copy” is given, all pages of a specific letter are duplicated with background text marking as copies.

name: scrlttr2copy

caption: Koma-Script ‘report’ class

descriptions.text:
The class provides the “report”-like element of the Koma-Script collection.

The document layout of the class is more ‘calm’ than that of report, and it offers much more flexibility than report via other elements of the Koma-Script collection.

name: scrreprt

caption: Control of page headers and footers in LaTeX

descriptions.text:
The package was designed to ease integration into documents using the Koma-Script suite. It incorporates a set of predefined, configurable page styles.

As of 2015, the author considers this package as obsolete and recommends using its successor scrlayer-scrpage instead.

name: scrpage2

caption: Show the time of a LaTeX run

descriptions.text: The package provides time information for the current LaTeX run.

name: scrtime

descriptions.text: The package provides a means of sending all LaTeX \newrite, table of contents, and other miscellaneous output via the LaTeX .aux file. The mechanism subverts the mechanism of \newrite, and means there will never be a “No room for new \write” message.

name: scrwfile

descriptions.text:
This LaTeX package provides a command \scsnowman which can display many variants of “snowman” (“yukidaruma” in Japanese).

TikZ is required for drawing these snowmen.

name: scsnowman

topics.details: jokes, distractions, tongue-in-cheek packages, and other entertainment material

caption: LaTeX support files for SDAPS

descriptions.text:
This bundle contains LaTeX classes and packages to create machine readable questionnaires. Metadata is generated for the whole document and it is possible to process created forms fully automatically using the SDAPS main program.

Features include:

  • PDF Form generation
  • Advanced array like layouting
    • Can flow over multiple pages and repeats the header automatically

    • Has complex layout features like rotating the headers to safe space
    • Ability to exchange rows and columns on the fly
  • Different question types:
    • Freeform text
    • Single/multiple choice questions
    • Range questions
  • Layouting questions in rows or columns
  • Possibility to pre-fill questionnaires from LaTeX

name: sdaps
