descriptions.text: The package provides macros to produce the ‘Box notation’ of SDRT (and DRT), to draw trees representing discourse relations, and finally to have an easy access to various mathematical symbols used in that theory, mostly with automatic mathematics mode, so they work the same in formulae and in text.

name: sdrt

descriptions.text: This family (distributed as Metafont source) provides a basic set of cyrillic glyphs, in an encoding that (apparently) only this family uses.

name: scyrillic

topics.details: fonts for Cyrillic and related scripts

caption: Thesis Template of Shandong University

descriptions.text: Thesis Template of Shandong University.

name: sduthesis

name: secdot

descriptions.text: The se2thesis bundle provides a document class for writing a theses with the Chair of Software Engineering II at the University of Passau, Germany. The class is based on Markus Kohm’s KOMA-Script classes and provides several additions and customizations to these classes. While the class provides some basic settings, mostly regrading the type area, fonts, and the title page, it still provides large degrees of freedom to its users. However, the package’s documentation also provides recommendations regarding several aspects, for example, recommending BibLaTeX for bibliographies.

name: se2thesis

caption: Put security classification marks in a document

descriptions.text:
The package puts a mark in the margin at the start of each paragraph, and at the top of a page when a paragraph runs over onto a new page.

The marks are programmed by commands \unclassified (mark ‘(U)’), \confidential (mark ‘(C)’), or \secret (mark ‘(S)’). The command \nosecret switches off marking.

name: secret

caption: A macro to format section numbering intuitively

descriptions.text:
This package provides a macro \setsecnum to format section numbering intuitively.

\setsecnum{1.1.1} will set the section numbering format to arabic.arabic.arabic and the depth to 3.

The package uses LaTeX3.

name: secnum

caption: Number theorems by section

descriptions.text: The package formats equation numbers with a section number prefix, with the number itself reset for each section.

name: seceqn

caption: Create fancy boxed ((sub)sub)sections

descriptions.text: Sectionbox is a LaTeX package for putting fancy colored boxes around sections, subsections, and subsubsections, especially for use in posters, etc. It was designed with the sciposter class in mind, and certainly works with that class and with derived classes.

name: sectionbox

caption: Modifying section commands in LaTeX

descriptions.text: The package implements a pretty extensive scheme to make more manageable the business of configuring LaTeX output.

name: section

descriptions.text: This package provides LaTeX support for section breaks, used mainly in fiction books to signal changes in a story, like changes in time, location, etc. It supports the asterism symbol, text content, or custom macros as the section break mark symbol.

name: sectionbreak

topics.details: highlighting typeset material, fancy frames, watermarks, etc.

caption: Improve the performance of \see macros with makeindex

descriptions.text: The package amends the \see and \seealso macros that are used in building indexes with makeindex, to deal with repetitions, and to ensure page numbers are present in the actual index entries. on these indirecty

name: sectsty

Defines a command \outputonly, whose argument is a list of pages to be output. With the command present (before \begin{document}), only those pages are output.

This package was inspired by code published by Knuth in TUGboat 8(2) (July 1987).

name: selectp

descriptions.text: This package selects the input encoding by specifying pairs of input characters and their glyph names.

name: selinput

topics.details: input encoding support for TeX engines

Requires a file of page numbers, which specifies the numbers of pages to print (in generated order).

The code was published in TUGboat 8(2) (July 1987).

name: selectpage

topics.details: select pages to be output, etc.

caption: Selectively disable typographic ligatures

descriptions.text:
The package suppresses typographic ligatures selectively, i.e., based on predefined search patterns. The search patterns focus on ligatures deemed inappropriate because they span morpheme boundaries. For example, the word shelfful, which is mentioned in the TeXbook as a word for which the ff ligature might be inappropriate, is automatically typeset as shelf\/ful rather than as shel{ff}ul.

For English and German language documents, the package provides extensive rules for the selective suppression of so-called “common” ligatures. These comprise the ff, fi, fl, ffi, and ffl ligatures as well as the ft and fft ligatures. Other f-ligatures, such as fb, fh, fj and fk, are suppressed globally, while exceptions are made for names and words of non-English/German origin, such as Kafka and fjord.

For English language documents, the package further provides ligature suppression macros for a number of so-called “discretionary” or “rare” ligatures such as ct, st, and sp.

The package requires use of a recent LuaLaTeX format (for example those from TeX Live 2012 or 2013, or MiKTeX 2.9).

name: selnolig

support for variations of typographic style

caption: Help for writing programming language semantics

descriptions.text: Eases the typesetting of notation of semantics and compilers. Includes T-diagrams, various derivation symbols and inference trees.

name: semantic

caption: Semantic, keyval-based mathematics

descriptions.text:
The SemanTeX package for LaTeX delivers a more semantic, systematized way of writing mathematics, compared to the classical math syntax in LaTeX. The system uses keyval syntax, and the user can define their own keys and customize the system down to the last detail. At the same time, care has been taken to make the syntax as simple, natural, practical, and lightweight as possible.

Furthermore, the package has a companion package, called stripsemantex, which allows you to completely strip your documents of SemanTeX markup to prepare them e.g. for publication.

The package is still in beta, but is considered feature-complete and more or less stable, so using it at this point should be safe. Still, suggestions, ideas, and bug reports are more than welcome!

name: SemanTeX

caption: Meaningful semantic markup in the spirit of the Text Encoding Initiative

descriptions.text:
The package provides simple commands to allow authors (especially scholars in the humanities) to write with a focus on content rather than presentation. The commands are inspired by the XML elements of the Text Encoding Initiative. Commands like \term and \foreign are aliases for \emph. \quoted and \soCalled are aliases for quoting commands. These commands could be easily redefined for different formats.

The package also provides a footnote environment so that long footnotes can be more cleanly separated from the main text.

Because the author is a music scholar, the package also includes some macros for musical symbols and other basic notations for musical analysis.

name: semantic-markup

topics.details: support for studies in the humanities

caption: Semaphore alphabet font

descriptions.text: These fonts represent semaphore in a highly schematic, but very clear, fashion. The fonts are provided as Metafont source, and in both OpenType and Adobe Type 1 formats.

name: semaphor

topics.details: font available in Adobe Type 1 format
fonts with specific small application areas

caption: Create beautiful semester timetables and more

descriptions.text:
This package defines several useful environments for a beautiful printable semester plan. It includes a timetable (which is using the schedule-Package) as well as appointments, deadlines, and exams.

The package requires color, TikZ, schedule, and fontawesome. Furthermore, documents need to be compiled with LuaLaTeX.

name: semesterplanner

topics.details: LuaTeX and packages that require it
typeset calendars, diaries, planning charts, etc.

caption: Put only special contents on left-hand pages in two sided layout

descriptions.text: This package supports the preparation of semi one sided documents. That is, two sided documents, where all text is output on right-hand pages—as in a one-sided documents—and only special contents are output on left-hand pages on user request, e.g., floating objects.

name: semioneside

topics.details: layout of objects on the page

caption: Seminar proceedings

descriptions.text:
The package provides functionality for typesetting seminar proceedings based on KOMA-Script's scrreprt class and etoc. It offers an alternative to \chapter that typesets the speaker and if necessary the typist of the notes for the talk in question.

Moreover, the class provides two types of table of contents. A global table of contents showing only the talks of the seminar and the respective speakers and a local table of contents for each talk showing the sections and subsections of the respective talk.

name: semproc

caption: Make overhead slides

descriptions.text:
A class that produces overhead slides (transparencies), with many facilities. The class requires availability of the fancybox package.

Seminar is also the basis of other classes, such as prosper. In fact, seminar is not nowadays reckoned a good basis for a presentation — users are advised to use more recent classes such as powerdot or beamer, both of which are tuned to 21st-century presentation styles.

Note that the seminar distribution relies on the xcomment package, which was once part of the bundle, but now has a separate existence.

name: seminar

caption: Deals with stripped SemanTeX documents

descriptions.text:
This package is a small LaTeX package that adds a collection of simple macros for parentheses and bullets. It exists for one purpose only: To be loaded by documents which were originally typeset using the package SemanTeX, but which have been stripped of SemanTeX markup using the package stripsemantex which is part of SemanTeX. Therefore, unless your document is one of those, simply don't use this package.

And even if your document is one of those, there is a good chance you will not have to load it after all. In most cases, you will be able to replace the macros it provides by macros from other packages.

name: SemTeX

caption: Numbered lists for sentences

descriptions.text:
The package defines sentences and subsentences list environments, whose entries may be referenced by number.

The package requires the maybeload and redefine packages.

name: sentences

caption: Transliteration of semitic languages

descriptions.text: A small set of commands to assist in transliterating languagees such as Arabic, Hebrew and the Ethiopian languages.

name: semtrans

caption: Support footnotes and endnotes from separate files

descriptions.text: The package supports footnotes and endnotes from separate files. This is achieved with commands \sepfootnotecontent and \sepfootnote; the former defines the content of a note, while the latter typesets that note.

name: sepfootnotes

caption: Print numbers in a "friendly" format

descriptions.text: Provides a command to print a number with (potentially different) separators every three digits in the parts either side of the decimal point (the point itself is also configurable). The macro is fully expandable and not fragile (unless one of the separators is). There is also a command \sepnumform, that may be used when defining \the<counter> macros.

name: sepnum

caption: Split long sequences of characters in a neutral way

descriptions.text:
When one needs to type long sequences of letters (such as in base-sequences in genes) or of numbers (such as calculations of transcendental numbers), there's no obvious break points to be found. The package provides a command \seqsplit, which makes its argument splittable anywhere, and then leaves the TeX paragraph-maker to do the splitting.

While the package may obviously be used to typeset DNA sequences, the user may consider the dnaseq as a rather more powerful alternative.

name: seqsplit

caption: Support for use of memoir in Serbian

descriptions.text: The package provides a number of commands for adjusting memoir output to Serbian style.

name: serbian-book

topics.details: documentation in, and support for typesetting Serbian

caption: Commands for Serbian words with apostrophes

descriptions.text: The package provides a collection of commands (whose names are Serbian words) whose expansion is the Serbian word with appropriate apostrophes.

documentation.details: List of word commands and their expansion

name: serbian-apostrophe

topics.details: documentation in, and support for typesetting Serbian

caption: Updated date typesetting for Serbian

descriptions.text: Babel defines dates for Serbian texts, in Latin script. The style it uses does not match current practices. The present package defines a \date command that solves the problem.

name: serbian-date-lat

topics.details: documentation in, and support for typesetting Serbian

caption: Redefines \thepart to be used in Roman lettered Serbian

descriptions.text: The package redefines \thepart, to produce “PART <alphabetical version of the number>”, in Roman lettered Serbian.

name: serbianpart

topics.details: documentation in, and support for typesetting Serbian

caption: Serbian cyrillic localization

descriptions.text: This package provides abstract, chapter, title, date etc, for serbian language in cyrillic scripts in T2A encoding and cp1251 code pages.

name: serbian-def-cyr

topics.details: documentation in, and support for typesetting Serbian

caption: Control ligatures in Serbian

descriptions.text: The package suppresses fi and fl (and other ligatures) in Serbian text written using Roman script.

name: serbian-lig

topics.details: documentation in, and support for typesetting Serbian

caption: Session and timing information in lecture notes

descriptions.text: This LaTeX2e package makes it possible to add timing marks to lecture notes in order to help managing the time available for presenting a given section of the document. It also provides tools to record and estimate the progress throughout the course.

name: sesstime

topics.details: support for teachers and teaching administrators

caption: Generate serial letters

descriptions.text: The serial package provides a wrapper to the KOMA Script letter class scrlettr for the generation of serial letters. It contains different interfaces to data base generated adress files. Additionally, a configuration file allows easy customization of the letterheads etc. Requires scrlettr.cls from KOMA-Script and the following are recommended: inputenc, textmerg, delimtxt.

name: serial

caption: Class and package for sesamath books or paper

descriptions.text: The package contains a sesamanuel class which could be used to compose a student's classroom book with LaTeX, and also a sesamanuelTIKZ style to be used for TikZ pictures in the sesamath book.

name: sesamanuel

caption: Typeset cards for Set

descriptions.text: The package will typeset cards for use in a game of Set.

name: setdeck

topics.details: process game diagrams, gamebooks, and other amusements

caption: Set space between lines

descriptions.text: Provides support for setting the spacing between lines in a document. Package options include singlespacing, onehalfspacing, and doublespacing. Alternatively the spacing can be changed as required with the \singlespacing, \onehalfspacing, and \doublespacing commands. Other size spacings also available.

name: setspace

caption: Set hbox in outer horizontal mode

descriptions.text: If math stuff is set in an \hbox, then TeX performs some optimization and omits the implicit penalties \binoppenalty and \relpenalty. This packages tries to put stuff into an \hbox without losing those penalties.

name: setouterhbox

caption: An enhancement of the setspace package

descriptions.text: This package adds support for all font sizes, even non-integer resp. non-pt sizes to package setspace. This not only improves compatibility with KOMA-Script but also corrects the stretch value of the usual font sizes.

name: setspaceenhanced

caption: Assigning dimensions of a box to a length register

descriptions.text:
Commands to assist the reuse of boxes (set up by \sbox or by the lrbox environment); the \settobox... commands behave similarly to the \settowidth (etc.) commands. For example: 

        \newsavebox{\mybox}
        \newlength{\mylength}
        \sbox{\mybox}{Hello World}
        \settoboxwidth{\mylength}{\mybox}

name: settobox

caption: Automatic strut computation

descriptions.text: Provides means of generating struts, “standard“ or with extended height or depth.

name: setstrut

topics.details: support for variations of typographic style

caption: Scale text to make it fit a given width

descriptions.text:
The command \scaletowidth decides on a scale for the current font such that the text will fit the given width.

This package is an adaptation for LaTeX of the settosize package for plain TeX; it is now superseded by textfit, which is a development for current LaTeX.

name: settosize-ltx

topics.details: package only known to work with LaTeX 2.09

caption: Southeast University Machine Learning Assignment template

descriptions.text: This is a template for the Southeast University Machine Learning Assignment that can be easily adapted to other usages. This template features a colorful theme that makes it look elegant and attractive. You can also find the template available on Overleaf.

name: seu-ml-assign

caption: Scale text to given width

descriptions.text:
The package defines a command

\set <text> \in <font> \to <size>

that chooses the “best” magstep that will fit the given text into the width, and typesets the text accordingly.

name: settosize

caption: Package for typesetting arabic exam scripts

descriptions.text: The package provides a modified version of the exam package made compatible with XeLaTeX/polyglossia to typesetting arabic exams.

name: sexam

topics.details: documentation in and support for typesetting Arabic

caption: LaTeX template for theses at Southeastern University

descriptions.text: This template is for theses at Southeastern University, Nanjing, China.

name: seuthesis

caption: LaTeX class for theses at Southeast University, Nanjing, China

descriptions.text:
This project provides a LaTeX document class as well as a bibliography style file for typesetting theses at the Southeast University, Nanjing, China.

It is based on the seuthesis package which, according to the author of seuthesix, is buggy and has not been maintained for some time.

name: seuthesix

caption: Standard form 298

descriptions.text: A LaTeX package for generating a completed standard form 298 (Rev. 8-98) as prescribed by ANSI Std. Z39.18 for report documentation as part of a document delivered, for instance, on a U.S. government contract.

name: sf298

caption: Typesetting science fiction/fantasy manuscripts

descriptions.text: The class is designed for typesetting science fiction and fantasy manuscripts. Sffms now includes several options for specific publishers as well as extensive documentation aimed at new LaTeX users.

name: sffms

topics.details: prepare documents for a specific publisher

caption: A LaTeX 2.09 article style with an sf switch

descriptions.text: The package is a variant of standard article that has an sf option (for sans typesetting) and various of the ‘fixed names’ (such as ‘Contents’) defined in macros (and thus variable).

name: sfarticle

topics.details: package only known to work with LaTeX 2.09

caption: Draw signal flow graphs

descriptions.text: Defines some commands to draw signal flow graphs as used by electrical and electronics engineers and graph theorists. Requires fp and pstricks packages (and a relatively fast machine).

name: sfg

topics.details: package using PStricks for graphical output

caption: Sans headers

descriptions.text: Print part/chapter/section headers with the sans-serif font of the current family in the standard book/report/article document classes.

name: sfheaders

caption: Sans-serif mathematics

descriptions.text:
sfmath is a simple package for sans serif maths in documents.

After including the package, all maths of the current document is displayed with sans serif fonts.

name: sfmath

caption: A set of definitions for Unix system documentation

descriptions.text: A set of macros defining fonts and the typesetting of names in those fonts.

name: sfwmac

topics.details: macros and tools for preparing documentation
package only known to work with LaTeX 2.09

caption: LaTeX style for typesetting strategic games

descriptions.text:
Formats strategic games. For a 2x2 game, for example, the input:

        \begin{game}{2}{2}
                  &$L$         &$M$\\
        $T$       &$2,2$       &$2,0$\\
        $B$       &$3,0$       &$0,9$
        \end{game}
produces output with (a) boxes around the payoffs, (b) payoff columns of equal width, and (c) payoffs vertically centered within the boxes.

Note that the game environment will not work in the argument of another command.

name: sgame

topics.details: process game diagrams, gamebooks, and other amusements

caption: Suppport for LaTeX formulae as SGML PCDATA

descriptions.text: Replacement control sequences for the characters >, <, and & (as column separator) and for the command \&. The replacements make it possible to enter LaTeX formulae as SGML PCDATA.

name: sgmlcmpt

caption: Shade the background of any box

descriptions.text: Two packages that shade the background of any box by device-independent techniques (based on pixel shading). The two packages implement alternative pixel positioning algorithms.

name: shadbox

topics.details: highlighting typeset material, fancy frames, watermarks, etc.

caption: Shade boxes using PostScript specials

descriptions.text:
The file as presented may be run to produce an example of the output that may be expected: text may be enclosed in rectangular or in rounded-corner (what LaTeX calls ‘oval’) boxes, and the background of the box is shaded.

The technique of using PostScript specials (thus tying use to dvips-based production) contrasts with the specially-concocted fonts used by the shade package.

name: shadebox

topics.details: highlighting typeset material, fancy frames, watermarks, etc.

caption: Shadow boxes

descriptions.text: Defines a command \shabox (analgous to \fbox), and supporting mechanisms.

name: shadow

topics.details: highlighting typeset material, fancy frames, watermarks, etc.

caption: Theorem environments that are shaded

descriptions.text:
Extends the \newtheorem command. If you say \newshadetheorem{theorem}{Theorem} in the preamble then your regular \begin{theorem} .. \end{theorem} will produce a theorem statement in a shaded box. It supports all the options of \newtheorem, including forms \newshadetheorem{..}[..]{..} and \newshadetheorem{..}{..}[..].

Environments declared using the package require their body to remain on one page; the mdframed package can frame and shade theorems, and its environments break at the end of a page; users are generally recommended, therefore, to use mdframed.

In the same spirit, the author told us in January 2020: “These materials are obsolete. There are a number of more recent, more powerful packages that have capabilities that greatly extend the simple ones here. A new project should use one of those. These files only continue to be available to help people who are working with an old project.”

name: Shaded theorems

topics.details: highlighting typeset material, fancy frames, watermarks, etc.

caption: Shade pieces of text

descriptions.text: The package provides a shaded backdrop to a box of text. It uses a Metafont font (provided) which generates to appropriate shading dependent on the resolution used in the Metafont printer parameters.

name: shade

topics.details: highlighting typeset material, fancy frames, watermarks, etc.

caption: LaTeX package for putting text on a shaded background

descriptions.text: Works by specifying the background with PostScript \special commands, suitable for use with dvips

name: shading

topics.details: highlighting typeset material, fancy frames, watermarks, etc.

caption: Produce text with a shadow behind it

descriptions.text: The package introduces a command \shadowtext, which adds a drop shadow to the text that is given as its argument. The colour and positioning of the shadow are customisable.

name: shadowtext

topics.details: highlighting typeset material, fancy frames, watermarks, etc.

caption: A simple Hebrew typesetting bundle

descriptions.text: A package intended for simple documents with some Hebrew (using some words, an address, a short abstract, without fussing around with TeX--Xet, hebrew screen fonts or keyboard encodings).

name: shalom

topics.details: documentation in and support for typesetting Hebrew

caption: A macro to typeset paragraphs in specific shapes

descriptions.text:
\shapepar is a macro to typeset paragraphs in a specific shape. The size is adjusted automatically so that the entire shape is filled with text. There may not be displayed maths or ‘\vadjust’ material (no \vspace) in the argument of \shapepar. The macros work for both LaTeX and plain TeX. For LaTeX, specify \usepackage{shapepar}; for Plain, \input shapepar.sty.

\shapepar works in terms of user-defined shapes, though the package does provide some predefined shapes: so you can form any paragraph into the form of a heart by putting \heartpar{sometext...} inside your document. The tedium of creating these polygon definitions may be alleviated by using the shapepatch extension to transfig which will convert xfig output to \shapepar polygon form.

name: shapepar

caption: Draw polygons, reentrant stars, and fractions in circles with MetaPost

descriptions.text: The shapes set of macros allows drawing regular polygons; their corresponding reentrant stars in all their variations; and fractionally filled circles (useful for visually demonstrating the nature of fractions) in MetaPost.

name: shapes

caption: Transfig patch supporting shapepar

descriptions.text: ShapePatch is a patch against Transfig, which adds the capability to export XFig figures to shape definitions for shapepar. Shapepar itself will form a paragraph into a specified shape, and the size of the shape is automatically adjusted so that the given paragraph completely fills the shape. ShapePatch effort: one simply draws the required shape with XFig and then convert it to a shape definition for shapepar, either by calling fig2dev manually or by choosing “Export/Shape” in XFig (if you install the additional XFig patch).

name: shapepatch

caption: A Shavian spelling alphabet font

descriptions.text: G B Shaw was a seasoned proponent of English spelling reform, and after his death, the Shaw trust held a competition for a “rational” English alphabet. This font won.

name: shavian

topics.details: font for an ‘invented’ language or script

caption: Float environment to document the shell commands of a terminal session

descriptions.text: The package provides a simple, though fancy float environment to document terminal sessions — like command executions or shell operations. The look and feel of the package output imitates the look of a shell prompt.

name: shdoc

topics.details: highlight syntax of computer code, etc.

caption: A collection of LaTeX packages and classes

descriptions.text:
The bundle collects packages and classes, along with one bibliography style and examples and scripts for converting TeX files. Many of the files in the collection are designed to support field biologists and/or Russian writers, while others have wider application.

The collection includes:

  • add2 – Save trees. Quick way to fit as many as possible into one page. Good for handouts.
  • altverse – Typesetting verses. Straightforward typesetting, using the xtab package to aid layout.
  • autolist – More lists. A means to define various sorts of list.
  • biokey – Flexible identification key tables in LaTeX. The package provides straightforward macros to typeset sets of biological identification keys. Layout is flexible, and the macros will be useful in other disciplines.
  • biolist – List observed species. Pretty formatting of species lists of flora and fauna.
  • boldline – Heavier lines in tables. The package provides commands replacing \hline and \cline, as well as a table preamble element that generates heavy lines.
  • cassete (with one ‘t’) – Print labels for audio cassettes. This is a LaTeX2e class file (the only other cassette package on CTAN is cassette (with two ‘t’), written for Plain TeX).
  • classif2 – Biological classification tables. The package defines an environment classif that simplifies the process of typesetting classification tables.
  • dline – Double line on the left of text.
  • drcaps – Simple dropped capitals. The package offers simple macros for dropped capitals, in a couple of forms.
  • etiketka – Class for typesetting business-card-sized information (including business cards).
  • flower – Typesetting lists of flower formulas.
  • isyntax – Interactively check LaTeX file syntax.
  • numerus – Spell numbers in Russian words.
  • punct – Within italicized text, punctuation is still straight, this is typographically more aesthetic.
  • qqru – Universal quotation marks, for Russian and English. It is able also to convert uniform typewriter “quotes” into left or right typographic quotes.
  • rusnat – Bibliography style file, now deprecated.
  • sltables – Simplified tables for LaTeX. These macros develop the concepts of the stables, which are designed to offer table macros whose use is “as simple as one might hope”. Some would claim that LaTeX’s built-in table specifications are as simple as one might hope, but this package offers many short-cuts and optimization of the mechanisms of tables.
  • starfn – Stars as footnote marks.
  • textfrac – Simple slanted fractions.

name: shipunov

caption: LaTeX compilation script for Linux (written in Bash)

descriptions.text: This script permits centralization of the many program calls necessary to completely compile a LaTeX document. In particular, the multiple calls of the LaTeX command necessary in order to create a table of contents, a bibliography or an index are carried out automatically. Are also managed the calls of the programs BibTeX and makeindex as well as the vizualisation of the resulting file (in DVI, PostScript or PDF format) by calling an external program. It is possible to stress characters in documents wich use the \input and \include commands to make references to some external files, and that in a transparent way by compiling only the main source file. Available in English and French languages.

name: shlatex

caption: Serbo-Croatian hyphenation (Latin alphabet)

descriptions.text: Serbo-Croatian may be written in either Cyrillic or Latin alphabets. These patterns deal with Latin-alphabet writing.

name: shhyphl

topics.details: documentation in, and support for typesetting Serbian

caption: Unified shell escape interface for LaTeX

descriptions.text:
This package provides a cross-engine interface, \ShellEscape, to running system commands, traditionally made available using \write18. It also makes \write18 access system commands (via Lua os.exec) on new LuaTeX, where \write18 does not have this feature by default.

This package is part of the latex-tools bundle in the LaTeX required distribution.

name: shellesc

caption: An OpenType Devanāgarī font designed for scholars

descriptions.text:
This package provides a free, open source, Unicode compliant, OpenType font with support for Devanāgarī, Latin, and Cyrillic scripts. It is available in two weights—regular and bold. The font is designed with over 1600 Devanāgarī glyphs, including support for over 1100 conjunct consonants, as well as vedic accents.

The Latin component of the font not only supports a wide range of characters required for Roman transliteration of Sanskrit, but also provides a subset of regularly used mathematical symbols for scholars working with scientific and technical documents.

The project has been launched under the auspices of the Science and Heritage Initiative (SandHI) at IIT Bombay, and builds upon the following two fonts for its Devanāgarī and Latin components respectively: (i) Yashomudra by Rājya Marāṭhī Vikās Saṃsthā, and (ii) PT Serif by ParaType. We would like to thank both these organisations for releasing their fonts under the SIL Open Font Licence, which has enabled us to create Shobhika.

name: shobhika

topics.details: fonts for languages of the Indian subcontinent
fonts for Cyrillic and related scripts
font with adaptations to several languages

caption: Guide to using amsmath and related packages to typeset mathematical notation with LaTeX

descriptions.text:
The Short Math Guide is intended to be a concise introduction to the use of the facilities provided by amsmath and various other LaTeX packages for typesetting mathematical notation.

Originally created by Michael Downes of the American Mathematical Society based only on amsmath, it has been brought up to date with references to related packages and other useful information.

name: short-math-guide

caption: Table of contents with different depths

descriptions.text: A package to create another table of contents with a different depth, useful in large documents where a detailed table of contents should be accompanied by a shorter one, giving only a general overview of the main topics in the document.

name: shorttoc

topics.details: deal with Tables of Contents, and of other such things

caption: Automatically shortify titles of mathematical journals

descriptions.text:
This small dummy package just contains a simple list of full and short journal names aswritten in
AMS standard: https://mathscinet.ams.org/msnhtml/serials.pdf

name: shortmathj

caption: Enables shortcut file import to the input tool Shortcut

descriptions.text:
Typing LaTeX commands can be facilitated by the Windows input tool Shortcut.

The creation of a shortcut base just with the input window of Shortcut is cumbersome. Here is a tool for the import of shortcut files in plain text, together with a shortcut file containing more than 140 shortcuts.

name: shortcuttool

caption: Compact lists by running several items per line

descriptions.text: Provides four environments for typesetting lists of short items which may be laid out horizontally to save space.

license.name: Do Not Sell Except by Arrangement

name: shortlst

caption: Abbreviated verbatim commands

descriptions.text:
The package defines a command \MakeShortVerb that makes a single character active, expanding to give the effect of a \verb command. Thus, after \MakeShortVerb{\|}, the text |stuff| has the same effect as \verb|stuff|.

The package is part of the LaTeX distribution.

name: shortvrb

caption: Variants of \show for LaTeX2e

descriptions.text: This small package aims at making debugging (especially in an interactive way) easier, by providing \show variants suited to LaTeX2e commands (whether with optional arguments or robust) and environments. The variant commands also display the internal macros used by such commands, if any. The \showcs variant helps with macros with exotic names.

name: show2e

topics.details: support for package or document debugging

caption: Typesetting LaTeX source code

descriptions.text: This package provides a way to typeset LaTeX source code and the related result in the same document.

name: showexpl

topics.details: print (La)TeX code verbatim alongside the rendered result

caption: Show characters inside a box

descriptions.text:
The package typesets a character inside a box, showing where reference point is, and displaying width, height, and depth information of the character.

The output is like that on page 63 of “The TeXBook” or page 101 of “The METAFONTbook”. The package itself is motivated by Knuth’s macros in the file manmac.tex.

Users should note that using a small size for the character inside the box does not make any sense: use a large size.

name: showcharinbox

topics.details: support for font development, testing and characterisation

caption: Variants on printing dimensions

descriptions.text: A package for LaTeX providing a number of commands for printing the value of a TeX dimension. For example, \tenthpt{\baselineskip} yields the current value of \baselineskip rounded to the nearest tenth of a point.

name: showdim

topics.details: support for package or document debugging

caption: Draw a page-layout diagram

descriptions.text:
The package shows a (simple, uncluttered) diagram of the page layout; similar (but more complex-looking) diagrams may be obtained from the layouts and geometry packages.

The package is available as part of the eso-pic distribution.

name: showframe

topics.details: layout of objects on the page

caption: Marking of hyphenation points

descriptions.text:
The package shows the hyphenation points in the document by either inserting small triangles below the baseline or by typesetting explicit hyphens.

The markers are correctly placed even within ligatures and their size adjusts to the font size. By option the markers can be placed behind or in front of the glyphs.

The package requires LuaLaTeX.

name: showhyphenation

topics.details: support for package or document debugging
LuaTeX and packages that require it

caption: Show all possible hyphenations in LuaLaTeX

descriptions.text: With this package, LuaLaTeX will indicate all possible hyphenations in the printed output.

name: showhyphens

topics.details: LuaTeX and packages that require it

caption: Showing kerns in a document

descriptions.text:
The package displays all kerning values in the form of colored bars directly at the respective position in the document. Positive values are displayed in green, negative values in red. The width of the bars corresponds exactly to the respective kerning value.

By option the bars can be placed behind or in front of the glyphs.

The package requires LuaLaTeX.

name: showkerning

topics.details: LuaTeX and packages that require it

caption: Show label, ref, cite and bib keys

descriptions.text:
The showkeys package modifies the \label, \ref, \pageref, \cite and \bibitem commands so that the ‘internal’ key is printed, without affecting the appearance of the rest of the text, so far as is possible (the keys typically appear in the margin).

The package is part of the latex-tools bundle in the LaTeX required distribution.

name: showkeys

caption: A letter document style for use at SHSU

descriptions.text: An document style (based on article) to typeset letters in a form appropriate for use at Sam Houston State University.

name: shsulet

caption: Print the tags of bibliography entries

descriptions.text: Prints the tag right-aligned on each line of the bibliography.

name: showtags

caption: Show label commands in the margin

descriptions.text:
This package helps you keep track of all the labels you define, by putting the name of new labels into the margin whenever the \label command is used.

The package allows you to do the same thing for other commands. The only one for which this is obviously useful is the \cite command, but it’s easy to do it for others, such as the \ref or \begin commands.

name: showlabels

caption: An unofficial LaTeX thesis template for ShanghaiTech University

descriptions.text: This package, forked from ucasthesis, is an unofficial LaTeX thesis template for ShanghaiTech University and satisfies all format requirements of the school. The user just needs to set \documentclass{shtthesis} and to set up mandatory information via \shtsetup, then his or her thesis document will be typeset properly.

name: ShtThesis

caption: A symbol for the shuffle product

descriptions.text: The bundle provides a LaTeX package and a font (as Metafont source) for the shuffle product which is used in some part of mathematics and physics.

name: shuffle

caption: Styles for SIAM publications

descriptions.text: Packages for plain TeX and both LaTeX and old LaTeX 2.09, with instructions for submissions. The bundle includes usage templates for all three packages.

license.name: Do Not Sell Except by Arrangement

name: siam

caption: A comprehensive (SI) units package

descriptions.text:
This is a complete re-implementation of units support for LaTeX, building on the existing SIunits and sistyle packages. The package incorporates ideas from the unitsdef and numprint packages, and aims to provide a consistent and logical interface.

This is an earlier version of the package now known as siunitx; that package should be used for new applications.

name: si

topics.details: support for writers of scientific documents

caption: Typeset captions sideways

descriptions.text: Defines environments called SCfigure and SCtable (analogous to figure and table) to typeset captions sideways. Options include outercaption, innercaption, leftcaption and rightcaption.

name: sidecap

topics.details: rotate typeset objects on their page

caption: Rotated floats for LaTeX 2.09

descriptions.text:
The package provides tools for creating floats with rotated (landscape) bodies, using the rotate package. The package is restricted to PostScript output.

The package is superseded by the LaTeX 2e rotating package.

name: side

topics.details: rotate typeset objects on their page
package only known to work with LaTeX 2.09

caption: Typeset notes containing rich content, in the margin

descriptions.text: The package allows typesetting of texts with notes, figures, citations, captions and tables in the margin. This is common (for example) in science text books.

name: sidenotes

caption: Place referenced notes, alerts, figures and tables into the document margin

descriptions.text:
Sidenotesplus is a comprehensive package for placing labeled or referenced notes, temporary alerts, bibliography references, figures and tables into the margin. Marginals can be either floated or at fixed positions relative to the text. Twoside symmetry is preserved. For BibLaTeX users, macros for side references are provided.

Three margin styles are provided. Two-page symmetric layouts either as (i) Ragged outer with note reverences in the margin separator or (ii) justified with last line ragged outer. And (iii) a classic look, justified with last line ragged right and note reference to the left of the note, but two-page symmetry is lost.

The command \sidenote mimics the \footnote command and provides labelled (numbers, alphabetic, roman) references. However, un-numbered and custom symbols can also be specified.

Temporary sidealerts are rendered only if the package option alerton is specified. Alerts are useful as to do reminders during document development.

Furthermore, captions for figures and tables can also be placed into margin. Also, full width environments for figures, tables and text are provided. The text environment can be partially widened, suitable if that extra space for an equation is required.

name: sidenotesplus

caption: SIGGRAPH conference class

descriptions.text: Document class for formatting papers according to the specifications for submission to the annual ACM SIGGRAPH conference.

name: siggraph

caption: A LaTeX class for typesetting stage plays

descriptions.text: This is a LaTeX class for typesetting stage plays, based on the plari class written by Antti-Juhani Kaijanaho in 1998. It has been updated and several formatting changes have been made to it—most noticibly there are no longer orphans.

name: sides

caption: Create beautifully typeset sign charts

descriptions.text: The package allows users to easily typeset beautiful looking sign charts directly into their (La)TeX document.

name: signchart

caption: Selective filtering of error messages and warnings

descriptions.text:
The package allows the user to filter out unwanted warnings and error messages issued by LaTeX, packages and classes, so they won’t pop out when there’s nothing one can do about them.

Filtering goes from the very broad (“avoid all messages by such and such”) to the fine-grained (“avoid messages that begin with…”).

Messages may be saved to an external file for later reference.

name: silence

caption: Lyx template for Hebrew article format

descriptions.text: The template applies to the article-hebrew form used in Sikumuna.

name: Sikumuna

topics.details: documentation in and support for typesetting Hebrew

caption: Template for a simple resume or curriculum vitae (CV), in XeLaTeX

descriptions.text: Template for a simple resume or curriculum vitae (CV), in XeLaTeX. Simple template that can be further customized or extended, with numerous examples.

name: simple-resume-cv

caption: John Cleese’s Silly Walk as page numbering style

copyright.owner: Phelype Oleinik, Paulo Cereda, samcarter, and Ulrike Fischer

descriptions.text: This simple LaTeX package provides John Cleese’s iconic silly walk routine as a page numbering style. Other counters, as well as integers, can be typeset in this “silly” style, too.

name: sillypage

topics.details: jokes, distractions, tongue-in-cheek packages, and other entertainment material
control sequence and typesettting of page numbers

caption: Insert 'terminal' or 'context menu' or 'viewers' like in an OS

descriptions.text:
This is a package to present, like in an OS:

  • a fake terminal (with tcolorbox);
  • a fake context menu with sub-menus (with TikZ);
  • a fake viewer (with tcolorbox).

name: sim-os-menus

caption:
Template for a simple thesis or dissertation (Ph.D. or master's degree) or technical
  report, in XeLaTeX

descriptions.text: Template for a simple thesis or dissertation (Ph.D. or master's degree) or technical report, in XeLaTeX. Simple template that can be further customized or extended, with numerous examples. Consistent style for figures, tables, mathematical theorems, definitions, lemmas, etc.

name: simple-thesis-dissertation

caption: A simple package to format Backus-Naur form (BNF)

descriptions.text:
This package provides a simple way for typesetting grammars in Backus-Naur form (BNF). The included bnf environment parses BNF expressions (possibly annotated), so users can write readable BNF expressions in their documents. It features a flexible configuration system, allowing for the customization of the domain-specific language (DSL) used in typesetting the grammar. Additionally, the package comes with sensible defaults.

The package requires expl3, xparse, mathtools, and tabularray..

name: simplebnf

caption: Simple CD, DVD covers for printing

descriptions.text: The package provides printable cut-outs for various CD, DVD and other disc holders. The name of the package comes from its implementation and ease of use; it was designed just for text content, but since the text is placed in a \parbox in a tabular environment cell, a rather wide range of things may be placed.

name: simplecd

topics.details: typeset badges, covers or labels for things (or people)

caption: A simple class for writing curricula vitae

descriptions.text: A derivative of the cv class available to lyx users (renamed to avoid the existing cv package).

name: simplecv

caption: Simple Icons for LaTeX

descriptions.text: Similar to FontAwesome icons being provided on LaTeX by the fontawesome package, this package aims to do the same with Simple Icons. For reference, visit their website: https://simpleicons.org/.

name: simpleicons

topics.details: fonts that provide collections of symbols
metrics, macro incantations and other support for symbol fonts
font available in Adobe Type 1 format

caption: A simple key/value system for TeX and LaTeX

descriptions.text: The package provides a simple key/value system for TeX and LaTeX.

name: simplekv

caption: Simple nodes in four colors written in TikZ for LaTeX

descriptions.text:
This is a LaTeX macro package for generating simple node-based flow graphs or diagrams built upon the TikZ package. The package provides two basic commands, one to generate a node and one to create links between nodes. The positioning of the nodes is not handled by the package itself but is preferably done in a tabular environment.

In total, four simple node types are defined, loosely based on the nomenclature and color patterns of the popular Java script Bootstrap.

name: simplenodes

caption: Easy typesetting of invoices

descriptions.text: This package lets you easily typeset professional-looking invoices. The user specifies the content of the invoice by different \setPROPERTY commands, and an invoice is generated automatically with the \makeinvoice command.

name: simpleinvoice

caption: Drawing lenses and mirrors for optical diagrams

descriptions.text: This package provides some of macros for drawing simple lenses and mirrors for use in optical diagrams.

name: simpleoptics

caption: Simpler Wick contractions

descriptions.text:
In every quantum field theory course, there will be a chapter about Wick’s theorem and how it can be used to convert a very large product of many creation and annihilation operators into something more tractable and normal ordered.

The contractions are denoted with a square bracket over the operators which are being contracted, which used to be rather annoying to typeset in LaTeX as the only other package available was simplewick, which is rather unwieldy.

This package provides a simpler syntax for Wick contractions.

name: simpler-wick

caption: Define matrices by given list of values

copyright.owner: Yvon Henel aka Le TeXnicien de surface

descriptions.text: Macros to define and write matrices whose coefficients are given row by row in a list of values separated by commas.

name: simples-matrices

caption: Simple Wick contractions

descriptions.text: The package provides a simple means of drawing Wick contractions above and below expressions.

name: simplewick

caption: A Simplified Introduction to LaTeX

descriptions.text: An accessible introduction for the beginner.

name: simplified-latex

caption: Write your books in a simple and clear way

descriptions.text:
This package provides a LaTeX class for typesetting books with a simple and clear design.

Currently, it has native support for Chinese (simplified and traditional), English, French, German, Italian, Japanese, Portuguese (European and Brazilian), Russian and Spanish typesetting. It compiles with either XeLaTeX or LuaLaTeX.

This is part of the minimalist class series and depends on minimalist.sty from the minimalist package.

The package name “simplivre” is taken from the French words “simple” and “livre” (= “book”).

name: simplivre

topics.details: support for more than one (natural) language

caption: Metafont source for Simpsons characters
name: simpsons

topics.details: fonts designed more for fun than for actual use

caption: Typeset Parsi in LuaLaTeX

descriptions.text:
The package provides an automatic and unified interface for Parsi typesetting in LaTeX, using the LuaTeX engine.

The project to produce this system is dedicated to Ferdowsi The Great.

name: simurgh

topics.details: LuaTeX and packages that require it

caption: Calculate sin function values

descriptions.text: The file provides macros to calculate the sine of angles from -90 to +90 degrees.

name: sines

caption: Fonts and macros for typesetting Tibetan

descriptions.text: A set of files for typesetting the Tibetan language in TeX or LaTeX.

name: sirlin

caption: Support for the Sinhala language

descriptions.text: A collection of Metafont fonts and macros, to support typesetting of Sinhala, in particular using the samanala transcription scheme.

name: sinhala

topics.details: support for languages of the Indian subcontinent

caption: Package to typeset SI units, numbers and angles

descriptions.text:
This package typesets SI units, numbers and angles according to the ISO requirements. Care is taken with font setup and requirements, and language customisation is available.

Note that this package is (in principle) superseded by siunitx; sistyle has maintenance-only support, now.

name: SIstyle

topics.details: support for writers of scientific documents
support for variations of typographic style

caption: Save the optional argument of \item

descriptions.text: The package modifies \item commands to save the optional argument in a box.

name: sitem

caption: A comprehensive (SI) units package

descriptions.text:
Typesetting values with units requires care to ensure that the combined mathematical meaning of the value plus unit combination is clear. In particular, the SI units system lays down a consistent set of units with rules on how they are to be used. However, different countries and publishers have differing conventions on the exact appearance of numbers (and units). A number of LaTeX packages have been developed to provide consistent application of the various rules: SIunits, sistyle, unitsdef and units are the leading examples. The numprint package provides a large number of number-related functions, while dcolumn and rccol provide tools for typesetting tabular numbers.

The siunitx package takes the best from the existing packages, and adds new features and a consistent interface. A number of new ideas have been incorporated, to fill gaps in the existing provision. The package also provides backward-compatibility with SIunits, sistyle, unitsdef and units. The aim is to have one package to handle all of the possible unit-related needs of LaTeX users.

The package relies on LaTeX 3 support from the l3kernel and l3packages bundles.

name: siunitx

topics.details: support for writers of scientific documents

caption: International System of Units

descriptions.text:
Typeset physical units following the rules of the International System of Units (SI).

The package requires amstext, for proper representation of some values.

Note that the package is now superseded by siunitx; siunits has maintenance-only support, now.

name: siunits

topics.details: support for writers of scientific documents
support for variations of typographic style

caption: Fonts and macros for typesetting chess games

descriptions.text:
This package provides macros and fonts in Metafont format which can be used to typeset chess games using PGN, and to show diagrams of the current board in a document. The package builds on work by Piet Tutelaers — the main novelty is the use of PGN for input instead of the more cumbersome coordinate notation (g1f3 becomes the more readable Nf3 in PGN).

An Adobe Type 1 implementation of skak's fonts is available as package skaknew; an alternative chess notational scheme is available in package texmate, and a general mechanism for selecting chess fonts is provided in chessfss.

name: skak

topics.details: process game diagrams, gamebooks, and other amusements
fonts for typesetting chess problems and diagrams

caption: Documentation and extraction for packages and document classes

descriptions.text:
The class provides the functionality and implementation of packages and document classes. It is loosely based on the ydoc and ltxdoc classes, but has a number of incompatible differences.

The class defines a MacroCode environment which offers an alternative to the usual docstrip method of installing packages. It has the ability to generate both documentation and code in a single run of a single file.

name: skdoc

topics.details: macros and tools for preparing documentation

caption: The skak chess fonts redone in Adobe Type 1

descriptions.text: This package offers Adobe Type 1 versions of the fonts provided as Metafont source by the skak bundle.

name: SkakNew

topics.details: fonts for typesetting chess problems and diagrams
font available in Adobe Type 1 format
process game diagrams, gamebooks, and other amusements

caption: Tools for a repository of long-living documents

descriptions.text:
The package provides macros that help to build a document repository for long living documents. It focuses on structure and re-use of text, code, figures etc. The basic concept is first to separate structure from content (i.e., text about a topic from the structure it is presented by) and then separating the content from the actual published document, thus enabling easy re-use of text blocks in different publications (i.e., text about a protocol in a short article about this protocol as well as in a book about many protocols); all without constantly copying or changing text.

As a side effect, using the document classes provided, it hides a lot of LaTeX from someone who just wants to write articles and books.

name: skb

topics.details: creating archival copies, or copies for distribution

caption: A 3d sketch language translator

descriptions.text:
Sketch is a small, simple system for producing line drawings of two- or three-dimensional objects and scenes. It began as a way to make illustrations for a textbook after we could find no suitable tool for this purpose. Existing scene processors emphasized GUIs and/or photo-realism, neither of which was useful to us. We wanted to produce finely wrought, mathematically-based illustrations with no extraneous detail.

The input language is reminiscent of PSTricks, so will be easy for current PSTricks users to learn; output is for use either by pstricks itself, or by pgf.

name: sketch

topics.details: convert a foreign graphics format for use with TeX

caption: Placeholders for unfinished documents

descriptions.text: This package lets you produce placeholder elements for documents under development, similar to the skeleton screens used while loading contents in many applications and websites. It also has a mechanism for attaching explanatory endnotes to these placeholders, or to anything else in your document. The same note mechanism can also be used with ordinary content, e.g., as a to-do mechanism.

name: skeldoc

topics.details: dummy text generator for tests and examples
general notes (not including endnotes or footnotes)

caption: Extensions to the maths command repertoir

descriptions.text: The package provides a selection of new maths commands and improved re-definitions of existing commands.

name: skmath

caption: Create proficiency tests

descriptions.text:
This package attempts to make it easy for even a LaTeX novice to prepare proficiency tests, especially in combination with the exam document class. Thus, almost all command names are very similar.

After defining skills in the preamble or in an external file, they are declared using labels, and can optionally be set as global skills. A skills table is generated to summarize the evaluated competencies and to allow for writing down the resulting proficiency level.

A user’s guide attempts to explain all of the possibilities in a readable way, with many examples.

name: skills

caption: Key-value parsing combining features of xkeyval and pgfkeys

descriptions.text: The package integrates the features of xkeyval and of pgfkeys by introducing a new type of handlers. Style keys, links, changing key callbacks and values on the fly, and other features of pgfkeys are introduced in a new context.

name: skeyval

caption: Create commands using parameters and keyval in parallel

descriptions.text: The package provides tools for defining LaTeX commands and environments using combinations of parameters and keys. All the facilities of the ltxkeys and skeyval packages are available to the user of skeycommand.

name: skeycommand

caption: ‘Simple’ class for reports, etc

descriptions.text: The class is intended for simple documents (e.g., reports handed in as coursework and the like). The class is small and straightforward; its design was inspired by that of the PracTeX journal style.

name: skrapport

caption: A font to draw a skull

descriptions.text: The font (defined in Metafont) defines a single character, a black solid skull. A package is supplied to make this character available as a symbol in maths mode.

name: skull

topics.details: fonts designed more for fun than for actual use

caption: Access different-shaped small-caps fonts

descriptions.text: This package enables the use of small capitals in different font shapes, e.g., slanted or bold slanted for all fonts that provide appropriate font shapes. (Note that a separate .fd file is needed to define font shapes such as ‘scsl’ or ‘scit’.)

name: slantsc

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other font support

caption: Both column and row headings in a tabular cell

descriptions.text: The package defines commands to produce tabular cells with diagonal lines in them, with text above and below the line to label the column and row that the cell is in.

name: slashbox

caption: Put a slash through characters

descriptions.text:
Useful for the Physicist’s ‘Feynman slashed character’ notation.

The package is distributed as part of the carlisle bundle.

name: slashed

caption: LaTeX support for writing Swedish

descriptions.text: LaTeX macros to deal with the national characters in 7-bit-encoded Swedish. The collection includes a program (l2sl) that will translate an existing LaTeX document into slatex format.

name: slatex

caption: A pretty-printer for Scheme code in TeX documents

descriptions.text: SLaTeX is a Scheme program that allows you to write programs or program fragments ‘as is’ in your TeX or LaTeX source. It is particularly geared to the programming languages Scheme and other Lisp dialects, such as Common Lisp. The formatting of the code includes assigning appropriate fonts and colors to the various tokens in the code (keywords, variables, constants, data), at the same time retaining the proper indentation when going to the non-monospace (non-typewriter) fonts provided by TeX.

name: slatex-scheme

caption: Slanted emphasis in LaTeX 2.09

descriptions.text: A jiffy package to cause \em in LaTeX 2.09 to use \sl in place of the standard \it. Note that the package will not work in LaTeX 2e.

name: slem

topics.details: package only known to work with LaTeX 2.09

caption: Slanted emphasis in LaTeX

descriptions.text:
A LaTeX package defining commands \itswitch, \slswitch, \textitswitch, and \textslswitch, which switch between slanted or italic type and upright type. The commands may be used to represent emphasis with slanted type.

The package is part of the frankenstein bundle of packages.

name: slemph

caption: Slovenian hyphenation patterns

descriptions.text: The function of this package is encompassed in that of the hyph-utf8 package, for future applications.

name: slhyph

topics.details: support for typesetting, and documentation in Slovenian

caption: Typeset slides accompanied by notes

descriptions.text: A class package for the easy production of a slide collection with annotations. Builds on the report style (or variants); document structure is based on chapters, with the slides themselves represented by sections.

name: slidenotes

topics.details: macros and tools for preparing documentation

caption: Class for creating slides

descriptions.text:
This is a standard LaTeX2e class for the production of overhead transparencies (foils), replacing the older SliTeX format. Can be used in conjunction with lscape and fancyhdr, for example.

There are many better means of producing slides (and particularly beamer-based presentations) — see the presentation topic in the online catalogue.

This package is part of the LaTeX distribution.

name: slides

caption: Simplified tables for LaTeX

descriptions.text:
These macros develop the concepts of the stables, which are designed to offer table macros whose use is “as simple as one might hope”.

Some would claim that LaTeX's built-in table specifications are as simple as one might hope, but this package offers many short-cuts and optimisation of the mechanisms of tables.

The package is part of the shipunov bundle.

name: sltables

caption: Generate slideshow with MetaPost

descriptions.text: The package provides a means of creating presentations in MetaPost, without intervention from other utilities (except a distiller). Such an arrangement has its advantages (though there are disadvantages too).

name: slideshow

caption: Promote small caps to a font family, so NFSS can deal with different shapes

descriptions.text: A set of files that uses the fonts available in version 1.3 of the DC fonts to provide support for all 4 shapes of small caps. SC becomes a family, rather than a shape (\scshape is replaced by \scfamily). Thus you can write \textbf{\scfamily\slshape ...} to get small caps bold slanted.

name: smallcap

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other font support

caption: Choose an "adjacent" size in LaTeX

descriptions.text:
Defines two commands \larger and \smaller. Starting with text size \small, \larger will give you \normalsize and \smaller will give you \footnotesize—in each case, one step on the hierarchy of LaTeX sizes.

This LaTeX 2.09 package is superseded by the more subtle relsize package for current LaTeX.

name: smaller

topics.details: package only known to work with LaTeX 2.09

caption: Create listoffigures etc. in a single chapter

descriptions.text: The package allows you to create a list of figures and list of tables in a chapter named ‘List’ that contains separate sections for each list of figures, tables, etc.

name: smalltableof

topics.details: deal with Tables of Contents, and of other such things

caption: Typeset Smalltalk program fragments

descriptions.text:
Defines an environment smalltalk for typesetting program code.

The package was written for LaTeX 2.09, but it runs under current LaTeX.

name: smalltalk

caption: Automatic math symbol styling for LaTeX documents

descriptions.text: In LaTeX typesetting, one usually needs to use different variants of a math symbol to clarify the meanings. For example, in linear algebra literature, it is common to use boldfaced symbols to represent vectors, and normal symbols to represent scalars. However, applying these variants by typing \mathbf, \mathrm commands manually can be daunting. This package aims to provide an automatic and customizable approach for math symbol styling which eliminates the need to enter style commands repeatedly.

name: smart-eqn

caption: Generate diagrams from lists

descriptions.text: The package will create ‘smart’ diagrams from lists of items, for simple documents and for presentations.

name: smartdiagram

caption: Make hyphens print as minus signs where appropriate

descriptions.text: This package activates the minus sign such that it guesses whether to print as a hyphen or as minus sign in text mode (which is one of the most common typographical errors in LaTeX texts).

name: smartmn

topics.details: support for variations of typographic style

caption: Classes for Société mathématique de France publications

descriptions.text: The Société mathématique de France provides a set of classes, packages and BibTeX styles that are used in its publications. They are based on AMS classes (whose code is sometimes recopied) and mainly ‘upward-compatible’. Their main features are: quite different design; new environments for typesetting some information in two languages (altabstract, alttitle, altkeywords); if necessary, use of babel (option frenchb) and deactivation of some features of frenchb. Includes smfart.cls, smfbook.cls, smfplain.bst, smfalpha.bst, amongst others.

name: smflatex

caption: Extend LaTeX's \ref capability

descriptions.text:
The package extends the LaTeX labelling system: whenever a label is set, the values of counters (selected by the user) are recorded, along with the label. The value of these counters can be recalled with a command similar to \pageref.

The package also adds commands \s[name]ref (for each counter [name] that the user has selected); these commands display something only if the value of the [name] counter is changed from when the label was set. Many commands are provided to serve as a macro programming environment for using the extended labels.

name: smartref

caption: Converting between common metric and Imperial units

descriptions.text:
This LaTeX package implements a \SmartUnit macro for converting between (some) metric and Imperial units.

The package requires pgfkeys and siunitx.

name: smartunits

caption: Create LaTeX documents and more from simple texts

descriptions.text: SmileTeX is a small compiler for win32 systems, which takes simple text files and creates LaTeX documents and furthermore PDF, DVI and HTML documents from them. It automatically calls all tools necessary to include nearly all types of images and Excel tables, it recognizes equations, hyperlinks, sections, lists, special characters, references, long comments, table of contents, colors, etc. Additionally, it comes with a WinEdt highlighting scheme and menus.

name: SmileTeX

caption: List the external dependencies of a LaTeX document

descriptions.text: The snapshot package helps the owner of a LaTeX document obtain a list of the external dependencies of the document, in a form that can be embedded at the top of the document. It provides a snapshot of the current processing context of the document, insofar as it can be determined from inside LaTeX. If a document contains such a dependency list, then it becomes possible to arrange that the document be processed always with the same versions of everything, in order to ensure the same output. This could be useful for someone wanting to keep a LaTeX document on hand and consistently reproduce an identical DVI file from it, on the fly; or for someone wanting to shield a document during the final stages of its production cycle from unexpected side effects of routine upgrades to the TeX system.

name: snapshot

topics.details: creating archival copies, or copies for distribution

caption: A todo that snaps to the closer side

descriptions.text:
This package is an alternative to todonotes, from which it differs in the following ways:

  • Depending on where you call \snaptodo, the note is put in the left or the right margin, whichever is closer.
  • The notes bump each other so they never overlap; the lines never overlap either.
  • Aesthetic and customizable style.

name: snaptodo

topics.details: general notes (not including endnotes or footnotes)

caption: Typeset notes, in the margin

descriptions.text:
The package provides a macro \sidenote, that places a note in the margin of the document, with its baseline aligned with the baseline in the body of the document. These sidenotes are numbered (both in the text, and on the notes themselves).

The package loads the package etoolbox, pgfopts and marginnote.

name: snotez

caption: Commands for dealing with Sobolev spaces (and relatives)

descriptions.text:
Provides commands which are useful when dealing with Hilbert and Sobolev spaces (which occours very often, for example, in numerical analysis). It also provides the \Norm, \SemiNorm, \Scalar and \Crochet commands which are also involved in the same context.

The package is part of the bosisio collection.

name: sobolev

caption: Makes appearance of standard styles more "sober"

descriptions.text:
The package makes headings less overbearing, and reduces the size of various skips (notably those around headings, and within and around lists).

Similar effects are achieved, in a more satisfactory fashion, in some of the classes in the ntgclass collection.

name: sober

topics.details: layout of objects on the page

caption: Shaped notes for MusicTeX

descriptions.text: Shaped note schemes have different-shaped note-heads for different position on the scale, or for a selection of positions. Snote implements two such schemes: a four-note scheme (\fasola) and the Funk seven-note system (\doremi).

name: snote

caption: Manage the "soft fonts" in a LaserWriter printer

descriptions.text: A collection of DOS utilities to convert between PK fonts and fonts for use in Hewlett-Packard LaserWriter printers.

name: softfonts

topics.details: process fonts for use with TeX (includes installation)

caption: LaTeX Support files for the SoftMaker Alte Schwabacher font

descriptions.text:
This package offers LaTeX support files for the Softmaker Alte Schwabacher font, offered (free) from SoftMaker in May 2009, but not included here.

The package requires support files from the softmakerfreefont package, which also offers further information.

name: softmaker-alteschwabacher

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other support for miscellaneous fonts (not on CTAN)
support is for a font not available on CTAN

caption: LaTeX Support files for SoftMaker Bonita

descriptions.text:
This package offers LaTeX support files for the Softmaker Bonita font (regular), offered (free) from SoftMaker in September 2010, but not included here.

The package requires support files from the softmakerfreefont package, which also offers further information.

name: softmaker-bonita

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other support for miscellaneous fonts (not on CTAN)
support is for a font not available on CTAN
