caption: Storing information for reuse

descriptions.text:
The package provides “store boxes” whose user interface matches that of normal LaTeX “save boxes”, except that the content of a store box appears at most once in the output PDF file, however often it is used.

The present version of the package supports pdfLaTeX and LuaLaTeX; when DVI is output, store boxes behave the same as save boxes.

name: storebox

caption: Store the name of a defined command in a container

descriptions.text: The package provides macros for command definition that save the name of the command being defined in a file or a macro container. The list could be useful for spelling exceptions in text editors that do not support TeX syntax.

name: storecmd

caption: Draw objects constructed from strands

descriptions.text:
This package permits to draw objects constructed from strands, like set partitions, permutations, braids, etc.

It depends on forarray, ifthen, TikZ, xfp, xstring, and xkeyval.

name: strands

caption: Create string diagrams with LaTeX and TikZ

descriptions.text: This LaTeX package has been designed for effortless and aesthetically pleasing creation of string diagrams.

name: string-diagrams

caption: Structural organic chemistry

descriptions.text:
The package performs depth-in traversal of a structure using descriptions of bonds and vertex labels. Additional features include input of mass spectra and simple flow charts.

The package uses emtex \special commands for line drawing (though the cataloguer managed to compile the documentation using his distribution of dvips, which includes support for those extensions).

name: streetex

caption: Strictly balanced brackets and numbers in command names

descriptions.text:
This is a small, LuaLaTeX-only package providing you with three, sometimes useful features:

  • It allows you to make brackets [...] “strict”, meaning that each [ must be balanced by a ].
  • It allows you to use numbers in command names, so that you can do stuff like \newcommand\pi12{\pi_{12}}.
  • It allows you to use numbers and primes in command names, so that you can do stuff like \newcommand\pi'12{\pi '_{12}}.

name: stricttex

topics.details: LuaTeX and packages that require it

caption: Converting a string between different encodings

descriptions.text: This package provides \StringEncodingConvert for converting a string between different encodings. Both LaTeX and plain-TeX are supported.

name: stringenc

caption: String manipulation for cosmetic and programming application

descriptions.text:
The package provides a large and sundry set of macros for the manipulation of strings. The macros are developed not merely for cosmetic application (such as changing the case of letters and string substitution), but also for programming applications such as character look-ahead, argument parsing, conditional tests on various string conditions, etc.

The macros were designed all to be expandable (note that things such as \uppercase and \lowercase are not expandable), so that the macros may be strung together sequentially and nested (after a fashion) to achieve rather complex manipulations.

name: stringstrings

caption: A TikZ command set for structural mechanics drawings

descriptions.text: This package provides a collection of TikZ commands that allow users to draw basic elements in material/structural mechanics. It is thus possible to draw member forces, nodal forces/displacements, various boundary conditions, internal force distributions, etc.

license.name: GNU General Public License, version 3 or newer

name: structmech

caption: Create tear-off stubs at the bottom of a page

descriptions.text: The \stubs command creates as many repetitions as possible of its argument, at the bottom of the page; these stubs may be used (for example) for contact information.

name: stubs

caption: Various macros

descriptions.text:
A collection of tools and macros, providing:

  • miscellaneous float control,
  • page styles for floats,
  • multipage tabulars,
  • even columns at end of twocolumn region,
  • switching between one- and two-column anywhere,
  • simulating the effect of “midfloats”,
  • a package to manipulate numerical lists and arrays.

name: sttools

caption: Draw Nassi-Shneiderman charts

descriptions.text:
Even in the age of OOP one must develop algorithms. Nassi-Shneiderman charts are a well known tool to describe an algorithm in a graphical way. The package offers some macros for generating those charts in a LaTeX document.

The package provides the most important elements of a Nassi-Shneiderman charts, including processing blocks, loops, mapping conventions for alternatives, etc. The charts are drawn using the picture environment (using pict2e for preference).

name: struktex

caption: Management and styling of student handout projects

descriptions.text:
This package can be used to generate a single master document that contains a set of individual student handouts. The package has two main functions.

First, it provides a simple framework for organizing handout source code, and supplies a set of import management tools for selectively importing a subset of the handouts into the master document. Selective import is convenient when compilation of all of the handouts is unnecessary, for example when working on a new handout.

As a secondary feature, the package defines a basic visual style for handouts. This style can be easily changed.

name: Student Handouts

caption: An interactive LaTeX course for students

descriptions.text: The package contains interactive teaching material for students (in German).

name: studies-lm

caption: Make a web page to compare styles

descriptions.text: The bundle supports the preparation of web pages that allow users to compare a number of article styles.

name: style-showcase

caption: Create a .dtx file from a .sty file

descriptions.text:
The package provides a Perl script that converts a .sty file (LaTeX package) to .dtx format (documented LaTeX source), by surrounding macro definitions with macro and macrocode environments. The macro name is automatically inserted as an argument to the macro environemnt.

Code lines outside macro definitions are wrapped only in macrocode environments. Empty lines are removed.

The script should not be thought to be fool proof and 100% accurate but rather as a good start to the business of making a .dtx file from an undocumented style file.

Full .dtx files are generated. A template based on the skeleton file from dtxtut is used. User level macros are added automatically to the “Usage” section of the .dtx file. A corresponding .ins file can be generated as well.

name: sty2dtx

caption: Handling multiple versions of user-defined macros

descriptions.text: This package allows creating and maintaining different versions of the same command, in order to choose the best option for every document. This includes expandable and protected commands.

license.name: GNU General Public License, version 3 or newer

name: styledcmd

caption: MetaPost macros for drawing Chinese and Japanese abaci

descriptions.text:
These macros are described in

Denis Roegel: MetaPost macros for drawing Chinese and Japanese abaci, TUGboat (volume 30, number 1, 2009, pages 74-79)

name: suanpan

topics.details: process game diagrams, gamebooks, and other amusements
use, and support for use, of Metapost

caption: Support for sub-captions

descriptions.text:
The package provides a means of using facilities analogous to those of the caption package, when writing captions for subfigures and the like.

The package is distributed with caption.

name: subcaption

caption: Unify maths subscript height

descriptions.text: This package is based on code (posted long ago to comp.text.tex by Donald Arseneau) to equalise the height of subscripts in maths. The default behaviour is to place subscripts slightly lower when there is a superscript as well, but this can look odd in some situations.

name: subdepth

topics.details: position sub- and superscripts (left and right sides)

caption: Package for subequation numbering

descriptions.text:
Sometimes it is necessary to be able to refer to subexpressions of an equation. In order to do that these subexpressions should be numbered. In standard LaTeX there is no provision for this. To solve this problem Stephen Gildea once wrote subeqn.sty for LaTeX 2.09; Donald Arsenau rewrote the macros and Johannes Braams made them available for LaTeX2e.

Note that this package is not compatible with the package subeqnarray (written by Johannes Braams), but it can be used together with the LaTeX class options leqno and fleqn.

name: subeqn

caption: Equation array with sub numbering

descriptions.text:
This package defines the subeqnarray and subeqnarray* environments, which behave like the corresponding eqnarray and eqnarray* environments, except that the individual lines are numbered like 1a, 1b, 1c, etc. To refer to these numbers an extra label command \slabel is provided.

Users are urged to consider the alignment capabilities of the amsmath bundle, which produce better results than eqnarray-related macros.

name: subeqnarray

caption: Multifile documents

descriptions.text:
This is an experimental package aiming to provide a different approach for multidocument works (mainly, books with a document per chapter). Unlike the \include mechanism, every subdocument is a complete normal LaTeX document and may be typeset separately. What the package does is sharing the .aux files.

The present release is an alpha version, and no attempt has yet been made to allow it to work with, say, hyperref.

name: subdocs

topics.details: include complete documents in other documents

caption: Automates layout when using the subfigure package

descriptions.text: Defines an array/matrix-type environment that is used with the subfigure package to automate the placement of subfigures (or tables or text). The subfigures are placed left-to-right, top-to-bottom.

name: subfigmat

caption: Figures broken into subfigures

descriptions.text:
The package provides support for the manipulation and reference of small or ‘sub’ figures and tables within a single figure or table environment. It is convenient to use this package when your subfigures are to be separately captioned, referenced, or are to be included in the List-of-Figures. A new \subfigure command is introduced which can be used inside a figure environment for each subfigure. An optional first argument is used as the caption for that subfigure.

This package supersedes the subfigure package (which is no longer maintained). The name was changed since the package is not completely backward compatible with the older package The major advantage of the new package is that the user interface is keyword/value driven and easier to use. To ease the transition from the subfigure package, the distribution includes a configuration file (subfig.cfg) which nearly emulates the subfigure package.

The functionality of the package is provided by the (more recent still) subcaption package.

name: subfig

caption: Deprecated: Figures divided into subfigures

descriptions.text:
Provides support for the manipulation and reference of small or ‘sub’ figures and tables within a single figure or table environment. It is convenient to use this package when your subfigures are to be separately captioned, referenced, or are to be included in the List-of-Figures. A new \subfigure command is introduced which can be used inside a figure environment for each subfigure. An optional first argument is used as the caption for that subfigure.

The package is now considered obsolete: it was superseded by subfig, but users may find the more recent subcaption package more satisfactory.

name: subfigure

caption: Sub-numbering for figures and tables

descriptions.text:
This package enables sub-numbering of floats (figures and tables) similar to the subequations-environment of the amsmath package.

The subfloat package is not to be confused with the subfig package which generates sub-figures within one normal figure, and manages their placement; subfloat only affects captions and numbering.

name: subfloat

caption: Sub-number counters

descriptions.text:
The macros in this package allow all counters to be subnumbered, as for example 4a, 4b, 4c, simply by bracketting the objects to be so numbered with appropriate on/off commands. They will work with any user-defined counters too.

The package is part of the preprint bundle.

name: sublabel

caption: Individual typesetting of subfiles of a “main” document

descriptions.text: Using this package the user can handle multi-file projects more comfortably, making it possible to both process the subsidiary files by themselves and to process the main file that includes them, without making any changes to either.

name: subfiles

topics.details: include complete documents in other documents

caption: A database of chemicals

descriptions.text: The package provides the means to create a database-like file that contains data of various chemicals. These data may be retrieved in the document; an index of the chemicals mentioned in the document can be created..

name: substances

caption: Provides the \textsubscript command

descriptions.text:
Provides a command \textsubscript, which is the counterpart to LaTeX's \textsuperscript command. From 2006 on this command was made available by the fixltx2e package distributed with LaTeX itself, and starting with the LaTeX 2015 releases it became part of the LaTeX kernel. Thus, these days this code is only necessary if you run on a very old LaTeX distribution and want to make use of this command.

Subscript is one of a series of fragments designed for use by package writers and others.

name: subscript

topics.details: support for variations of typographic style

caption: Obsolete package to combine font families for different font encodings

descriptions.text:
This package used to facilitate the task of setting up a font family as a substitute for another one in a specified font encoding.

It has been obsoleted by the NFSS command \DeclareFontFamilySubstitution added to the LaTeX kernel in its 2020-02 release (cf. ltnews31).

Existing documents can be updated by removing \usepackage{substitutefont} and replacing all instances of \substitutefont with \DeclareFontFamilySubstitution.

name: substitutefont

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other font support

caption: A range of sub- and superscript commands

descriptions.text: The package provides a comprehensive and flexible set of commands for combinations of left and right sub- and superscripts.

name: subsupscripts

topics.details: position sub- and superscripts (left and right sides)

caption: Deal with substrings in strings

descriptions.text:
The package provides commands to deal with substrings of strings. Macros are provided to:

  • determine if one string is a substring of another,
  • return the parts of a string before or after a substring, and
  • count the number of occurrences of a substring.

name: substr

caption: Easy text-style subscripts in math mode

descriptions.text: This LaTeX package gives easy access to text-style subscripts in math mode by providing an optional argument to _. This is implemented by using the \text{} command from the amstext package.

name: subtext

caption: A set of sudoku-related packages

descriptions.text:
The bundle provides three packages:

  • printsudoku, which provides a command \sudoku whose argument is the name of a file containing a puzzle specification;
  • solvesudoku, which attempts to find a solution to the puzzle in the file named in the argument; and
  • createsudoku, which uses the random package to generate a puzzle according to a bunch of parameters that the user sets via macros.

The bundle comes with a set of ready-prepared puzzle files.

name: sudokubundle

topics.details: process game diagrams, gamebooks, and other amusements

caption: Create sudoku grids

descriptions.text:
The sudoku package provides an environment for typesetting sudoku grids.

A sudoku puzzle is a 9x9 grid where some of the squares in the grid contain numbers. The rules are simple: every column can only contain the digits 1 to 9, every row can only contain the digits 1 to 9 and every 3x3 box can only contain the digits 1 to 9.

More information, including help and example puzzles, can be found at sudoku.org.uk. This site also has blank sudoku grids (or worksheets), but you will not need to print them from there if you have this package installed.

name: sudoku

topics.details: process game diagrams, gamebooks, and other amusements

caption: Calligraphic font for typesetting handwriting in Sütterlin style

descriptions.text: Calligraphic font for typesetting handwriting in Sütterlin (characters which were used for writing in German-speaking countries in the first half of the 20th century, introduced at Prussian schools in 1915). The font is named after Ludwig Sütterlin, a German teacher and typographer.

name: sueterlin

caption: A document class for typesetting theses, books and articles

descriptions.text: The class can be used to typeset any kind of book (originally designed for use in the humanities).

name: suftesi

caption: Define commands with suffixes

descriptions.text: The \WithSuffix command enables you to define and maintain command variants like \macro* and even \macro\/; the package requires eTeX version 2.

name: suffix

caption: SAS(R) user group conference proceedings document class

descriptions.text: The class may be used to typeset articles to be published in the proceedings of SAS(R) User group conferences and workshops. The layout produced by the class is based on that published by SAS Institute (2021).

name: sugconf

caption: Attach superior figures to a font family

descriptions.text: The package allows the attachment of an arbitrary superior figures font to a font family that lacks one. (Superior figures are commonly used as footnote markers.) Two superior figures fonts are provided—one matching Times, the other matching Libertine.

name: superiors

topics.details: fonts that provide collections of symbols
metrics, macro incantations and other font support
font available in Adobe Type 1 format

caption: Abbreviate the word “Suppose”

descriptions.text:
This package provides commands for abbreviating the word “Suppose” in six fonts and with other variations.

The author recommends only using these commands when the immediately succeeding strings are mathematical in nature. He does not recommend using them in formal work.

The package requires amsmath, amsfonts, and graphicx.

name: suppose

topics.details: macros for defining abbreviations in documents

caption: A multi-page tables package

descriptions.text: The package was a predecessor of longtable; the newer package (designed on quite different principles) is easier to use and more flexible, in many cases, but supertabular retains its usefulness in a few situations where longtable has problems.

name: supertabular

topics.details: typeset tables that may be too big for a page

caption: Macros for SuperSymmetry-related work

descriptions.text: The package provides abbreviations of longer expressions.

name: susy

caption: Typeset a Stanford University thesis

descriptions.text:
This is a LaTeX 2.09 document style option (for report style), but looks as if it might work with current LaTeX.

The package source contains usage instructions.

name: suthesis

caption: A set of verbatim text manipulations

descriptions.text:
The sverb package reimplements much of the verbatim and moreverb packages in a way that is arguably more efficient.

The package is part of the mdwtools bundle.

name: sverb

topics.details: print (La)TeX code verbatim alongside the rendered result

caption: Typeset Subversion keywords

descriptions.text: The svn package lets you typeset (in LaTeX) the value of Subversion keywords. It is approximately an equivalent to the rcs package, but for Subversion rather than CVS. Details of Subversion (a replacement for CVS) is available from the project’s home site.

name: svn

topics.details: support for keeping track of document development

caption: How to include an SVG image in LaTeX using Inkscape

descriptions.text:
The document demonstrates the use of SVG images in LaTeX documents. Using the “PDF+LaTeX output” option of Inkscape, it is possible to include SVG in documents, in which LaTeX typesets the text. This results in uniform text style throughout the document, including text in images; moreover, LaTeX commands may be used in the image’s text, providing such things as mathematics and references.

The document also describes how to automate the conversion from SVG to PDF+LaTeX using Inkscape.

name: svg-inkscape

caption: Subversion keywords in multi-file LaTeX documents

descriptions.text:
This package lets you typeset keywords of the version control system Subversion inside your LaTeX files anywhere you like. Unlike the otherwise similar package svn the use of multiple files for one LaTeX document is well supported.

The package uses the author’s filehook and currfile packages.

The package interacts with an external Perl script, to retrieve information necessary for the required output.

name: svn-multi

topics.details: support for keeping track of document development

caption: Define SVG named colours

descriptions.text: The package defines the W3C Scalable Vector Graphics (SVG) colour names for use with both the color and PSTricks packages.

name: svgcolor

caption: Include and extract SVG pictures in LaTeX documents

descriptions.text:
This bundle contains the two packages svg and svg-extract.

The svg package is intended for the automated integration of SVG graphics into LaTeX documents. Therefore the capabilities provided by Inkscape — or more precisely its command line tool — are used to export the text within an SVG graphic to a separate file, which is then rendered by LaTeX. For this purpose the two commands \includesvg and \includeinkscape are provided which are very similar to the \includegraphics command of the graphicx package.

In addition, the package svg-extract allows the extraction of these graphics into independent files in different graphic formats, exactly as it is rendered within the LaTeX document, using either ImageMagick or Ghostscript.

name: svg

topics.details: convert a foreign graphics format for use with TeX

caption: A font with symbols for use in physics texts

copyright.owner: Pablo Garcia Risueno, Apostolos Syropoulos, and Natalia Verges

descriptions.text: The svrsymbols package is a LaTeX interface to the SVRsymbols font. The glyphs of this font are ideograms that have been designed for use in physics texts. Some symbols are standard and some are entirely new.

name: svrsymbols

caption: Swedish bibliography styles

descriptions.text: The bundle contains Swedish versions of the standard bibliography styles, and of the style plainnat. The styles should be funtionally equivalent to the corresponding original styles, apart from the Swedish translations. The styles do not implement Swedish collation.

name: swebib

caption: Plain TeX support for writing Swedish

descriptions.text: Subverts several characters for Swedish non-ascii letters, and uses <> for delimiters.

name: swetex

caption: Typeset Subversion keywords

descriptions.text: A package for incorporating the values of Subversion keywords into typeset documents. Information about Subversion (a replacement for CVS) is available from the project’s home site.

name: svninfo

topics.details: support for keeping track of document development

caption: Edit doc.sty and normal LaTeX files with GNU Emacs

descriptions.text: DocTeX mode is for editing buffers containing self-documenting LaTeX code that uses the doc package, including the ltxdoc document class. DocTeX mode was designed to be significantly more useful than the alternatives provided by standard Emacs and AUC TeX (AUC TeX has since caught up in this regard). SwifTeX mode is for editing buffers containing normal LaTeX files and provides an alternative to the LaTeX modes in the standard Emacs distribution and in AUC TeX.

name: swiftex

topics.details: plug-ins for editors, for better (La)TeX and Meta* support

caption: Subversion variants of \Provides... macros

descriptions.text: The package introduces Subversion variants of the standard LaTeX macros \ProvidesPackage, \ProvidesClass and \ProvidesFile where the file name and date is extracted from Subversion Id keywords. The file name may also be given explicitly as an optional argument.

name: svn-prov

topics.details: support for keeping track of document development

caption: Insert large images that do not fit into a single page

descriptions.text: Five different display modes are defined in order to place in a document large figures that do not fit into a single page. A single user macro is defined to handle all five display modes.

name: swfigure

caption: Graphical/textual representations of swimming performances

descriptions.text:
The package provides two macros that produce representations of a swimmer's performances. The user records data in a text file and specifies as arguments of the macros the date range of interest. The macros extract the relevant information from the file and process it: \swimgraph produces a graph of the times in a single swimming event (specified as an argument), plotting long course and short course times in separate lines. Records and qualifying times, stored in text files, may optionally be included on the graph. \swimtext produces a written record of the times in all events.

Files of current world and Canadian records are included.

The package requires the PSTricks and keyval packages. For attractive output it also requires a colour output device.

name: Swimgraf

caption: Obfuscate email addresses (now obsolete)

descriptions.text:
The package (roughly) parses an email address, and writes it out as a series of boxes in a jumbled order, but with positioning commands to make the result print correctly. This performance will confuse address-harvesters that look inside your PostScript or PDF files on the web.

This package is considered obsolete; its facilities are now provided by the randtext package.

name: switcheml

caption: Typeset a swung dash in LaTeX

descriptions.text: The swung dash (U+2053) is a useful character traditionally used in typsetting dictionaries, but not supported by most typefaces. This package provides one simple command to typeset a swung dash in XeLaTeX and LuaLaTeX, by applying transformations to the given font's glyph for a tilde.

name: swungdash

topics.details: support for variations of typographic style

caption: Macros to use the Symbats3 dingbats fonts

descriptions.text: This package makes available for LaTeX the glyphs in Feòrag’s OpenType Symbats3 neopagan dingbats fonts.

name: symbats3

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other support for symbol fonts
fonts that provide collections of symbols
support is for a font not available on CTAN

caption: Work with SymPy and PyLuaTeX

descriptions.text:
This package provides some commands (mostly for French users) to perform SymPy commands and format the result with some adjustments in formatting:

  • \sympycalc to perform a generic SymPy command;
  • \sympyfact or \sympydev to factor or expand;
  • \sympyderiv, \sympyprim or \sympyintegr to derive or integrate ;
  • \sympyreso to resolve equations
  • ...

name: SympyCalc

topics.details: call external code and process the result
LuaTeX and packages that require it

caption: Typeset syllogisms in LaTeX

descriptions.text: The package provides a simple, configurable, way for neatly typesetting syllogisms and syllogistic-like arguments, composed of two premises and a conclusion.

name: syllogism

caption: Generate a list of symbols with different subgroups

descriptions.text:
This extension can be used regardless of the platform.

It defines a new command

\addsymbol[group]{symbol}{description}

and the list of the symbols sorted by groups and symbols can be shown with

\listofsymbols

The program makesym (source, and DOS executable provided), is used to process symbol details, for subsequent typesetting runs.

The index is generated with a \listofsymbols command.

name: symbolindex

caption: Lines thicker in the middle than at the ends

descriptions.text: Defines commands that create rules split into a (specified) number of pieces, whose size varies to produce the effect of a rule that swells in its centre.

name: swrule

topics.details: highlighting typeset material, fancy frames, watermarks, etc.

caption: Include symbolic computation (using sympy) in documents

descriptions.text: The bundle supports inclusion of symbolic-python (sympy) expressions, as well as graphical output from the sympy plotting module (or from matplotlib).

name: sympytex

topics.details: call external code and process the result

caption: Reference management tool for BibTeX

descriptions.text:
Synapsen is a hypertextual card index or reference organizer, especially designed for BibTeX, and offering support for the requirements of BibLaTeX.

The Software is written in JAVA, and runs on all major operating systems (Windows, Mac OS X, Linux, Unix).

The software features automatic or individual connections between cards; direct search and download from public bibliographic sources; fully compliant BibTeX output for LaTeX; support for word processors via RTF output; Unicode support; support for SQL database to secure future accessibility of data.

name: Synapsen

caption: SyncTeX output file parser

descriptions.text: These are the sources (in C) of a parser module for SyncTeX output.

name: synctex-parser

topics.details: support for package or document debugging

caption: Typeset syntax descriptions

descriptions.text:
The package implements a simple, clear, graphical description of simple syntaxes.

The package is part of the mdwtools bundle.

name: syntax-mdw

caption: A tool for generating syntax diagrams from BNF

descriptions.text: A tool for generating syntax diagrams from BNF. The diagrams use the LaTeX picture mode and can be included in any LaTeX2e document.

name: syngen

caption: Easy drawing of syntactic proofs

descriptions.text: The package provides a set of macros based on PSTricks that will enable you to draw syntactic proofs easily (inspired by the Gamut books). Very few commands are needed, however fine tuning of the various parameters (dimensions) can still be achieved through “key=value” pairs.

name: synproof

caption: Create “railroad” syntax diagrams

copyright.owner: Johannes Pieper, André Hilbig, Johannes Kuhaupt,                     Daniel Spittank, Ludger Humbert, Adrian Salamon

descriptions.text:
This package provides TikZ styles for creating special syntax diagrams known as “railroad” diagrams.

The package was originally distributed as part of the schule bundle.

name: syntaxdi

caption: Creation of syntax diagrams

descriptions.text: Create syntax diagrams using special environments and commands to represent the diagram structure.

name: syntax2

caption: Run a document through LaTeX for syntax checking

descriptions.text:
The package provides a command \syntaxonly that suppresses output from a LaTeX run. (The purpose, of course, is to check the syntax of a LaTeX file without the overhead of generating output.

The file is part of the LaTeX distribution.

name: syntonly

topics.details: support for package or document debugging

caption: Labels for tracing in a syntax tree

descriptions.text: This package adds support for traces in trees created using either the synttree or the qtree package. The package provides two commands (\traceLabel and \traceReference) to set and use a trace.

name: syntrace

caption: Typeset syntactic trees

descriptions.text: A package to typeset syntactic trees such as those used in Chomsky's Generative grammar, based on a description of the structure of the tree.

name: synttree

caption: A font for Syriac written in Estrangelo

descriptions.text: The font is specified in a single Metafont file.

name: syriac

topics.details: fonts reproducing archaic scripts or inscriptions
font available in Adobe Type 1 format

caption: Support for Systems and Control Letters

descriptions.text: A LaTeX 2.09 document style for preparing papers for the journal.

name: systcontrolletters

topics.details: package only known to work with LaTeX 2.09

caption: Format systems of equations

descriptions.text:
The package allows you to enter systems of equations or inequalities in an intuitive way, and produces typeset output where the terms and signs are aligned vertically.

The package works with plain TeX or LaTeX, but e-TeX is required.
Cette petite extension permet de saisir des systèmes d'équations ou inéquations de façon intuitive, et produit un affichage où les termes et les signes sont alignés verticalement.

name: systeme

caption: Draw tangles, trees, Hopf algebra operations and other pictures

descriptions.text: A LaTeX2e package for drawing tangles, trees, Hopf algebra operations and other pictures. It is based on emTeX or TPIC \specials. Therefore, it can be used with the most popular drivers, including emTeX drivers, dviwin, xdvi and dvips, and (using some code from ConTeXt) it may also be used with pdfLaTeX.

name: t-angles

topics.details: graphics produced by one of the *TeX engines

caption: Standard package for activating ec fonts

descriptions.text: Obsolete package for activating T1 font encoding. The replacement fontenc package with (optional) argument T1 does this task more satisfactorily.

name: t1enc

topics.details: input encoding support for TeX engines

caption: A pair of fraktur font families in T1 encoding

descriptions.text:
These fonts were (it seems) originally developed for use with Czech and other Eastern European languages, and then extended for more general use. They don't, in fact, cover the entire T1 encoding, but they come pretty close. The fonts are distributed as Metafont source.

Both font families come in both upright and "slanted" shape, and in both medium and bold weight (an interesting choice, given that the “medium” is already pretty heavy).

name: t1-fraktur

topics.details: font for gothic or blackletter shapes

caption: Utilities for PostScript fonts

descriptions.text:
There are here two little programs written in C (using t1lib) for scanning Type 1 fonts, and doing:
– compute the ‘black area’ of each glyph, with how much percent of the square containing the glyph is black, and
– checking if the ‘extremas’ (see Adobe Type 1 specifications) of the outline are correct, and tell which one are missing.

There is also here a PostScript dictionary containing three algorithms for automatic kerning (the kerning is computed ‘on the fly’ instead of being pre-computed by external software like TeX, groff or lout; very useful for some PostScript hacking). Two of these algorithms are quite classical; the third is original and is PostScript-optimized. The PostScript file in the distribution contains both demonstration code and the dictionary itself.

name: t1infos

caption: A C++ library for subsetting PostScript Type 1 fonts

descriptions.text:
T1Subset creates a subset of a PostScript Type 1 font. It is a header-only library as the complete functionalities are done in the header.

Note that only the unused glyphs are removed; subsetting of subroutines is not currently supported, although this may change in a future version.

In addition, only the following built-in encodings are currently supported: StandardEncoding, WinAnsiEncoding, and MacRomanEncoding. Other encodings may be supported in a future version.

license.name: GNU General Public License, version 3 or newer

name: T1Subset

topics.details: process fonts for use with TeX (includes installation)
support for font development, testing and characterisation

caption: Facilities for handling Adobe Type 1 fonts

descriptions.text:
This bundle contains several utilities for tasks such as making AFM files from the Type 1 fonts themselves, converting AFM files to PFM files, viewing Type 1 fonts, etc.

The utilities are said to run both under MS-DOS and under Unix.

name: t1tools

caption: Simple Type 1 font manipulation programs

descriptions.text:
A collection of simple programs for manipulating Adobe Type 1 fonts, comprising:
– t1ascii: convert PFB (binary) to PFA (ascii) fonts;
– t1binary: convert PFA to PFB fonts;
– t1disasm: convert PFA or PFB fonts to human-readable and -editable format;
– t1asm: reassemble such editable formats to a font;
– t1unmac: extract font resources from a Macintosh font file; and
– t1mac: generate a Macintosh font from a Type 1 font.

name: t1utils

caption: Tabbing with accented letters

descriptions.text: By default, some of the tabbing environment's commands clash with default accent commands; LaTeX provides the odd commands \a', etc., to deal with the clash. The package offers a variant of the tabbing environment which does not create this difficulty, so that users need not learn two sets of accent commands.

name: tabbing

caption: Preprocessor for LaTeX tabular environments

descriptions.text:
Tab4tex is a SNOBOL program that transforms a text file with very simple tagging into a LaTeX table using the tabular environment.

The tags support several kinds of alignments, horizontal and vertical bars, and some basic text formatting (italics, bold, small caps).

name: tab4tex

topics.details: import files in a non-TeX (or different TeX) format

caption: Support for using T2 encoding

descriptions.text:
The T2 bundle provides a variety of separate support functions for using Cyrillic characters in LaTeX:

  • the mathtext package, for using Cyrillic letters ‘transparently’ in formulae;
  • the citehack package, for using Cyrillic (or indeed any non-ascii) characters in citation keys;
  • support for Cyrillic in BibTeX;
  • support for Cyrillic in Makeindex; and
  • various items of font support.

name: t2

topics.details: support languages written using Cyrillic alphabets

caption: Maintain vertical alignment of figures

descriptions.text:
Knuth designed his original fonts with tabular figures (figures whose width is uniform); this makes some layout problems rather simple. In more recent times, fonts (such as Minion Pro), which offer proportionally spaced figures, are increasingly being used.

The package provides mechanisms whereby such proportional figures may still be aligned in tabular style (for example, in the table of contents).

name: tabfigures

topics.details: support for variations of typographic style

caption: Draw a variations table of functions and a convexity table of its graph

descriptions.text:
Draw a variations table of functions and a convexity table of its graph

This version offers two environnements, to draw variations table of a function and a convexity table of its graph.

name: table-fct

caption: Save a tabbing environment in a box

descriptions.text:
Defines an environment tabbingbox, which puts tabbing environment commands in a box. This is one way of getting a bunch of lines into a box, where the width of the box is that of the widest line.

The macros use the maybeload and redefine macro bundles.

name: tabbingbox

caption: Permit footnotes in tables

descriptions.text: The package provides the command \tablefootnote to be used in a table or sidewaystable environment, where \footnote will not work (and when using \footnotemark and \footnotetext, and adjusting the counter as necessary, is too much work).

name: tablefootnote

caption: Variation tables in MetaPost

descriptions.text: Utility macros for creating tables of signs and of variations. The LaTeX package tablor provides an interface to this package.

name: tableauVariations

topics.details: mathematical tables of signs and variations

caption: Construct tables of signs and variations

descriptions.text: The package uses PSTricks; the user may define the width of the table, the number of lines and the height of each line. Placement of labels within the boxes may be absolute, or as a percentage of the width; various other controls are available.

name: tableaux

topics.details: mathematical tables of signs and variations

caption: Tagging tables of contents

descriptions.text: The package provides the commands to flag chapters or sections (or anything else destined to become a TOC line). The command \nexttocwithtags{req1,req2,...}{excl1,excl2,...} specifies which tags are to be required and which ones are to be excluded by the next \tableofcontents (or equivalent) command. In a document that uses a class where \tableofcontents may only be used once, the command \tableoftaggedcontents{req1,req2,...}{excl1,excl2,...} may be used to provide several tables.

name: tableof

topics.details: deal with Tables of Contents, and of other such things

caption: Tables without the need for a preamble

descriptions.text: The original of this package was written for Plain TeX, and seems to have been lost. This version works for LaTeX 2.09, but not (apparently) for current LaTeX; it seems odd to have converted it for LaTeX, since LaTeX's tables model seems to cover most of what the package does (albeit rather differently).

name: tables

caption: Styles for tables with new commands

descriptions.text:
This package tries to introduce a separation of text and style in tables by defining reusable table commands and a simple interface to define a style for a table. Furthermore the package defines commonly used column styles and a bugfix command for lists in tables.

However, the author told us in March 2023: “I wrote [this package] about ten years ago, [...] since at that time no package with layout options for tabulars was available. [...] However since nowadays much better packages are available that do the same job, but are much more professional in code base, usability and results, I want to remove my package from CTAN.”

name: tablestyles

caption: Tabulated lists of short items

descriptions.text: This package offers environments and commands for one-level and two-level lists of short items (e.g., exercises in textbooks). The environments support optional arguments of item numbering similar to the enumerate or paralist packages.

name: tablists

caption: Create tables of signs and of variations

descriptions.text:
The package allows the user to use the computer algebra system XCAS to generate tables of signs and of variations (the actual plotting of the tables uses the MetaPost macro package tableauVariations). Tables with forbidden regions may be developed using the package.

A configuration file permits some configuration of the language to be used in the diagrams.

The tablor package requires that shell escape be enabled.

name: tablor

topics.details: mathematical tables of signs and variations

caption: Typesetting pretty tables of signs and variations according to French usage

descriptions.text:
This is a complete and easy-to-use package for typesetting pretty tables of signs and variations according to French usage.

  • The syntax is similar to that of the array environment and uses intuitive position commands.
  • Arrows are drawn automatically (using PSTricks by default or TikZ as an option).
  • Macros are provided for drawing twin bars, single bars crossing the zeros, areas where the function is not defined, or placing special values.
  • Several features of the variation tables can be customized.

name: tablvar

topics.details: mathematical tables of signs and variations

caption: A template for the University of Tabriz

descriptions.text: The package offers a document class for typesetting theses and dissertations at the University of Tabriz. The class requires use of XeLaTeX.

name: tabriz-thesis

topics.details: XeTeX, material supporting it, and packages requiring it

caption: "Tab" to a measured position in the line

descriptions.text: \tabto{<length>} moves the typesetting position to <length> from the left margin of the paragraph. If the typesetting position is already further along, \tabto starts a new line.

name: tabto-generic

topics.details: layout of objects on the page

caption: Better vertical spacing in tables and arrays

descriptions.text: Modifies LaTeX’s array and tabular environments to keep text from touching other text or hlines above or below. Several new parameters are defined and some standard macros are re-defined. The package slows down compilation of tables, since each entry is boxed twice.

name: tabls

caption: “Tab” to a measured position in the line

descriptions.text:
\tabto{<length>} moves the typesetting position to <length> from the left margin of the paragraph. If the typesetting position is already further along, \tabto starts a new line; the command \tabto* will move position backwards if necessary, so that previous text may be overwritten.

The command \TabPositions may be used to define a set of tabbing positions, after which the command \tab advances typesetting position to the next defined ‘tab stop’.

name: tabto-ltx

topics.details: layout of objects on the page

caption: How to use tables in LaTeX

descriptions.text: A tutorial on typessetting tables with some examples (in German).

name: tabsatz

caption: “Tabbing” front-end to stackengine

descriptions.text:
The package provides a front end to the stackengine package, to allow tabbed stacking. In most cases, an existing stackengine command may be prepended with the word “tabbed”, “align” or “tabular” to create a new tabbed version of a stacking macro.

In addition, hooks in the package’s parser that tabbed strings of data may be parsed, extracted, and reconstituted (not requiring use of any stacking constructions).

name: tabstackengine

caption: Flexible LaTeX tabulars

descriptions.text:
The package provides an environment, tabu, which will make any sort of tabular (that doesn’t need to split across pages), and an environment longtabu which provides the facilities of tabu in a modified longtable environment. (Note that this latter offers an enhancement of ltxtable.)

The package requires the array package, and needs e-TeX to run (since array.sty is present in every conforming distribution of LaTeX, and since every publicly available LaTeX format is built using e-TeX, the requirements are provided by default on any reasonable system). The package also requires xcolor for coloured rules in tables, and colortbl for coloured cells. The longtabu environment further requires that longtable be loaded. The package itself does not load any of these packages for the user.

The tabu environment may be used in place of tabular, tabular* and tabularx environments, as well as the array environment in maths mode. It overloads tabularx’s X-column specification, allowing a width specification, alignment (l, r, c and j) and column type indication (p, m and b).

\begin{tabu} to <dimen> specifies a target width, and \begin{tabu} spread <dimen> enlarges the environment’s “natural” width.

name: tabu

topics.details: typeset tables that may be too big for a page

caption: Remove excess space at left and right of tabular

descriptions.text: The tabular environment is changed so that the outer \tabcolseps are compensated and a \hline has the same length as the text. No @{} is needed.

name: tabularborder

caption: Calculate formulas in a tabular environment

descriptions.text:
Given a list of numbers and one (or more) formulas, the package offers an easy syntax to build a table of values, i.e., a tabular in which the first row contains the list of numbers, and the other rows contain the calculated values of the formulas for each number of the list.

The table may be built either horizontally or vertically and is fully customizable.

name: tabularcalc

caption: Tabular environments with height specified

descriptions.text:
The tabularht package defines some environments that add a height specification to tabular and array environments. The default set of new environments take a value for their height in the first argument: defined environments are: tabularht, tabularht* and arrayht. If package tabularx is also loaded, the package also defines environments tabularxht and tabularxht*.

The places where stretching is to happen are signalled by
\noalign{\vfill}
immediately after the \\ that ends a row of the table or array.

name: tabularht

caption: Tabular environments with key-value interface

descriptions.text: The tabularkv package creates an environment tabularkv, whose arguments are specified in key-value form. The arguments chosen determine which other type of tabular is to be used (whether standard LaTeX ones, or environments from the tabularx or the tabularht package).

name: tabularkv

caption: Typeset tabulars and arrays with LaTeX3

descriptions.text:
LaTeX tables are implemented using TeX commands such as \halign, \noalign, \span, and \omit. In order to implement new features, many macro packages have modified the inner table commands inside LaTeX. This makes package code complicated, difficult to maintain, and often conflicts with each other.

At present, the LaTeX3 programming layer is basically mature. This tabularray package will discard the old \halign commands and directly use LaTeX3 functions to parse the table, and then typeset the entire table. Under the premise of being compatible with the basic syntax of LaTeX2 tables, this macro package will completely separate the content and style of the table, and the style of the table can be completely set in keyval way.

name: tabularray

topics.details: typeset tables that may be too big for a page

caption: Examples from the book "Typesetting tables with LaTeX"

descriptions.text: The bundle presents the examples of the book “Typesetting tables with LaTeX” (ISBN 978-1-906860-25-7), as standalone documents.

name: tabulars-e

topics.details: copies of examples from a published book

caption: A variation on the tabular environment

descriptions.text: The package offers a modification of the tabular environment, which deals with the problem of column heads that are significantly wider than the body of the column.

name: tabularew

caption: Tabulars with adjustable-width columns

descriptions.text:
The package defines an environment tabularx, an extension of tabular which has an additional column designator, X, which creates a paragraph-like column whose width automatically expands so that the declared width of the environment is filled. (Two X columns together share out the available space between them, and so on.)

The package is part of the latex-tools bundle in the LaTeX required distribution.

name: tabularx

caption: Tabular with variable width columns balanced

descriptions.text: The package defines a tabular*-like environment, tabulary, taking a ‘total width’ argument as well as the column specifications. The environment uses column types L, C, R and J for variable width columns (\raggedright', \centering, \raggedleft, and normally justified). In contrast to tabularx's X columns, the width of each column is weighted according to the natural width of the widest cell in the column.

name: tabulary

caption: Verbatim text respecting TAB characters

descriptions.text:
The (LaTeX 2.09) package provides a version of the verbatim environment that respects TAB and FF (control-L) characters; the space between tab-stops is programmable. A \inputverbatim command is also available.

Note that the facilities of this package (apart from FF support) are provided by the LaTeX 2e package moreverb.

name: tabverb

caption: Tools for experimenting with tagging using pdfLaTeX and LuaLaTeX

descriptions.text: The package offers tools to experiment with tagging and accessibility using pdfLaTeX and LuaTeX. It isn’t meant for production but allows the user to try out how difficult it is to tag some structures; to try out how much tagging is really needed; to test what else is needed so that a pdf works e.g. with a screen reader. Its goal is to get a feeling for what has to be done, which kernel changes are needed, how packages should be adapted.

name: tagpdf

caption: Document configuration with tags

descriptions.text: The package allows the user to generate multiple documents from a single source, by marking pieces of the document with tags and specifying which marked pieces to include or exclude.

name: tagging

caption: Typesetting tables showing variations of functions

descriptions.text: This LaTeX package is meant to ease the typesetting of tables showing variations of functions as they are used in France.

name: tabvar

topics.details: mathematical tables of signs and variations

caption: Word-by-word glosses, translations, and bibliographic attributions

descriptions.text:
This package provides environments and commands for pairing lines, bottom lines, and tagged lines, intended to be used in particular for word-by-word glosses, translations, and bibliographic attributions, respectively.

This LaTeX package is inspired by Marcel R. van der Goot's classic Plain TeX macros in gloss.tex .

name: tagpair

caption: A LaTeX class for presentations

descriptions.text:
The talk document class allows you to create slides for screen presentations or printing on transparencies. It also allows you to print personal notes for your talk. You can create overlays and display structure information (current section / subsection, table of contents) on your slides. The main feature that distinguishes talk from other presentation classes like beamer or prosper is that it allows the user to define an arbitrary number of slide styles and switch between these styles from slide to slide. This way the slide layout can be adapted to the slide content. For example, the title or contents page of a talk can be given a slightly different layout than the other slides.

The talk class makes no restrictions on the slide design whatsoever. The entire look and feel of the presentation can be defined by the user. The style definitions should be put in a separate sty file. Currently the package comes with only one set of pre-defined slide styles (greybars.sty). Contributions from people who are artistically more gifted than the author are more than welcome!

name: talk

caption: A Greek cult font from the eighties

descriptions.text: A cult Greek font from the eighties, used at the University of Crete, Greece. It belonged to the first TeX installation in a Greek University and most probably the first TeX installation that supported the Greek language.

name: talos

topics.details: font for Greek (archaic, classical and modern)

caption: Experimentally use \holdinginserts with LaTeX floats

descriptions.text: LaTeX’s figures, tables, and \marginpars are dangerous for footnotes (and probably also \enlargethispage). Here is a proposal (a ‘patch’ package) to help, by using \holdinginserts in a simple way. It replaces the original problem with a new one — it is an experiment to find out whether the new problem is less bad (or it is just a contribution to the discussion, maybe just a summary of previous work). The files provide further information.

name: tamefloats

topics.details: offer of a facility that may never make its way to production use

caption: A manual about bibliographies and especially BibTeX

descriptions.text: An (as-complete-as-possible) manual about bibliographies in LaTeX, and thus mainly about BibTeX.

name: TameTheBeast

topics.details: documentation of BibTeX, etc., on their own

caption: Generate compilable source from web

descriptions.text: This is the component of Knuth’s literate programming system that produces a compilable source from the web representation of a program.

name: tangle

caption: Tamil support for Omega/Aleph

descriptions.text:
Omega for Tamil is a package for typesetting Tamil using Omega; it is also compatible with Aleph.

The package includes only one font family, Washington Tamil by Thomas Ridgeway et.al.

The package also includes supporting files for using the Tamil fonts from ‘ISM Publisher’ by C-DAC India.

name: tamil-omega

topics.details: support for languages of the Indian subcontinent
fonts for languages of the Indian subcontinent
Omega and packages that use it
font available in Adobe Type 1 format

caption: A simple Web system

descriptions.text:
A simple web system (with both tangle and weave capabilities), on the lines of noweb.

The system's selling points are that it's written in standard C, which tends to make porting easier, and that it supports inter-file cross references.

name: tango-weevil

caption: Use colors from the Tango color palette

descriptions.text:
The Tango color palette defines some color names and their RGB codes. This LaTeX macro package implements these color names, so one can easily access these colors by their names.

The package relies on the xcolor package, so please refer to the documentation to that package to learn how to access the defined colors.

name: tangocolors

caption: Tangram puzzles, with TikZ

descriptions.text:
This package provides some commands (with English and French keys) to work with tangram puzzles:

  • \begin{EnvTangramTikz} and \PieceTangram to position a piece,
  • \TangramTikz to display a predefined Tangram.

name: TangramTikZ

topics.details: process game diagrams, gamebooks, and other amusements
problems and puzzles, and their solutions

caption: TeX macros for typesetting complex tables

descriptions.text: The package offers a simple notation for pretty complex tables (to Michael J. Ferguson’s credit). With PostScript, the package allows shaded/coloured tables, diagonal rules, etc. The package is supposed to work with both Plain and LaTeX. An AWK converter from ASCII semigraphic tables to TAP notation is included.

name: tap

caption: A simple geometrical font

descriptions.text:
Tapír is a simple geometrical font mostly created of line and circular segments with constant thickness. The font is available as Metafont source and in Adobe Type 1 format.

The character set contains all characters in the range 0–127 (as in cmr10), accented characters used in the Czech, Slovak and Polish languages.

name: tapir

topics.details: support for typesetting, and documentation in Slovak
font available in Adobe Type 1 format

caption: Horizontally columned lists

descriptions.text: The reason for the creation of the tasks environment was an unwritten agreement in German maths textbooks (especially (junior) high school textbooks) to organize exercises in columns counting horizontally rather than vertically. This is what the tasks package helps to achieve.

name: tasks

caption: Generate cassette labels from a simple database

descriptions.text:
This LaTeX 2.09 package expects a database which lists cassette details (including track details) in a TeX-based format.

The package megatape extends this one.

name: tape

topics.details: typeset badges, covers or labels for things (or people)

caption: Macros for category-theoretic diagrams

descriptions.text: A carefully-designed and consistent set of macros, that work equally in Plain TeX and LaTeX, using fonts included in all modern distributions by default.

name: taylor

caption: Extracts from "TeX by Example"

descriptions.text: Some macros (tbemacros.tex) and their usage (tbesamples.tex) from the book.

license.name: Do Not Sell Except by Arrangement

name: tbe

topics.details: copies of examples from a published book

caption: Doc/docstrip for tcl

descriptions.text: The tclldoc package and class simplify the application of the doc/docstrip style of literate programming with Dr. John Ousterhout’s Tool Command Language (Tcl, pronounced “tickle”, a.k.a. The Cool Language). The tclldoc package is a bit like the doc package is for LaTeX, whereas the tclldoc class more parallels the ltxdoc class.

name: tclldoc

topics.details: macros and tools for preparing documentation

caption: Provide compatibility names for textcomp.sty

descriptions.text: When TS1 (text symbol) support was integrated into the LaTeX kernel, some of the encoding-dependent names used in older versions of the textcomp package were changed. This package re-declares those names for compatibility use in old documents.

name: tccompat

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other font support

caption: LaTeX editor written in TCL

descriptions.text:
TclTexEd is an editor written in the scripting language Tcl/Tk and is highly specialized for writing LaTeX documents.

The editor works both on Unix and Windows systems if a Tcl/Tk interpreter (>8.0) is installed.

name: tcltexed

topics.details: editor designed (or adapted) for use with (La)TeX

caption: Local browsing of the Catalogue on Mac OS X

descriptions.text: TCOBrowser is a Cocoa viewer application dedicated to the TeX Catalogue Online, using the XML version of the catalogue. It was written to provide an easy way for Mac OS X users to access documentation and information about TeX and TeX-related packages available through CTAN, as well as some of the documentation on their local system.

name: tcobrowser

topics.details: support for work with the CTAN archive

caption: Coloured boxes, for LaTeX examples and theorems, etc

copyright.owner: Prof. Dr. Dr. Thomas F. Sturm

descriptions.text:
This package provides an environment for coloured and framed text boxes with a heading line. Optionally, such a box may be split in an upper and a lower part; thus the package may be used for the setting of LaTeX examples where one part of the box displays the source code and the other part shows the output. Another common use case is the setting of theorems. The package supports saving and reuse of source code and text parts.

The package depends on the pgf, verbatim, environ, and etoolbox packages.

name: tcolorbox

topics.details: print (La)TeX code verbatim alongside the rendered result

caption: The TeX Directory Structure standard

descriptions.text: Defines a structure for placement of TeX-related files on an hierarchical file system, in a way that is well-defined, and is readily implementable.

name: tds

topics.details: standards, or other normative documents, about TeX and friends

caption: A ticking digital clock package for PDF output

descriptions.text: A ticking digital clock package to be used in Pdf-LaTeX documents, for example in presentations.

name: tdclock

caption: Vietnamese Windows support

descriptions.text:
A package for Vietnamese TCVN encoding which is widely used in MS-Windows applications.

The package is distributed as part of the ‘vietnet’ bundle.

name: tcvn

topics.details: input encoding support for TeX engines

caption: Macros for French teachers of mathematics

descriptions.text: A collection of macros for French maths teachers in collèges and lycées (and perhaps elsewhere). It is hoped that the package will facilitate the everyday use of LaTeX by mathematics teachers.

name: tdsfrmath

caption: Browser plugin for viewing TeX and LaTeX sources

descriptions.text: The techexplorer hypermedia browser is a cross-platform, cross-browser plug-in for delivering high volume or advanced mathematics over the web. With techexplorer you can publish sophisticated mathematics and scientific content to the web using TeX or LaTeX.

name: techexplorer

topics.details: support for LaTeX(-alike) on the web, or feeding into other applications

caption: Typesetting for the humanities

descriptions.text: A suite of LaTeX packages for typesetting literary texts.

name: Technica

topics.details: support for studies in the humanities

caption: Generate Technical Reports using USC thesis style

descriptions.text: The package acts as a style option for the USC Thesis style, allowing the user to typeset technical reports.

name: techreport

caption: A package to format technical documents

descriptions.text: The package provides a very simple LaTeX document template, in the hope that this use of LaTeX will become attractive to typical word processor users. (Presentation is as if it were a class; users are expected to start from a template document.)

name: technics

caption: Template for theses on the Technion graduate school

descriptions.text: This is a template for writing a thesis according to the Technion specifications.

name: technion-thesis-template

caption: Help for users of TeX and LaTeX

descriptions.text: The package is output from a large project that aims to collect people’s postings, web pages and the like, to optimise searches and to answer questions efficiently.

name: TeEncontreX

caption: A (primitive) token list editor

descriptions.text:
Just like sed is a stream editor, ted is a token list editor. Actually, it is not as powerfull as sed, but its main feature is that it really works with tokens, not only characters.

The ted package provides two user macros: \Substitute and \ShowTokens. The first is maybe the most useful: it performs substitutions in token lists (even inside braces). The second displays each token of the list (one per line) with its catcode (in the list, not just the current one), and can be useful for debugging or for TeX learners.

Ted is designed to work well even if strange tokens (that is, unusual {charcode, catcode} pairs or tokens with a confusing meaning) occur in the list.

name: ted

topics.details: support for package or document debugging

caption: Format German phone numbers

descriptions.text:
The package provides a command \telprint for formatting German telephone numbers.

The package is part of the oberdiek bundle.

name: telprint

caption: (La)TeX Support for writing the Telugu Language

descriptions.text: TeluguTeX is (La)TeX Support for writing the Telugu Language, comprising Metafont fonts and macros.

name: telugu

topics.details: fonts for languages of the Indian subcontinent
support for languages of the Indian subcontinent

caption: Templates for TeX usage

descriptions.text:
A set of templates for using LaTeX packages that the author uses, comprising:
– scrlttr2.tex: a letter, written with scrlttr2.cls from the KOMA-Script bundle;
– dinbrief.tex: a letter according to the German (DIN) standards, written with dinbrief.cls;
– kbrief.tex: a brief memo (‘Kurzbrief’) to accompany enclosures, as used in German offices, again based on dinbrief;
– vermerk.tex: a general form for taking down notes on events in the office; and
– diabetes.tex: a diary for the basis-bolus insulin therapy of diabetes mellitus, using scrartcl.cls from the KOMA-Script bundle.

name: templates-fenn

caption: Greek and Cyrillic to accompany Times

descriptions.text:
This package, derived from TemporaLGCUni by Alexej Kryukov, is meant as a companion to Times text font packages, providing Greek and Cyrillic in matching weights and styles.

OpenType and Type1 fonts are provided, with LaTeX support files giving essentially complete LGR coverage of monotonic, polytonic and ancient Greek, and almost full T2A coverage of Cyrillic.

name: tempora

topics.details: font available in Adobe Type 1 format
font for Greek (archaic, classical and modern)
fonts for Cyrillic and related scripts

caption: Commands useful in LaTeX templates
